author: themancalledzac
body:
Builds `POST /api/read/user/share/email`. The frontend has been calling it since its PR #251 merged, and it 404s today.

## The item could not be built as specified

The board scoped this as "one `@PostMapping`, one `sendShareLinkEmail`, one request record, no new response type". That is not buildable: the endpoint would have nothing to put in the email. The frontend sends `{ toEmail }` and nothing else, and V56 stored only the SHA-256 of the token, so the share URL cannot be reconstructed server-side. The only two ways out were to rotate on send -- which the item explicitly forbids, since it cuts off a recipient still using the old link -- or to store a copy the owner can read back.

The frontend already assumes the second. Its `ShareSettings.token` docblock reads *"Null when it cannot be recovered -- a link minted before the backend stored a decryptable copy"*, which is the contract from `fec14e7`, a commit written 2026-08-14 and orphaned when it landed 14 minutes after its PR merged. This PR is that commit rebased onto `main`.

## What it does

V58 adds `token_cipher`. `token_hash` KEEPS its job as the unique lookup index, so `resolveByRawToken` is untouched; the new column holds the same token under AES-256-GCM, keyed on the existing `app.access-token.secret`, purely so the owner's page can display it. **No new env var.** Encrypted rather than plaintext because the key lives in configuration, not the database -- a dump on its own still yields nothing, which is the property hashing was there to provide.

`TokenCipher` sits alongside `TokenUtil` rather than replacing it. Hashing is correct when the server only needs to RECOGNISE a credential; encryption when its owner needs to READ it back. Decryption returns null on every failure -- absent, truncated, wrong key, tampered -- so a rotated secret degrades to the same "reset to get a new link" state as a pre-V58 row instead of breaking the page.

The endpoint sends the link already in circulation rather than minting one; a test pins that `mintOrRotate` is never called. An unrecoverable link is a 409, not a silent no-op. No `afterCommit` hook is needed here, unlike the invite flow, because nothing is written and a rollback cannot erase the token.

## Three adaptations `fec14e7` could not have known about

All from MR 15 #6 landing underneath it.

- Its migration was numbered V57, which `main` now uses for `lowercase_text_format_type`. Renumbered to V58, and every V57 reference in the share files with it.
- Its `emailLink` opened with an `isRealUser` guard, and it carried a test pinning a 401 from every route. MR 15 #6 moved that enforcement into `SecurityConfig`'s `/api/read/user/**` matcher and deleted exactly those assertions, so the guard is dead code and the test would have reinstated a pattern this repo removed on purpose. Both dropped; `/share/email` is added to `UserRoutesAuthorizationWebMvcTest` instead, where the rest of the surface is pinned.
- `frontendBaseUrl` was a `@Value` field. Converted to a constructor argument, matching `AdminUserController`, since CLAUDE.md forbids field injection.

## What changing the share-link lifecycle would do

Rotating on send would revoke the link every prior recipient holds, and every cookie minted from it, since the flyby cookie value IS the raw token. There is one row per user and rotation happens in place, so opt-ins survive but access does not. The failure is invisible from both ends: the sender gets `sent: true` either way. Not done.

What this PR does change is storage, not lifecycle. `share_link` stops being useless on its own: a database dump **plus** the configured `ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET` now yields live share links. That is the accepted tradeoff and the reason the value is encrypted rather than stored plainly.

**Before deploy.** Rotating `ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET` no longer affects only gallery HMAC tokens. Share links keep resolving, because lookup is still by hash, but every stored token becomes unreadable -- so every owner's page falls back to "reset to get a new link" and `/email` returns 409 for everyone. The same applies to `share_link` rows that already exist: no ciphertext, so their owners see that fallback until they reset once. Degradation, not breakage, by design.

Unchanged: mint/rotate semantics, the GENERAL ceiling, scope resolution, cookie lifetime.

## Deliberately not in scope

The share email copy does NOT mirror the invite email: it says the link keeps working until the sender resets it, where the invite says "works once, expires in 7 days". Opposite promises; the bodies should not drift toward each other. The three senders stay duplicated rather than folded into a shared template -- that is MR 24.

**Known follow-up:** no rate limit on the email endpoint. A per-user limiter along the lines of `AuthLoginLimiter` is the right next step before this sees real use.

## Verification

1,361 tests, 0 failures, 0 checkstyle violations. Three mutations verified red: sending a freshly minted link, dropping the trailing-slash strip, and returning the ciphertext undecrypted.

author: danialrami
body:
## What this implements

Unit 15 of the `lsbx` Rust rewrite (`docs/specs/2026-08-24T0030Z_rust-lsbx-rewrite/units/15-stdio-mcp-server.md`) — the `lsbx-mcp` crate, Door 4 from SPEC.md §4.8. Every one of `LsbxOps`'s 18 real public async methods gets exactly one `#[tool]`-annotated method on `LsbxMcpServer`, generated via the real `rmcp` crate (v3.1.4, confirmed on crates.io/docs.rs before writing any code, not assumed from training-era memory of an older 0.x API) using its `#[tool_router]`/`#[tool]`/`#[tool_handler]` macros.

**Built clean-room. Both Google Jules AI sessions for this unit never reached a usable state** — one failed outright, one is stuck waiting on an unanswered question. Nothing from either session is reflected anywhere in this PR.

## `LsbxOps` method list cross-checked against

Direct read of `crates/lsbx-ops/src/lib.rs` at `main`'s tip immediately before branching — commit `86506e28d0b4448527379e4487e7cab03341180d` (PR #15, "feat(unit-10): implement shared operations facade") — re-confirmed by a second direct re-read immediately before writing this crate. That file's own module doc comment ("Reconciling the unit contract's literal interface against the real merged source") documents exactly how `LsbxOps`'s real shape diverged from this unit's own contract's older literal listing during Units 08/09/10's implementation — this PR is written against that real, current shape, not the contract's superseded prose:

- `LsbxOps::new`'s real signature has an added `backend_name: String` parameter (no `Backend::name()` exists on the real trait).
- `create`'s request type is the real `lsbx_lifecycle::create::CreateRequest` (fields: `profile, name, task_id, lease, ready_timeout, verify, healthchecks` — no `id` field).
- `golden_build`/`golden_verify` take an explicit `pubkey: &str` (and `golden_verify` also `verify_name: &str`) that the contract's literal request structs don't carry, because `Backend::create_from_golden` requires one and no façade-level crate generates ephemeral keypairs.
- `golden_build` returns the real `GoldenBuildOutcome { config, build_vm_tag }`, not a bare `GoldenConfig`.
- 6 operations (`list`, `info`, `console_url`, `golden_register`, `golden_delete`, `golden_list`, `config_show`, `logs_query`) are implemented directly in `lsbx-ops` against `SandboxStore`/`ImageRegistry`'s real public methods rather than delegated to a lower crate — none of which exist as separate lower-crate functions.

**Unit 11 (`lsbx-cli`) has not merged as of this branch's base commit** — confirmed by enumerating every merged PR against `main` (PRs #1-#15, all titled/bodied for units 01-10, none for unit-11/`lsbx-cli`) and by the root `Cargo.toml`'s `members` list, which ends at `crates/lsbx-ops` with no `crates/lsbx-cli` entry. Per this unit's own mechanics, the CLI-parity test is therefore built against `LsbxOps`'s own method list — the more fundamental source of truth in any case, since a CLI's `Command` enum is itself just one more thin adapter over the same façade (SPEC.md §3: `lsbx-cli` and `lsbx-mcp` are siblings under `lsbx-ops`, neither derived from the other). `tests/test_cli_parity.rs` documents this explicitly and is written so that, once Unit 11 lands, extending it to also cross-check `lsbx_cli::cli::Command`'s real variants is additive, not a rewrite.

## The 18 registered tools (1:1 with `LsbxOps`'s 18 real public methods)

`create, destroy, renew, reap, list, info, console_url, exec, put, get, status, golden_build, golden_verify, golden_register, golden_delete, golden_list, config_show, logs_query`

`registered_tool_names()` reads this list off the real `ToolRouter` `#[tool_router]` actually built (never hand-maintained separately), and `tests/test_cli_parity.rs` fails the build if it and a hardcoded, source-cross-checked `LsbxOps` method list ever diverge.

## Acceptance criteria

- **1:1 tool correspondence, checked not asserted**: `tests/test_cli_parity.rs`'s `registered_tool_names_matches_lsbx_ops_public_methods_exactly` enumerates both lists and fails the build on any divergence (missing tool, extra tool, or count != 18).
- **Schema derivation, not hand-written JSON Schema**: every tool params type (`CreateParams`, `DestroyParams`, ... 18 total, plus 3 small enum mirrors for `GoldenFlavor`/`GoldenMode`/`StreamingMode` and one `GoldenConfig` mirror for `golden_register`) derives `schemars::JsonSchema`; `src/tools.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)]` module asserts the derived schema's `required`/`properties` actually reflect each struct's real fields (e.g. `create`'s schema requires `profile`/`lease_secs`/`ready_timeout_secs` but not the `#[serde(default)]` fields).
- **Same `Envelope<T>` shape as CLI `--json`/HTTP gateway**: every tool body funnels its `Result<T, LsbxError>` through one `envelope_result()` helper that calls the real `lsbx_kernel::envelope::Envelope::from_result` (Unit 01) and serializes it as the tool's text content — confirmed end to end in `tests/test_error_taxonomy_mapping.rs`'s `successful_call_uses_the_real_envelope_success_shape` and every domain-failure test.
- **stdio transport**: `run_stdio_server(ops: Arc<LsbxOps>)` in `src/lib.rs` serves over `rmcp::transport::stdio()` and blocks on `service.waiting()` until the client disconnects.
- **Misused-call error taxonomy**: two real layers, both proven by `tests/test_error_taxonomy_mapping.rs`'s 12 tests — (1) missing/malformed arguments never reach a tool body at all, rejected by `rmcp`'s own `Parameters<T>` extraction with a real `ErrorCode::INVALID_PARAMS`, exercised directly via `rmcp::handler::server::tool::parse_json_object` against 5 different params types; (2) a well-formed call whose value is invalid (unknown sandbox id, unknown golden key, duplicate registration) reaches `LsbxOps`, and its real `LsbxError` renders via the same `Envelope<T>` shape with `code` equal to the identical `ExitCode` value (`error_map.rs`'s `lsbx_error_to_mcp_error`, unit-tested against all 7 real `LsbxError` variants individually plus a "all 7 produce distinct codes" test).

## Boundaries respected

Every tool body is a direct, thin call-through into `LsbxOps` — no operational logic lives in this crate. The only non-trivial code here is the mechanical translation layer the unit contract itself calls for: owned `JsonSchema`-deriving params structs converted into `LsbxOps`'s real (often borrowed) request types at the call site, and the one shared `envelope_result`/`error_map` plumbing. Does not touch `Envelope<T>`'s definition (Unit 01) — reuses it as-is.

## Verification — 3-tier gate, all green

Ran against a from-scratch `rustup`-installed `cargo`/`rustc` 1.98.0, with a locally reconstructed mirror of every real dependency crate (`lsbx-kernel`, `lsbx-store`, `lsbx-keys`, `lsbx-backend-demo`, `lsbx-golden`, `lsbx-lifecycle`, `lsbx-ops` — each transcribed verbatim from its real merged source, fetched directly from `main` at this branch's base commit, and independently confirmed to pass its own real test suite before this crate was tested against it) to actually exercise the full gate end to end, matching the same approach Unit 10's own PR (#15) used for the identical no-local-clone-credentials situation.

```
cargo check -p lsbx-mcp --message-format=json        # 0 errors, 0 warnings
cargo clippy -p lsbx-mcp --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo test -p lsbx-mcp --test test_cli_parity        # 2 passed, 0 failed
cargo test -p lsbx-mcp --test test_error_taxonomy_mapping   # 12 passed, 0 failed
cargo test -p lsbx-mcp                                # 26 passed, 0 failed (12 unit + 2 + 12)
cargo check --workspace                                # 0 errors, 0 warnings, all 11 crates
```

Root `Cargo.toml`: added `"crates/lsbx-mcp",` to `members` (11th entry) and `lsbx-mcp = { path = "crates/lsbx-mcp" }` to `[workspace.dependencies]`, following the exact same one-line-each pattern as every prior unit. Branched fresh off `main`'s current tip (`86506e28d0b4448527379e4487

author: alongd
body:
Eighth and final defect on the round-0 → round-1 handoff. With the master equation solving, round 1 ran to the end of the physics and then tripped the loop's own output-vs-network consistency check.

## The defect

`strip_rmg_index_suffix` removed a **single** trailing `(<int>)` group. But the index **accumulates across rounds**: a hybrid network declares the previous round's already-indexed labels (`O=C=O(5)`), and when the next round explores that hybrid, Arkane appends *another* index to the network file it writes (`O=C=O(5)(3)`) while its `output.py` keeps the single-indexed form. The two artifacts of one run therefore sit one index level apart, and stripping only the last group left them apart (`O=C=O` vs `O=C=O(5)`) — so a genuinely single-run pairing was refused.

```
-_RMG_INDEX_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(r'\(\d+\)$')
+_RMG_INDEX_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(r'(?:\(\d+\))+$')
```

## Why stripping every group is safe

The same argument that licensed stripping one: the index only ever disambiguates a base label from itself, and a SMILES-derived base never itself ends in `(<int>)` — charges are bracketed (`[C-]#[O+]`), ring closures are bare digits. So any trailing `(<int>)` group is an index, not identity, and collapsing all of them cannot merge two distinct species.

This deliberately does **not** loosen the consistency check, which exists because a mismatched pairing genuinely occurred before and produced a silently wrong result. The guard was right; the normalization it relied on was incomplete.

## Verification

Verified independently by regenerating the hybrid through the production entry point and driving the real explorer on it:

- **Round 1 completes** — final network and PES diagram both produced, no failure status.
- **The physics is unchanged, exactly.** Rate coefficients are bit-identical to the pre-fix run: `k_rev (TST) = A=8.73653e+11 s⁻¹, n=0.308264, Ea=106.537 kJ/mol`, and with tunneling `A=0.201422, n=3.90893, Ea=71.7449 kJ/mol`. This change is bookkeeping downstream of the solve and must not move the numbers — it doesn't.
- Zero `Singular matrix` occurrences; both `network0_full.py` and `network0_reduced.py` written.
- Mutation: reverting the regex to the single-strip form turns 5 tests red, including `test_round_one_reexploration_of_a_real_hybrid_completes` — the real-artifact test, not a fixture.
- `tests/test_pdep`: **1915 passed**, up from 1910. Tests added, none removed.

With this, the loop explores a surface, computes a transition state on a cluster, splices it back with matched degrees of freedom, re-explores its own output, and completes round 1 with a real rate coefficient.

author: opaland
body:
## Contexte

Trouvaille de la relecture adverse du Sprint 5 (issue de session, jamais reprise depuis) : `EF.api()` (`frontend/common.js`), le helper d'appel API central utilisé par tout le frontend, n'avait aucun timeout sur son `fetch()` — un serveur qui cesse de répondre en cours de requête (crash, coupure réseau) laissait l'appelant bloqué indéfiniment, bouton figé sur « … », sans jamais afficher d'erreur.

## Changements

- **`frontend/common.js`** : `AbortController` avec délai par défaut (`EF.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, 20 s), dépassable par appel via `opts.timeoutMs`.
- **`frontend/archives.js`, `frontend/traces.js`, `frontend/diag.html`** : les routes qui font elles-mêmes un aller-retour réseau externe côté serveur (import d'édition Wikipédia, import par lien Suunto/Sports-Tracker, import Suunto direct, diagnostic multi-services) reçoivent un délai étendu (60 s) plutôt que d'hériter du défaut pensé pour un appel local.
- **`test/apiTimeout.test.js`** (nouveau, 5 tests) : comportement du timeout lui-même — abandon avec message explicite, aucune fuite de `timeoutMs` vers `fetch()`, résolution normale inchangée, erreur réseau non-timeout non masquée.
- **`test/apiTimeoutOverrides.test.js`** (nouveau, 4 tests) : verrouille l'invariant « toute route connue pour proxyer un aller-retour réseau externe a un `timeoutMs` étendu » — via un vrai parseur JS (espree), pas un grep.

## Trouvaille de relecture adverse, corrigée

Le premier jet n'étendait que 2 routes (import d'édition, import par lien) et en avait oublié 2 autres, structurellement identiques : **`/api/diagnostic`** sonde 6 services externes en séquence côté serveur (8 s de délai chacun, pire cas ~48 s) — reproduit empiriquement par la relecture adverse (serveur réel, hôtes externes simulés injoignables) : le client affichait « le serveur ne répond pas » après 20 s alors que le serveur travaillait encore à 25 s. **`/api/suunto/import`** (rafraîchissement de jeton OAuth + téléchargement FIT externe) manquait la même extension par analogie avec sa route sœur déjà corrigée. Les deux sont maintenant étendues à 60 s, et l'invariant est verrouillé par `test/apiTimeoutOverrides.test.js` plutôt que par les 4 lignes trouvées — vérifié discriminant en rejouant la régression exacte de `diag.html` (le test échoue sans le correctif, passe avec).

## Vérification

- `npm test` : 305/305 verts (296 existants + 9 nouveaux).
- `npm run lint` : propre.
- Vérification manuelle en navigateur réel (Playwright, mode hors-ligne) : liste des étapes de l'éditeur (délai par défaut) et import d'édition (délai étendu, fixture hors-ligne réelle) fonctionnent tous deux sans régression ni erreur JS.
- Relecture adverse : confirmé qu'aucun appelant existant de `EF.api()` ne passait déjà `opts.signal` (pas de conflit), que `POST /api/stages/:id/generate` est bien asynchrone côté serveur (retourne immédiatement, pas affecté), que `clearTimeout` est appelé dans tous les chemins de sortie, et que les `catch {}` silencieux existants n'aggravent rien (ils avalaient déjà toute erreur avant ce commit).

author: godley44
body:
Two changes to the Lil Bull weekly pipeline.

## Change 1 — weekly-insight ticker swap

The brief now analyzes **S&P 500 (^GSPC)** (kept — market backdrop), **SanDisk (SNDK)** (replaces ^IXIC), and **Intel (INTC)** (replaces ^DJI), rendered as `S&P 500`, `SNDK`, `INTEL` everywhere (table, stances, feed-error notes, model prompt example). Indicator math (MACD, StochRSI, MA crossovers per timeframe), frames, auth, cron wiring, and proposal filing are **untouched** — same analysis, new subjects.

- **Yahoo fetch verified live for both new symbols**: same `v8/finance/chart` endpoint, `instrumentType: EQUITY`, USD — SNDK and INTC return clean candle series exactly like ^GSPC. `yahooCandles()` needed no changes (`encodeURIComponent` already handled the only symbol quirk, `^`).
- **Dollars vs points** handled at the data boundary: key-level values are pre-rendered strings that carry their unit (`$1493.12` for stocks, `7652.86` points for the index) and the model is instructed to quote them exactly — stances and the WhatsApp Key Levels can never mix units.
- **Known data quirk, already graceful**: SNDK only trades since 2025-02 (re-listing), so its monthly/quarterly SMA50/200 cells render `MA n/a` until the history exists; INTC's monthly feed (~168 candles) also lacks the 200 needed for monthly SMA200. `readFrame` was built for this — "n/a", never invented numbers. Documented in the function header.

## Change 2 — WhatsApp framing template

`FRAMING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (still the marked TUNE ME constant) now targets the owner-approved template: 🐂 header, 📅 week line, Market Outlook with 🟢/🟡/🔴 stance lines per symbol, ⚖️ Weekly Lean + conviction, 2–3 sentence narrative, Key Levels ($ for stocks, points for the index), 📆 calendar bullets, Bottom Line, and the **mandatory verbatim closer** "Analysis only — not financial advice. Trade your own plan." Kept: the no-invented-data ban, the ~1200-char cap, and no-markdown-tables. Added: a fallback rule so an old brief naming a different lineup still frames correctly (one stance/level line per symbol the brief actually covers).

## Tests

38/38 green in CI: template-shaped framed fixture, new-lineup brief fixtures with dollar levels and an `MA n/a` cell, new prompt non-negotiable asserts (template header, emoji mapping, verbatim disclaimer, current lineup), escape-safety inside code blocks re-verified. Stray SPX/NASDAQ/Dow references in comments and the root README cleaned up.

## Deploy notes

⚠️ `weekly-insight` runs from the **deployed Supabase edge function** — merging this PR does not update it. To make Monday's cron use the new lineup: `supabase functions deploy weekly-insight --no-verify-jwt` (or paste via the dashboard) after merge. No cron, secret, or Vault changes needed. The bot side auto-deploys via Render on merge (this PR touches `services/godley-os-bot/`).

author: mfethe1
body: Points `fleet_default_speaker` at the Home Assistant Voice PE satellite adopted in the Study on 2026-08-24 (ESPHome node `home-assistant-voice-0acc7e`, `10.0.10.178`) instead of `media_player.kitchen_display`. ## Why this is a correctness fix, not a preference A Cast device drops off the network when idle and answers `unavailable` to `states()`. That trips the guard in `fleet_voice.yaml` and the announcement is swallowed with no error anywhere — exactly the silent-drop failure that guard was written to catch. author: katsiarynakavaleuskaya
body:
## Goal

Eliminate the backend packaging collision in which `/app/alembic` shadows the
installed Alembic distribution, while preserving the existing migration tree,
public API, runtime environment contract, and production boundary.

## Business reason

Private staging cannot execute any migration while `/app/alembic` shadows the installed Alembic distribution. This bounded image prerequisite restores deterministic migration startup without changing schemas, dependencies, public API, production, or runtime configuration.

## Scope

- Delete the empty top-level regular-package carrier `alembic/__init__.py`.
- Make repository imports declarative through `alembic.ini`; remove the
  imperative `sys.path` mutation from `alembic/env.py`.
- Exclude local Python bytecode after Docker context allowlists reopen.
- Add a non-root final-production-stage import/filesystem/single-head guard.
- Add deterministic import, negative-carrier, SQLite replay, PostgreSQL
  full-graph/OID-cleanup, subprocess-redaction, and Docker-contract tests.
- Extend only the existing `pgvector_compat` path selector with `alembic.ini`,
  `alembic/env.py`, and `alembic/versions/**`.
- Update only the existing PROD-OBS-1 ledger hunk.

Material scope is ten paths. The canonical review mapping is the reserved
eleventh and final path.

## Out of scope

- Workflow changes beyond the exact existing `pgvector_compat` selector hunk;
  Compose, deploy scripts, requirements, or lockfiles.
- Migration revisions or schema changes.
- Server-local `PYTHONPATH` or patched image workarounds.
- Staging or production deployment, credentials, release tags, or host changes.
- Prometheus production activation, `T0`, the 30-day watch, or alias removal.
- The independently owned VIP/TestClient main-repair PR.

## Files changed

- Packaging and import ownership: `.dockerignore`, `Dockerfile`, `alembic.ini`, `alembic/__init__.py`, and `alembic/env.py`.
- Deterministic proof: `tests/test_alembic_image_import_contract.py`, `tests/test_pgvector_compat.py`, and the exact `pgvector_compat` selector hunk in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- Durable governance: `alembic/AGENTS.md` and the existing PROD-OBS-1 hunk in `docs/roadmap/BACKLOG_LEDGER.md`.

## Key decisions

- The repository migration directory remains ScriptDirectory data, while the installed distribution exclusively owns `alembic.*` imports.
- Existing image `PYTHONPATH=/app` remains unchanged; the fix must pass under the real production image contract.
- The final image guard rejects package carriers and bytecode before importing Alembic, then proves installed-module ownership and exactly one migration head as the non-root runtime user.
- PostgreSQL evidence is resource-bounded migration-state projection only; it is not a complete database-state or production-safety claim.

## Split justification

The 10-path diff is intentionally one indivisible infrastructure prerequisite: removing the carrier without the image guard would permit regression, adding the guard without deterministic SQLite/PostgreSQL and selector proof would be false confidence, and separating the CI selector would allow Alembic revisions to bypass the required full-graph job. No migration revision, dependency, deploy script, Compose file, public API, or production action is mixed into the lane.

## Carryover

Private-staging activation after merged PR #2324 stopped before any migration
revision executed because `/app/alembic` shadowed the installed distribution.
This PR closes only that repository/image prerequisite. The canonical ledger
item remains open for staging baseline, production activation, `T0`, the full
watch window, consumer classification, and future alias retirement.

## Tests

- `check_preflight.py` — PASS.
- `check_agent_consistency.py` — PASS.
- Focused Alembic/import/migration/Docker/security bundle — PASS; the eight
  PostgreSQL service cases use the documented local `feature_disabled` protocol.
- `make validate-changed` — PASS after the material commit.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — PASS before commit and before push.
- Final Experiment Runner strict Apple oracle — accepted; 3/3 immutable oracles
  PASS, exact four post-review correction paths applied, shared tree untouched.
- `git diff --check`, unmerged-path census, and tracked-worktree census — PASS.

Exact material head `4c98e34e2d5a2f506943bf710fc7cf826712a3d9` passed CI run `32857936140` attempt 4: Python 3.11/3.12/3.13, `test-pr`, `pgvector-compat`, lint, OpenAPI, security, coverage and diff coverage, iOS, plus exact-head Docker build/security, Actionlint, CodeQL, RAG, Frontend, and CD security workflows. Phase2 and merge-readiness are intentionally completed only by the canonical mapping/seal cycle.

## Security

- Installed distribution ownership is checked with resolved containment and
  regular non-symlink carriers; `/app/alembic` is ScriptDirectory data.
- Final image guard runs as `pulseplate` after production hardening and before
  staging inheritance, with no network or database access.
- Child migration processes receive a closed environment and use
  `sys.executable`; credentialed URLs and encoded/decoded passwords are redacted
  from bounded failure diagnostics.
- PostgreSQL destructive authority requires exact GitHub Actions markers, an
  exact query-free loopback service tuple, live database/user/port identity,
  a generated name, pre-absence, server OID receipt, same-OID recheck, exact
  quoted drop, and post-absence. No `FORCE`, `IF EXISTS`, session termination,
  wildcard, or caller-supplied database name is admitted.
- No suppression, allowlist, secret, provider, or production authority is added.
- Repeated-upgrade evidence is explicitly a resource-bounded migration-state
  projection with fixed count/byte/time caps, cap-plus-one failure, consistent
  snapshots, pre-materialization size checks, server-side streaming, and exact
  admitted/excluded surfaces; it is not a complete-database or production-safety claim.

## Premortem

- Decision: `proceed`; no new material finding.
- Most likely residual risk: a historical PostgreSQL migration incompatibility;
  exact-head `pgvector-compat` must be terminal-success.
- Most dangerous risk: unowned database cleanup or credential leakage; the
  exact tuple, OID receipt, cleanup recheck, closed environment, and redaction
  tests fail closed.
- Evidence hash: `sha256:817283b5531f77390acc9205eb765094ce7fab886ccc3d3662f9831f32a3188e`.

## Experiment Runner Evidence

- Mode: `oracle_only_governance_reviewer`.
- Exact material head: `4c98e34e2d5a2f506943bf710fc7cf826712a3d9`.
- Base / merge-base: `f95a329d899d5ac4fa73f198e90cfed44d0fc45c`.
- Packet: `artifacts/orchestration/experiments/packets/alembic-packaging-final-18bd013af5eb.json`.
Artifact: `artifacts/orchestration/experiments/results/alembic-packaging-final-18bd013af5eb-result.json`
- Packet SHA-256: `d3732a5dde76be6108a30a16358c527779a0974458a7db30440c4554ba0f669e`.
- Result SHA-256: `1066efb101e76d76580c411917eba41577fc212900bd83b9d67a4324e8529d9d`.
- Result: accepted; 3/3 immutable oracles PASS; `mutated_paths=[]`; shared tree untouched; `coauthor_required=true`.

## Lane Start Provenance

Packet: `artifacts/orchestration/task_packets/e50db9f6247e.json`
- Required pre-open sequence completed:
  `agent-coordinator -> logic-agent -> philosophy-agent -> dev-operator -> architecture-specialist -> security-auditor`.

## Next best step

Publish the single canonical mapping-only closeout, pass the strict exact-head wrapper and mandatory review wait, then request separate human squash-merge authorization for the exact live head. Deployment and private-staging retry remain later, separately authorized actions.

## Rollback

- Before merge: close the PR and discard only this owned branch/worktree.
- After merge but before staging: do not admit or deploy the new digest; retain
  the previous staging failure receipt.
- During a later separately authorized staging retry: on migration failure,
  preserve the databas

author: ryancinsight
body:
Repairs the `Fuzz parsers` job that has failed on main since #162: the sanitizer build fails with 'sanitizer is incompatible with statically linked libc' when the fuzz target is built without an explicit name/bin section. Names the target so cargo-fuzz links it dynamically.

Follow-up to the lock-guard promotion (#164) which surfaced this pre-existing failure.

<!-- RECURSEML_SUMMARY:START -->
## High-level PR Summary
Fixes the failing `Fuzz parsers` CI job by switching the fuzz target build from the musl target to the gnu target. The musl target uses static linking (`+crt-static`) which is incompatible with the address sanitizer used by libFuzzer, causing the build to fail. The fix explicitly specifies `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` as the target, which uses dynamic linking and allows the sanitizer to function properly.

body:
## 概要

`docs/adr/**` と `docs/dev/**` がコードを `path:12` の形で引用していたため、コードを 1 行足すだけで引用が無音でずれていた。行番号引用をやめてパスとシンボル名で示す規約にし、それを機械的に落とす検査を入れる。あわせて既に生じていたずれをすべて直す（TASK-550）。

## 変更内容

- **`scripts/check-doc-citations.sh`（新規）**: `docs/adr/**` と `docs/dev/**` に対して ①行番号引用（`path:12` / `path:12,34` / `path:12-20`）の禁止 ②引用パスの実在、の 2 つを検査する。既定実行のたびに self-test を通す（検知そのものが壊れてグリーンになるのを防ぐ）
- **`scripts/doc-citation-allowlist.txt`（新規）**: 除外は「文書パス|引用」の組で書く。グローバルに素通しにすると別文書での陳腐化を検知できなくなるため。現在 10 件（ADR の歴史記述 5・例示の架空名 2・R2 のオブジェクトキー 2 ほか）
- **`scripts/setup-git-hooks.sh`**: 上記を pre-commit へ配線
- **`.claude/CLAUDE.md`**: 「設計文書の三層構造」節の下に規約と実測根拠を記録。ADR の Context が現状調査を含むなら見出しに調査日を書くことも併記
- **`docs/adr/0004`〜`0007` / `docs/dev/**`**: 検知された既存のずれを修正

**単独シンボル名の実在検査は入れない。** 実測で ADR 内の識別子 79 件中 9 件が NOTFOUND、うち 8 件は「存在しないこと自体を述べた正しい記述」だった（`preBuildScripts` は project.yml に無い、`allowFileAccessFromFileURLs` は非公開プリファレンス、`verifiedBotCategory` は Cloudflare の API フィールド等）。偽陽性 89% で、除外リストのほうが本体になる。ADR は「採らなかった案」「まだ実装していない決定」を論じる層なので原理的に噛み合わない。

### 直したずれ

行番号引用 64 件（0004=6 / 0005=11 / 0006=17 / 0007=28 / flaky-test 調査=2）。`docs/superpowers/**` はスナップショット層なので対象外・無修正。

検査を回して新たに見つかったパス不存在 20 件: `viewer-src/*.js`（TASK-499 で全廃、現 `.ts`）13 件、`befold-cli/*.swift`（現 `BefoldCLI/`）6 件、`BefoldApp/befold/App/GitCommandRunner.swift`（TASK-435.5 で撤去）1 件。

引用の突き合わせで見つかった記述そのもののずれ:

- **ADR 0006: 「`GIT_OPT_SET_SEARCH_PATH` で無効化するのは system と xdg の 2 つで global は有効のまま」が実装と逆。** 実際は `GitLibrary.disabledConfigLevels == [GIT_CONFIG_LEVEL_SYSTEM]` のみで、xdg は `~/.config/git/ignore` を巻き添えにするため TASK-467 で撤回済み。担保テストとして挙がっていた `keepsGlobalConfigSearchPathEnabled` も不在（実在は `disablesOnlySystemConfigSearchPath` / `keepsUserConfigSearchPathsEnabled`）
- ADR 0004: `bot-other` → 実装は `bot:other`
- ADR 0005: `loadFileURL` の置き場、`Package.swift` のリソース列挙件数
- ADR 0007: `DOWNLOAD_URL` は起票時点では実在し、本 ADR の実装（PR #518）が `DOWNLOAD_PATH` へ改名していた。Context の見出しを「現状（実測 / 2026-08-14 時点）」に改めた
- `docs/dev/rules/product-code.md`: 「`.js` と `.ts` が混在する（移行の途中）」→ TASK-499 で完了済み（`allowJs: false`）
- `docs/dev/flaky-test-filewatcher-investigation.md`: `waitUntilWithRetry` の置き場、`BEFOLD_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` の値

## 検証

- `scripts/check-doc-citations.sh` — 指摘 0 件。`--self-test` も OK
- `scripts/check-doc-symbols.sh` — 指摘 0 件
- `markdownlint-cli2` — 78 ファイル 0 issues
- **フックが実際に落ちることを確認**: `docs/dev/cli-launch.md` に `site/src/views/shared.tsx:13` を足して commit すると、pre-commit が該当行を指して拒否した
- ADR 0006 の修正内容は `GitLibraryTests.swift` と `GitLibrary.swift` を直接読んで裏取り済み

未検証で残るもの（Notes に別タスク候補として記録）:

- **ADR 0003 が Accepted のまま未実装**。`appliedGitStatusGeneration` は今も `SidebarNavigator` にあり、`FileListModel.appliedGitStatusSequence` は存在しない
- **`scripts/check-doc-symbols.sh` の `is_allowlisted` に同型の不具合の疑い**。`pipefail` 下で `grep -q` をパイプ末尾に置いており、除外が効かない形になりうる（本 PR で同じ書き方をして実際に踏み、`<<<` へ書き換えた）

Swift / JS のコードには触れていないため、ビルド・テストへの影響は無い。

author: gaboxqc
body:
The Odds API key works. Ran the full chain; the first real cup fixtures broke three things.

## The key works, and fixtures are free as claimed

```
odds-api: ENG.FA_CUP — 2 scheduled fixture(s)
odds-api: budget {'remaining': 485, 'used': 15, 'spent_this_run': 0, ...}
build_fixtures: by source: {"odds_api": 2, "openfootball": 715, "openligadb": 2}
```

`spent_this_run: 0` with 485 credits left — the free-`/events` claim confirmed **against the live API**, not from the docs. The other five cups have no upcoming events yet and say so.

## What the two ties broke — the same mistake in three places

Long Eaton United v AFC Rushden and Diamonds, and MK Dons v Slimbridge AFC, are FA Cup **qualifying** ties. Club Elo rates tiers 1–2, so all four clubs took the pooled prior.

### 1. A confident answer built on no information

Equal priors means the Elo difference is **exactly zero** — the fitted model has no rating signal, so it discriminated on form and xG features that don't exist for either club:

| path | MK Dons (home, tier 4) v Slimbridge (tier 8) |
|---|---|
| precomputed | **28.8% / 22.8% / 48.4%** — eighth-tier side favoured |
| Elo fallback | **45.4% / 25.6% / 29.1%** — home advantage, correct shape |

And the precomputed one *overrides* the better answer. Precompute now omits a fixture where **neither** side has a measured rating, so the fallback answers it. One prior against one measured rating is left alone — there the Elo difference is real, and Hamburg Eimsbütteler BC v Dortmund stays at 9.1%.

This is the **second** failure of this kind on this path. The first was a *null* rating giving 52.9% to a fifth-tier side (#40); filling it with the pooled prior fixed that and created this one, because two equal priors are as uninformative as two nulls and the model does not abstain either way.

### 2. The coverage floor was one fixture from failing the run

`map_fixture_clubs` measured coverage over *every* club and exits 1 below 95%. Two cup ties took it to **95.1%**. A full FA Cup round of 100+ non-league ties would fail it outright, for an entirely correct fixture list.

Scoped to **league** clubs, where an unmapped club really is a mapping bug:

```
league coverage 100.0% (96/96) — this is the number the floor applies to
5 cup entrant(s) have no Club Elo rating, which is expected
```

The real signal was perfect all along, dragged down by clubs Club Elo was never going to rate.

### 3. Four tests assumed a world without cups

`test_precompute.py` took the first N upcoming fixtures and asserted every one was precomputed. The earliest rows can now legitimately be ones precompute *declined*, so they now select a fixture that actually has precomputed rates — and a new test covers the declined ones reporting the fallback.

## Note on the pattern

That is now **three** guards written when only leagues existed, each firing on correct cup behaviour: this coverage floor, `collect_live_odds`'s keyed-share floor (#35), and the fully-rated fixture test (#40). Worth watching for a fourth as more cups arrive.

## Testing

`1189 passed`, ruff clean. Full chain re-run end to end: fixtures → club map → predictions → live odds → card.

author: nssatlantis
body:
This PR implements proposal #193: Fix bounty completion race: atomicize the pay/refund + completion check in db/\_bounty.py
http://192.168.0.40:8000/posts/193

---

## Summary

Item 3500 on #163 Resilience Audit — never-lose-data domain. Fixes three atomicity gaps in the bounty completion lifecycle in `db/_bounty.py`.

## Changes

- `db/_bounty.py` — Four changes:
  1. **Extract `_check_bounty_completion()`** helper — reusable, idempotent completion check (reads `paid_count`/`locked_count`/`max_prs`, marks completed + notifies staker when all are met).
  2. **Move completion check inside the lock loop** in `pay_bounty_rewards()` — after each lock payment, immediately check completion in the same transaction scope. Collapses the two-phase window where a concurrent `lock_bounties_for_pr` could see `'active'` on a bounty that should be `'completed'`.
  3. **Add post-lock completion guard** in `lock_bounties_for_pr()` — after inserting a lock and incrementing `locked_count`, re-read the bounty row. If `paid_count == max_prs` (bounty just completed between our SELECT and INSERT), roll back the orphaned lock, decrement `locked_count`, and delete the `karma_spend`. Defense-in-depth against the same race.
  4. **Add zero-lock completion check** at the top of both `pay_bounty_rewards()` and `refund_bounty_locks()` — when no locks are found for a PR, query for any active bounty that is fully paid but never marked completed. Catches the edge case where all locks were processed by prior calls but completion was never triggered.

## Verification

- `tests/run_all.py` — all 40 test files pass
- `ruff` clean, `mypy` clean
- Existing `tests/test_bounty.py` covers happy paths (pay, refund, self-stake, completion)
- The three race conditions from the proposal are addressed by construction: (a) in-loop completion collapses the two-phase window, (b) post-lock guard prevents orphaned locks on completed bounties, (c) zero-lock check catches missed completions

body:
## 対応Issue / SPEC節
Closes #102

SPEC/WORKFLOW.mdの復旧・並行性契約: 「scheduler lock、PID、process start time、nonceで二重実行とPID reuseを防ぐ」「revision/CASでlost updateを検出する」

## 変更内容と理由
`Scheduler._persist()` は `store.save_state()` を直接呼び出しており、CLIの全write経路（`pause`/`resume`/`cancel`/`run`）が使っている `with store.lock():` を経由していませんでした。将来 `subsched run` の実行ループ中に別プロセスから `subsched pause`/`cancel` 等が実行された場合（SPECが想定する「pause中は実行中Taskを継続」シナリオ）、Schedulerの書き込みとCLIコマンドの書き込みが競合し、どちらかの更新が silent に失われる可能性がありました。

`_persist()` を他のwrite経路と同じプロセスレベルロックで保護し、ロック内で読んだ現在revisionを `expected_revision` としてCASチェックにも渡すようにしました（ロック運用が正しい限り常に一致するため実害はありませんが、不変条件が破られた場合の多層防御として機能します）。

## state / capacity / billing / security / recoveryへの影響
- 書き込みタイミングがロック経由になる以外、永続state schemaや挙動は変わりません。
- ロック取得に失敗した場合（他プロセスが保持中）は `SchedulerLockError` が `_persist()` から送出されます。これは既存のCLIコマンドと同じ失敗モードです。

## 実行したunit/integration/E2Eと品質ゲート
- 新規integrationテスト `tests/integration/test_scheduler_persist_locking.py`:
  - 他プロセス（実ファイルロック）がロックを保持している間、`Scheduler.discover()`（内部で`_persist()`を呼ぶ）が`SchedulerLockError`を送出し、失敗した書き込みが永続化されないことを確認
  - 正常系でロックが確実に解放され、後続のCLI相当の書き込み（`with store.lock(): store.save_tasks(...)`）がブロックされないことを確認
- `uv run pytest -q` → 327 passed（既存325 + 新規2）
- `uv run ruff check .` → All checks passed
- `uv run mypy src` → No issues found
- `uv run pytest --cov=subsched --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80` → coverage 88.37%
- `uv export --frozen --no-hashes --no-emit-project | uvx pip-audit -r /dev/stdin` → No known vulnerabilities found
- `tests/e2e/` + `tests/integration/` 全件パス（43件）

## 実行できなかったlive検証と理由
- 真の複数OSプロセス間での競合（別Pythonプロセス2つを起動しての検証）は未実施。新規テストは実ファイルロック機構（`os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL)` + PID/起動時刻照合）を経由しており、単一テストプロセス内でも同等のロック衝突パスを検証できているため、スコープ内での確認としては十分と判断しました。

## migration / rollback / NEEDS_HUMAN条件
- 破壊的変更なし。ロック取得失敗時の挙動（`SchedulerLockError`送出）はCLIの既存コマンドと同じ形なので、呼び出し側の追加対応は不要です。
- rollbackは本コミットのrevertのみで完結します。

author: oliv-yu
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-74731
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-103625

## What Is Being Fixed

Being indexed and being indexed under `nestedFieldArray` are two different things, and nothing in the object model said so. `ObjectEntryModelDocumentContributor` decides what reaches the nested document with a rule keyed on `ObjectDefinition.isModifiableAndSystem()`: a modifiable and system definition contributes every indexed field except its metadata fields, and any other definition contributes only its indexed non-system fields.

That rule was not exposed anywhere, so every caller that needed it reimplemented it. The copies could disagree, and a change to how entries are indexed had to be made in each of them. A Dynamic Collection over a CMS Structure showed what that costs: Collections applied its own copy, offered `title` in its order by and filter dropdowns, and because CMS Structure is `system=false` its `title` is never written to `nestedFieldArray`, so ordering silently fell through to the secondary sort and a contains filter rendered an empty collection.

## How It Is Being Fixed

`ObjectFieldBag` now precomputes the `nestedFieldArray` selection alongside the indexed and non-system indexed subsets it already held, exposed as `getNestedIndexedObjectFields()`. The constructor takes the modifiable and system flag, because the object definition rather than the field decides which of the two rules applies, which is a breaking change to `com.liferay.object.model.bag` and moves it to 2.0.0.

`ObjectEntryModelDocumentContributor` and `ObjectEntryKeywordQueryContributor` then read the selection from the bag instead of each deriving it, so the indexing side has one definition. Which fields the rule selects is asserted in `ObjectFieldBagTest`, so the accessor verifications the keyword query contributor test used to make are dropped.

This does not change which fields are indexed. The contributor's behaviour is deliberate and unchanged.

## PR Check

**pr-check: PASS** — tested on `91ecba253620c486cf84735b210d0a482856bdc3`

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Service Builder | PASS |
| Source Format | PASS \* |
| Transaction Usage | PASS |
| Per-Module Compile | PASS |
| Integration Test Compile | PASS |
| Cross-Module Compile | PASS |
| Baseline | PASS |
| Java Unit Tests | PASS |

\* `formatSource` passes on all three modules this PR touches and leaves their files untouched. The branch-wide `format-source-current-branch` run reports three violations, all in `layout-impl` and `petra` files that this PR does not contain, which it picks up from the gap between the branch base and `master`.

Validations ran against the branch base rather than current `master`, so this is a statement about these six commits, not about their merge with today's `master`.

Cross-module compile covered `object-web` and `site-cms-site-initializer`, the other two source-level importers of `com.liferay.object.model.bag`, plus `dynamic-data-mapping-form-web` and `roles-admin-web`, which reach the package through a method chain without naming it.

### Integration Coverage

The unit tests do not reach the indexing path, so the integration tests around object entry indexing were run against a bundle with all three modules deployed and started.

| Test | Tests | Failures | Ignored | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ObjectEntryModelDocumentContributorTest` | 6 | 0 | 0 | 4.320s |
| `ObjectEntrySearchHighlightTest` | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0.196s |
| `ObjectEntryIndexerContributedFieldsTest` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1.201s |
| `ObjectEntryIndexerIndexedFieldsTest` | 2 | 0 | 0 | 1.597s |
| `ObjectEntryIndexerReindexTest` | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3.691s |
| `ObjectEntryLocalServiceIndexerTest` | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3.272s |
| **Total** | **18** | **0** | **0** | |

These 18 tests cover the branch where a definition is not modifiable and system, which is the one that selects a field with `!objectField.isSystem()`. They confirm that reading the selection from the bag leaves document contribution, contributed and indexed fields, reindexing, and the local service indexer hook unchanged.

They do not cover the branch where a definition is modifiable and system. No test in `object-test` constructs a definition with that flag set, so the rule the new constructor parameter selects on is asserted only by `ObjectFieldBagTest` as a unit test, and `ObjectEntryKeywordQueryContributor` has no integration test in the tree. Covering it would mean a case over a modifiable and system definition asserting that a metadata field stays out of `nestedFieldArray` while a non-metadata system field is written to it.

author: simyung-h1r
body:
Scout flagged the wording in the 00Z window rather than editing the file — the right division — and I am acting on it the same window rather than letting it sit.

**The finding.** Mon 08-24 settle: **2Y 4.24 again, 0bp** — a second consecutive settle off 4.19, so follow-through is met by the letter. But read across all six settles — **4.19 ×4, then 4.24 ×2** — the invariant is the **pinning behaviour**, not the level. The front finds a precise level and sits on it; what changed is the level it pins at, one notch. That is a **re-pin, not a hawkish climb**, and the second settle being *flat* is the evidence.

**The gate I got wrong.** It read *"a second consecutive move off 4.19 makes it a regime"* — which conflates **moved-and-stayed** with **moving**. A flat second settle satisfies "off 4.19" while being the opposite of an accelerating regime, so a reporter could have satisfied my test while describing something it was never meant to license.

Rewritten to name which thing is under test: **a new PIN** = the 2Y keeps settling ~4.24; **a hawkish TREND** = successive settles *above* 4.24. A durability test must say whether it tests a **level** or a **trend**.

Also updated: the **rotation settled** (Dow +0.26% green vs Nasdaq −0.77% red, a 1.03pp spread), and Friday’s single reflation story no longer covers the tape — gold is the one constant but its *company* changed, inflation-hedge → safe-haven. Base levels re-anchored to the Monday settle.

**On the file’s own rule that a window should leave it smaller:** I flagged growth twice without acting, so this time I compressed — folded the six-row falsifier verdict *log* into a summary line (the compression I promised last week), trimmed the reconciliation note to what is still operative, and tightened two blocks. **1,519 → 1,655 words**: still net up, because a resolved regime test and a corrected gate are live state, but the compression was actually done rather than noted.

author: realemmetts
body:
## Why

The first no-click v4.3.0 crates run proved the exact-SHA validator, but crates.io rejected its trusted-publishing exchange because crates.io does not support the workflow_run event. The failure occurred before crates.io issued a publication token. Version 4.3.0 remains unpublished and no v4.3.0 tag exists.

Failed automatic run: https://github.com/QubeTX/qube-machine-report/actions/runs/32791618652

## Fix

- start Crates.io Publish automatically on same-repository pushes to main, an event crates.io supports
- keep the validator uncredentialed while it polls the trusted CI workflow for this exact SHA
- fail closed on missing, duplicate, failed, mismatched, or drifting CI/main identity
- re-fetch the selected CI run and verify workflow, repository, branch, SHA, attempt, status, and conclusion
- preserve the fresh protected OIDC publisher, exact-byte reproduction, public provenance checks, and diagnostics-only manual dispatch
- update executable provenance guards and the release documentation

## Local evidence

- git diff --check
- Actionlint YAML/expression validation
- full release provenance fixture suite
- forbidden workflow_run and legacy-token scan
- cargo package --locked --list
- cargo publish --dry-run --locked
- three independent review agents assigned to the exact commit

## Acceptance

After this PR passes all exact-head checks and is merged, the main push must start both CI and Crates.io Publish automatically. The crates validator must wait for exact-SHA CI success before the OIDC publisher runs. No manual dispatch or approval click belongs in the normal publication path.

Do not tag until the automatic exact-main crate publication and public provenance both pass.

author: mikesandoval10creator
body:
## What

The 1-second interval that updates `emergencyDashboard.elapsedTime` lived **inside** the `onSnapshot` callback from Firestore. The `return` of that callback is ignored by Firestore, so:

1. The interval survived `unmount`, leaking every time the user left the emergency dashboard.
2. The interval was duplicated on every project doc change, making `elapsedTime` update multiple times per second and show the wrong value.

This is a **vida-safety P0** because the elapsed-time counter is shown on the rescue coordination screen — wrong values can mislead the supervisor about how long the worker has been in distress.

## Why

Hy3-audit 2026-08-20 `3c3aa66d-73fe-81cb-ae47-c568a723e56b`. The fix is straightforward and the bug is high-impact but contained to one component.

## Fix

- New state: `emergencyStartMs` (null when no active emergency).
- `onSnapshot` writes the start time into that state instead of creating the interval inline.
- A new `useEffect` with `[emergencyStartMs]` dep creates the interval and runs `clearInterval` in its cleanup. React runs the cleanup before re-running the effect, so changes to `emergencyStartMs` replace (not duplicate) the interval.

## Scope

- `src/components/emergency/EmergencyDashboard.tsx`: +19 / -7 (1 file)

No deps added. No API changes.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/components/emergency/EmergencyDashboard.test.tsx`: **3/3 PASS** (existing)
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors on changed files
- Pre-commit ratchets: connectivity ✅ render ✅ router-test ✅ open-reads ✅ measured-state ✅

## Honest disclosure

No new tests added. The existing test suite exercises the project doc path but doesn't specifically test the interval cleanup. A dedicated test that:
1. Renders the dashboard with `emergencyStartTime` set.
2. Asserts only one `setInterval` is active.
3. Re-renders with a new `emergencyStartTime`.
4. Asserts the previous interval was cleared and a new one created.
5. Unmounts and asserts the interval is gone.

...would be ideal but is a separate scope. I left a note in the source code (`// [P0][VIDA-SAFETY] Hy3-audit...`) so a future test author has a clear reference. If Daniel wants the test before merge, I can add it as a follow-up.

## Closes

- Notion: `3c3aa66d-73fe-81cb-ae47-c568a723e56b` (Hy3-audit Interval timer de emergencia nunca se limpia)
- Area: Vidas / Risk tier: risky

body:
Handles all six items from the improvement list. Branched from `main`, so it's independent of #43/#45 — no stacking, though both touch `CHANGELOG.md` and a small conflict there is likely whichever merges second.

452 insertions, 7 deletions. No existing content was merged or deleted.

## 1–2. Contributor onramp

Nine `help wanted` issues (#46–#54) were just opened against a repository with **no `CONTRIBUTING.md`**. An outside contributor had no documented answer for any of: run `bash scripts/validate-all.sh`; `references/integrations.md` is generated, don't hand-edit it; update `CHANGELOG.md`; the enforced size limits. I had to reverse-engineer all of that this session and paste it into all nine issue bodies — which is exactly the signal it belonged in one file.

- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — prerequisites (Git, Bash, Python 3.10+, nothing to install), the validator as the single gate, the two generated files and how to regenerate them, how to add a catalog entry honestly, portable-skill vs host-adapter structure, and the size limits the validator enforces (100/180/15/40 lines).
- **`SECURITY.md`** — a private reporting path, and more usefully a *Boundaries* section stating the design limits most likely to be misread: validation is not a publication guarantee, deleting a file doesn't erase history, `verified` is a metadata claim rather than a test, and nothing here sandboxes an agent. Also scopes out third-party integration vulnerabilities, which will otherwise land here.
- **Issue templates** — an integration proposal mirroring the shape of #46–#54 (including a required "What you could not verify" section), a bug report, and contact links routing security reports away from public issues.

## 3. Doc reachability

`docs/optimizing-context.md` and `docs/mcp-efficiency.md` were **unreachable** — nothing outside `CHANGELOG.md` linked them. Both are real user-facing guides nobody could find.

The one-time fix isn't the interesting part. `check-links.sh` catches one direction of drift (a link whose target is gone) and structurally cannot catch the other (a target nothing links to), which is how trimming an index row strands a file. So this adds **`scripts/check-doc-reachability.sh`** for that direction, in the same style as its counterpart — pure bash + git, no model, no network — and wires it into `validate-all.sh`.

Backtick mentions count as routes, deliberately: `CLAUDE.md` and `ROUTING.md` route to files using `` `docs/foo.md` `` rather than markdown links. Without that, the checker would have false-positived on `docs/agent-template.md` (my first hand-rolled regex did exactly that).

Orphans fixed: the two guides above are now rows in the README documentation table; `docs/launch-copy.md` is linked from `docs/positioning.md`, which is what it applies.

## 4. Maintenance doc overlap

`docs/maintenance.md` and `docs/repo-maintenance.md` each gave a slightly different version of the same "Every working session" and weekly cadence.

I did **not** merge them — the split is defensible and the README already distinguishes them. Each now opens with a one-line **Scope** statement and links the other; the workspace cadence lives in `maintenance.md`, repository conventions in `repo-maintenance.md`. `repo-maintenance.md`'s duplicated session section becomes "Before committing" (the part genuinely its own), and its `Weekly`/`Monthly review` headings become `Reviewing tracked context`/`Periodic deep review` so they no longer read as a rival cadence.

If you'd rather actually merge them into one file, say so — that's a taste call I deliberately didn't make unilaterally.

## 5. Minimum-Python CI — this one found a real bug, and corrected me

The kernel's floor was never executed: the Linux job takes the runner default, the Windows job pins 3.13. A floor no job runs is a claim, not a guarantee.

I first pinned the job at **3.9**, reasoning from `str.removeprefix` in `kernel.py:795`. Before pushing I ran an AST scan at `feature_version=(3,9)` and fixed four PEP 604 unions it found in two test files, so I expected green.

**It failed anyway — 11 errors.** `contextos/kernel.py` calls `Path.write_text(newline=...)` in four places, and the `newline` kwarg is **3.10+**. That is a runtime signature difference, not syntax, so no static scan was ever going to catch it. It needed a job actually running the interpreter.

So the true minimum is **3.10**, the job is pinned there, and there's a comment at the pin so nobody lowers it without moving those four call sites. All three jobs are now green.

This has a consequence outside this PR — see below.

## 6. Covered above (`SECURITY.md`)

## Validation

`bash scripts/validate-all.sh` — 168 tests, 11 skipped, all checks passed, including the new reachability check:

```
✓ No broken local links in 85 tracked markdown files
✓ All 21 tracked docs are reachable from other markdown
```

All three CI jobs pass on the current head, including the new 3.10 job.

## This corrects a review finding on #43

Finding 5 of my review on #43 said to replace `major == 3` with `sys.version_info >= (3, 9)`. **That number was wrong**, and #45 implements it — `scripts/python-env.sh` there currently accepts a 3.9 interpreter that will then crash on the first `propose` with `TypeError: write_text() got an unexpected keyword argument 'newline'`.

#45 needs the same 3.10 correction before it merges. Flagged on that PR too.

## Things to push back on

- **The maintenance-doc split** (item 4) — I scoped rather than merged. Merging is the other reasonable answer.
- **`SECURITY.md` points at GitHub private vulnerability reporting.** That needs to be enabled in Settings → Security for the link to work. Worth checking before merge.
- **Tone of the boundaries section** in `SECURITY.md` is deliberately blunt about what this project does not do. If that reads as underselling, it's easy to soften — but I'd argue it's the honest framing given the positioning doc's own "Claims to avoid" list.

author: nestor-forex
body:
**No cambia la app.** Añade una regla nueva al banco de pruebas, la mide, y el resultado es que no entra.

## Por qué esta regla y no otra variante más

Todo lo medido hasta ahora en esta app eran variantes de la misma idea: mirar qué divisa está fuerte y perseguirla. Sobre 35 meses eso da 46% en **todos** los umbrales de ADX. El problema no era el umbral: era la familia de reglas.

El rompimiento de apertura pregunta otra cosa — por dónde sale el precio cuando entra el volumen de Londres o de Nueva York. Es la herramienta estándar del intradía en Forex y esta app nunca la ha tenido.

## El resultado

Vara neutra 1:1, spread descontado, ~35 meses de velas H1 reales.

| Cómo se define "rompió" | Ops | Acierto | Por 1R |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cierra fuera, rango de 1h | 19.571 | 44% | −0,26 |
| Cierra fuera, rango de 2h | 15.509 | 45% | −0,20 |
| **Cierra fuera, rango de 3h** | **13.484** | **46%** | **−0,17** |
| Toca el borde, rango de 1h | 21.372 | 42% | −0,26 |
| Toca el borde, rango de 2h | 23.665 | 40% | −0,28 |
| Toca el borde, rango de 3h | 22.435 | 40% | −0,27 |

El mejor, troceado: Londres 46%, Nueva York 45%, compras 46%, ventas 45%, pares con dólar 47%, cruces 43%. **Ningún corte llega a 50.**

Objetivos más lejos empeora (−0,13 → −0,21 de 1× a 3×). Exigir rangos anchos mejora algo pero no salva (−0,17 → −0,09) y deja solo un tercio de las operaciones.

**Trece mil operaciones.** El margen de error del 46% ahí es de menos de un punto. No es ruido ni una ventana corta: es un no.

Que `toque` vaya peor que `cierre` en los tres rangos es justo lo que predice un mercado sin memoria más un coste fijo: tocar el borde dispara mucho más y cada disparo paga spread.

## La trampa que había que esquivar

Lo cómodo para filtrar rangos estrechos era `par.atrAbs`. Pero ese ATR es el del **final** de toda la serie: usarlo para juzgar una sesión de hace dos años es mirar el futuro, y habría inflado el resultado sin dar ningún síntoma.

En su lugar se usa la anchura media de las 24 velas **anteriores** al arranque de la sesión. La comprobación 3 de `prueba-apertura.mjs` lo caza: corre sobre media serie y sobre la serie entera y exige que el tramo común salga idéntico, también **con** el filtro puesto — que es justo donde el ATR del futuro se habría notado.

## Por qué el modo `toque` se puede juzgar con el resolver de siempre

El resolver juzga desde la vela **siguiente** a la de entrada, así que lo que pasa dentro de la propia vela que rompe no se mira. Como el stop está en el borde contrario, la única forma de que esa vela tocara el stop es que tocara los dos bordes — y ese caso se descarta entero, porque la vela no guarda el orden en que ocurrieron y no hay manera honesta de saber cuál fue primero.

Lo que sí puede perderse es que esa vela llegara al objetivo: eso sería una **ganancia** no contada. El sesgo que queda va en contra nuestra, no a favor.

## Qué cambia en el código

| Archivo | Qué |
|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/apertura.mjs` | nuevo — la regla |
| `scripts/prueba-apertura.mjs` | nuevo — 26 comprobaciones sin internet |
| `scripts/backtest.mjs` | sección 10, cuatro tablas |
| `src/lib/marketCalc.js` | expone `closes` por par (aditivo; nadie más lo lee) |
| `.github/workflows/backtest.yml` | corre la prueba **antes** de descargar; 45 min |
| `CLAUDE.md` | el resultado, para que no se repita el intento a ciegas |

## Lo que este PR deja escrito para la próxima vez

Con esto van tres familias distintas medidas sobre años, y las tres pierden después de costes. Queda un aviso en `CLAUDE.md`: **no proponer una cuarta variante sin decir antes qué la hace distinta de estas tres.**

Y queda señalado lo único que ha salido positivo por tres caminos independientes: trocear por el RSI de entrada (extendido 12% · −0,74 contra zona sana 50% · +0,22 en el historial real). Eso es un filtro sobre las reglas que ya existen, no una regla nueva.

Corrida: [run 32791283355](https://github.com/Nestor-forex/Nestor-forex-intradia/actions/runs/32791283355) · 16 minutos · en verde.

author: cweber12
body:
Implements the QARTOD QC stage — `kelpcompare qc` — per docs/04 §1 and ADR-004.

Before this branch, every stored row carried `qc_flag = 2` (not evaluated) and
`src/kelpcompare/qc/` was an empty stub. ADR-004 rests the project's scientific
credibility on the claim that its non-NOAA/SCCOOS sensors are defensible because
they pass the tests reviewers already recognize; that claim had no code behind
it. This branch supplies it.

**This changes what `qc_flag` and `qc_tests` mean for every stored row**, which
is why docs/03 and docs/04 change in the same commits that change the behavior,
and why the design was settled in plan mode before any code was written.

---

## What it does

`kelpcompare qc` reads the `observations/` zone, groups rows into series, runs
three QARTOD tests via `ioos_qc`, and re-derives `qc_flag` / `qc_tests` from the
full set of per-test verdicts. Flags only, never deletions (hard rule 4).

```
$ kelpcompare qc --data-root <root>
    PROJ:YELLOW-BUOY  sea_water_temperature  3029 rows  1:3022 4:7

1 series evaluated -- 1:3022 4:7
manifest: .../raw/_manifests/20260825T000659324Z-qc.json
```

| Test | Thresholds from | Status |
|------|-----------------|--------|
| gross range | `valid_range` in `parameters.json` (+ optional `qc.gross_range.suspect_span`) | implemented |
| spike | `qc.spike` in `parameters.json` | implemented |
| rate of change | `qc.rate_of_change` in `parameters.json` | implemented |
| climatology | — | deferred, reason recorded in docs/04 §1 |
| flat line | — | deferred, reason recorded in docs/04 §1 |
| neighbor validation | — | blocked on public-source fetchers, recorded in docs/04 §1 |

## Evidence: the docs/06 §5 check 6 prediction, now checked

docs/06 §5 check 6 predicted, before this stage existed, that on the reviewed
TidbiT deployment the gross-range test would flag nothing in-window, and that
the install transient — a reading taken in air while the logger was being
deployed — would show up independently as a spike / rate-of-change failure.
That prediction is now an assertion in the test suite, and it holds:

| Claim | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Rows stored, before and after | 3029 → 3029 (no deletions) |
| In-water rows | 3022, all at `qc_flag = 1`, min 17.76 °C |
| Verdicts on every in-water row | `deployment_window:pass;gross_range:pass;spike:pass;rate_of_change:pass` |
| Gross range flags anywhere in the file | **none** |
| Out-of-window rows | 7, all still at `qc_flag = 4` |
| The 14.78 °C install transient | `deployment_window:fail;gross_range:pass;spike:fail;rate_of_change:suspect` |
| Run manifest `qc_flags` | `{"1": 3022, "4": 7}` |

Two independent tests condemning one reading that gross range is happy with is
the intended redundancy, not duplicated effort.

## Design decisions, and what was rejected

These were resolved in plan mode because each changes the design materially.

**1. Flags land in place, not in a sidecar zone.** `qc` rewrites the
`observations/` partitions through the existing `write_observations`, preserving
each row's `fetch_run_id`; the partition file is renamed to the qc run that last
flagged it. *Rejected:* a separate `qc/` zone joined at query time — it
contradicts docs/03 (both columns belong to the observations table) and would
force every notebook, dashboard query and feature build to join, creating two
sources of truth for one column. *Rejected:* adding a `qc_run_id` column — the
partition filename plus `qc_tests` already answer "which run, which tests", and
a schema change would touch every existing test for no new information.

*Accepted cost, documented in docs/03 and covered by a test:* re-ingesting an
export that overlaps already-flagged rows brings them back at `qc_flag = 2` with
a newer `fetch_run_id`, and the newest run wins. That is honest — they have not
been evaluated since they were re-ingested — and re-running `qc` restores them.

**2. The window verdict is one more test vector; the roll-up re-derives.** `qc`
reads the verdicts already in `qc_tests`, replaces only those of the tests it
ran, and rolls the whole set up again. Precedence: `9` missing wins outright,
then `4` fail, `3` suspect, `1` pass, `2` not evaluated. A row failed for being
outside its deployment window therefore stays at `4` however much a gross-range
test likes its value, and running `qc` twice is a no-op.

Note for reviewers: **this deliberately diverges from `ioos_qc.qartod_compare`,
which ranks MISSING lowest.** docs/03 gives `9` to a row whose value is absent,
and there is nothing in an absence to judge — a verdict about where the
instrument was must not turn a missing reading into a measurement that failed.
Every other step matches QARTOD. The divergence is documented in the module
docstring, in docs/03, and asserted in `tests/test_qc_flags.py`.

*Rejected:* a monotonic ratchet where `qc` can only raise severity — it would
make the flag a function of history rather than of the data, so a corrected
deployment window could never clear a flag, and `qc` would not be idempotent.

**3. Thresholds live in the parameter registry, not in code** (ADR-004), added
in their own `data(registry)` commit. `parameters.json` gains an optional `qc`
block; gross range keeps taking its fail span from the existing `valid_range`
rather than repeating it, so the hard bounds have one home. **An absent block
means those tests do not run for that parameter** — the loader refuses unknown
keys, empty blocks, and thresholds declared for tests that do not run, because a
silently disabled test is indistinguishable, in the stored flags, from a test
that ran and passed.

**4. Neighbor validation is out of scope.** It is blocked: no public-source
fetcher exists yet, so there is no neighbor series to compare against, and tests
may not hit the network. The dependency is recorded in docs/04 §1 and
docs/00-README rather than left implicit.

## Scientific risk a reviewer should weigh

The default analysis filter is `qc_flag <= 2`, so a **suspect flag removes data**
just as surely as a deletion would. Thresholds are set generously and are
explicitly provisional — they were tuned against a single three-week deployment,
which is n=1. Setting them tighter would preferentially remove the brief cold
excursions docs/04 §2 relies on as a nitrate proxy: the signal, not the noise.
The `_comment` in `parameters.json` and docs/04 §1 both say so, and revising them
is a registry edit plus a re-run, not a code change.

Two flag-reading properties are documented in docs/04 §1 because they surprise
people:

- The spike test judges a sample against the midpoint of its neighbours, so a
  spike large enough to fail necessarily pushes both neighbours past the suspect
  threshold. One bad reading costs three rows from a `qc_flag <= 2` query.
- `flat_line` is deferred partly because it fires on genuinely quiescent water —
  the reviewed deployment holds within instrument resolution for over four hours
  at one point.

## Review guide — five slices, each independently green

`pytest` and `ruff check .` pass at **every** commit, not only the last.

| # | Commit | What to check |
|---|--------|---------------|
| 1 | `data(registry): declare QARTOD spike and rate-of-change thresholds` | Are the threshold values defensible? Registry plus its docs/03 schema paragraph only; no code reads it yet |
| 2 | `feat(qc): read QARTOD thresholds from the parameter registry` | The loader refuses rather than ignores. `tests/test_parameters.py` (new) |
| 3 | `feat(qc): roll observation flags up from per-test verdicts` | The roll-up semantics and the MISSING divergence. Also moves the flag vocabulary into `storage.py` — it is docs/03 schema, and two stages were about to keep separate copies |
| 4 | `feat(qc): run the QARTOD tests over a stored series` | What counts as one series; every row tested including window-failed ones; the reference acceptance case |
| 5 | `feat(cli): add kelpcompare qc` | The command, the manifest, in-place write behavior, idempotence, re-

author: jmorrison-juniper
body:
# Spec Conformance Checklist

**Linked Spec Issue**: #2017 (and #2015)

Closes #2017. Closes #2015.

## What this changes

`require_org_access` in `mist-ops-platform/src/api/middleware/auth.py` returned
at once when `CurrentUser.is_msp` was true.

```python
def require_org_access(org_id: str, user: CurrentUser) -> None:
    if user.is_msp:
        return
    ...
```

`is_msp` is one global boolean. The Mist `/api/v1/self` answer sets it when
**any** privilege row carries `scope == "msp"`. The flag never named **which**
MSP account the operator administers. One MSP administrator therefore read and
wrote **every organization** on the platform. That set held the organization of
a different MSP, and it held an organization with no MSP relationship at all.

`require_org_access` is the single chokepoint for authorization in this
service, so the bypass defeated every check that pull request #2012 and pull
request #1983 added.

## How the fix works

1. `collect_msp_ids` keeps the `msp_id` of every MSP scoped privilege row. The
   caller now names the MSP accounts that it administers.
2. `resolve_msp_org_ids` reads the organizations that those MSP accounts own
   from `Organization.msp_id`.
3. `CurrentUser` carries `msp_ids` and `msp_org_ids`.
4. `require_org_access` grants an organization in two ways only. A direct Mist
   grant lists the organization on the caller account, or an MSP that the
   caller administers owns the organization. Every other request returns 403.

The check falls closed on every failure path.

| Condition | Result |
| - | - |
| The `is_msp` flag is true and no MSP row carries an identifier | 403 |
| The organization has a NULL `msp_id` | 403 |
| A different MSP owns the organization | 403 |
| The application state holds no database engine | 403 |
| The lookup query raises | 403 |
| Mist sends an `msp_id` that is not a UUID | 403 |

A caller that holds no MSP privilege row runs **no** extra query, so a plain
operator pays no added cost. The session privilege cache stores `msp_ids`, so a
cached MSP caller keeps the correct scope through the 5 minute period. A
session record written before this change carries no `msp_ids` key, so that
caller falls closed until the next sign in. That is the safe direction.

## Test evidence

New file `mist-ops-platform/tests/unit/api/test_msp_org_scope.py`, 11 tests.
They failed before the fix and pass after it.

- An MSP operator receives 403 for the organization of a different MSP.
- An MSP operator receives 403 for an organization with no MSP owner.

author: themancalledzac
body:
The frontend was the only gate on `/api/proxy/actuator/**` and has now fixed its side. The backend was already sound -- exposure is `include=health` only, and `InternalSecretFilter` 403s everything but the three health URIs -- so this is defence in depth on a surface already closed twice over.

## Why it is still worth doing

Working rule 1 says an injected env var outranks a property. `MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINTS_WEB_EXPOSURE_INCLUDE=*` in a deployed `.env` would silently register `/actuator/env` and `/actuator/configprops`, with nothing in the repo to notice. Boot applies exclude after include, so an explicit exclude list survives that.

And nothing anywhere asserted the actuator exposure at all.

## What it adds

`management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude=env,configprops,beans,mappings,heapdump,threaddump,loggers,shutdown` -- every endpoint that dumps configuration, dumps process state, or mutates the running app.

`ActuatorExposureTest` pins the shipped value. It reads `src/main/resources` directly per working rule 2, since `src/test/resources/application.properties` shadows the shipped file during tests and a `ClassPathResource` lookup would assert against the stub and pass vacuously.

## The part the item did not ask for, and the part that matters

Pinning the string only proves the string is there. The hardening rests on "exclude beats include" -- an ordering the board asserts and nobody in this repo had checked.

`ActuatorExposureEndToEndTest` boots the app with `include=*` on top of the shipped exclude and asserts the eight endpoints 404 while `/actuator/health` still 200s. It holds.

It is also not vacuous: with the exclude emptied and `include=*`, `/actuator/env` answers 200 on the app port. That is what the property is buying.

General form, worth reusing: when a hardening change rests on a framework ordering guarantee, test the guarantee, not the config string.

## Verification

1,357 tests, 0 failures, 0 checkstyle violations. Two mutations verified red: deleting the shipped exclude line, and running the end-to-end test with an empty exclude.

author: themancalledzac
body:
**Re-targets #325 to `main`. Same two commits, no code change.**

#325 was opened against `0324-f3-reordermove-move` as a stacked PR. #324 merged to main at 23:59:31; #325 merged 13 minutes later — but into its stale base branch, not main. GitHub only auto-retargets a stacked PR when the base branch is *deleted* after merging, and `0324-f3-reordermove-move` was not deleted.

Net effect: `gh pr view 325` reports `MERGED`, which is true and misleading. **F6 never reached main.** On `main` today, `SharedRendererProps` still has all 16 members and `EditRendererProps` does not exist.

This PR carries `9953f19` and `243ad09` onto main unchanged. `0333cc0` (F6's base) is already an ancestor of main, so this applies cleanly.

After merging, **delete both `0324-f3-reordermove-move` and `0325-f6-editmodelayer-context`** so neither can be used as a base again.

---

Original description follows.

## What changed

Twelve of `SharedRendererProps`' sixteen members had exactly one caller, `EditModeLayer`. Every public caller of `ContentBlockWithFullScreen` carried twelve optional props it never set, and two components re-declared them only to forward them untouched.

`EditModeLayer` now supplies those twelve through `RendererProvider`. `Component` reads the ambient value and re-provides it merged with its own props and derived values, so `BoxRenderer` still sees one flat value and `Component` never imports from `edit/` to build it.

The twelve are **removed** from the prop interfaces, not left alongside the context path. Keeping both would let any of them arrive two ways with precedence invisible at both the call site and the provider.

## Three of the item's own measurements were wrong

- **`EditModeLayer` is the sole caller of 12 members, not 13.** The board's table reads "all 8 reorder + 4 cover/select = **13**"; 8 + 4 = 12.
- **Six call sites, not seven.** `CollectionRailContext.tsx` mentions the component but has no JSX call site.
- **`onImageLoadError` has zero callers anywhere in `app/`.**

So `SharedRendererProps` went **16 → 4**, not 16 → 3. Reaching 3 means deleting `onImageLoadError` as dead plumbing — a separate change, deliberately not bundled.

Measurement trap: `grep 'prop={'` misses JSX boolean shorthand, and four of the six call sites pass `enableFullScreenView` that way.

## `Component` consumes one of the twelve

`currentCollectionId` isn't just forwarded — `Component` reads it to set `isPublicView`, which decides whether a failed image is dropped so the row reflows (public) or kept for an admin to delete (manage).

## Tests

246 suites / 4423 tests pass, +1 suite and +24 tests on a 245 / 4399 baseline.

The new `EditModeLayer.rendererContext.test.tsx` exists because the provider was **entirely unpinned**: deleting the `RendererProvider` outright left all 245 suites passing. Red-checked both ways — deleting the provider fails 14 of the 24; dropping one member fails exactly that member's test.

## Sizing: the src estimate missed in the wrong direction

**+53 src / +218 test, against −20 src / +40–60 test.** It predicted a shrink and the item grew, because the twelve declarations were relocated rather than deleted, and because the estimate double-counted a −13 that #321 had already banked.

## Not verified in a browser

Spring backend down (`ECONNREFUSED` on `meServer()`). Group F's ":3000 verify" is outstanding on F2 and F6 together.
