author: frankieramirez
body:
Implements the full [v0.1 spec](https://github.com/frankieramirez/bushel/blob/main/SPEC.md). Closes out the build phase of the [wayfinder map](https://github.com/frankieramirez/bushel/issues/1).

## What's here

**Architecture** — the four layers from the spec (`runner → client → engine → ui`):
- **Runner**: the subprocess seam (`run` + `spawn_stream`/`KillHandle`), mocked at the args→bytes level
- **Client**: arg building, serde parsing (unknown-field tolerant — shapes are only patch-stable), error classification by exit code then stderr substring, version check against a tested range kept next to the fixtures
- **Engine**: Elm-style single-writer loop over one `AppEvent` channel. 1s poll tick; images/volumes on pane entry, after actions, every 10th tick; stats piggyback with client-side CPU% from consecutive cumulative samples; pending actions confirmed by polls (2-tick cap) and announced only at confirmation; synthetic restart; log follower (`logs -n 200` backlog then `logs -f`, killed on selection/tab change or container stop, 10k ring); 2s probe while the service is down; degraded banner after 3 straight parse failures; external stops announced
- **UI**: Ratatui + tachyonfx port of the [layout prototype](https://github.com/frankieramirez/bushel/issues/7)'s validated look — hybrid split, action menu, command-preview confirms (delete/prune/kill only), message log, pull streaming in the detail pane, service-down takeover with one-key `--enable-kernel-install` start. Micro-motion ≤150ms, `reduced-motion` kills everything, truecolor→256 and Unicode→ASCII fallbacks

**Testing** — 72 tests: per-version CLI fixtures (curated + verbatim `container` 1.2.0 captures) through the real parsers, 31 headless engine tests (inject events, assert state), keymap tests. Also verified live against `container` 1.2.0: list, logs follow, stop/start/restart, inspect, action menu, kill confirm — all exercised through a pty harness against a real container.

**Packaging** — CI (fmt / clippy `-D warnings` / test), cargo-dist release workflow (macOS binaries on `v*` tags, Homebrew formula published to `frankieramirez/homebrew-tap`), README install/use docs.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- SPEC self-contradicts on log backlog depth (feature cut says ~1000, architecture says `logs -n 200`) — implementation follows the architecture section
- ADR 0001 could explicitly exempt prototype-gated ambient effects from the ≤150ms rule (the code documents this)
- Demo GIFs / final mark — deferred branding work
- Release prerequisites: create the tap repo + tap-publish token before tagging `v0.1.0`

author: olavopitonjunior
body:
O bench de hoje roda 2 fixtures **sintéticas em texto puro**. Ele não manda imagem nem PDF para modelo nenhum — mede extração sobre texto que já estava legível, e isso decidiria qual modelo faz OCR.

Medido em 24/08 num PDF sintético bem diagramado, os quatro candidatos acertaram **16/16**. Sintético limpo não separa modelo nenhum. Quem separa é escaneado torto, carimbado, amarelado, fotografado de celular com sombra — que é o que chega no formulário.

## Braços

O desenho **separa duas variáveis** que mudariam juntas num bench ingênuo: o modelo e o `responseSchema`. Sem os dois primeiros braços, um ganho do schema apareceria como mérito do modelo novo, e trocaríamos de modelo quando bastava consertar a chamada.

| chave | o quê |
|---|---|
| `baseline` | `gemini-2.5-flash` **sem** schema — produção exata de hoje |
| `schema` | `gemini-2.5-flash` **com** schema — isola o ganho do schema |
| `lite35` | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` |
| `lite31` | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` |
| `gemma` | `gemma-4-31b-it` |

Falta o braço de **duas etapas**, que responderia se o objeto superset numa chamada é o melhor formato. Depende dos schemas por categoria, que nascem depois deste bench — até lá a pergunta segue **em aberto**, e prefiro dizer isso a fingir que os cinco braços a respondem.

## Critérios

Em `src/lib/ai/bench/vision-scoring.ts` — em `src/` e **testado** (28 testes), porque a métrica que decide a troca de modelo não pode existir só dentro de um script.

**Alucinação e omissão são medidas separadas**, e é a decisão que organiza o resto:

> campo **vazio** o corretor percebe e preenche; campo **preenchido errado** ele assina.

Por isso alucinar mais é **veto** — acurácia melhor não compensa.

Também: acurácia ponderada (CPF, matrícula e nome pesam 3×), acerto de categoria, taxa de JSON aproveitável, p50/p95 e custo/documento com `geminiUsageToTokens` — sem os thoughts, o `2.5-flash` apareceria com 1/5 do custo real justamente no relatório que decide a troca.

## O gabarito não pode ser o `extractedData`

Ele é saída do `gemini-2.5-flash`, o modelo que está sendo julgado. Usá-lo faria o bench **premiar quem concorda com o incumbente e punir quem o corrige** — diria "ninguém supera o modelo atual" por construção. Entra como `_rascunhoDoModeloAtual`; o `esperado` nasce vazio e o runner **recusa rodar** sem anotação humana. Mesma razão para `categoriaEsperada` existir separada de `categoriaSugerida`.

## Sete achados do code review

O primeiro invalidaria o bench inteiro, em silêncio:

**`campos: { type: "OBJECT" }` sem `properties` não dá erro — devolve `campos: {}` vazio.** Verificado contra a API. Os quatro braços com schema reportariam 100% de omissão, 0% de alucinação, e o critério de veto nunca dispararia. O harness produziria um número confiante e completamente errado.

Os outros:

- **Braço vazio saía APROVADO.** Chamadas todas falhadas agregam em zeros, e zeros passavam em toda comparação. O espelho era pior: baseline vazio reprovava todo candidato contra algo que nunca rodou.
- **Falha de API era descartada**, então um modelo que estoura quota em metade do corpus reportava a mesma acurácia de um que respondeu tudo. Agora conta como omissão total e tem coluna própria.
- **`--confirmo-o-banco` só checava se a flag existia.** Apontado para produção, passava sem reclamar. Agora compara com o `DATABASE_URL` real e mostra o host (sem a senha). Uma trava que não trava é pior que nenhuma, porque produz confiança.
- **`pull-fixtures` sobrescrevia o `ground-truth.json`**, destruindo horas de anotação manual a cada reexecução. Agora mescla por `id`.
- **`String(valor)` colapsava objeto em `"[object Object]"`**, então dois arrays diferentes contavam como acerto — crédito de graça nos campos mais difíceis.
- **Valor monetário BR marcava alucinação por formatação**: `350000` contra um gabarito `"R$ 350.000,00"`, em campo crítico que alimenta o veto.

## Travas de PII

O repositório é **público** e os documentos são de pessoas reais.

- A regra do `.gitignore` veio **no commit anterior**, antes de o downloader existir — verificada com `git check-ignore`. O gitleaks do pre-commit procura padrão de credencial, não CPF dentro de um PDF escaneado.
- `--org` obrigatório (sem escopo, varreria tenants de clientes).
- Nome de arquivo derivado do **ID**, não do `filename` original, que traz o nome da pessoa e viraria PII em `ls`, em log e em print de tela.

## Verificação

- `npm run test -w apps/web` → **4512 testes passando** (28 novos). Só falha `me/password/route.test.ts`, por `otplib` ausente neste ambiente — pré-existente.
- `npm run typecheck` → nenhum erro novo. `eslint --max-warnings=0` limpo.
- Travas exercitadas à mão: confirmação divergente aborta sem vazar senha, confirmação correta passa, `--limite` inválido é recusado.

## O que este PR NÃO faz

**Não roda o bench.** Isso precisa de decisão sua: qual org fornece o corpus, e alguém conferindo o gabarito campo a campo contra cada documento. Sem essa anotação, o bench mede concordância com o modelo atual — que é exatamente o viés que ele existe para evitar.

author: tassiocamara
body:
Fecha as oito issues abertas da auditoria de autenticação (#236–#243), conserta
a trava de rolagem que impedia qualquer compra, e reverte uma decisão minha de
ontem que a pesquisa mostrou errada.

## As oito issues

As oito se confirmaram no código. Três eram maiores do que o texto delas dizia.

| # | Veredito |
| --- | --- |
| #236 freio no god-mode e no reset | confirmada — `django.views.View` não roda `throttle_classes` do DRF |
| #237 `fields = "__all__"` vaza tokens | confirmada — `access_token`, `refresh_token` e `id_token` iam para o navegador |
| #238 senha trocada não derruba sessão | confirmada |
| #239 enumeração | confirmada nos quatro pontos |
| #240 `expires_in` como epoch | confirmada — o token nascia expirado em 01/01/1970 |
| #241 500 no `space` | confirmada, **e maior** |
| #242 `zxcvbn` sem limite | confirmada, **e maior** |
| #243 `autoComplete="off"` | confirmada, **e maior** |

**Onde passei do texto da issue**, porque metade do conserto não conserta:

- **#241** — o `app` parecia protegido, mas UUID malformado levanta
  `ValidationError`, que não estava na captura. Os dois derrubavam.
- **#242** — a issue citou três lugares; havia seis chamando `zxcvbn` direto.
  Viraram `senha_e_forte`, que corta em 128 caracteres **antes** de medir.
- **#243** — além dos dois arquivos citados: login do god-mode, campos de
  segredo do painel e a tela de senha da ADR 0025.
- **#239** — o `ADMIN_USER_DEACTIVATED` chegava antes da conferência de senha,
  contando de graça que aquele e-mail é administrador. Passou para depois.

## A trava da tela de compra

O `DefaultLayout` é uma moldura `h-screen overflow-hidden`: corta e não oferece
barra. Toda tela que vive nele traz o próprio rolador — as três da ADR 0025 não
traziam.

Medido antes: o formulário tem **1209px** de altura natural, e o botão
"Continuar para o pagamento" ficava em `top: 1161`, fora da tela em 640, 768,
900 e 1080. A roda do mouse não movia nada (`scrollY` 0 → 0). **Ninguém
conseguia comprar.**

Medido depois, no dev, com cache desligado:

| altura | rola? | botão dentro? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 640 | sim (`scrollTop` → 569) | sim, `top: 592` |
| 900 | sim (→ 309) | sim, `top: 852` |
| 1080 | sim (→ 129) | sim, `top: 1032` |
| 1300 | não precisa | sim, `top: 1161` |

Nas duas telas centradas o rolador vem por fora e a centralização usa
`min-h-full`, não `place-items-center`: grade centrada que transborda deixa o
topo do conteúdo fora do alcance da rolagem. Verificado a 240px de altura — o
título fica em `top: 24`, alcançável.

## A reversão: `EmailCheckEndpoint`

A primeira versão da ADR 0026, escrita ontem, **manteve** o `existing` alegando
prática de mercado. A pesquisa desmontou o argumento:

1. **[ASVS 5.0, 6.3.8](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x15-V6-Authentication.md)**
   — *"Verify that valid users cannot be deduced from failed authentication
   challenges, such as by basing on error messages, HTTP response codes, or
   different response times."* Sem exceção para login em dois tempos: a
   [folha de dicas da OWASP](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)
   sequer menciona esse desenho.
2. **A Okta vende a correção como recurso** — *User Enumeration Prevention* — e
   a [implementa](https://support.okta.com/help/s/article/how-to-configure-user-enumeration-prevention-in-okta-identity-engine)
   mostrando **o mesmo segundo passo** exista ou não a conta, com *"both email
   and password options in the second step"*. Isso derruba meu argumento de que
   esconder custaria o código mágico.
3. **Uma afirmação minha era falsa.** Eu escrevi que o freio por IP *"é o que o
   próprio OWASP recomenda"* nesse caso. A OWASP não diz isso em lugar nenhum.

### O que passou a valer

Com `ENABLE_SIGNUP=0` o `EmailCheckEndpoint` devolve resposta **constante** e
**não consulta o banco** — o que fecha junto o canal de tempo que a 6.3.8 cita.

Com `ENABLE_SIGNUP=1` nada muda. Não é meio-termo: é o mesmo critério que a
Okta documenta ao dizer que o recurso dela *"fails to function if the
organization uses Self-Service Registration"* — onde qualquer um cria conta, a
existência vaza pela tela de cadastro de qualquer jeito.

A tela "não há conta com este e-mail", entregue na 1.43.1, **era** o oráculo, e
saiu. O caminho de quem ainda não é cliente virou **link fixo** na tela de
entrada, visível antes de qualquer e-mail — igual para todo mundo, e por isso
não responde pergunta nenhuma.

## Provas

- **1748 testes da API** e **307 do front**; `pnpm check` 60/60; lint da API limpo.
- **16 testes de contrato novos**, entre eles: os dois corpos do `email-check`
  são idênticos, e a guarda de "não consulta o banco" foi **provada por
  injeção** (mover o desvio para depois da consulta faz o teste reprovar).
- **No navegador**, contra o dev com cache desligado: as duas telas — e-mail com
  conta e e-mail sem conta — ficam **idênticas byte a byte**, descontado o
  e-mail digitado.
- A guarda de `autoComplete` varre `web`, `space` e `admin` e também foi provada
  por injeção.
- O `test_user_exists` do upstream **prendia o defeito** da #239; foi reescrito
  para afirmar o oposto, em par com o `test_password_validity`.

## Fora do escopo, e por quê

- **Criptografia em repouso** das colunas de token (segunda recomendação da
  #237): envolve gestão de chave e migração das linhas existentes.
- **`USER_ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED` no caminho do app** tem o mesmo vazamento que
  corrigi no god-mode, mas aquele bloco é o conserto da GHSA-rmmf-rj2q-3rrg e
  roda também no caminho OAuth, onde não há senha para provar antes. Reordenar
  ali é risco de outra natureza.
- **`MagicGenerateEndpoint`** dispara e-mail para qualquer endereço válido. Não
  é oráculo — a resposta é a mesma e o código vai para a caixa da vítima —, mas
  é vetor de envio não solicitado. Link mágico está desligado em produção.

## De brinde

A suíte reprovou às 00h03 UTC num teste de prazo que compara carimbo de tempo
com data: `test_faturamento_abandono` cruzava a meia-noite e transformava 29
dias em 30. Relógio parado ao meio-dia, mais um teste que prende a borda das
23h59.

Closes #236, #237, #238, #239, #240, #241, #242, #243

author: maxir23
body:
Closes #74

## What it does

Adds the New task modal, opened from a column's plus button with that column
preselected. Until now a new project had no way to create a card: the plus
button existed but was disabled.

## Scope

- New `CardAssignee` joining Card and User, unique per pair, so a card can
  have several assignees. Assignees are written alongside the card in the
  same transaction as its creation.
- Modal at 540px on desktop and tablet, full screen on mobile. The header
  shows the project and the target column; closing discards the draft.
- Fields: title, description, column as a segmented control, label as
  single-select chips, assignees as toggleable avatars, and a due date.
- The due date uses a real date picker rather than the prototype's free text,
  which the spec itself flags as a prototype-only shortcut.
- Create is disabled until the title has content. The card lands at the end
  of the chosen column with the next code in sequence, and the creator is
  assigned when nobody was picked.
- The label editor moves out of the board header and into the modal, where
  the spec puts it. The header control was a temporary entry point while this
  modal did not exist; it is gone now.
- The column plus button is enabled and opens the modal aimed at its column.

## Notes

- Due dates are compared against the viewer's local calendar day, not UTC.
  Storing them at UTC midnight while comparing in UTC made a card due today
  read as late from 21:00 local time in a negative-offset timezone.
- Due dates are still day-only. Supporting a time of day, converted into each
  viewer's timezone, is its own slice: it changes what the field means and
  affects the card detail too, so it is better decided once for both screens.

## Out of scope

- The card detail modal, subtasks, comments.
- Archiving and deleting.
- Filters, visibility, sharing, the activity log, board search, shortcuts.
- Toasts. The board has no toast system yet; it arrives with the detail
  slice.

## How to test

1. `pnpm exec prisma migrate dev` creates `CardAssignee`.
2. The plus button on any column opens the modal with that column selected.
3. Create stays disabled until the title has content; creating places the
   card at the end of the column with the next code, visible without a
   reload.
4. Assignees persist; a card created without one belongs to its creator.
5. The due date persists, renders on the card, and only turns late after
   local midnight.
6. The label editor works from inside the modal, and the header control is
   gone.
7. Escape closes the modal and focus returns to the plus button.
8. `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:run` pass.

author: naufalrafiathl
body:
Follow-up to #60 (ENG-802). **No behaviour change** — comments and tests only.

## Why this exists

#60 was squash-merged at `d451317`, moments before my last push (`e2df98c`) landed. The merged code is correct and green, but the five fixes from a second review pass did not make it in. This is exactly that commit, cherry-picked onto the merged base.

## What is in it

1. **The route header named the wrong contract section.** It cited the BE contract's *"What the route must implement (ENG-726)"* table as what the file implements. After ENG-802 it isn't — those rows describe the pre-802 direct-insert route, and the contract itself says so in a note ENG-770 added directly above them:

   > Once ENG-802 repoints it at `waitlist_join`, both collapse to a single `204` and the duplicate row disappears. Do not implement the table below and the section above at the same time.

   The header now names the *"The waitlist_join function (ENG-770)"* section, which is what the file actually implements. Left as-is, the next reader lands on the superseded table and concludes the contract disagrees with the code.

2. **Two claims were asserted in a "measured" register without having been measured** — `?select=*` → `204` and `?select=id` → `42703`. Now actually measured against the running function:

   ```
   POST /rest/v1/rpc/waitlist_join?select=*   -> 204, no body
   POST /rest/v1/rpc/waitlist_join?select=id  -> 400 42703 "column waitlist_join.id does not exist"
   ```

   Both hold. In a repo whose specs are headed "MEASURED, NOT INFERRED", the distinction is the point.

3. **Test 11 was the file's last all-negative test.** A lone `expect(selectMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` passes just as happily if the route `400`s on the address or stops calling the RPC entirely. It now asserts status and the RPC call first — the trap this same file cites twice elsewhere and `.rx/gotchas.md` documents.

4. **New test 15 records what a unique violation reaching the route now does.** Deleting the mapping *and* grep-banning the literal turned that from an implementation detail into an unexamined absence. It falls to the generic `500`, which is acceptable **only** because the function cannot produce it.

   The comment states the real consequence plainly: anti-enumeration is now a **database** invariant, not a route one. If `waitlist_join` ever gained a conflict *target*, duplicates would answer `500` where a fresh join answers `200` — the oracle this epic exists to close, back again, and after ENG-803 this route is the only signup path. **Nothing in this repo can catch that**; ENG-770's RLS tests own it.

5. **The harness comment was wrong about its own mechanism.** It claimed a throwing `fromMock` produces "a rejected POST". It does not — the throw lands inside the route's own `try`/`catch` and resolves as a `500`. The guarantee comes from the explicit assertions, not an unhandled rejection. A comment that misstates why a guard works is what stops the next reader checking it.

## Verification

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| `npm test` | 51 files / **849** passed (was 848 on the merged base; +1 = test 15) |

Mutation spot-check on this branch: leaking `error.details` into the `500` body still fails test 9 (1 failed / 50 passed). Scoped lint clean — repo-root `npm run lint` is unusable.

## Follow-up still open on `stablepass-be`

Not fixable from this repo: the contract's `### Insert idiom — the only supported one` heading, and the `409` duplicate column of the `waitlist` PostgREST row, both predate ENG-770 and are **not** covered by that note. They now describe a write path this route no longer takes. Natural home is ENG-803.

## Surface

```
app/api/waitlist/route.ts        (comments only — no logic change)
test/waitlist-route.test.ts      (test 11 hardened, test 15 added, harness comment corrected)
```

Propagate errors from block lowering instead of continuing with incomplete HIR.

This prevents the Rust compiler from emitting partial output when it encounters unsupported syntax, including nested TypeScript `this` parameters.

This landed earlier as #37232, which exposed an existing FBT diagnostic ordering issue. Resolve local FBT bindings before checking whether an `<fbt>` tag comes from a module import, so the compiler reports the earlier, more useful Todo instead of a later invariant.

- `cargo test --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml -p react_compiler_lowering`

author: lonewolf-077
body:
## Summary
Adds the first pass of Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) for ShopWave's AWS deployment, based on the System Design Doc (Section 13). Since we don't have an AWS account yet, this PR is scoped to **offline validation only** — the provider is configured with dummy credentials and skip flags so `terraform init`/`terraform plan` can run and validate syntax + the full resource dependency graph with zero real AWS API calls.

## What's included
- **`main.tf`** — AWS provider block configured with dummy credentials (`mock_access_key`/`mock_secret_key`) and `skip_credentials_validation`, `skip_requesting_account_id`, `skip_metadata_api_check`, `skip_region_validation` all set to `true`. Clearly commented as offline-only, not for use against a real account.
- **`vpc.tf`** — VPC (`10.0.0.0/16`) spanning two hardcoded AZs (`us-east-1a`/`us-east-1b`) for HA, with public + private subnets, an Internet Gateway, one NAT Gateway per AZ, and route tables/associations for both tiers.
- **`data.tf`** — RDS PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ, `db.t3.medium`, gp3, encrypted) for User/Order/Payment/Inventory; ElastiCache Redis replication group (2 nodes, automatic failover) for Cart/Auth sessions; S3 bucket for File/Media service product images (versioning, SSE-AES256, public access fully blocked). Security groups on RDS/Redis restrict ingress to VPC CIDR only.
- **`.gitignore`** — excludes `.terraform/`, state files, `.tfvars`, and other local/secret-bearing artifacts from version control.
- **`.terraform.lock.hcl`** — committed per Terraform convention to pin the `hashicorp/aws` provider version (v5.100.0).

## Testing summary
- `terraform init` — succeeds, installs `hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0` (resolved to 5.100.0).
- `terraform plan` — initially failed on `data "aws_availability_zones"` (a live lookup that isn't suppressed by the provider's skip flags, unlike resource creation). Fixed by hardcoding the AZ list instead of dynamically discovering it.
- After the fix: `terraform plan` completes cleanly — **27 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy**, zero errors, zero real AWS calls made.

## Open questions / not yet resolved
- `aws_db_instance.postgres` has a placeholder plaintext `password` (`REPLACE_ME_WITH_SECRETS_MANAGER_ARN`) — needs to be swapped for a real Secrets Manager reference before any real `terraform apply`. Flagging rather than resolving here since we have no AWS account to test against yet.
- No remote backend configured (state is local only) — fine for solo offline validation, but will need an S3 + DynamoDB backend before this is used for a real shared deployment.
- EKS (mentioned in the System Design Doc's cloud infra section) is not covered in this PR — scoped to networking + data stores only. EKS/compute is a natural next Terraform module.

## Notes for Person B
- This PR does not touch anything you own (Catalog/Cart/Order/Payment/Infra you've been driving) — it's additive, in a new `infrastructure/` folder.
- No AWS account exists yet for either of us, so nothing here has been (or can yet be) applied for real — this is purely local syntax/dependency-graph validation.
- Once we do get AWS access, the next steps are: real credentials, a remote state backend, and resolving the RDS password/Secrets Manager item above before ever running `apply`.

## Carried-forward items (untouched by this PR)
- Day 18 file-service PR still not opened.
- Day 18's auth-on-upload decision for `/files/upload` still open.
- CI matrix gaps for discount-service/wishlist-service still open.
- All Day 11–17 carried-forward items remain open.

`/sitemap` serves a sitemap index; `/sitemap/{blog,pages}/<n>` serve chunked url-sets of published `BlogPost` + `Page` records — each `<loc>` from the class `$collectionRoute` + `Handle`, `<lastmod>` from `Modified`. Lean by design: selects only `Handle` + `Modified` (never the content clob), chunked at 10k (under the 50k-URL limit). Hostname from `SITE_PRIMARY_HOSTNAME` (authoritative — `getConfig('primary_hostname')` derives from HTTP_HOST). Implements `specs/behaviors/search-indexing.md`; the `lastmod` pairs with the ETag work (#23) so re-crawls only re-fetch changed posts.

**Verified against production data** (34,431 published posts / 59 pages): the index lists 1 pages + 4 blog chunks; chunks return exact counts (10000×3 + 4431; 59); `lastmod` present; no functional/noindexed path appears in any sitemap.

Leaves reference it from robots.txt (`Sitemap:` line, separate per-leaf change).

author: denzmilk
body:
Closes #899. **Security fix, and it carries a migration — merging deploys it to the live database.**

## What was wrong

`is_admin` sits on `profiles`. `profiles_update` is written per **row** (`auth.uid() = id`), as every RLS
policy is. Supabase grants `UPDATE` on every **column** of a new `public` table. So an ordinary signed-in
player could `PATCH /profiles?id=eq.<self>` with `{"is_admin": true}` — their own row, policy satisfied —
and `public.is_admin()` then returned true for them. That is the function `feedback_admin_select` uses, and
`20260806000003` had re-granted `select on public.feedback to authenticated` so the policy could work at all.

Proven by applying every migration to a real Postgres and trying it, before writing any fix:

```
feedback rows visible BEFORE flip: 0
self-flip of is_admin: ACCEPTED
feedback rows visible AFTER flip: 1
read back: [{"body":"my password is hunter2","contact":"victim@example.com"}]
```

Every player's report text, their **contact email address**, their user id and their diagnostic meta.

## The part worth keeping

**No individual migration was wrong.** `20260806000001` is right to give feedback no select policy;
`20260806000003` is right that a policy cannot grant what the role does not hold; `20260806000004` is right
that admin should come from the GitHub allowlist. The hole is the **interaction** — a privileged flag on a
client-writable row — and there is no wrong line for a text search to find. This is precisely
[ADR-0031](https://github.com/denzmilk/wordtide/blob/develop/docs/decisions/0031-the-sql-is-tested-by-running-it.md)'s
argument, and the reason the harness had not caught it is that **`feedback` had no SQL coverage at all**: its
RLS was asserted by grepping a migration for the *absence* of a select policy (`flow-harness.mjs:8915`),
which is true and beside the point.

## The fix — two independent reasons, as this schema already does for DELETE

1. **`UPDATE` is granted per column.** A table-level grant covers every column and a column-level revoke
   does not subtract from it, so it is `revoke update on public.profiles` then
   `grant update (username, display_name, avatar, is_public)`. A future privileged column now fails **closed**.
2. **A trigger pins the flag** for `anon`/`authenticated` — still true if a later migration re-grants the
   table by hand, which is one careless line. It tests the **role**, so the GitHub allowlist path is
   untouched (it is `security definer` and runs as the owner). INSERT is covered as well as UPDATE: a client
   whose profile row was missing could otherwise create it pre-promoted.

Asserted first, before the refusals: **the admin page still has a way in.** A fix that locked out the
legitimate path would be worse than the hole.

## Sixteen checks the feedback table never had

Who can read (anon refused at the privilege level; an ordinary player *holds* the privilege and RLS returns
nothing — including for their own reports; an admin reads), who can file (anonymously yes; as somebody else
no), that nobody edits or deletes a report from a client, and every column bound — kind, 2000-character body,
8 KB meta, contact format.

**Four fail against the schema as it was**, including the escalation itself.

## Not exploitable yet, and that is luck

OAuth providers are not enabled, so there are no player accounts (#22). It goes live the moment sign-in
does, and a leak of this table is not something a later fix un-leaks.

## Testing & sign-off

`npm test` green. **Not user-facing** — this removes an ability nobody was meant to have; a player can still
change their name, avatar and visibility exactly as before (asserted). Nothing to try on `/preview/`.

author: dhsorens
body:
Stacks on **#12824** (`lane-b4`), which supplies the `rlp_walk_init` / `rlp_walk_next` anchors. Review the last four commits only; base is `main` so the diff shows #12824's commits too.

`Addresses #12799`

## ⛔ The task I was given was already done. The finding is what was left.

I was asked to prove whole-routine `cpsTripleWithin`s for `headers_parent_hash` and `header_validate_parent_hash`. **Both already had them, and both were already rowed.** I checked by statement shape before writing anything, and a second search agreed independently:

| routine | existing triple | row |
|---|---|---|
| `headers_parent_hash` | `headers_parent_hash_spec_within` (`HeadersParentHashMain.lean:24`), `cpsTripleWithin 312` at `hphBase` over `CodeReq.ofProg hphBase headersParentHash_prog` | `.proven`, no gate |
| `header_validate_parent_hash` | `header_validate_parent_hash_spec_within` (`HeaderValidateParentHashUnified.lean:1018`), 3-way post over `fullCode` | `.conditional`, gate `hOutLen` |

So item 1 needed nothing, and item 2's only outstanding residual **was the gate**. That is what this PR removes.

Both callees of item 2 were already genuinely **composed, not assumed** — `headers_parent_hash_spec_within` is applied at `Unified.lean:93`, and `zkvm_keccak256` enters through the keccak arm chain; `fullCode = hvphCode ∪ headersCode ∪ keccakCode`. I did not have to change that.

## Extents, derived from the symbol table — not from any prose

`nm` on `gen-out/regionmap/stateless_guest.elf` (sha256 `fb7dabca4552…6239`), `t/T/w/W` symbols sorted by address, `hi` = next symbol:

| routine | extent | bytes | insns | `prog.length * 4` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `headers_parent_hash` | `0x8000bff0`→`0x8000c078` | 136 | 34 | `34 * 4 = 136` ✅ |
| `header_validate_parent_hash` | `0x8000c078`→`0x8000c124` | 172 | 43 | `43 * 4 = 172` ✅ |

Both cross-checks agree, and the disassembly matches the `Program`s instruction for instruction. The `#guard`s at `HeadersKeccak.lean:329` and `:464` already pinned 34 and 43.

## The gate was not a gate

`hOutLen : (headersParentHash_out thisBytes C0).length = 32` claimed to exclude *"malformed inputs whose extraction yields ≠ 32 bytes"*. **There are no such inputs.**

```
headersParentHash_out tb cb = if headersParentHash_ok tb
                              then (tb.drop (skip + 1)).take 32
                              else cb
```

`headersParentHash_ok`'s third conjunct is already `skip + 33 ≤ tb.length`, so on the success branch the `take 32` is **saturating**; on the failure branch the routine never writes and the result **is** `cb`. Given only `hclaim0 : C0.length = 32` — which is forced anyway, `claimedOwn` being the fixed 32-byte `GuestAddrs.hvph_claimed` slot — the length is 32 either way.

New lemma `headersParentHash_out_length` proves exactly that, and `hOutLen` is now discharged inside the theorem instead of demanded from callers.

* **Tier:** `.conditional` → **`.proven`**, `gate :=` **removed entirely** (not reworded).
* Propagated through both consumers, which no longer ask for it either: `header_validate_parent_hash_hcallee_from_spec` and the unified-route call theorem. Strictly weaker premise sets; **no post and no step bound changed**.

## Non-vacuity

Every contract touched here gets a satisfiable instance **and** a negative control, both as witness `abbrev`s in `Routines.lean` — not merely named in a `notes :=` string.

* `hphSampleHeader_reaches_success` — the instance lands on the **success** branch (`0xe1 a0` + 32 bytes), so the saturating `take 32` is what closes it, not the trivial passthrough.
* `headersParentHash_out_length_refutable_without_hclaimed` — the **negative control**: on a non-list prefix with a 31-byte entry buffer the conclusion is provably **false**, so `hclaimed` is load-bearing.

⭐ **And a gate hole the promotion exposed.** The dispatcher's three full-premise covers — `_extract_fail_cover`, `_match_cover`, `_mismatch2_cover`, one per arm, each instantiating every static premise at once with live data — **existed but were in no gate**: no witness `abbrev`, and `Routines.lean` did not import their module. A `.proven` row whose satisfiability evidence nothing forces is precisely the shape the discipline exists to prevent. All three are now imported, abbrev'd, and cited as coverRefs.

## Registry counts, re-derived from the row set

Not edited by delta. Re-counted from the rows themselves: **188 = 149 `.proven` + 36 `.conditional` + 3 `.partly`**, 159 distinct symbols. The `decide`-checked totals were updated to match and elaborate.

## Gates

All 40 in the local sweep pass, including `lake build`, `check-axioms` (443 witnesses, classical only), `check-forbidden-tactics`, `check-no-warnings` (0), `check-file-size`, `check-registry-coverage`, `lake exe axiomsweep --check` (0 `sorryAx`; 74 SailEquiv declarations, the documented scoped exception), and `import-graph-metrics.py --check` (**no baseline bump needed** — the complement is measured post-#12811).

⚠️ **Honest skip:** `check-doc-links.sh` did **not** run — no `ripgrep` binary on this machine, so it exits on the missing-binary path rather than checking anything. CI runs it for real.

⚠️ **One file here is not my work:** `docs/4ch8f-transcription-queue.md` is lane-b4's own drift (`rlp_walk_init` gate 3 → 2, because #12824 closed one of its gates). `check-transcription-queue` was **already failing on `origin/lane-b4`** before my first commit; I regenerated it mechanically so this branch sweeps clean. No claim changed.

author: jeremydmiller
body:
Closes the gap #4108's first real capped job exposed within hours of merging: CIKafka wedged on `batch_processing_with_kafka.end_to_end`, the new stall detector **named the test and its pid in the log** (`STALLED: … has been in flight 300s on lane 0 (pid 3814)`) — and the partial ledger never happened. The runner signals only the step's own shell on cancellation, and nothing in the `bash → build.sh → dotnet run` chain forwards SIGTERM to the grandchild where `registerCancellationCapture` lives.

## The fix: a pid handshake

- `registerCancellationCapture` (build/StallCapture.cs) publishes `Environment.ProcessId` to `.nuke/temp/build.pid` when it arms.
- Workflow test steps run through **`build/run-with-cancellation-relay.sh`**, whose INT/TERM trap signals **exactly that pid** — deliberately *not* the process group, which would also kill the wedged worker the handler wants `dotnet-dump` to capture — then holds the step open (bounded) while the handler writes the ledger and takes stacks, inside the runner's own hard-kill deadline.
- Applied to `tests.yml`, `http.yml`, `slow-tests.yml`, and `dotnet.yml`'s test steps. The smoke/pack steps keep plain `./build.sh` — no supervisor, nothing to relay to.

## Proven by simulating the runner locally

SIGTERM sent to the relay while CoreTests was mid-run:

```
[stall] relaying cancellation to the build process (pid 56144)
[stall] cancellation signal received — writing the partial ledger before the runner discards the run
=== CoreTests: PARTIAL — the run was still in flight when this view was taken
    533 passed, 2107 indeterminate …
```

and on disk: `{"IsPartial": true, "CleanPasses": 533, "Indeterminate": 2107}` — the 533 verdicts heard on the live stream survive, everything unverdicted is honestly Indeterminate, and the uploaded artifact is what outlives the cancelled job's discarded logs (#4098).

Also fixes a compile-time latent in #4111's sibling file: `StallCapture.cs` was missing `using Nuke.Common.IO;` for the `AbsolutePath` extensions the pid write needs.

author: nhckdvrl
body:
Post-result audit of G1_RESULTS.md against the actual data and evaluator code
found three overclaims. All corrected here (not silently — the correction
itself is the point).

## 1. "Both navigation effects clear CI-excludes-zero in both directions" — wrong

`nav_effect_upper_live` on `right` has CI `[-0.400, 0.000]` — touches zero,
doesn't exclude it. Only `nav_effect_upper_replayed` (the clean `LR-RR`
contrast, upper-body held constant) independently clears the bar in both
directions. That's promoted to the headline: `N_100,d = S(LR) - S(RR)`,
`N_100,left=+0.20 [0.067,0.367]`, `N_100,right=-0.20 [-0.367,-0.033]`.

## 2. "RR==RL exactly, upper-body changes nothing" — conflated equal means with zero effect

Checked per-config: on `left`, `RL-RR` is literally `0` on all 30 configs
(hence bootstrap CI exactly `[0,0]`). On `right` it's `+1/-1/28-unchanged`
(hence `[-0.1,+0.1]`, not `[0,0]`) — real opposing per-config movement that
cancels in the mean. Same trap as G0's original pooled `delta_high`. Corrected
to: no *average* upper-body contribution above the minimum worthy effect was
established — not "the channel does nothing."

## 3. Evaluator predicate was looser than "reversal"

`g1_core.py`'s `nav_real = any(...)` over both directions never checked
opposite sign — it would call the same verdict for e.g. `left=+0.20,
right=0.00`. Recorded as an audit note; doesn't change G1's conclusion, which
never depended on the verdict enum. `g2_core.py` carries a corrected predicate
forward (independently-significant AND opposite-signed), verified against the
existing G1 data before any new row: reproduces `R_100=0.400`,
`reversal_established=True`.

## G2 pre-registration: does the reversal hold across the force grid?

100N is one of G0's three frozen forces. `G2_PREREGISTRATION.md` freezes the
next step before running it: complete `LR`/`RL` at `50N`/`150N` (240 new
rollouts; `100N` reused unchanged from G1, `RR`/`LL` reused from G0 at all
three forces). Explicitly defers asking *why* the navigation channel is
directionally miscalibrated until the force grid answers whether the
phenomenon generalizes past one operating point.

Local logic tests: `46 passed` (35 + 11 new for `g2_core.py`).

author: twillis209
body:
## Summary

Adds a rigorous correctness-testing layer to the fork, fixes one latent bug, and lands two performance changes — all verified **byte-identical** to current outputs.

### Test infrastructure (main deliverable)
- **Synthetic fixture** (`tests/make_fixture.py`): deterministic BAM+VCF exercising phased/unphased hets, hom-ref/alt, `./.`, multiallelic `1|2`, non-PASS, indels, spliced/insertion/soft-clipped reads, duplicates, improper pairs, low MAPQ/baseq, and third-allele noise reads, across two chromosomes with a two-sample VCF.
- **Golden parity harness** (`tests/test_parity.py`): runs the full pipeline in six option scenarios (reintegration on/off, prefilter on/off, `gw_phase_vcf 2`, MAF-weighted phasing, unphased-vars off) and requires byte-identical outputs vs committed goldens. Only documented normalizations applied: aReads/bReads ordering, `##bcftools_*` header lines. `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` pins set-iteration order.
- **Unit tests** (`tests/test_units.py`) pin the new helpers against reference implementations of the historical logic, including exact `str()` formatting and degenerate genotypes (`10|2`, short sample columns, FORMAT=GT-only).
- Fast-path coverage was proven by mutation testing (corrupting the fast path makes parity fail).

Run with `pytest tests/`. Regenerate goldens **only from a verified-good tree** with `python tests/test_parity.py --regenerate`.

### Bug fix
- `phaser.py`: the read→variants merge across pool outputs tested a stale `variant` loop variable instead of `read`, so a read appearing in multiple pool outputs (e.g. multi-BAM runs) had its variant list overwritten rather than accumulated. Single-BAM outputs are unchanged (parity-verified). Extracted into `merge_read_vars()` with unit tests.

### Performance
- **Vectorized noise test**: conflicting-configuration p-values are computed in one batched `binom.cdf` call instead of one scalar scipy call per variant pair (~23 µs → ~0.07 µs per pair, bit-identical results incl. int/float `str()` formatting in `variant_connections.txt`).
- **`write_vcf` unphased-record fast path**: appends phaser tags without splitting/rejoining the sample column. Guarded (GT first in FORMAT, no phaser tags already present, sample not longer than FORMAT); anything else takes the unchanged slow path. Honest measurement: ~2% off the write loop on a 2M-line VCF — per-line Python streaming (~1.5 µs/line) is the floor, so gains here are bounded.

### Notes for cluster use (no code change)
- `--threads N` works on Linux (fork start method); it is silently broken on macOS (spawn) — not addressed here per project priorities.
- `--io_threads 2-4` parallelizes the samtools/bgzip pipe ends.
- For cohort runs, the existing recommendation (reintegration off + separate batch reintegration) avoids the Python-streaming-bound stage entirely. A `bcftools annotate` reintegration engine was evaluated and deliberately **not** built: it would leave hom-site `PG`/`PW` tags missing and make FORMAT heterogeneous across records, breaking per-site consumers and fixed-index parsers.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 12 passed (units + 6 end-to-end parity scenarios)
- [x] Parity suite run twice to confirm run-to-run stability
- [x] Mutation check: corrupted fast path → parity fails; reverted → green
- [ ] Recommended before merge: parity + timing run on real data (NA06986 / NA20808) on the target Linux cluster (`scripts/download_test_case.sh`, `scripts/run_test_case.sh`)

author: shangyian
body:
### Summary

`/sql/measures/v3` can generate a query that references a column that its upstream CTE doesn't project, which fails with an unresolved-column error when run.

This is because of two processes that disagreed: the pruning process decided which columns each CTE should keep by looking at the requested dimensions' join paths, while the set of CTEs to emit comes from the full transitive closure of the dependency graph. Any node that lands in that closure without sitting on a join path (e.g., an intermediate transform, or a dimension pulled in only as another node's parent) was never consulted. Its own body got emitted unpruned, still referencing every column it reads, but the upstream it reads from was pruned as though the join-path nodes were its only readers.

This widens the needed-column scan to walk the same closure the CTE set is built from, so both halves agree on who the readers are. 

### Test Plan

Added a new test for the exact failing case, with a dimension pruned to one requested attribute, and a transform that reads a different column from that dimension while never being a requested dimension itself.

- [ ] PR has an associated issue: #
- [x] make check passes
- [x] make test shows 100% unit test coverage

Deployment Plan

None. Behaviour change is confined to SQL generation; queries that were already valid generate the same SQL, and the widened scan only ever adds columns to a projection.

author: adrian-haldenby
body:
## Summary

- add causal, vectorized factor primitives for panel alignment, ranks, robust z-scores, rolling beta, residual returns, and weighted blends
- add pooled factor admission and one-shot holdout checks with next-open outcomes, Newey-West statistics, BH correction, chronological stability, and a frozen cutoff
- expose `factor-scan` / `factor-holdout` through the jobs CLI, MCP, and background op runner, with compact research-agent guidance
- add `Mixed Factor Balance · 4h` as the first starter in the selector: a long-only crypto plus HIP-3 equity/commodity allocator using trend, relative value, low-volatility quality, and funding carry
- extend the existing buffered rank and target-weight helpers for long-only baskets and independently rebalanced sleeves

## Corrected research outcome

The initial exploratory results were discarded after finding two research-harness defects: cached 4h frames contained 1h candles, and funding buckets were labeled at their start. A rank-buffer overflow was also fixed before final selection. The promoted evidence uses validated raw 4h OHLC, right-labeled completed funding buckets, next-open execution, and 8 bps one-way costs.

Market-neutral candidates failed their frozen tails, so the final topology removes the short-book drag without turning the starter into the existing momentum strategy:

- crypto sleeve: trend quality plus low volatility and carry; frozen tail **+8.60%**, Sharpe **4.09**
- onchain sleeve: relative value plus residual strength and low volatility behind a broad trend/breadth gate; frozen tail **+0.56%**, Sharpe **2.31**

Exact jobs_v1 replay at the catalog default of 1x, including fees and funding:

- 180-day net return: **+32.45%** vs **+23.64%** buy-and-hold
- Sharpe: **2.00**
- max drawdown: **-13.80%**
- recent 7-day return: **+10.95%**
- chronological segments: **3/4 positive** (`+3.13%, +15.95%, -3.34%, +14.58%`)
- all six 4h rebalance phases positive: **+8.91% to +51.97%**
- 192 trades, $201.83 fees, -$160.73 funding, zero stop triggers, zero liquidations

The 1x-5x sweep had no liquidations, but 2x-5x exceeded the catalog -20% historical account-halt budget. The selector therefore remains defaulted to 1x and explicitly flags the higher settings as outside budget.

## Limitations

- the evidence window is 180 days and overlaps the recent crypto run-up
- one of four exact chronological segments was negative
- the long-only topology was evaluated after observing the factor-family failure, so forward paper tracking remains required
- the onchain sleeve holds cash when its broad trend-and-breadth gate is off

## Quality pass

- reused the shared factor primitives and removed the duplicate research panel builder
- extended one buffered-rank helper instead of adding a parallel allocator
- added sleeve-scoped target diffing so one sleeve cannot close positions owned by another
- added regression coverage for exact basket size, scope isolation, causal precompute, catalog ordering, leverage evidence, and the live lookback window
- replaced a brittle synthetic null fixture that deterministically admitted noise at the configured 10% FDR

## Validation

- `677 passed` across `wayfinder_paths/tests/test_jobs_*.py`
- `80 passed` in the focused factor, portfolio bridge, and starter suites after final cleanup
- Ruff format/check on every changed Python file
- `git diff --check`
- exact jobs_v1 replay completed with no validation issues and the catalog 66-bar live window

## Dependency

Stacked on #704 (`feat/jobs-research-robustness-toolkit`) so this PR contains the factor-specific delta.

author: theprimeagen
body: ## What A new standalone lab that introduces the **screenplay** idea: a screenplay is one or more scenes; a scene is anything that can start, update, render, and stop; `space` cuts to the next scene. The demo bill has two scenes: 1. **arrival** — a drifting starfield; the full zoomed-in craft (size-4, 26×10, W heading) slides in from the right edge with live left-to-right booster fire trailing off its tail, parks at center stage, then bobbles ±1 full cell on a sine with a 10-second period. (Half-cell bobbing would need half-shifted art the atlas doesn't have, so the bobble rides whole cells, as discussed.) 2. **the end** — `THE END` in the height-5 terminal-fonts banner, centered under the same sky. Plus a second adjusting tool in the adjustflame mold: **`cmd/adjuststars`**, the sky tuner — the whole starfield plays behind a panel of eight numbers (a fly **delay** and a **density** for each of the four star layers); `j`/`k` select, `h`/`l` change, and the sky reacts live. It's built as a `screenplay.Scene` on a one-scene bill, so the same lifecycle that runs the premiere runs the tool. **The sky now has the fire's file-config shape.** `stars.SkyConfig` mirrors `fire.HeatConfig`: a JSON file of the eight knobs with `DefaultSky`, `UseSky`/`ActiveSky`/`ResetSky` (the package-active setting), and `LoadSky`/`Save` with sentinel validation. `adjuststars` opens the file (`-config`, default `cmd/adjuststars/stars.json`, committed with stock values like `flame.json`), applies every nudge live, and `s` saves the file and quits. The premiere loads the same file at boot (`-stars`; missing file = stock sky) and its scenes cast `NewTunedStarfield()`, which follows the active sky every frame — **a tuned config just works in any scene**. Verified end to end: tune, save, reboot the premiere → 196 near stars on screen vs 13 stock. Backing it, **`stars.Field` grew a `Density [4]int` knob** (stars per 1000 cells per layer; zero value keeps the stock sky via `DefaultDensity`, floors keep layers alive, a cap stops floods). ## Design Built on the Charm v2 migration (#21) — this PR is **based on that branch** and should land after it. - `Scene` is the generic four-verb interface: `Start()` allocates, `Update(dt)` advances clocks (no render data), `Render(*Screen)` writes cells, `Stop()` deallocates. - `Screen` is the shared render target every scene gets a pointer to: a **Lip Gloss v2 `Canvas`** — one `uv.Cell` of content + style per terminal cell — plus `Resize`/`Resized()` bookkeeping so a terminal change repaints everything. - `Screenplay` owns the frame loop: clears the screen, runs update-then-render on the current scene only, `Next()` stops the old scene before starting the new, `Stop()` ends the run. - `Ensemble` keeps the "scene = cast of sprites" shape: the cast is assembled at `Start`, dropped at `Stop`. - The `screenplay` package speaks lip gloss cells only; the labs' xterm-256 art crosses over in `cast/blit.go`. Everything spaceship-specific stays isolated in `cast/`. - Bubble Tea v2 TUIs with the exec-tui `CLICOLOR_FORCE` → ANSI256 hook so tapes/CI keep their color; one fix riding along wires that same hook into `exec-tui/cmd/adjustflame`, whose runner page recorded as monochrome without it. ## Tests Written first (red suites committed separately), happy and unhappy paths throughout: screen/ensemble/screenplay lifecycle semantics, the blit bridge, ship flight path and flame placement, title and starfield actors, the demo TUI, the `stars.Density` knob, the adjuststars tuner (seeding, live sky reaction, rail clamps, keys), and the config file lifecycle (SkyConfig round-trips, sentinel validation, active-sky swap/reset, tuned starfield following `UseSky`, `Open`/save-and-quit/failed-save flows, the premiere's apply-if-present boot). All nine lab suites pass on the merged base. ## Demo Two-scene premiere (fly-in, full 10-second bob, spacebar cut to THE END): [screenplay_premiere_arrival_bob_then_the_end.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0362e-519d-788f-ac22-84910ff90cef/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenplay_premiere_arrival_bob_then_the_end.mp4) All eight engines firing in the adjustflame runner (with the color fix): [adjustflame_all_eight_engines_firing_10s.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0362e-519d-788f-ac22-84910ff90cef/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fadjustflame_all_eight_engines_firing_10s.mp4) Ten seconds of the arrival scene on the Lip Gloss v2 cell path: [screenplay_ship_flying_sideways_over_stars_10s.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0362e-519d-788f-ac22-84910ff90cef/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenplay_ship_flying_sideways_over_stars_10s.mp4) The sky tuner: dust delay dropped 4→1 (streaks), then near density raised 4→64 (the ✦ layer floods in): [adjuststars_tune_speed_and_density_of_four_star_layers.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0362e-519d-788f-ac22-84910ff90cef/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fadjuststars_tune_speed_and_density_of_four_star_layers.mp4) The premiere booted with that saved `stars.json` — the arrival scene flying the tuned sky, no code changes: [Arrival scene under the tuned sky config: dense bright stars around the parked ship](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0362e-519d-788f-ac22-84910ff90cef/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpremiere_arrival_scene_with_tuned_stars_json.png) Stills of both premiere scenes on the v2 cell path: [Scene 1: ship parked center with booster fire over the starfield](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0362e-519d-788f-ac22-84910ff90cef/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenplay_v2_scene1_ship_centered_lipgloss_cells.png) [Scene 2: THE END author: blackstarzck
body:
## 왜

문항 관리 확장 이력 표의 두 컬럼이 라벨만으로 **뜻이 반대로 읽힌다.**

| 컬럼 | 화면에서 보이는 것 | 실제 의미 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `원본 수정 시각` | 원본 생성 시각과 같은 값 → "수정된 적 없음"으로 읽힘 | 공급처가 `updated_at` 을 실제로 갱신하지 않으면 생성 시각이 그대로 들어온다. **변경 판정은 `content hash` 로 해야 한다** |
| `수신 횟수` | `2회` → "버전이 2개"로 읽힘 | 동일 payload 재수신 카운트다. **내용이 달라지면 이 값이 오르지 않고 새 버전 행이 생긴다** |

## 무엇을

공용 `createInfoColumnTitle` 을 재사용해 두 헤더에 안내 아이콘(`노출 상태 ⓘ` 와 동일한 형태)을 달았다. 신규 공용 컴포넌트는 만들지 않았다 — 이 헬퍼가 이미 "상태 enum 이 아닌 일반 컬럼용"으로 존재한다.

같은 `원본 수정 시각` 컬럼이 **인박스 목록에도** 있고, 그쪽에서는 그 값이 `이력 판정`(`out_of_order`·`timestamp_conflict`)의 근거값이라 오독 위험이 더 크다. 그래서 함께 처리했고, 문구는 화면별로 복사하지 않고 신규 상수 모듈에서 단일 관리한다.

폭 조정: `수신 횟수` 110→130, 확장 표 `scroll.x` 1320→1340 (아이콘 추가분).

## 문서

- `admin-page-tables.md` — 헤더 안내 툴팁 규칙을 **상태값 컬럼 → 계산·수신·집계 컬럼**까지 확장. 2개 이상 화면에 나오는 컬럼은 문구를 상수로 단일 관리한다는 규칙 명시
- page-IA 2건 + IA 변경 로그 + 문서 갱신 로그

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| `harness:check` | 통과 (lint · typecheck · import-boundary · typography · design-token 포함) |
| `test:e2e:mock` | **18/18** |
| `test:unit` | **846/846** |
| red→green 증명 | 컴포넌트만 `git stash` 하면 신규 단언이 **실패**하는 것 확인 후 복원 |
| 레이아웃 실측 | 헤더 `scrollWidth === clientWidth`(말줄임 0), 헤더 높이 8칸 39px 균일(줄바꿈 0) |

e2e 는 실제 hover 로 툴팁 문구가 뜨는 것까지 단언한다(양성 앵커 먼저).

## 영향 범위

- **DB·RPC·데이터 계약 무변경** — 표시 전용. 운영 DB 적용 불필요
- 감사 로그 계약 무영향

author: debugmcpdev
body:
Closes #464.

A hot-swap invalidates line numbers, but the replant was purely by line — a `statement:`-anchored breakpoint silently rebound to whatever now lives at the old line, reporting `verified: true`. Content identities must be honored whenever line numbers are invalidated, as `restart_debugging` already does.

## Fix

- After a successful redefine (`redefinedCount > 0`), `reresolveAnchors` — the restart machinery, with all its awkward parts already solved (fresh file read, `nearLine` proximity, #379 multi-candidate flagging, #271 stale-keeps-line) — re-resolves every statement anchor against the source on disk, and the affected files are re-sent via the existing per-file `setBreakpoints` sync. Ordered after `vm.redefineClasses` by construction (it runs on the redefine response), so the JDI replant binds moved lines against the **new** line table — the "not a drop-in" part the issue called out.
- The response carries the same `anchorResolution: { moved, stale }` shape `restart_debugging` returns, plus a `warning` when anchors went stale or a re-send failed.
- **Bridge drive-by fixed**: `handleClassPreparedForFunctionBreakpoints` now returns its replant count and `replantBreakpointsAfterRedefine` adds it in, so `replantedBreakpoints` stops under-reporting (visible below: it reports 2 for 1 line + … well, 2 line bps here).

## Verification — the issue's literal repro, live

Breakpoint at line 19 + statement-anchored breakpoint on `System.out.println("val2 = " + val2);` (line 23). Launch, pause at 19. Overwrite the source with the V2 file (statement shifts to 26), `javac -g`, `redefine_classes`:

```jsonc
→ { redefinedCount: 1, replantedBreakpoints: 2,
    anchorResolution: { moved: [{ from: 23, to: 26, statement: "System.out.println(\"val2 = \" + val2);" }], stale: [] } }
continue_execution
→ stops at RedefineTarget.main line 26      // previously: ran to completion
evaluate val2 → "99"                        // the hot-swapped value
```

- New unit tests: moved anchor (with post-redefine `setBreakpoints` ordering asserted), stale anchor + warning, nothing-redefined short-circuit.
- `JdiDapServer.java` compiles clean; full unit suites 3221 passed.

author: codinnvrends
body:
## Summary

This PR adds automated testing and CI infrastructure to the bePositive Flutter app, addressing the lack of tests beyond the generated stub and the absence of CI/CD workflows.

## Changes Made

### 1. GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/flutter_ci.yml`)
- Added comprehensive Flutter CI workflow that runs on push and pull requests to `main`
- Includes:
  - Flutter setup with version 3.35.0
  - Dependency resolution (`flutter pub get`)
  - Code formatting verification (`dart format`)
  - Static analysis (`flutter analyze --fatal-infos`)
  - Test execution (`flutter test --coverage`)
  - Coverage upload to Codecov (for PRs)

### 2. DatabaseHelper Unit Tests (`test/database_helper_test.dart`)
Comprehensive tests covering:
- **Schema & Initialization**: Database version, table structure, column verification
- **User Profile Operations**: CRUD operations with focus areas
- **Affirmation Operations**: Filtering by age group, gender, focus areas, and custom affirmations
- **Favorites Operations**: Add, remove, and query favorites
- **Notification Settings**: Save, load, and default settings
- **Custom Affirmation Operations**: Create, update, delete with cascading reminder deletion
- **Custom Reminder Operations**: CRUD with window scheduling
- **Schema Migration Tests**: Verification of v2-v5 migration columns and tables

### 3. Provider Unit Tests (`test/providers_test.dart`)
Tests for:
- **UserProvider**: Profile creation, updates, deletion, loading, focus area checking
- **AffirmationProvider**: Loading affirmations, filtering, favorites, daily streak, category filtering
- **NotificationProvider**: Settings management, time formatting, day display
- **Model Tests**: UserProfile, Affirmation, NotificationSettings (equality, copyWith, serialization)

### 4. Dependencies (`pubspec.yaml`)
Added test dependencies:
- `sqflite_common_ffi: ^2.3.3` - For SQLite testing on desktop/CI
- `mocktail: ^1.0.3` - For mocking in unit tests

### 5. Cleanup
- Removed incompatible `dart.yml` workflow (used `dart` commands instead of `flutter` commands)

## Testing

The tests can be run locally with:
```bash
flutter test
```

Or for coverage:
```bash
flutter test --coverage
```

## Reviewer Checklist

- [ ] Verify the CI workflow syntax in `.github/workflows/flutter_ci.yml`
- [ ] Check that test files cover the main functionality described in the issue
- [ ] Verify database tests properly clean up after themselves
- [ ] Ensure provider tests don't have side effects between tests

Closes #4

### Motivation

- Improve the TV control preview so operators can see animation, after-queue behavior and media readiness before sending live. 
- Modernize and enrich the TV dashboard visuals and queued-result presentation with structured winner cards, metadata chips and safer output formatting. 
- Make media (video/image) handling and result ordering more predictable by using publish timestamps and adding HTML-escaping to reduce injection risk.

- Extended the control panel preview in `tv-control.html` to include `animation-style`, `after-queue`, `control-video-url` and image list checks, producing contextual readiness/warning messages and a two-column preview layout.

author: cyberneel
body:
Local dev currently has no safe mode. Every route goes through the Admin SDK, so without credentials `npm run dev` returns 500 on every page — including the public marketing ones. The only way to run the app was to point a real service account key at `lhr-recruiting-2026`, which means local development reads and writes live recruiting data.

This wires up the emulator suite so that stops being the only option.

## What's here

- **`firebase.json`** — auth (9099), firestore (8080), storage (9199), UI (4000).
- **`firestore.rules` / `storage.rules`** — deny-all. All real access goes through the Admin SDK, which bypasses rules anyway, and the client SDK is only used for Google sign-in. Production rules stay in the console; these exist because the emulator requires a rules file.
- **`lib/firebase/admin.ts`** — a first branch that initializes without credentials when `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` is set. The production path and the loud throw when nothing is configured are untouched.
- **`lib/firebase/client.ts`** — connects the browser SDK to the emulators behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_EMULATOR`. Both halves have to be set together or the sign-in popup mints a token the server can't verify.
- **`scripts/seed-emulator.mjs`** — one admin, one applicant, and an open recruiting cycle. Everything else already has a hardcoded default in `lib/firebase/config.ts`, so seeding it would be redundant.
- **`npm run emulators` / `npm run seed`**.

## Getting started

```bash
npm run emulators   # terminal 1
npm run seed        # terminal 2, once
npm run dev
```

Sign in at `/auth/login` through the normal Google popup — the auth emulator shows a fake account picker where you enter one of the seeded addresses. They're `@utexas.edu` because `app/api/auth/session/route.ts` only admits that domain plus four specific gmails.

Requires a JRE for the Firestore emulator (`jre-openjdk-headless` on Arch, `default-jre` on Debian). The auth emulator is pure Node.

## Two choices worth flagging

**`npx -y firebase-tools` instead of a devDependency.** `bun.lock` and `package-lock.json` are both committed and CLAUDE.md says to keep them in sync; adding a devDep desyncs them unless whoever runs it has both package managers. npx costs a few seconds on first run and nothing after.

**The seed script hard-refuses to run without `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`.** It's the same shape as `wipe-cycle-data.mjs`, which does talk to production, and I didn't want a copy-paste of the wrong script to write test users into the real project.

## Not included

`.env` is gitignored, so nothing here configures itself. The emulator variables you need:

```
FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=lhr-recruiting-2026
FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:8080
FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:9099
FIREBASE_STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:9199
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_EMULATOR=1
```

Might be worth committing a `.env.example` in a follow-up — right now the required variables are only discoverable by grepping for `process.env`.

Verified with `npm run build`. Not yet run end to end against the emulators — the machine I set this up on is missing a JRE, so the wiring is reviewed but unexercised. Worth one person confirming sign-in works before anyone relies on it, since `createSessionCookie` against the auth emulator is the one piece I'd least want to be wrong about.

author: minhhoang1210
body:
Eight changes, from an audit of how the bot is actually used.

Permissions. /language and /name changed the whole server and any member could run them; both now need Manage Server, and Discord hides them from everyone else. /birthday channel needs it too but sits beside verbs that are for everybody, so it refuses in its own parse instead: the declarative gate covers a whole command, not one verb.

Player buttons. The transport row under a player card answered anyone who could see the message, so a bystander scrolling past could stop the music for the people in the call. Skip, pause, loop and stop now answer only someone in the voice channel the bot is playing in. Paging the queue stays open, because reading what is coming up costs the room nothing.

Database upkeep. pruneUsage and sweepLocks were reachable only through npm run db:migrate, so on a live bot usage_events grew without limit and a lock left by a crash sat until somebody noticed. Both now run on a six-hour clock. The README claimed the pruning already happened, which was true only if you ran the script.

Autocomplete on /play. Typing a title and hoping was the worst part of the bot: a typo came back as the wrong song, out loud. Suggestions come from YouTube's own endpoint rather than a search, because Discord allows three seconds and fires one per keystroke, where yt-dlp takes seconds and spawns a process each time. Cached, deduplicated in flight, and a failure is an empty dropdown rather than an error.

One global registration instead of one per guild. The bot re-registered its whole catalogue for every server at every boot, purely so descriptions read in the server's language, against a quota of 200 command writes per guild per day. Discord's own description_localizations do it properly: one global set carrying both languages, and each reader sees the picker in their client's language rather than the one their server picked. Run deploy-commands --clear-guilds once to drop the old per-guild sets.

A greeting on join. A new server got nothing at all, at the one moment somebody is definitely looking. Three commands worth trying, where the settings are, and which permissions the bot is missing, which is what almost every "it will not play music" turns out to be.

A private option. The lookup commands answer the whole channel whether or not anybody wanted that. /fish book, /fish top, /cook book, /cook menu and /achievements take private: true. A command that must be private stays so regardless, which is what keeps it from leaking a quiz answer.

/help on a dropdown. Four buttons carried a label each and no room for a fifth group. A select menu holds twenty-five, gives each entry its command count, marks the group being read, and rides the detail view so moving between groups is one click.

author: freeperro
body:
Owner: **"12 drop the button"**.

The control implied *copy this template's checklist and parts onto the job I'm
looking at*. That operation has never existed. A real
`POST /api/job-templates/{id}/apply` does exist — but it calls
`create_job_from_template` and returns a **new job**, so wiring the button to it
would have minted a duplicate job per click. That trap is why this was a
decision rather than a repoint. With 0 job templates on prod, nothing is lost.

Removes the button, its handler, and the ui_compat 501 stub. 28 lines deleted.

## Parts cost is not here — pulled a second time

Attempt 2 was stopped by adversarial review:

- **It broke a standing ruling.** It deduped bills against catalog estimates on
  **lowercased part name**. `core/part_pricing.py:30`: *"Matching is exact SKU
  only. The 2026-07-07 AUDIT-R1 review ruled fuzzy sku/name matching an
  undercount generator and that ruling stands."* The two sides don't even carry
  the same string — tier 1 keys on the vendor's free-text `description`, the
  tech typed `part_name`.
- **Its double-count fix was inert.** `confirm.py` stamped `superseded` on
  `needed`/`ordered` rows; costing reads `used`. Disjoint sets. The test passed
  because it asserted an equality true of any status.
- **Both attempts reconciled rows; money reconciles in units.** Used 4 / billed
  1 dropped three units and still reported the job complete.

Findings and the constraints a third attempt must satisfy: **#471**. The
symptom — job costing reports **$0 parts on all 25 prod jobs that have parts** —
is still live as **#457**.

## Evidence

- Backend matrix: **6990 passed / 91 skipped / 1 xfailed / 0 failed**
- Frontend: **229 files / 2097 tests / 0 failures**
- ruff 1199 vs baseline 1208; F821/F823 clean

## Not verified

No browser walk — three buttons become two in that header row, and jsdom can't
see layout.

author: vasmikrishna
body:
## Summary
- New fourth disjoint auth realm `pos` (AD-13): `aud:"pos"`, own secret `POS_JWT_SECRET`, principal `{ id: staffId, tenantId, outletId }` - mirrors the ops/admin realm pattern (AD-3/AD-10) exactly, including a `PosAuthGuard` registered globally alongside `OpsAuthGuard`/`AdminAuthGuard`.
- Two-step PIN login: `POST /pos/v1/auth/login {tenantId, pin}` verifies against active `StaffUser` rows (reuses `pinStatus()`/argon2 verbatim from Tenant Admin's staff module, now exported through the admin barrel). Single-outlet tenants finalise immediately; multi-outlet tenants get a short-lived, different-audience (`pos-pending`) handoff token plus an outlet list, finalised by `POST /pos/v1/auth/select-outlet {pendingToken, outletId}`.
- Lockout: 5 wrong attempts for the exact `(tenantId, pin)` pair locks it for 30s (`429 locked_out`), in-memory `Map` - documented single-instance-only tradeoff for this prototype.
- New `ClockEvent` model (RLS-protected, same pattern as every other tenant-owned table). A successful login records a clock-in unless one is already open for that staff member today, in the *outlet's own timezone*. `POST /pos/v1/clock/out` ends the open clock-in (`409 not_clocked_in` otherwise).

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` - clean
- [x] `pnpm test` (unit, incl. new `lockout.spec.ts` and `clock.util.spec.ts`) - 30/30 passing
- [x] `pnpm lint` - clean
- [x] `pnpm test:e2e` - 279/279 passing across 20 files, including two new suites:

## Summary
- An ops alert fired 2026-08-25 with `age_seconds=86403 stale_after=86400s` - a false positive, root-caused live against prod: the backup cron fires at a fixed `0 3 * * * UTC`, `pg_dump` takes ~7-11s to finish and land, and the freshness check runs on an independent ~180s loop with no wall-clock anchoring - so a sample can land in the few-second gap after yesterday's dump crosses exactly 24h old but before today's fresh dump lands. Every day's backup that week actually succeeded.
- Pads `OPS_BACKUP_STALE_SECONDS` from a bare 86400 to 86400+600 (+10min) to absorb the structural cron/dump-duration jitter without weakening the check's real purpose (catching a genuinely missing or multi-day-stale backup) by any operationally meaningful amount. Same shape as #365's cooldown-constant fix.
- Considered shifting the ops-monitor loop's cadence to avoid 03:00 UTC instead - rejected: the loop has no wall-clock anchoring to shift from (phase drifts with container start/restarts), so it wouldn't durably prevent recurrence and leaves cron-latency/dump-duration jitter unaddressed either way.

## Test plan
- [x] New regression test (`test_check_backup_freshness_tolerates_normal_cron_and_dump_duration_jitter`) reproduces the exact incident age (86400+3s), confirmed failing against the unfixed code, passing after.
- [x] Existing backup-freshness tests still pass (ages far past the padded threshold remain genuinely stale).
- [x] Full `github-app` suite: 1489 passed, 8 pre-existing skips (real Postgres/Redis, disposable `docker-compose.test.yml`).

body:
## What

Adds one entry to **Environments & Benchmarks**:

```markdown
- **[FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18580)** — Task synthesis framework that constructs executable terminal environments, instructions, reference solutions and verifiers from a shared realised environment state, then collects verified successful trajectories for agent fine-tuning.
```

`data/resources.json` and the entry-count marker were regenerated with `python scripts/build_index.py` (92 → 93 entries). No other entries, sections, or files were changed.

## Why

FACET ([arXiv:2608.18580](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18580), Kou Shi et al.) targets the environment/trajectory/data layer of the RL-for-agents loop for terminal (shell) tasks. Its distinguishing design is that every task artefact — the executable terminal environment, the natural-language instruction, a reference solution, and the verifier — is derived from one shared realised environment state, keeping the instruction, the solution, and the verification signal consistent with the same underlying state rather than letting independently generated pieces drift apart. On top of the synthesised tasks it collects verifier-validated successful trajectories, producing grounded interaction data for training terminal agents; the reported training use is downstream fine-tuning on those trajectories, which is why the description says "agent fine-tuning" rather than claiming RL as the paper's central algorithm.

Checks performed:

- **In scope** — the resource concerns the environment → verifier → trajectory portion of the loop, and the bullet names those elements.
- **Canonical link** — the suggestion arrived as a PDF link; swapped for the arXiv `/abs/` page per CONTRIBUTING.md.
- **No duplicate** — neither "FACET" nor arXiv ID 2608.18580 appears anywhere in `README.md` or `data/resources.json`.
- **Description** — one neutral, factual sentence in the surrounding section's wording conventions, with no superlatives or time-sensitive claims.

## Where

Under **Environments & Benchmarks** (Core), the most specific existing section: the headline contribution is constructing executable environments with deterministic verifiers, the same family as the neighbouring VibeWorlding and EnvHarness entries recently added there. The bullet is placed between those two, matching their chronological arXiv ordering (2608.15265 → 2608.18580 → 2608.19880).

author: maonakamoto
body:
## The bug

Articles reached the model with their entities still raw. `decodeEntities` covered six named entities, seven hardcoded decimal escapes, and **no hex escapes at all** — so a German-language source (what this tool is pointed at: `de` in `Accept-Language`, the republik.ch note in the file header) arrived as:

```
Der Wähler über die Straße
```

Nothing threw. The prompt just got worse, and the title rendered the same garbage on screen. A silent quality regression on every affected article.

Measured against the old decoder:

| input | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `Trump's plan` | `Trump's plan` | `Trump's plan` |
| `Straße` | `Straße` | `Straße` |
| `It’s — really…` | unchanged | `It's — really…` |
| `climate 🔥 crisis` | `climate  crisis` (dropped) | `climate 🔥 crisis` |
| `&lt;` | `<` (double-decoded) | `<` |

## Why replace rather than extend

This is the **second** fix in this class. #12 fixed *where* decoding ran (title as well as body) and left *what* it covered untouched. Adding rows a third time buys the same bug again at the next unlisted entity — the table is a hand-copied slice of WHATWG reference data, i.e. a second source of truth for something that already has one, and one that drifts silently.

`entities` is what parse5 and cheerio decode with: **zero runtime dependencies**, full named set, decimal + hex, correct astral code points. Net −18 lines of hand-rolled table.

Two further bugs fell out with it:
- `String.fromCharCode` truncated anything above U+FFFF, dropping emoji outright.
- `&` was replaced *before* `<`, so an escaped `&lt;` in prose double-decoded into a literal `<`.

## Structural fix

Title and body now share one `htmlToText`. The split between them is precisely what #12 had to repair — it can't reopen. Collapsing whitespace there also fixes multi-line `<title>` tags, which previously reached the UI with their newlines intact.

## The gate

`src/lib/article-fetch.test.ts` — 14 cases, first tests this module has ever had. **8 of them fail against the old decoder** (verified by stashing the fix and re-running), so this is a real regression gate, not decoration.

## Verification

`npm run verify` — lint clean, tsc clean, **20/20 tests** (was 6).

## Summary

Upgrades the docs site to Astro v7.2.6 and fixes a `cookie` resolution failure that the Astro bump surfaced in the prerender build.

- **Upgrade Astro and its official integrations** — `astro` 7.1.3 → 7.2.6, `@astrojs/check` 0.9.9 → 0.9.10, `@astrojs/markdown-remark` 7.2.1 → 7.2.4, `@astrojs/vue` 7.0.1 → 7.0.2. This is a minor release within v7, so no migration guide steps applied.
- **Declare `cookie` on the site workspace** — Astro 7.1.3 moved to `cookie@^2.0.1`, whose renamed exports (`parseCookie` / `stringifySetCookie`) were being resolved against the hoisted root `cookie@0.7.2` (pulled in transitively by the example apps' express dev servers), breaking the built output with `Named export 'parseCookie' not found`. Declaring it on `site` puts 2.0.1 in `site/node_modules` so the emitted chunk resolves the version Astro's runtime expects.

Only `site/package.json` and `package-lock.json` change; no source or config edits were needed.

### Notes

`@astrojs/vue@7.0.2` peers on `vue: ^3.5.24`, which the single hoisted `vue@3.5.33` satisfies. The Vue tree is unchanged — one hoisted Vue 3 copy, with `vue@2.7.16` nested only under `packages/vue` and `examples/vue` — so the root `overrides` block pinning `vue` for the Astro/Vite packages did not need adjusting.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx turbo run lint` — 6/6 workspaces pass; `astro check` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings
- [x] `npx turbo run build` — 5/5 workspaces pass; site static build completes
- [x] `npx turbo run test` — 144 Playwright tests pass across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
- [x] Confirm the deployed site preview renders correctly

Pre-existing and unrelated to this change: two `astro check` hints (an implicit `is:inline` analytics script in `site/src/layouts/Default.astro`, and a deprecated `document.execCommand` signature in `site/src/utils/copyToClipboard.js`), plus a Vite chunk-size advisory in the site build.
