<!-- triage-batch: b_f0ee463c3056 -->

## Summary

`sideeye <mode> --help` and `<mode> -h` print the usage text and exit 0, for the four modes that take flags — **answered at a position where it cannot delete anything**. Separately, `spike/upstream-report-status.sh` closes with the denominator it actually knows instead of leaving completeness to be inferred from the table.

`Closes #296`. **`#297` stays open** — see Open points 1.

## Verified

Every number below was produced by running the thing it describes.

- **The behaviour table was measured before any edit, and the ticket's transcript is wrong.** Nine invocations built and run first:

  | | rc | first line |
  |---|---|---|
  | `--help` / `-h` / `help` | 0 | usage banner |
  | `explore --help` | 3 | `an option is missing its value` |
  | `explore --help --state /tmp` | 3 | `unknown option` |
  | `preflight --help` | 3 | `an option is missing its value` |
  | `replay --help` | 3 | usage banner |
  | `demo --help` | 3 | `demo takes only --shim <lib>…` |
  | `mcp --help` | 3 | `mcp takes no arguments…` |

  Four distinct behaviours. #296 shows `explore --help` producing "unknown option"; that is what the **four-element** form produces. The single-flag form hits the arity guard, because the loop treats every unrecognised flag as one that takes a value. The failure is real; the transcript beside it is not what the binary prints.

- **The check was red before the branch existed**: 15 assertions across the four modes. Green after. Its mode list comes from `src/main.zig` (`parser_literals 1` minus the argument-free modes), never from a list written beside it.

- **Five mutations, each on a freshly cleared copy, each red.**

  | mutation | result |
  |---|---|
  | delete the help branch | FAIL per-mode help: 14 |
  | keep `--help`, drop `-h` | FAIL per-mode help: 7 |
  | move help into the parse loop | FAIL per-mode help: 3 |
  | freeze the report denominator to `6` | selftest rc=2, short leg caught it |
  | **help in the loop, operands swapped** | FAIL per-mode help: 3 |

  The third is the one that decides the design: moving help into the loop makes the behaviour look **fixed** — all eight invocations exit 0 with the right text — while three assertions still fail. **The dangerous design passes a behaviour-only test.**

  The fifth exists because review broke my assertion (below). Measured with it applied: the old grep saw **0 hits**, `explore --json X --help` **exited 0 and the sentinel was DELETED**, and the new runtime probe reported the failure. The evasion is real and it costs the caller their report.

- **The first mutation run was discarded.** `rm -rf` on the scratch copy was refused by a local guard, so `cp -R` layered each mutation on the previous one. Re-run with the copies actually cleared (and an existence check that aborts rather than stacking); the verdicts were identical, but the first run could not have told the difference — a monotonically falling count is what stacking produces too.

- **Real binary.** `demo` runs end to end and reports FAIL 1 of 6, crash point 5 of 5 — the help branch sits before `runDemo`, so the self-exec path is untouched. `--json` still writes its report. `explore --help` leaves a sentinel at a `--json` path intact.

- **Suites**: unit 185/185 · `acceptance.sh` ALL PASSED · `mcp-acceptance.sh` · `check-sealed-campaigns.sh` · `check-gitattributes.sh` (1258 files, 1230 documentation, 28 code, none unspecified) · `upstream-report-status.sh --selftest` — all rc=0. `sh -n` clean on both scripts; `git diff --check` clean.

- **`--selftest` measured in four invocation forms** (slashless with the directory off PATH, relative-with-slash, absolute, PATH-from-elsewhere), all rc=0. That set exists because of a regression this PR introduced and then removed — see Open points 2.

- **simplify: 適用1 / 見送り3.** Applied: the extras probe folded into the main per-mode loop (three loops over the mode set became two). Declined: reusing `acc_first()` (it returns a `head -1`'d string and discards rc, which is what this check needs); reducing process count (the probes measure different things, so the count does not fall); deriving the flag-taking mode set from the implementation rather than by subtraction (**that would let the check take its population from the code it checks** — the shape #295 was written to avoid).

- **Secret scan**: 560 diff lines, 0 hits, positive control fires. 0 local absolute paths.

- **Review**: R1 returned P1×2 / P2×2; R2 confirmed 3 FIXED, 1 PARTIALLY, no new P0, and the partial was fixed after being reproduced.

## Same-class scan

**Class: a check reads the source and knows only one spelling of the construct it looks for.** Raised by review — my source-shape assertion grepped for `eql(u8, argv[i], "--help")` and its comment claimed that moving help into the loop "in any form" would go red. It would not; `eql(u8, "--help", argv[i])` means the same and looks different.

    grep -nE 'grep.*(\$ROOT/src|src/main\.zig)' spike/acceptance.sh   →  3 hits

**The scan had to be run twice.** The first pattern carried a `[^|]*` between `grep` and the path — caution with no reason behind it — which excluded every line containing a pipe, and the line under investigation contains `(argv|rest)`. **The scan for this class missed its own instance of it.**

The other two hits are `parser_literals()` and the `rest[i]` scan feeding `acc_flags`, both from #295. They share the fragility and **fail in the opposite direction**: a flag written with the operands swapped drops out of the candidate set, stays on its synopsis line, and "every advertised flag has a parser branch" goes red. Missing a spelling makes those loud, not quiet. The one removed here was the only fail-open member. Left as they are.

## Open points

**1. `#297` is not closed, and the PR deliberately does not close it.** The script now says `read N of N reports listed in REPORTS`, which is true. Forget to add an eighth report and it will still say that, honestly, and exit 0. The claim shrank; the ability did not grow.

- **A — leave `#297` open, as here.** Its title ("cannot see a report that was never added to its list") is still true.
- **B — close it as "as much as is buildable".** Defensible only if option 1 in the ticket is accepted as impossible, and that is a stronger claim than the measurement supports.

Recommend **A**. The measurement that killed the ticket's option 1 is worth reading: its first candidate is a **false positive**. `alecthomas/devtodo#9` exists, was opened by this account, and is absent from the list — because it was filed and **withdrawn the same day** on the owner's judgement (`spike/assisted/NOVELTY.md`, agreed by `outcome-map.tsv` and `docs/target-classes.md`). A withdrawn report and an unlisted one have the same shape in the tracker; what separates them is a judgement kept in prose. A draft of this work read that absence as a missing row and would have added a withdrawn report to a list of standing ones.

**2. A defence added for a finding that did not reproduce, which then broke something that worked.** Review said `self=$0` breaks the new self-test leg under a PATH invocation. Measured: a PATH invocation gives `$0` as an absolute path, so it does not. The guard added anyway resolved through `command -v` **first**, which turned `cd spike; PATH=/usr/bin:/bin sh upstream-report-status.sh --selftest` from working into `could not resolve $0`. author: krist55555
body:
### What

Adds a troubleshooting entry under **Hardware-Specific Issues → NVIDIA GPU Issues** for a
generation failure specific to Blackwell-generation NVIDIA GPUs (`sm_103`).

### Why

On these cards PyTorch's default SDPA path can select the cuDNN backend, which reports:

```
cuDNN Frontend error: No valid execution plans built
```

With FLUX this fails at the first attention block in the UNet, so generation never produces an
image. The error message doesn't point at attention or at the GPU architecture, so it's hard to
diagnose from the log alone. Launching with `--use-split-cross-attention` avoids the cuDNN path
and resolves it.

### How this was verified

Hit and resolved on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (Blackwell, `sm_103`), Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.0 driver,
PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128, running FLUX.1-schnell on ComfyUI as of June 2026.

I also tried disabling the cuDNN SDPA backend from a `sitecustomize.py` before startup; that does
not work, since the flag is not retained through CUDA initialization. I noted that in the entry so
others don't repeat the same dead end.

I only claimed what I actually tested — I haven't verified whether other Blackwell parts
(e.g. consumer 50-series) hit the same cuDNN path, so the entry describes the architecture and the
symptom rather than asserting a specific card list.

### Notes

- Variants of this cuDNN error show up in the main repo without a documented resolution
  (e.g. Comfy-Org/ComfyUI#10090), which is part of why it seemed worth writing down here. I have
  not confirmed those reports share this root cause.
- I wrote the entry in the same style as the neighbouring NVIDIA/AMD entries (bolded symptom +
  commented shell block) rather than introducing new heading levels.
- English only — I didn't run `npm run translate`, since the script needs an API key and I'd rather
  not push machine translations you haven't reviewed. Happy to add them if you'd prefer.
- Happy to adjust the placement or wording — I wasn't sure whether this belongs in the existing
  NVIDIA subsection or warrants its own page as more Blackwell cards land.

body:
## Situation

- Renovate PR https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/pull/1566 attempted to update the `engines` field of [package.json](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/blob/master/package.json).

- This highlighted the discrepancy that the repo is not intended for publication as an npm package to any registry. Rather it is intended as an in-place factory for generating Cypress Docker images. Artifacts are published to [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/u/cypress). Users who want to build customized Cypress Docker images do not need to clone the repo. Instead they base their images on `cypress/factory` and specify configurations using parameters.

- The `engines.node` field is only relevant if it is expected that a published package will be used with different Node.js versions. Instead it is expected that script, builds and CI are run under the version of Node.js defined in [.node-version](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/blob/master/.node-version) - currently set to Node.js `24.15.0`.

## Change

In [package.json](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/blob/master/package.json)

- Set [private](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/configuring-npm/package-json#private) to `true`.

- Remove irrelevant content:
  - `main` (`index.js` does not exist)
  - `directories`
  - `engines`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Metadata-only `package.json` cleanup with no runtime, CI script, or dependency behavior changes beyond dropping the unused engines constraint.
> 
> **Overview**
> Marks the root `package.json` as **`private: true`** so the repo is treated as an internal tooling manifest for Docker image builds, not something meant for npm publication.
> 
> It also **removes publish-oriented fields** that no longer apply: the nonexistent `main` entry, `directories.example`, and **`engines.node`** (Node for local/CI scripts is expected to follow **`.node-version`** instead). `package-lock.json` is updated to match the root package definition.

## Summary

A TUI can leave a hidden terminal's viewer in alternate-screen and mouse-tracking mode after the TUI process has exited or been killed. When the surviving shell is revealed or reattached, pointer input is then encoded as terminal mouse reports and appears as raw `M...` / CSI fragments instead of normal shell interaction.

This change makes recovery event-driven and host-owned. It adds no reveal timer, polling loop, periodic reset, global remount, or steady-state typing/output delay.

## Reliability invariant

After a TUI exits or is killed, reveal, reattach, snapshot replay, or renderer remount must not deliver terminal-owned mouse or alternate-screen protocol bytes to the surviving shell. Recovery is permitted only when ordered shell completion and fresh execution-host process inspection establish sequence-bound shell ownership. Missing or revoked proof preserves incumbent behavior.

## Root cause and fix

The first incorrect boundary was renderer restore precedence: stale viewer-side agent status/title metadata could outrank fresh execution-host evidence that the shell had regained the PTY.

The fix establishes one ownership chain:

1. The host parser observes TUI mode involvement followed by ordered `OSC 133;D` command completion.
2. The execution host confirms that the spawned shell owns the PTY foreground.
3. At the first proven snapshot boundary, the host normalizes its own stale TUI modes once and publishes optional, output-sequence-bound `terminalOwner: 'shell'` plus normal-buffer state.
4. Reveal and reattach apply focused shell-safe grounding only with that proof.
5. New command, alternate-screen, mouse, or Kitty-keyboard mode bytes, lifecycle replacement, disposal, or a newer output sequence revoke proof.
6. Snapshot settlement follows only candidates present at its boundary, so later output cannot starve attach.

Ordinary output and live-TUI frames perform zero ownership inspections. A poisoned mode episode performs one inspection, not one after every later plain command. Direct SSH exposes no authoritative confirmation API, so it fails closed immediately to incumbent behavior instead of adding a network wait or guessing from relay state.

## Deterministic reproduction

`tests/e2e/terminal-hidden-child-tui-kill-mode-reset.spec.ts` runs the same journey for normal exit and cleanup-free SIGKILL:

- enter alternate screen; enable any-event/SGR mouse and hide the cursor;
- render a distinctive TUI frame and hide its tab;
- terminate the child while its parent shell survives;
- retain stale agent-working metadata, reveal, type a fixed shell marker, and send real pointer input;
- assert visible output, renderer and host normal-buffer/non-mouse state, host ownership metadata, exact PTY writes with no mouse report, ordered revocation, and unrelated-pane survival.

With only the focused host-proven recovery disabled, the normal-exit case retains any-event mouse mode and the SIGKILL case retains alternate screen plus mouse mode; both fail. The candidate passes both.

## Mixed-version behavior

| Client | Host | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| old | old | Incumbent behavior |
| new | old | Optional fields absent; incumbent behavior |
| old | new | Host-normalized snapshots recover when proof succeeds; the optional owner field is ignored |
| new | new | Host normalization plus focused renderer grounding with sequence-bound proof |

The wire change is optional-field compatible. The existing `alternateScreen` field now carries the normalized host truth after proof, so old clients can benefit from a new host without understanding `terminalOwner`. Local daemon and paired runtime paths use the shared proof. Direct SSH intentionally retains incumbent behavior. Mobile layout re-streams do not publish ownership on the unrelated layout sequence.

## Validation

- Reliability gate: 14 files, 1,564 passed, 3 existing skips.
- Mixed-version terminal wire: 5/5 passed, including old client/new host and new client/old host.
- Typecheck and changed-code quality: passed; zero new findings across 74 changed files.
- Electron E2E build: passed.
- Electron normal-exit and SIGKILL journeys: 2/2 passed in 31.3s.
- Earlier real-app journeys: 4/4 passed after correcting proof precedence.
- Local proof timing, 30 samples: median 84.6ms, p95 103.7ms, max 124.5ms; this runs after the ordered completion candidate, not during normal reveal/typing/output.
- Deterministic count coverage proves one inspection per poisoned episode and bounded snapshot settlement.
- Three independent architecture, product, and adversarial/performance reviews completed; validated findings were incorporated and the follow-up was re-reviewed.

## Risks and gaps

- Physical Windows ConPTY, WSL, and a full live paired headed/headless pointer journey remain evidence gaps. Every unproved path fails closed to incumbent behavior.
- Direct SSH does not receive this recovery until it gains an execution-host-owned confirmation primitive; it adds no new delay or regression here.
- A false-negative proof misses recovery and preserves today's behavior. Proof is deliberately conservative to avoid resetting a live or stopped/resumable TUI.
- A new host can normalize a proven stale snapshot for an old client. This intentionally improves that mixed-version row but broadens the effect of a host false positive; fresh process ownership, ordered modes, and revocation are the safety gates.
- The host performs one coalesced process inspection only after the relevant ordered completion boundary. No steady-state polling, timer, repeated post-recovery scans, or renderer churn was added.

No issue, message, deployment, or merge action was performed. This PR is not merged.

body:
## Summary

Puts a front end on the moderation backend from #46 — and gives it the per-person identity it was designed around.

**The identity problem.** The moderation service records *who* took each action, with roles looked up per-account. But `/admin` logged in with a single shared env-var credential, so there was nobody to attribute actions to. Two sign-in paths now:

- **Staff sign-in** — moderators and administrators sign in at `/admin/login` with their own game account username and password. Actions are attributed to them by name.
- **Server operator** — the existing shared credential still works and signs in as "server operator" with full admin authority. This is the bootstrap path: use it once to grant the first role, then let people use their own accounts. Its actions are audited as a `NULL` actor, the same convention `player_activity` already uses for system entries.

Migration 30 rebuilds `moderation_actions` so `actor_user_id` accepts that `NULL`, preserving existing rows and the index.

**The panel.** Each player record gains a Moderation section showing role, account state and suspension expiry, with warn / suspend / ban / restore controls (a reason is required), plus an immutable **Moderation history** listing actor, reason, state transition and timestamp. Administrators additionally get an "Assign role" control. The dashboard gains Role and Status columns and shows who is signed in.

**Role gating.** Moderators can warn, suspend and restore. Banning, role changes, granting items and forcing jail/hospital stay with administrators and the operator — enforced at the route (`admin_role_required`) *and* independently in the service layer, and hidden from the UI so moderators aren't shown buttons that would fail.

## Notes for review

- **Stale sessions fail closed.** An `/admin` session opened before this change has `admin_authenticated` but no role or actor. Rather than guess who is holding it — which would silently grant operator authority — it is cleared and must sign in again. Covered by a test.
- Staff sign-in returns one generic error for every failure (unknown account, wrong password, insufficient role, suspended/banned), so it never reveals which check failed. Banned and suspended accounts cannot reach operations.
- `deployment/README.md` documents both sign-in paths and how to grant the first role.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — 212 tests pass (20 new in `tests/production/test_moderation_panel.py`, driving the real Flask routes rather than the service layer)
- [x] `tests/auth/*.py` verified individually (not part of automated discovery) — all pass

- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — how to run it, how to check it, how to open a PR, and what good looks like in this repo.
- **`.github/pull_request_template.md`** — what changed, why, and what the review said and what I did about it.

## Why

Two reasons, and the first one is not optional.

**This is the first pull request in this repository that contains work.** Everything before it went straight to `main`, which the hackathon rules say does not count as reviewed work. That is fixed from here: every substantive change goes through a branch, a Qodo review, a human reviewer, and a merge.

**"Clone, understand, extend" needs the third verb.** A stranger can already clone this and run it. Extending it meant reading `packages/contract` and inferring the conventions. Now there is a page that states them.

While writing the extension guide I ran the experiment instead of assuming the answer, and it turned up something worth recording. Adding a class to `CHANGE_CLASSES` makes every `Record<ChangeClass, …>` a compile error, so the compiler hands you a to-do list:

```
dossier.ts(40,14): error TS2741: Property 'MODEL_DEPLOY' is missing …
resolve.ts(150,14): error TS2741: Property 'MODEL_DEPLOY' is missing …
```

But it names **two** of the three steps, not three. `Policy.classes` is a `Partial<Record<…>>`, so an unlisted class silently inherits `defaults` — `ANY` certificate, `quorum: 1`, no ceilings. That is a reasonable floor and a bad answer for anything genuinely irreversible. The guide now says to set the policy deliberately and explains what happens if you do not.

## What the review said, and what I did about it

_To be filled in after Qodo has run on this PR._

author: amitabhainarunachala
body:
## Why

The merge system has been fully deadlocked since 2026-08-19, by two stacked causes this PR fixes together:

**Layer 1 — pytest contract tests vs git 2.55 (wedged the queue).** The GitHub runner image (ubuntu24/20260816.277) upgraded git to 2.55.0 mid-day 2026-08-19. The pristine-checkout contract tests clone the repo, `git commit` a snapshot, fingerprint every file including `.git/**`, run a make target, and assert bit-identical trees — and on git ≥ 2.55 that setup commit forks a **detached background maintenance process** that writes `.git/objects/info/commit-graphs/*` into the clone, inside the measured window. Every merge-queue pytest run since 2026-08-19T17:54Z has failed the same 10 tests regardless of PR — 11 consecutive queue failures across 8 different PRs through 2026-08-25T05:43Z (runs 32284322706, 32322581241, 32323816139, 32324908749, 32326028358, 32327319441, 32328628319, and today 32812461484, 32812501674, 32812533927, 32812608096); main frozen at `abc8bd35` for five days. Proof the writer is the harness and not any target: the failure fires even in `test_make_rejects_cache_symlink_escape_before_prerequisites`, where make exits before doing anything (queue run 32323816139 artifact `pytest-results-3.11`: `10 failed, 16160 passed`; every failure diff contains only `commit-graphs` paths). The failure is **queue-context-specific**: PR-event full-suite runs pass on the same image (e.g. run 32811182006, 2026-08-25), a light 2-test control on the diag branch also passes unfixed (run 32813460784), and local git 2.43 never reproduces it — the background write only lands inside the measured window in the merge-queue checkout context. The fix removes the writer at its source in every context; the decisive cure-proof is this PR's own merge-queue run, the exact context that has failed 11/11.

**Layer 2 — DocOps TTL expiry (now blocks every PR too).** Because nothing could merge, the docops-reconcile lane's rolling counts PR (#1420, open since 2026-08-19T17:59Z) also couldn't land, so main's generated counts drifted 11 merges behind. Then `docs/docops/assertions.yaml` (`verified_at: 2026-08-09`, `ttl_days: 14`) **expired on 2026-08-23**, and TTL staleness is strict on every DocOps gate run — so the required gate fails on every PR and queue attempt on content-independent grounds (this PR's own first DocOps run 32813348495: the only FAIL was `staleness: DocOps assertions expired on 2026-08-23`; all count mismatches were correctly advisory WARNs).

## Surface area touched

- [x] `tests/...` — `tests/test_make_onboarding_contract.py`, `tests/test_orientation_graph.py`: the snapshot-setup helpers' own `git add`/`git commit` calls now pass `-c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0`, so no background writer is forked into the measured tree.
- [x] `docs/...` / DocOps — `docs/docops/AUTO_INVENTORY.md` + `docs/governance/SOVEREIGN_MANIFEST.md` regenerated via `check_docops_integrity.py --write-auto-sections --write-manifest-counts`; `docs/docops/assertions.yaml` `verified_at` re-stamped to 2026-08-25 **after** the strict gate passed against the refreshed values. Carrying generated count docs in a PR is normally the reconcile lane's job; this is outage recovery — the lane resumes ownership post-merge, and #1420 becomes obsolete.

### Worktree mirrors checked

No hot-path symbol touched.

## Interface mismatch impact

- [x] No new mismatch introduced

## Coherence Delta

- Organ touched: the titanium session-contract test harness + the DocOps counts/verification registry.
- Declared-vs-actual gap closed: (1) the tree-snapshot contract claimed to measure writes by the target under test but was measuring git's own background maintenance in queue runs since the 2.55 rollout, failing every merge attempt; (2) the SOVEREIGN_MANIFEST/AUTO_INVENTORY counts claimed values 11 merges stale, under an expired verification stamp. Both actuals now match declarations, mechanically re-verified.
- Proof that re-reads the map: contract strictness unchanged — any write by the target under test still fails snapshot equality; `check_docops_integrity.py` passes **strict** (not just advisory) on this tree; failure-mode evidence extracted from queue run 32323816139's `pytest-results-3.11` artifact via the one-shot workflow on branch `diag-pytest-name`.
- New drift introduced: none.

## Pre-flight check (collision prevention)

- [x] No BR-id cited
- [x] Overlap noted: #1420 (rolling reconcile) carries an older subset of the counts refresh; it should be closed after this merges.

## Verification

- [x] Manual smoke (describe below)

```
python3 -m ruff check tests/test_make_onboarding_contract.py tests/test_orientation_graph.py   # clean
python3 -m pytest tests/test_orientation_graph.py -q         # 18 passed
```

The pytest failure reproduces only in merge-queue runs on git ≥ 2.55 runners; this PR's own queue run is the decisive verification, in the exact context that failed 11/11 unfixed.

body:
## What
Follow-up to #28 (already merged/closed): the leadership status rename (`in_progress` → `enrolled`) landed in main before this fix, and the shared Convex deployment (`klt-cyber` project's **prod** deployment — currently doubling as staging, see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §Why) still has a `leadershipProgress` row with the old `in_progress` value, so the post-merge `convex deploy` in `deploy-staging.yml` fails schema validation.

## Why
Convex schema pushes validate every existing document. You can't tighten a literal union in the same deploy that still has non-conforming data — needs the widen → migrate → re-tighten sequence.

## How
- Widened `leadershipProgress.status` back to a 3-literal union (`in_progress | enrolled | completed`) as a transitional state.
- Added `convex/leadershipMigration.ts` — `migrateLeadershipStatus` (internal mutation, idempotent) rewrites any `in_progress` row to `enrolled`; `verifyLeadershipMigration` (internal query) confirms none remain. Mirrors the existing `departmentMigration.ts` pattern already in this codebase for the same kind of breaking-schema situation.
- `submitProfile`'s `leadershipStatusValidator` (what new submissions can write) was never widened — only `enrolled`/`completed` are accepted going forward, so no new row can reintroduce the legacy value.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit` clean across `convex`, `apps/mobile`, `apps/admin`.

## Deploy steps after this merges
1. This merge triggers `deploy-staging.yml` → `convex deploy` against the shared deployment; should now succeed (schema is backward compatible again).
2. Run the migration against that same deployment from a workstation with deploy access:
   ```
   pnpm exec convex run leadershipMigration:migrateLeadershipStatus --prod
   pnpm exec convex run leadershipMigration:verifyLeadershipMigration --prod   # expect { staleCount: 0 }
   ```
3. Follow-up PR: drop the `in_progress` literal from `schema.ts` (and the matching notes in `memberProfiles.ts`/`DATA_MODEL.md`) once verified clean, and redeploy.

## Scope

This PR is intentionally limited to typed, fire-and-forget calls from the four existing public client surfaces into the already-protected T084 consent-aware analytics contract.

- successful public issue view
- successful public article view
- successful first-page search submission result
- article share start

The universal runtime starts with `unknown` consent and no sink, so these calls emit nothing externally and cannot block the user interaction. Search passes only a numeric Unicode code-point count into the analytics runtime; no raw query/title/slug/URL enters an event.

author: gosselinkillianpro-source
body:
## 1. Le bouton « Je prends »

Il ne montrait rien. Trois causes, toutes corrigées :

| Cause | Effet | Correctif |
|---|---|---|
| Affiché seulement si `contactId && !investorId` | Invisible pour les inscrits ayant un compte SAH — la majorité de ceux qu'on appelle | Affiché pour tout inscrit |
| Aucun `router.refresh()` après succès | L'action passait en base, l'écran ne bougeait pas | Rafraîchissement systématique |
| Aucun affichage du propriétaire | Rien ne prouvait que le verrou existait | « Libérer » si la fiche est à moi, « suivi par X » si elle est à un collègue |

Renommé « Je prends » (cohérent avec la file d'appels), + action `releaseWebinarContact` pour libérer (un admin peut débloquer une fiche coincée sur un closer absent).

## 2. Le tableau de suivi — `/webinaires/suivi`

**Pris en charge → Appelé → Intéressé → Compte finalisé → A investi**, plus **Perdu** en sortie.

Une carte par **personne**, pas par inscription : quelqu'un inscrit à deux webinaires n'apparaît qu'une fois, rattaché au dernier live.

**La carte naît toute seule** — au clic « Je prends », ou dès qu'un appel est enregistré. Un appel qui finit en « profil incompatible » ou « mauvais numéro » range la carte dans Perdu.

**L'automatisme ne fait qu'avancer.** Un closer qui a classé quelqu'un « Intéressé » ne le voit pas retomber dans « Appelé » au second appel ; une carte tranchée « A investi » ou « Perdu » par un humain n'est plus touchée par aucun automatisme. Le déplacement à la main, lui, fait autorité dans les deux sens — c'est le closer qui a eu la personne au téléphone.

**Déplacement** : glisser-déposer natif (zéro dépendance ajoutée) + un sélecteur « déplacer vers » sur chaque carte, parce que le drag seul exclut le clavier et le mobile. Optimiste : la carte bouge tout de suite, le serveur suit.

**Sur la carte** : téléphone cliquable, capacité déclarée, présence live, KYC, montant souscrit depuis le webinaire, dernier appel et son résultat, rappel programmé (en rouge s'il est en retard), closer propriétaire. Une carte dont la personne a déjà souscrit se signale en vert : *« à passer en A investi »*.

Filtre par webinaire en haut de page, accessible aussi depuis chaque webinaire (« Tableau de suivi »).

## 3. Sous le capot

- **Migration 0019** — enum `contact_stage` + 3 colonnes sur `rdv_contacts`. ⚠️ **Déjà appliquée sur la base** (colonnes nullables, purement additives : l'ancien code tourne sans problème avec).
- Elle **rétro-alimente** le tableau depuis le travail déjà fait : 7 cartes au démarrage (6 appels déjà loggés, 1 fiche déjà prise) plutôt qu'un écran vide.
- **Pont investisseur → fiche contact** (`contactIdForInvestor`) : le suivi vit sur `rdv_contacts`, l'écran d'un webinaire cible un `investor_id`. Sans ce pont, tout le travail sur les gens ayant un compte SAH ne créait aucune carte.
- Règle de progression isolée dans un **module pur testé** (`src/lib/webinars/pipeline.ts`).

## Test plan

- [x] 14 tests unitaires sur la règle de progression (non-recul, carte tranchée intouchable, résultats d'appel qui ferment la ligne) — `tests/unit/webinar-pipeline.test.ts`
- [x] Flux complet rejoué sur la base réelle : prise en charge d'un inscrit **relié à SAH** (le cas qui ne marchait pas) → carte créée en « Pris en charge » ; pont investisseur → contact OK ; 8 cartes visibles par la requête du kanban. État restauré après le test.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm test:run` (78 tests) · `pnpm build` verts
- [x] `pnpm biome check src tests` : 4 erreurs a11y, toutes préexistantes sur `main` (`metric-info.tsx`, `mobile-nav.tsx`), aucune dans les fichiers touchés
- [ ] **Rendu non vérifié à l'écran** : le serveur de dev demande une connexion, je ne saisis pas de mot de passe. La logique est vérifiée en base, le build compile la route.

author: roji
body:
Managed out-of-process SDK connections currently launch the root Copilot SEA directly. The runtime now provides a dedicated `copilot-runtime` executable that loads the adjacent `runtime.node`, so SDK-managed subprocess connections should use that coherent wrapper/addon pair while preserving explicit external server and in-process modes.

## What changed

- Update Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java managed launch paths to resolve and spawn `copilot-runtime` (`copilot-runtime.exe` on Windows).
- Materialize and validate the wrapper beside `runtime.node`, retaining the root `copilot` executable only for residual and in-process compatibility.
- Preserve auxiliary runtime assets such as ripgrep, tgrep, built-in definitions, skills, and future package additions. Each SDK keeps unknown npm package entries by default while excluding known CLI/UI-only content.
- Preserve explicit CLI path, process, and server URL overrides without silently falling back to the SEA when managed wrapper artifacts are incomplete.
- Extend language-specific packaging, extraction, permissions, cache, and test coverage for the coherent runtime distribution.
- Fix a Python subprocess stderr-reader race and Java MCP stdio `cwd` serialization issue discovered during end-to-end validation.

## Validation

Validated all six SDKs against the immutable same-tip runtime release candidate `adce886fd1` across supported root SEA, in-process, and hostless wrapper transports. The final focused cache/resume gates and supported full-suite cells passed with exact artifact hash checks and no leaked runtime processes.

The auxiliary-asset follow-up adds focused staging, cache-migration, filtering, permission, and path-safety tests in all six SDKs. A real Node hostless-wrapper integration test also confirms built-in grep completes successfully through the staged ripgrep binary.

Known non-runtime exclusions remain documented from validation: hostless Node extension/factory lifecycle behavior (including the corresponding .NET extension tests), the Go invalid-model fixture, the Java literal-YAML fixture and order-dependent socket-helper contamination, and Rust forced-environment unit-test contamination.

## Review notes

This is a draft while the runtime platform packages and Java classifier publication complete. The production platform package is treated as the runtime distribution source: the root `copilot[.exe]`, selected `prebuilds/<platform>/runtime.node` and `copilot-runtime[.exe]`, and retained package-relative runtime assets are staged as one coherent version. Mixed or incomplete artifact sets are rejected.

author: gabepsilva
body:
#78 was merged with zero reviews. This is that review, plus the fixes.

Every finding below is reproduced against the merged commit `a488fdd`, and every fix ships with a regression test proven to fail without it (`make verify-regression`).

---

## 1. Teardown could not remove a registry it could not read

`main()` constructed an `Orchestrator` — whose constructor parses the state file — before dispatching the verb. `delete --team T` is the one command whose job is to delete that file, so a registry that will not parse made the team unrecoverable except by hand.

Against `a488fdd`:

```
$ printf 'not json' > "$TEAMS/issue-73/agents/orchestrator_state.json"
$ orchestrator delete --team issue-73
.../agents/orchestrator_state.json is not valid JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
exit=1
$ ls "$TEAMS/issue-73/agents"
orchestrator_state.json  orchestrator_state.json.lock      # removed nothing

$ echo '{"owen": {"backend": "retired-backend", "session_id": null}}' > .../orchestrator_state.json
$ orchestrator delete --team issue-73
Unknown backend 'retired-backend'. Available backends: claude, codex, grok, opencode
exit=1
```

The second case is the realistic one: a state file written by a build that had a backend this one does not. `rm -rf` was the only way out — which is precisely what teardown exists to spare the caller.

**Fix.** Teardown dispatches inside the team lock but ahead of `Orchestrator()`, and no longer routes through `VERBS`/`cmd_delete`. Everything else about it is unchanged: still `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB`, still scoped to `agents/`, still leaves `.lock` and `worktree/` alone.

Verified end-to-end on the corrupted team above:

```
$ orchestrator delete --team issue-73
deleted team 'issue-73'
exit=0
$ find "$TEAMS/issue-73" -maxdepth 1
.../issue-73  .../issue-73/.lock  .../issue-73/worktree
$ git worktree list          # no 'prunable'
```

## 2. `except BlockingIOError` claimed every incidental one for the team lock

The handler wrapped the whole dispatch — `Orchestrator()`, the turn, and the `print` of the reply — not just the lock acquisition. Only the acquisition can mean "the team is busy".

Against `a488fdd`, a **teamless** `talk` whose reply is written to a stdout someone left `O_NONBLOCK`:

```
created agent 'a' backend=big
team 'None' is in use by another command; try again once it finishes
exit code: 1
```

A real `BlockingIOError` from `print(result.reply)`, reported as a lock the caller never took, exit 1, original error discarded. This is the failure mode `OrchestratorError`'s own docstring already warns about:

> Catching the builtins around the whole dispatch swallowed any incidental one raised inside a backend too, and printed it as a bare one-word line with no traceback — turning a real bug into a mystery.

**Fix.** A `_team_locked(path, team, mode)` wrapper converts `BlockingIOError` to a new `TeamBusyError(OrchestratorError)` around `enter_context(_flock(...))` and nothing else. A genuinely lost race produces the identical message and exit 1 (the existing lock-race test passes untouched, and the live two-process race was re-run). Anything else now surfaces as itself:

```
  File "orchestrator/__init__.py", line 588, in cmd_talk
    print(result.reply)
BlockingIOError: [Errno 11] write could not complete without blocking
```

The writer-fairness rationale for `LOCK_NB` moved into `_team_locked`'s docstring, where the flag now lives.

## 3. `docs/configuration.md` still contradicts `--team`

#78 changed README.md's *"The entire registry lives in one JSON file"* to *"Without `--team`, …"* — and left the identical sentence in `docs/configuration.md:53`, a file it edited in the same commit. Fixed the same way.

## 4. #78 routed a latent logging leak into the mutation gate

#78 added `tests/test_cli_surface.py` to `pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection` (`pyproject.toml:125`). That gate runs its selection serially in one process (`-n0`), so `test_cli_surface.py:258-261`'s `main(["-v", …])` / `-vv` calls now share a process with `test_backends.py`'s `_messages(caplog) == []` assertions. `_configure_logging` raises the `orchestrator`/`backends` logger levels by name and nothing ever lowers them, so whether the gate passes depends on the order `pytest-randomly` picked:

```
$ uv run pytest -q -n0 -p no:randomly \
    tests/test_teams.py tests/test_cli_surface.py tests/test_backends.py
FAILED tests/test_backends.py::TestOrchestrator::test_validated_opencode_turn_warns_once_about_cli_schema_enforcement
FAILED tests/test_backends.py::TestOrchestrator::test_schema_warning_is_absent_without_schema_or_for_enforcing_backend
2 failed, 363 passed
```

Same result on `a488fdd`, and on `3656f2a` for the two files alone — the leak predates #78, but before #78 the leaker was not in any gate's selection. A mutation gate that passes on the seed is a mutation score earned by luck.

**Fix.** A new `tests/conftest.py` with one autouse fixture that saves and restores `orchestrator.OWN_LOGGERS`' levels around every test. The subset above now passes.

---

## Regression evidence

Per `AGENTS.md`, each fix has a test that fails without it. With `orchestrator/__init__.py` reverted to `a488fdd`:

```
FAILED tests/test_teams.py::test_teardown_removes_a_registry_it_cannot_parse[invalid json-not json]
FAILED tests/test_teams.py::test_teardown_removes_a_registry_it_cannot_parse[unknown backend-...]
FAILED tests/test_teams.py::test_an_incidental_blocking_io_error_is_not_a_busy_team[team_argv0]
FAILED tests/test_teams.py::test_an_incidental_blocking_io_error_is_not_a_busy_team[team_argv1]
4 failed
```

All four pass with it. Finding 4's evidence is the subset command above, red without `tests/conftest.py` and green with it.

## What the review checked and found correct

Not everything was broken — for the record, re-verified against the merged code on a scratch clone:

- V1–V5 all exit 2 and leave the filesystem exactly as they found it, including `a/b`, `..`, `.` and `""`, and `--team` alongside an explicit `AGENTS_ARMY_HOME` / `AGENTS_ARMY_STATE_FILE`.
- `WORKDIR` reaches the backend as the team's worktree; `STATE_FILE` and `SKILLS_DIR` resolve under the team root; an explicit `AGENTS_ARMY_SKILLS` still wins.
- Two teams with the same agent name keep independent registries and session ids.
- Teardown leaves `worktree/` and its git metadata intact — `git worktree list` reports nothing `prunable`.
- A live two-process teardown-versus-`LOCK_SH` race refuses with exit 1 and removes nothing.
- Teamless behavior is byte-identical.
- `pyproject.toml` change: none in this PR (#78's addition of the two test files to the mutation selection is kept — finding 4 fixes the leak it exposed rather than narrowing the selection back).

## How to verify

```sh
uv sync --locked --all-groups
make ci
```

`make ci` passes here: 764 tests, mutation score **98.9%** (2260 killed / 2286, floor 98.0%), all gates green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01RyS58uM68kPMxL3csAmHsk

author: damirn
body:
Syncs the Telnyx spandsp fork with upstream [`v3.1.1`](https://github.com/freeswitch/spandsp/releases/tag/v3.1.1) (`8f1e1646bd`).

Required by [TELCORE-379](https://linear.app/telnyx/issue/TELCORE-379/sync-freeswitch-fork-with-upstream-v1112): FreeSWITCH v1.11.2 raises its configure floor to `spandsp >= 3.1.1` (upstream `1d77a57750`) and this fork sat at `3.0.0`, so `./configure` fails outright on the FreeSWITCH sync branch until this lands.

Tracked in [TELCORE-410](https://linear.app/telnyx/issue/TELCORE-410/sync-spandsp-fork-with-upstream-v311), which carries the full per-conflict write-up.

## Scope

Merge base `e08c74d`. The fork carried 7 commits of its own; upstream contributed 66 (52 non-merge) across 300 files — years of development including V.150.1/SPRT, SSLFax, the Windows port, the Godard TED rework and a T.38 FTT-handling fix.

## Conflicts — 2, both resolved in favour of the Telnyx code

Both are in the fax decode path hardened by TEL-6678 (`abd318c`), and both have the same shape: **upstream v3.1.1 made no functional change to the conflicted function** — its only edit was adding `/*endif*/` block-comment markers as part of a house-style sweep over the file.

**`src/t4_rx.c` — `tiff_row_write_handler()`**

Taking the upstream side would have reverted TEL-6678's growth-overflow guard back to the unchecked `100*len`. Worse, the `span_realloc` that assigns `t` lives inside the Telnyx side of the hunk while the shared trailing context still reads `s->tiff.image_buffer = t;` — so an upstream-side resolution compiles cleanly and then assigns an **uninitialised pointer**.

**`src/t4_t6_decode.c` — `t4_t6_decode_restart()`**

TEL-6678 reordered the two `span_realloc` calls so both allocations succeed before any state is updated (via a second local `bufptr2`); the base code assigned `s->cur_runs` between them, leaving state half-updated if the second failed. Taking upstream would have reintroduced that path.

In both cases the Telnyx logic is kept verbatim, with upstream's `/*endif*/` markers added so the style matches the rest of the file and future merges stay quiet.

## Telnyx changes verified to survive

| Commit | Change | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `abd318c` | TEL-6678 — overflow guards in `t4_rx.c` + `t4_t6_decode.c` | present, both conflicts above |
| `b9dd656` | ENGDESK-32040 — queuing modulation during `HDLC_SIG_END` | auto-merged into `src/t38_gateway.c` |
| `6d36810` | TEL-4718 — earlier upstream sync | subsumed |

## Verification

`./autogen.sh && ./configure && make -C src` completes clean. `spandsp.pc` reports `Version: 3.1.1`, which satisfies the FreeSWITCH v1.11.2 floor.

## Reviewer notes

**ABI bump 3 → 4.** `SPANDSP_LT_CURRENT` goes 3 → 4, so the library is now `libspandsp.so.4` (build emits `libspandsp.so.4.0.0`). Upstream renamed the Debian packaging to match (`libspandsp3-dev` → `libspandsp4-dev`, same for runtime and doc). Everything downstream must be **rebuilt**, and anything *naming* `libspandsp3` must be **updated** — `fs_docker_deps` → `freeswitch_docker_base` → `telnyx_b2bua_builder`.

**Upstream CI removed** (second commit). The merge brought in 13 new `.github/` files (Debian bullseye/bookworm/trixie Dockerfiles, `build-dispatch.yml`, `build.yml.disabled`, `scan-build.yml`, `windows.yml`). The fork has never carried a `.github/` tree — not at the fork HEAD (`abd318c`) and not at the merge base (`e08c74d`) — so these arrived without conflict simply because there was nothing on our side to collide with. They are dropped in `70daedd`, matching the fork policy applied to the FreeSWITCH fork in `b707240174`: `.github/` carries Telnyx automation only.

`.drone.yml` is deliberately **not** reverted. The fork never customised it — it is byte-identical to the merge base — so upstream's `pull: true` → `pull: always` change and the re-signed hmac is a clean take, not a Telnyx version being overwritten.

**Where to aim fax regression testing.** Upstream `227b312` (T.38 gateway FTT handling) and `7b0b8cf` (T.38 packetisation-time rework) both land in `t38_gateway.c` / `t38_core.c` — the same file ENGDESK-32040 patches. That plus the two `t4_*` decode paths is the surface most likely to regress.

author: developer1-cybersmith
body:
## Summary

Extends the S3-1 eval harness with real-world (non-synthetic) PDF coverage, and fixes every real defect that coverage and the live 20-PDF run surfaced — each one root-caused against real evidence (Langfuse traces, reproduced pure-function output, or a genuine RED-GREEN test) and live-verified against real providers, not just unit tests.

- **D126** — restored real credentials before a live eval run (a stale test override was silently disabling the real path).
- **D127** — real-world PDF fixture generator + opt-in live tier, so the eval harness isn't 100% synthetic/computer-generated PDFs anymore (scans, messy layouts, real documents).
- **D128** — low-confidence OCR now explicitly flagged instead of silently accepted.
- **D129** — registered (not fixed here, deferred to Sprint 4): concurrent multi-user testing gap.
- **D130** — root-caused and fixed the eval harness's multi-hour runtime: long fixtures had no real chapter structure, so every one fell through to the R5 whole-document fallback; also added live progress visibility (`progress.jsonl`) so a multi-hour run is observable from the outside.
- **D131** — registered (deferred, paired with D129): unbounded chapter size is a real-student risk too.
- **D132** — the actual dominant cost once D130 was fixed: `image_generator_node` generated slide images one at a time (86-95% of every real lesson's time, measured across 6 real lessons via Langfuse). Fixed with bounded concurrent fan-out (`asyncio.Semaphore` + `asyncio.gather`); an adversarial-review pass caught a real blocking-call bug (Storage upload was still sync) before it shipped. Live-verified: 2.3x speedup on one fixture, then cross-category confirmed (1.83x-2.41x) against real Langfuse traces matching the predicted concurrency formula within 1-6%.
- **D133** — `slide_generator_node` was hard-failing when the LLM appended an inferred title to an otherwise-perfectly-copied `segment_id` (4/20 real failures in the completed live run). Applied the same retry-on-mismatch pattern already proven for the identical problem in `lesson_planner_node` (D77). Live-verified: all 4 previously-failing fixtures now pass; the retry was observed firing on real production data, confirmed against the real Langfuse trace.
- **D134** — `extract_text_only()` crashed with `AttributeError` on ANY real PDF with a table of contents. The pre-existing code (D58/D63) called `item.get_dest()`/`item.get_title()` — methods that do not exist on `pypdfium2.PdfOutlineItem` in the project's pinned `pypdfium2==4.30.0` (`uv.lock`). Confirmed by installing that exact version and inspecting it: only plain `.page_index`/`.title` attributes exist. Had been invisible because (a) no prior fixture ever produced a PDF with a real bookmark/TOC, and (b) local dev venvs had silently drifted to 5.x where the method-based API is real. A real production book would hit this on essentially every upload with an outline — rated **High** severity. Fixed by replacing the nonexistent method calls with the real 4.30.0 attribute access; RED-GREEN verified under the correctly-pinned version.
- **D135** — CI's `api` job had never installed `tesseract`, so the OCR fallback path (CLAUDE.md's documented "Tesseract (in-container)" stack) had never once run in CI on any PR. Found only because this PR's new real-world OCR tests (`test_real_world_extraction.py`) are the first to require the binary. Fixed by adding an `Install tesseract` step to the `api` job, mirroring the existing `postgresql-client` pattern in the migration job.

Every fix followed the same discipline: root cause confirmed with real evidence (not guessed), RED-GREEN test verification where applicable, full regression suite re-run independently, and live re-verification against real AI providers before calling it closed. author: luigisiu
body:
## Why

Sharing the app meant telling people to build it from source. `build.sh` signs ad-hoc, which is fine on the machine that built it and rejected on every other Mac — Gatekeeper shows the "Apple could not verify this app is free of malware" dialog and the only workaround is right-click → Open.

Now that there's a Developer ID certificate on the account, releases can be signed and notarised properly, so the app opens with a double click like any other download.

## What's here

**`mac-app/release.sh`** — build → sign → notarise → staple → zip, producing `build/dist/Glowgrid-<version>.zip` ready to attach to a GitHub release.

It's a separate script rather than a flag on `build.sh` on purpose. Release signing needs the network, takes minutes instead of seconds, and burns a notarisation submission every run. None of that belongs in the loop you run fifty times a day, so `build.sh` keeps its instant ad-hoc signature and this script reuses it for the compile before replacing the signature.

**`mac-app/Glowgrid.entitlements`** — the hardened runtime blocks protected resources unless they're declared, so Bluetooth and calendar are listed. Camera and microphone deliberately are not: the app reads whether those devices are *in use* via CoreAudio and CoreMediaIO and never opens a stream, so requesting capture permission would put a recording indicator in the menu bar for a capability it doesn't want.

## Two traps worth calling out

Both of these produce something that passes every local check and fails for users:

- **The distributable zip is built after stapling.** The notarisation ticket lives inside the bundle. Zip before stapling and you ship an app that macOS still has to phone home about — so anyone offline, or anyone hitting an Apple outage, gets the malware warning on a perfectly good app.
- **`notarytool` exits 0 when Apple *rejects* your app**, because the round trip itself succeeded. The script reads the verdict out of the JSON instead of trusting `$?`, and on rejection it fetches and prints Apple's log — which names the offending binary and the reason. Without it you're guessing.

## Verified

```
flags=0x10000(runtime)
Authority=Developer ID Application: … (M7SS3X57KG)
Authority=Developer ID Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
Timestamp=25 Aug 2026 at 11:26:14
```

Both entitlements embedded, `codesign --verify --strict` clean, and the hardened-runtime build launches without crashing on CoreBluetooth init. `spctl` currently reports `source=Unnotarized Developer ID`, which is the expected state until a notarisation run happens.

**Notarisation verified.** A full `./release.sh` run completed: Apple accepted the submission, the ticket stapled, and `spctl` now reports `accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID`.

Checked the way a downloader actually receives it — unzipped the artifact, marked it quarantined as Safari would, and it passes both `xcrun stapler validate` (so the ticket survived the zip round trip and works offline) and Gatekeeper. Universal binary confirmed as `x86_64 arm64`. The zip is 1.1 MB.

## Docs

The "Sharing it with someone else" section no longer says "build it yourself". It now covers the signed download, the release process, why three separate mechanisms are involved, and the two non-obvious bits: the secure timestamp is what keeps the app launching after the certificate expires, and changing signing identity resets permission grants so the first launch re-prompts for Bluetooth.

author: mpscholten
body:
## Summary

- cache stable transcript blocks in fixed groups of 32
- leave the growing final chunk and interactive/animated chunks uncached
- isolate transcript chunking and cache eligibility in `Agent.CLI.TUI.Transcript`
- add focused cache-policy tests and an optimized retained-redraw benchmark
- regenerate the checked-in Nix package expression

## Why

Brick must lay out the complete child of a vertical viewport to determine its scroll range. The transcript already cached individual completed blocks, which avoided repeated Markdown parsing, but every scrolling redraw still traversed and combined one image per retained block. That work grows linearly with long-running sessions.

The new outer cache reduces stable history to roughly one cached image per 32 blocks. Only full chunks are cached because Brick retains cache entries until invalidation; caching the growing final chunk with a changing endpoint would retain obsolete large images. Chunks containing expanded, selected, hovered, streaming, running, retrying, or flashing content bypass the outer cache.

The pure chunking and eligibility policy lives in `Agent.CLI.TUI.Transcript`; `Agent.CLI.TUI.App` retains only renderer-specific drawing and interaction-state assembly.

## Benchmark

Optimized `-O2` benchmark, 25 retained redraws per sample, median of 9 samples, `+RTS -T`:

| Workload | Per-block cache | Chunk cache | Allocation before | Allocation after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 10,000 blocks, 2 body lines | 513.3 ms | 10.5 ms | 1,059,965,960 B | 70,212,176 B |
| 5,000 blocks, 8 body lines | 246.5 ms | 9.9 ms | 554,401,520 B | 62,207,016 B |

Commands:

```sh
nix develop -c cabal build --offline agent-cli:bench:transcript-scrolling-bench
bin=$(nix develop -c cabal list-bin agent-cli:bench:transcript-scrolling-bench)
"$bin" per-block-cache 10000 2 9 +RTS -T
"$bin" chunk-cache 10000 2 9 +RTS -T
"$bin" per-block-cache 5000 8 9 +RTS -T
"$bin" chunk-cache 5000 8 9 +RTS -T
```

The benchmark isolates repeated retained redraw/layout work triggered by scrolling. A real resumed long session was also exercised with repeated PageUp/PageDown in tmux, including after the module extraction.

## Validation

- `cabal repl agent-cli:lib:agent-cli`: loaded `Agent.CLI.TUI.Transcript` and `Agent.CLI.TUI.App`
- `nix develop -c cabal test --offline agent-cli:agent-cli-test --test-option=--match --test-option=fullscreen`
  - 44 examples passed
  - 300 generated-frame property cases passed
  - 100 incremental-redraw property cases passed
  - 5 focused transcript cache-policy examples passed
- optimized benchmark rebuilt and rerun after extraction
- tmux smoke test on a resumed long session passed without visual corruption

author: erik-sutton95
body:
## What & why

Fixes [#132](https://github.com/erik-sutton95/OpenPocketCine/issues/132). Turning LUT on in library playback felt like ~22–23 fps while LUT-off stayed buttery.

Preview LUT was already a GPU `CIColorCube` on `AVPlayerItemVideoOutput` (not `AVVideoComposition`). The hitch was the **pull clock**: display link preferred 24 / max 30 / min 15. 30p proxies pulled down, and the system could shed toward 15. LUT-off is `AVPlayerLayer` at the clip rate.

This PR:
- Pulls Metal-compatible 420 (not 32BGRA) and grades on `opv.playback-pull`
- Polls the display (24–120 Hz) and only bakes a **new** player frame
- Hides `AVPlayerLayer` once Metal owns LUT replace (live already hides VT); overlay keeps the identity layer
- Leaves export bake on `AVVideoComposition`
- Notes Android playback already matches live GLES (`PlaybackFeedView`); no TextureView `getBitmap`

Physical: iPhone 16 Pro Max, 720p proxy, official D-Log2 Rec.709 cube — LUT on now tracks clip rate.

## TestFlight notes

Replaced `ios/TestFlight/WhatToTest.en-US.txt`.

- **Fixes:** Turning LUT on in library playback no longer stutters. Play and scrub should feel like LUT off.
- **What to test:** Open a 720p clip, play with LUT off, then turn on the official D-Log2 cube. Play and scrub should stay as smooth as LUT off, and the picture should still grade.

## Checklist

- [x] `just check` — CI **CI gate** on this PR.

author: z6v6e6r
body:
## Current gate: STOP on post-branch main drift

After this branch was created from then-current `origin/main` (`a2f70dedf2dde35589a53cfede7ba1841e6370df`), `main` advanced 12 commits to `ce66c466e1aa3c9c2f82d8d792dfdb4d630d1384`. Those commits do not overlap the 11 implementation files, and GitHub reports the PR mergeable, but they introduced the exact-range secret scanner plus `.gitleaksignore`. The scanner reads `.gitleaksignore` from the PR head; this older head does not contain that later base file, so CI run `32832262493` fails with exit 128 before scanning. Per the task's drift stop condition, no rebase, merge-from-main, cherry-pick, scanner weakening, rerun, merge, or live workflow was performed. A separately authorized refresh onto current `main` is required before CI evidence can be considered current.

## Problem

The successful Timeweb AMD64 `publish` workflow produced immutable image evidence, but the canonical `release-manifest.json` and `release-manifest.sha256` depended on one or two later reconciliation dispatches. That split source, workflow, run identity, checksum custody, and canonical artifact creation across runs.

## What changes

- Makes one successful `.github/workflows/publish-timeweb-amd64-images.yaml` `publish` dispatch produce the complete canonical pair after all five image jobs and inventory validation succeed.
- Downloads only same-run/same-attempt evidence, verifies every producer checksum sidecar, resolves the approved application commit to its Git tree, and fails closed on missing, duplicate, mutable, mismatched, or substituted evidence.
- Defines explicit `PHUB_TIMEWEB_RELEASE_MANIFEST_V2` fields for application `gitCommit` and `gitTree`, publication workflow SHA/run ID/run attempt, and exactly five digest-pinned `linux/amd64` images with runtime digest, provenance, and SBOM evidence.
- Uploads exactly `release-manifest.json` and `release-manifest.sha256` as the same-run canonical artifact, while retaining the richer internal publication evidence artifact.
- Keeps the existing V1 schema as `deploy/timeweb/release-manifest.v1.schema.json`; historical V1 manifests remain readable, but V1 cannot satisfy V2 same-publication expectations.
- Removes canonical release production and prior-reconciliation chaining from the reconciliation workflow. Reconciliation remains optional, manual, read-only recovery evidence and cannot create a competing canonical manifest.

## Files

- Publication/reconciliation workflows: `.github/workflows/publish-timeweb-amd64-images.yaml`, `.github/workflows/reconcile-timeweb-amd64-publication.yaml`
- Contracts: `deploy/timeweb/release-manifest.schema.json`, `deploy/timeweb/release-manifest.v1.schema.json`, `scripts/timeweb-release-manifest-contract.js`
- Producer/validators: `scripts/build-timeweb-release-manifest.js`, `scripts/verify-timeweb-release-manifest.js`, `scripts/verify-timeweb-publication-evidence-checksums.js`
- Tests/runbook: `scripts/verify-timeweb-release-manifest.test.ts`, `scripts/timeweb-amd64-publication-workflow.test.ts`, `docs/runbooks/timeweb-amd64-image-publication.md`

## Validation

- Automatic PR CI run `32832262493`: `quality`, `dependency-security`, and all five AMD64 `docker-build` jobs passed. `secret-scan` failed before scanning because the post-branch base workflow executes `git show "$HEAD_SHA:.gitleaksignore"`, while that file exists only in the 12 newer `main` commits; the log reports `fatal: path '.gitleaksignore' exists on disk, but not in 'd38ef1b...'`.
- Focused Timeweb contract/workflow tests: 27/27 passed.
- `npm run format:check`: passed.
- `npm run lint`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm run build`: passed.
- `npm run runtime:imports`: passed after build completed.
- `npm run contracts:lint`: passed with the repository's six existing OpenAPI warnings.
- Broad Vitest run excluding the Docker-only runtime-secret test: 409 files / 2952 tests passed; three unrelated operational tests timed out and the Timeweb suite hit sandbox `listen EPERM`. The Timeweb suite passes separately with loopback permission.
- Full `npm run check`: stopped at the existing Docker parser test because the local Docker daemon is unavailable; build/runtime imports were run separately and passed.
- Independent release, security, fail-closed workflow, and test-gap reviews: PASS, no remaining actionable P0-P3 findings.

## Compatibility and safety

- No OpenAPI, database schema, runtime service, deploy input, image tag, or production data contract is changed.
- The canonical artifact remains non-authorizing; publication success does not authorize deploy, VPS provisioning, or database mutation.
- No workflow dispatch, image publication, reconciliation run, deployment, migration, runtime mutation, or live data operation was performed for this PR.

## Remaining live evidence

After merge authorization, the separate operational gate remains: merge exact reviewed head, dispatch one exact `publish` run, verify its five GHCR digests/platform/provenance/SBOM and canonical artifact checksum, then separately approve any Timeweb deployment.

author: david-j-stoll
body:
## Context & Motivation

GitHub is removing the Node.js 20 runtime from Actions runners on **2026-09-16**. JavaScript actions still bundling Node 20 will fail after that date. All six workflows in this repo pin Node-20 actions — `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-python@v5`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4` and `actions/github-script@v7`.

This repo carries the **largest** exposure of the three (14 pins) and the only genuinely breaking upgrade (`github-script`).

- Linear: [MFB-1105](https://linear.app/myfriendben/issue/MFB-1105/bump-github-actions-to-node-24-compatible-versions-before-sept-16-2026)
- Ref: [Deprecation of Node 20 on GitHub Actions runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/)
- Companion PRs: MyFriendBen/benefits-api#1721 and MyFriendBen/benefits-calculator#2186. The ticket is scoped to `benefits-api`; an audit found `data-queries` equally affected and it was not previously tracked.

## Changes Made

14 pins across 6 files. Version strings only — no other line in the diff.

| Action | From | To | Count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | **v7** | 8 |
| `actions/setup-python` | v5 | **v7** | 3 |
| `actions/setup-node` | v4 | **v7** | 1 |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v4 | **v7** | 1 |
| `actions/github-script` | v7 | **v9** | 1 |

Files: `format-check.yml`, `rls-check.yml`, `terraform-plan.yml`, `terraform-apply.yml`, `dbt-on-merge.yml`, `dbt-nightly.yml`. This repo uses no composite actions.

`DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md` also contains the old pins in example snippets. It is explicitly marked a historical document, describes a staging environment that no longer exists, and is never executed — **left as-is** rather than rewritten, to avoid falsifying the record.

## Testing

- Migrations to run: none
- Configuration updates needed: none
- Environment variables/settings to add: none
- Manual testing steps:

**✅ Already verified — green on this PR:**

| Action | Verified by |
| --- | --- |
| `actions/github-script@v9` | **`plan` job posted its "Terraform Plan 📖" comment to this PR with real plan output** |
| `actions/checkout@v7` | `SQLFluff`, `Prettier (YAML)`, `Terraform fmt`, `plan` |
| `actions/setup-python@v7` | `SQLFluff (dbt SQL models)` |
| `actions/setup-node@v7` | `Prettier (YAML)` |

The first row is the one that mattered. `github-script@v9` is the only genuinely breaking upgrade in this whole effort: `require('@actions/github')` no longer resolves (the package is now ESM-only), and `getOctokit` is an injected script parameter, so any script redeclaring it raises `SyntaxError`. The plan comment rendering on this PR is direct proof the script survived — and note the failure mode would have been a *missing comment*, not a red X, since the job can pass without it.

Other breaking changes checked against actual usage:

- `setup-python@v7` removed the `pip-install` input — all three call sites use `cache: 'pip'` + `cache-dependency-path` instead.
- `checkout@v7` blocks fork checkout on `pull_request_target` / `workflow_run` — neither trigger exists here.
- `upload-artifact` — the naming/overwrite break was v3→v4, already behind us.

## Deployment

- Post-deployment scripts needed: none
- Production config updates: none
- Admin updates needed: none
- Notify team/users of: nothing required — but see the sequence below; **two workflows here are unverified, and one of them is the only untested `upload-artifact@v7` call site in the entire change.**

**⚠️ Not exercised by this PR:**

| Workflow | Trigger | Unverified exposure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dbt-nightly.yml` | `schedule` (06:00 UTC) + `workflow_dispatch` | checkout + setup-python + **upload-artifact** |
| `dbt-on-merge.yml` | `push: main` | checkout + setup-python |
| `rls-check.yml` | `pull_request`, paths-filtered | 1 × checkout — see below |

**Recommended sequence:**

1. **Before merge** — trigger `dbt-nightly.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` from this branch. Confirm it completes *and* still uploads the `dbt-artifacts-production` artifact (`manifest.json`, `run_results.json`). This is the only `upload-artifact@v7` call site in this repo and it is otherwise untested until an overnight cron run.
2. **On merge to main** — watch `dbt-on-merge.yml`. Its exposure is `checkout` + `setup-python` only, both already proven by `format-check.yml` on this PR, so residual risk is low.
3. **First night after merge** — if step 1 was skipped, the 06:00 UTC `dbt-nightly.yml` run is the first real signal and a failure will surface as an overnight break. Don't skip step 1.

`rls-check.yml` is `pull_request`-triggered but paths-filtered to `dbt/models/postgres/marts/**`, which this PR doesn't touch, so it did not run. Its single `checkout@v7` is identical to eight verified call sites — negligible risk, but noted for completeness.

There is no Terraform apply concern: `terraform-apply.yml` (`push: main` + `workflow_dispatch`) shares its `checkout` + `setup-terraform` shape with `terraform-plan.yml`, which is green on this PR.

## Notes for Reviewers

- **Known limitations:**
  - `dbt-on-merge.yml` cannot be exercised pre-merge; its exposure is fully covered by other verified jobs.
  - **Third-party actions are out of scope.** `hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3` (3 call sites) and `google-github-actions/auth@v2` (2 call sites) have not had their bundled runtimes verified against the deadline.
- **Future considerations:**
  - `format-check.yml` pins `node-version: "20"` for prettier. That's the *toolchain* Node, not the action runtime, so this deprecation does not affect it — but Node 20 is EOL and deserves its own bump. Deliberately excluded here to keep this diff purely mechanical.
  - No `dependabot.yml`. Enabling the `github-actions` ecosystem is the durable fix.

body:
Follow-up to #205, found by curling all ten docs routes after it deployed rather than by reading the code.

`/docs/outcomes` and `/docs/changelog` return 406 to `Accept: text/markdown`. They are generated — from the outcome taxonomy and from the package changelogs — rather than written in `content/docs/`, so they have no markdown source and never did. The code comment claimed a missing twin meant a broken build. It does not.

The body now names the reason and points at `llms-full.txt`, which does carry that content. A unit test pins the two-page list so it cannot grow by accident.

Both still go through negotiation deliberately: excluding them would hand the request to Start's router, which answers a non-HTML `Accept` with a 500. A 406 with a useful body beats that.

**Worth a decision, not fixed here:** `/docs/outcomes` is arguably the page an agent most wants as markdown — it is the taxonomy this project exists to explain. Giving it a generated twin is a real improvement and a bigger change than this one.

author: wscha231
body:
## Summary

This follow-up addresses the review findings from #4 without giving back the 7-day direction gain.

- Keep the train-only empirical-CDF value as a **direction score**, not an event probability.
- Fit a held-out, monotone isotonic label map and shrink it toward the time-decayed UP base rate for user-facing `probability_up`, confidence, and Brier scoring.
- Use direction scores for threshold selection, predicted labels, AUC, trading signals, hybrid bias, and threshold sweeps.
- Blend ensemble probabilities with Brier weights, while blending direction scores with balanced-accuracy weights.
- Preserve the post-candle live price gap as a bounded +/-1.5 percentage-point adjustment, without restoring the rejected momentum/RSI/regime overlay.
- Propagate both values through recent holdout, long-run OOF checkpoints, resume/merge, ensemble rows, and backward-compatible threshold sweeps.

## Review hardening

- Purge the internal calibration boundary by the full forecast horizon for both 7-day and 30-day classifiers.
- Fall back from `direction_score_up` to `probability_up` **per row** across legacy checkpoint restore, diversification, ensembles, thresholds, and emitted rows.
- Add SQLite schema v4 plus idempotent migration, persistence, and public JSON export for `direction_score_up`.
- Resolve all three automated review threads with regression coverage.

## Why this design

The attached crypto-forecasting papers consistently support chronological walk-forward evaluation, multivariate inputs, ensemble methods, and evaluating direction/trading outcomes separately from point-price error. They also highlight volatility sensitivity and uncertainty limitations. This change follows those supported parts. It does **not** add CNN-LSTM/VAE complexity yet because the current ETH sample is small and those architectures have not passed this repository's purged 36-fold direction/trading gate.

## Evidence

- `103 passed` in the complete local test suite.
- `git diff --check` and Python compilation pass.
- GitHub Actions run **32834227774**: **PASS** on deployed data through 2026-08-25; static leakage tests, 3-fold OOF smoke, candidate gate, and artifact upload all succeeded.
- Latest deployed-data 7d smoke:
  - best regression RMSE **170.64** vs no-change **182.12** (**6.30%** point edge)
  - best regression directional accuracy **0.6222**
  - classification balanced accuracy **0.8500**
  - ROC AUC **0.9875**
  - Brier **0.1775**
  - leakage-safe threshold validation: **true**
- Latest deployed-data 30d smoke:
  - best regression RMSE **601.85** vs no-change **629.65** (**4.42%** point edge)
  - best regression directional accuracy **0.7444**
  - classification balanced accuracy **0.5833**
  - ROC AUC **1.0000**
  - Brier **0.1621**
  - the evaluator retains its expected warning that a partial 3-fold 30d smoke cannot certify every threshold row; the scheduled full OOF gate is authoritative.
- Prior purged 36-fold 7d core direction replay:
  - direction-weighted blend balanced accuracy **0.5980**
  - ROC AUC **0.6381**
  - symmetric 0.60 score threshold: **59.78%** accuracy on **92/686** actionable dates

## Semantics after this PR

- `direction_score_up`: relative directional evidence used to decide UP/DOWN/FLAT.
- `probability_up`: label-calibrated event probability used for display, confidence, and Brier.
- Existing artifacts without `direction_score_up` fall back to `probability_up` per row.

The 30-day modeling path remains otherwise unchanged; this PR only adds the mandatory calibration-boundary purge to its established holdout calibration.

author: tenntenn
body:
A relative `href` in a previewed Markdown file is written against that file's
own directory in the tree. The review page is served from the server root, so
`./notes.md` resolved to `/notes.md`, the SPA catch-all answered it with `200
text/html`, and the reader landed in a second copy of sbnn that read
`notes.md` as a group name, found no such group, and showed "Waiting for a
diff". `renderMarkdown` set `target="_blank"` on every `<a href>`, bare
fragments included, so it happened in a tab of its own.

## What changed

**`resolvePreviewLinks` (`web/src/markdown.ts`)** — a string pass over the
sanitiser's output, the same shape as `resolvePreviewImages` and for the same
reason (raw HTML in a document carries `<a>` too, and it can be tested where
there is no DOM):

- a relative href is resolved against the previewed file's directory —
  `./notes.md`, `notes.md`, `../README.md` and `/README.md` from
  `docs/guide.md` become `docs/notes.md`, `docs/notes.md`, `README.md`,
  `README.md`. A query or fragment on the href is dropped for the lookup:
  what this page can open is a file, not a place inside one.
- a path this page carries becomes `<a href="#d1:f2-abcd1234">`, the fragment
  `urlState` already uses to address a file section, so the link is followed
  in place.
- anything else stops being an anchor. It is drawn as the path it resolved to
  and the statement that the review does not carry it, which is the honest
  answer when there is nothing here to open. A link that quietly goes nowhere
  says neither.
- an absolute or remote href, and a bare fragment, are handed back byte for
  byte.

**`PreviewStack`** builds the path-to-section map and passes it down. Which
files the page carries is known there and not in the renderer, and an exported
page answers it the same way. A path touched by two rounds resolves to the
newest.

**The target hook** now marks only a link that is genuinely another page —
`http`, `https` or protocol-relative. A relative href, a bare `#fragment` and
a `mailto:` are not, and `target` is *removed* rather than merely not set,
because the Markdown comes from a diff and may carry its own
`<a target="_blank">`.

**`web/test/resolve-ts.mjs`** — the DOMPurify stand-in keeps the callbacks it
is handed instead of dropping them. The target hook is registered at import
time and never exported, so that is the only way to ask it about an href in a
process with no DOM. The change is additive; the other 123 tests are
unaffected.

The third bullet of #89 (the SPA answering an asset-looking path with
`index.html`) landed separately in #215 and is not touched here.

## How you tested it

`web/` does have a test runner — `pnpm test` runs `node --test` over
`test/*.test.ts` — so the earlier claim in this PR that one could not be added
was wrong. 15 tests were added in `web/test/preview-links.test.ts`.

```console
$ cd web && pnpm test
# tests 138
# pass 138
# fail 0
$ npx tsc -b && pnpm run build
✓ built in 1.32s
```

## Description

The external-usage `source` slug pattern allows a colon, so an importer could post rows tagged `otari-ai:gateway` or `otari-ai:claude_code`, the same tags otari.ai's backfill writes. Those lookalike rows inflate the migration's reconciliation totals and show up as a false MISMATCH during a cutover.

Any source starting with `otari-ai:` (case-insensitive) is now rejected with the same reserved-source 422 the bare `gateway` slug already gets. The exact-match `gateway` check is unchanged, and this is a prefix check rather than a colon ban, so `foo:bar` is still accepted. Validation on new imports only: no migration, no change to stored rows.

The OTLP route is the second door into the same rows: it derives a `source` from the caller-supplied `otari.client_name` and hands it to the batch schema, so the new reservation would have turned such an export into a 500. The reservation now lives in one `reserved_source_reason` helper that both doors read: a 422 for a direct import, and a fallback to the default `otel` source for an exporter, matching how `gateway` is already handled there.

Follow-up (not here): otari-ai#1815 reserves the same prefix in `usage_admin_service.py` and `workspace_activation_service.py`. Once both land, the three copies of the prefix could converge on one shared definition.
