author: sanyasandal
body:
## Problem
On blog / Resource Center pages below **1300px**, the "Resource center" **secondary nav scrolled away** on scroll. The primary nav is `position: fixed` (pinned), but the secondary nav was left in flow — [header.js](blocks/header/header.js) only repositions it at `≥1300px`. So the pinned header on mobile/tablet was just the 56px primary nav, and anything offset for the full header height (e.g. the blog TOC's `top: 117px`) floated with **article text bleeding through the gap**.

Prod keeps the secondary nav pinned directly under the primary (full ~117px header).

## Fix (`blocks/header/header.css`, `≤1299px`)
Pin the secondary nav below the fixed primary nav and let its spacer reserve the row height (it's now out of flow):
```css
.header.has-secondary-nav .ies-secondary-nav { position: fixed; top: 56px; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 49; background: #fff; }
.header.has-secondary-nav .ies-secondary-nav-spacer { height: 61px; }
```

## Verified (localhost, mobile 390px)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Blog article, scrolled | primary (0–58) + **secondary pinned (56–117)** + TOC flush at 117, no bleed ✅ |
| `/blog` listing, scrolled | secondary pinned (56–117) ✅ |
| Top of page | primary/secondary stacked, hero content starts at 117 (no overlap) ✅ |
| Resource center dropdown | still opens, visible in viewport ✅ |
| **Desktop ≥1300px** | unchanged (existing JS-driven pinning) ✅ |
| Non-blog page (`/accounting`) | no secondary nav → unaffected ✅ |

## Blast radius
`blocks/header/header.css`, scoped to `.has-secondary-nav` — i.e. **Resource Center / `/blog*` pages only**, `≤1299px`. Non-secondary-nav pages (the rest of the site) and desktop are untouched.

## Related
Complements the blog-TOC mobile fixes in #823 (the TOC's `top: 117px` now sits flush under the fully-pinned header instead of over a gap).

Closes #828

URL for testing:

- https://fix-blog-secondary-nav-sticky-mobile--intuit-erp--aemsites.aem.page/

author: dergel
body:
Sichert eine vorhandene `.htaccess`, bevor das Setup sie ersetzt, und fragt vorher nach. Umsetzung des Anliegens aus #589 von @danspringer.

* Die vorhandene Datei wird als `.htaccess-backup-<Zeitstempel>` im Data-Verzeichnis des AddOns gesichert. Die zehn neuesten Sicherungen bleiben erhalten.
* Schlägt die Sicherung fehl, bleibt die vorhandene Datei unangetastet und `copyHtaccess()` gibt `false` zurück.
* Die Rückfrage erscheint nur, wenn tatsächlich eine Datei überschrieben würde. Der Handler hängt am `document` und übersteht pjax.
* Enthält außerdem die Changelog-Einträge für #563 und #589.

Gegen eine laufende Installation geprüft: die Sicherung ist bitgleich zur ursprünglichen Datei, die neue `.htaccess` entspricht der Vorlage. Von 14 Sicherungen bleiben genau die zehn jüngsten. Bei nicht schreibbarem Data-Verzeichnis liefert `copyHtaccess()` `false` und die vorhandene Datei ist unverändert. Mit vorhandener Datei trägt der Button `data-confirm`, ohne Datei nicht.

Gegenüber dem Stand in #589: der Dateiname des JavaScripts passt zur Einbindung in `boot.php` (dort fehlte die Datei im Branch), die Sicherungen sind begrenzt, die Rückfrage erscheint nur bei vorhandener Datei, und ohne schreibbare Sicherung wird nicht überschrieben. `pjax: false` für die Setup-Seite ist nicht nötig, weil der Handler delegiert registriert ist.

author: sw-mwieland
body:
`islazy.LeftTruncate` returns `s[max:]`, the part of the string *after* `max` bytes, not the first `max` bytes. Three consequences, all visible in `scan`:

- **It never bounds the length**: A 900 byte name comes back 700 byte long, so #202 is still reproducable. A URL past roughly 455  characters fails with `could not write screenshot to disk: open ...: file name to long`, the whole result is dropped, and nothing is logged unless `--log-scan-errors` is set.
- **It keeps the wrong half**: For URLs between ~200 and ~455 characters the write succeeds but the same scheme and host are discared and only the query-string tail survives. Scanning `http://host/?q=aaaa...` produced `aaaa...jpg`, no host unidentifiable, and two long URLs sharing a tail collide. That works against #242, where filenames were deliberately made parseable.
- **It slices by byte**: `SafeFileName` keeps non-ASCII letters, so the cut can land inside a multi-byte rune and produce and invalid UTF-8 filename.

Replaced with `islazy.Truncate`, which keeps the start of the string, stays within the limit, and appends a short hash of the full value so names that only differ past the cut stay distinct. The extension is now appended after truncation instead of being part of what gets cut.

Filenames shorter than the limit are completely unaffected.

Adds unit tests for `islazy.Truncate` covering the length bound, prefix preservation, prefix-sharing inputs, and rune safety.

author: locnguyn
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

- Precompute null-safe request identifiers before entering the affected REST `try/catch` blocks.
- Use those precomputed values in exception handlers instead of dereferencing `request` from catch paths.
- Cover create/register/grant/revoke/statistics/job-template handlers listed in #10172 while keeping the existing `ExceptionHandlers` mappings and endpoint contracts unchanged.
- Add a regression test for a null group request body to verify that the original error is marshalled instead of being replaced by a secondary `NullPointerException`.

### Why are the changes needed?

Several REST catch paths call methods such as `request.getName()`, `request.getRoleNames()`, or `request.getJobTemplate()` after an exception has already occurred. If the request itself is null, the catch block can throw another `NullPointerException`, masking the primary failure and preventing the existing exception handlers from returning the intended error response.

Fix: #10172

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration contract changes. For malformed/null request bodies, error responses now preserve the original exception-handling path instead of being replaced by a secondary catch-path `NullPointerException`.

### How was this patch tested?

- `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17 ./gradlew :server:compileJava -PskipITs --no-daemon`
- `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17 ./gradlew :server:test --tests org.apache.gravitino.server.web.rest.TestGroupOperations.testAddGroupWithNullRequestBodyDoesNotExposeNpe -PskipITs --no-daemon`

## PR #6와의 관계

`feature/gateway-qt-integration`이 PR #6으로 먼저 `develop`에 병합됐습니다.
이 브랜치는 이 PR의 브랜치(`perf/fhss-slot-batch-tx`)와 같은 지점
(`dd3abd9`, "SlotAwareTransport로 SYNC 충돌 문제 해결" 커밋)에서 갈라진
뒤 그 상태에 머물러 있었고, 그 이후 나온 성능 개선·버그 수정·실기기
검증 로그가 전부 빠져 있었습니다. 이 PR이 그 나머지를 마저 반영합니다.
로컬에서 미리 확인한 결과 현재 `develop` 기준으로 **충돌 없이 깨끗하게
병합**됩니다.

## 왜 필요했나 — 배경

호핑 중엔 게이트웨이가 보내는 DATA가 커널이 자동으로 내보내는 SYNC(동기화)
신호와 타이밍이 겹치면 패킷이 깨지는 문제가 있었습니다. 이건 PR #6에 이미
포함된 `SlotAwareTransport`(슬롯 경계를 확인한 뒤에만 DATA를 보내는
`ITransport` 래퍼)로 해결됐습니다. 그런데 그 위에서 실기기로 계속 돌려보니
"슬롯 안전창은 지키는데 실제로는 못 끝난다"는 문제들이 연달아 나왔고, 이
PR은 그걸 하나씩 실기기 로그로 원인을 잡아 고친 기록입니다.

## 이 PR에서 고친 것들 (원인 → 수정 순서로, 실제 발생 순서)

### 1. `fix(ota): serialize FHSS transfer by slot`
`OtaSession`(송신 상태기계)이 슬롯 개념을 모른 채 자기 타이밍대로
쏘고 있어서, `SlotAwareTransport`가 슬롯을 지켜도 그 위 레이어가 어긋난
타이밍에 호출하면 소용없었습니다. 전송을 슬롯 단위로 직렬화하도록
`otasession.cpp/h`를 수정.

### 2. `perf(fhss): 슬롯 안전창 재사용해서 슬롯당 여러 패킷 전송`
기존엔 슬롯(300ms)당 패킷을 1개만 보내서 7825청크 전송에 40분 가까이
걸렸습니다. `SlotAwareTransport::ensureSafeWindow()`가 한 번 연 "안전창"
(슬롯 경계 + `kPostSyncGuardMs`부터 다음 슬롯 경계 − `kTailGuardMs`까지)을
같은 슬롯 안에서는 대기 없이 재사용하도록 바꿔서, 슬롯 하나에 여러 패킷을
연달아 보낼 수 있게 했습니다.

### 3. `fix(discover): DISCOVER 전 FHSS 잔류 상태를 명시적으로 초기화`
**증상**: FHSS 테스트를 먼저 돌린 뒤 DISCOVER를 하면 "응답 없음"만
반복됨(148/149 실기기 재현).
**원인**: 이전 FHSS 세션이 커널 드라이버를 호핑 상태로 남겨뒀는데,
DISCOVER 쪽 코드는 연결만 열고 `stopFhss()`/`setChannel(0)`을 전혀 안
불러서, DISCOVER 패킷이 계속 엉뚱한(호핑 중인) 채널로 나갔습니다.
**수정**: `stopFhss() → setChannel(0) → flushRx() → startRx()` 순서를
명시적으로 추가하고, 각 단계가 실패하면 원인을 숨기지 않고 바로 종료.

### 4. `fix(fhss): 전송 시작 전 동기화 대기 2s → 4s`
**증상**: 148 실기기 로그에서 매번 SYNC를 못 잡고 세션이 폐기됨.
**원인**: ACTIVATE 직후 ESP32는 랑데부 채널(1번)에 고정된 채 SYNC를
기다리는데, Gateway는 이미 8채널을 순회 중이라 1번으로 돌아오는 건
8슬롯(300ms×8=2.4초)마다 한 번뿐입니다. 연속 3번 SYNC를 받아야 "획득"으로
치는데 그 0.9초까지 더하면 최악 3.3초가 걸립니다. 기존 대기(2초)로는
ESP32가 아직 SEARCHING(탐색) 상태일 때 OTA_START/DATA가 먼저 도착해버려서,
ESP32가 그 DATA를 처리하느라 다음 SYNC를 놓치고 랑데부로 되돌아가
2.4초를 또 기다리는 일이 반복돼 영원히 동기화를 못 하는 교착이었습니다.
**증거**: 세션이 폐기되어 DATA가 멈추자마자 300ms 만에 깨끗이 SYNC를
잡은 게 결정적 증거였습니다.
**수정**: 대기를 4초(3.3초+여유)로 늘리고, firmware-esp32 쪽
`OTA_FHSS_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS`도 5초→10초로 같이 올림(Gateway 대기 시간이
ESP32 타임아웃보다 짧아야 하는 짝 값이라 한쪽만 바꾸면 안 됨).

### 5. `fix(fhss): 슬롯 내 연속 전송에 반이중 왕복 간격(150ms) 강제`
**증상**: 2번(슬롯당 여러 패킷) 최적화 이후, 오히려 홀수 seq(순번)만
계속 유실됨.
**원인**: CC1101은 반이중(half-duplex, 송신·수신을 동시에 못 하는)
트랜시버라 ESP32가 ACK를 보내는 동안은 아예 수신을 못 합니다. 실측
로그에서 ESP32의 ACK 왕복이 121ms 걸리는데, Gateway는 같은 슬롯에서
5개를 16ms 간격으로 쐈으니 ACK 송신 중 지나간 패킷이 통째로 사라졌습니다.
**수정**: 직전 전송 이후 `kMinPacketGapMs`(150ms = 실측 121ms+여유)가
지날 때까지 대기하도록 강제. 결과적으로 슬롯당 2개가 물리적 한계입니다
(원래 1개보다 2배). 더 올리려면 ESP32가 DATA마다 즉시 ACK하지 않고
배치 단위로 한 번만 ACK해야 하는데, 이건 다음 과제로 남겨둠.

### 6. `fix(fhss): 재전송 한도 기본값 5 → 20`
**원인**: ESP32가 SYNC를 잃으면 재획득에 최악 3.3초가 걸리는데, 재전송
1회가 150~300ms라 5회로는 1초 남짓밖에 못 버텨서 ESP32가 복구되기 전에
Gateway가 먼저 포기했습니다.
**수정**: 20회로 상향(진짜 끊긴 경우엔 20회를 다 쓰고 정상적으로
실패하므로 무한 대기는 안 됨). firmware-esp32의
`OTA_FHSS_RESYNC_GRACE_MS`도 3초→10초로 같이 올림(짝 값).

### 7. `fix(fhss): 연속 무응답 시 송신을 멈춰 ESP32 재동기화를 양보`
**증상**: 4번에서 고친 "동기화 전에 DATA를 쏘면 그 DATA가 동기화를
방해하는" 교착이, 전송 시작 시점뿐 아니라 **전송 도중**에도 똑같이
재현됨(148 실기기: 1036청크 지점에서 12.6초 완전 무응답 후 실패 —
ESP32의 10초 유예보다 Gateway가 더 오래 조용했다는 뜻이라, 재전송
한도를 더 늘려도 소용없는 상황이었습니다).
**수정**: `SlotAwareTransport`에 "재동기화 양보(quiet window)" 도입 —
연속 8회(약 1.2초) 무응답이면 4초 동안 완전히 송신을 멈추고 ESP32가
조용히 재동기화할 시간을 줌. 정상 동작 중에는 트리거되지 않도록 여유
있게 잡음. firmware-esp32의 `loss_count`(SYNC 손실로 치는 문턱)도
5→12로 올림(원래 음성용으로 정해진 값이 OTA의 잦은 ACK 송신과 안 맞았음).

## 검증

실기기(라즈베리파이 ↔ ESP32) 2회 완주:
- 7949/7949청크 전량 완주
- 7825/7825청크 전량 완주

(둘 다 END ACK 기준 무결성 확인. SHA256 파일 해시 검증은 아직 다음 과제)

## ⚠️ 알려진 제약 — 리뷰어가 꼭 봐야 할 부분

**비호핑 대비 처리량이 약 5.8배 느립니다.** 원인은 5번에서 물리적 한계로
확인된 "슬롯당 2개"인데, 실측해보니 실제로는 슬롯 하나에 2패킷만 들어가고
그다음 슬롯은 통째로 건너뛰는 낭비가 있었습니다(윈도우 전환 6000개 이상
전수조사, 100%가 이 패턴). **버그는 아니고 성능 특성이며 전송 자체는
안정적으로 완주합니다.**

이 성능 문제는 이미 별도 브랜치(`perf/fhss-slot-gap-tuning`)에서 원인
규명·수정·실기기 재검증까지 끝났습니다(슬롯 전환 정상 비율 99%대로
개선). 그 검증 과정에서 추가로 드러난 ESP32 쪽 버그 2건(인터럽트 워치독
크래시, OTA 재동기화 시 세션 강제종료)도 같이 고쳐서 현재 최장 진행률
38%까지 확인했습니다. 이건 다음 PR로 별도 진행합니다.

## 참고 문서

- `docs/note/design-notes-gateway-ota-es.md` 41~71절 — 이번 PR 및 후속
  작업 전체의 원인 조사·의사결정 기록
- `docs/fhss-hopping-guide.md` — 호핑 동작 원리
- `docs/troubleshooting-fhss-hopping.md` — 안 될 때 증상별 대처
- `artifacts/fhss1/`, `artifacts/fhss2/` — 실기기 완주 검증 원본 로그

author: sebitr
body:
Recreates the *User settings redesign* handoff in the codebase. Nine destinations sat loose in an avatar dropdown and three long pages at `/profile` and `/admin/telemetry`; they collapse into one surface at `/settings` — three short groups of rows, each carrying the value it leads to, so most visits end on the hub without opening anything.

## What it looks like

```
/settings                    hub — identity card, three groups, sign out
├─ /account                  photo, display name, email, danger card
├─ /security                 passkeys, password, Apple
├─ /notifications            five switches, push + devices, muted groups
├─ /appearance               theme, language
├─ /money                    currency, dates, numbers
├─ /groups                   a directory, not an editor
├─ /data                     export a group, bring expenses in
├─ /admin                    telemetry (instance admins only)
└─ /help                     version, links, install
```

Two rules run through it: **everything writes the moment it is touched** and confirms with an Undo — no Save button anywhere — and **exactly two things ask twice**, signing out and deleting the account, because those are the two with no way back.

## Design fidelity

The prototype was drawn in Balancia's own dark palette, so every colour in it is already a semantic token here (`bg-card`, `--primary`, `--positive`, `--input`…) and the screens work in both themes without a second palette. Its px sizes are **mapped onto the seven-step scale rather than transcribed** — a literal sits out the point every step gains below `md`, which is how the entry screens once ended up rendering a 10px label on a phone.

One new token: `--scrim`, for the confirmation sheet. Dark in both themes, because a cream page under a cream veil reads as having gone quiet rather than as waiting for an answer.

Three deliberate departures from the handoff, each noted in the code:

- **Toasts** stay top-centre with the app's 8s undo window rather than moving to a 3.4s bottom toast. The `Toaster` is app-wide and `toastUndoable` is the established way back; changing it for one feature would change it everywhere.
- **"Push to this iPhone" → "Push to this device"**, and "Match my phone" → "Match my device". The app is a PWA on Android and desktop too.
- **"Send a test"** is kept on the push card. The design does not draw it, but push is the one thing that can be switched on, report itself on, and still never arrive — it is the only way to tell "on" from "working".

## Two things the design asked for that had nothing behind them

You asked for both to be built for real rather than stubbed.

**A photo on the account.** New columns on `users`, a service, and `/api/profile/avatar` (GET/POST/DELETE). The browser squares and re-encodes to a 512px WebP before sending, which also drops the EXIF block — an avatar carrying the GPS of the room it was taken in would be a privacy leak served from a public URL. None of that is trusted: the route sniffs the type from the file's magic bytes, enforces a 1 MB cap, generates the key server-side, and sweeps the object it replaces. No new runtime dependency — `sharp` is dev-only, and the codebase already does canvas work client-side.

**Closing an account.** A real `DELETE`, not a flag — the schema was already built for it. Everything that *is* the account cascades away (sessions, passkeys, the Apple link, push, notifications, membership); everything that is *history* references a `participant` and stays standing under the name it was recorded against, which is exactly what the screen promises. Deleting rather than disabling also frees the address, so somebody who closes an account and thinks better of it can sign up again.

Two things the cascades cannot decide, and this does:

- a group the account **owned** promotes its longest-standing remaining member — a group nobody can rename or archive is not a crash, which is why nothing else would catch it;
- a group with **no other member at all** goes with the account, rather than becoming rows nobody can ever reach.

## Migration and compatibility

`0023` adds three nullable avatar columns and one CHECK. `/profile`, `/profile/security`, `/profile/notifications` and `/admin/telemetry` answer `permanentRedirect` **with their query string**, because `/confirm-email` and the Apple round trip both used to land on them with one.

## Removals

Six components are deleted rather than left beside their replacements — two implementations of the same undo semantics drift apart. Their coverage moved with them: the format and push tests are ported onto the new cards, and the account-deletion and avatar services get integration tests of their own. Dead message keys are trimmed from both catalogues, and French is complete.

## Verification

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` | clean |
| unit + component | **2288 passed**, 154 files |
| integration | **302 passed** against a scratch Postgres |
| e2e | **updated, not run** — needs a built app and a browser |

Ten integration failures in `rates.test.ts` and `expenses.test.ts` are **pre-existing**: I ran the same two files from a detached worktree at `origin/main` and got the identical ten. This branch touches neither rates, env, expenses nor categorization.

author: edgehero
body:
Closes #200.

A reader of v1.0.0 bounced off the top of the page: they want to be in the loop, and the first sentence they meet is "while you are not watching". The facts that say a human starts and lands every forge job sit at `README.md:497`, roughly 480 lines below, inside the GitHub automation section. The "one off interactive session" line then reinforces the misread, because it makes the comparison interactive pi versus unattended pi-dispatch, when the real distinction is who is watching the terminal, not who approves the work.

## The change

Two sentences, no new section, nothing moved.

**Banner paragraph, the category line.** Maps the project onto the category the reader already has, so the second half of the review ("why not one of the billion claws") has an answer above the fold:

> This is not another agent to weigh against the one you already use; it is the queue, the budget and the box for the pi you already run, steered by the `.pi/` setup your repo already has.

**"When to use it", the in the loop paragraph.** Placed above the one off line, so it lands before the misread is created, and linking down to the section that already spells out the per forge gates:

> On a forge you stay in the loop at both ends: a job starts only when someone with write access to the repo asks for one, by a label, an `@pi` comment or a review, and what comes back is a pull request you review and land, because pi-dispatch never merges anything, not on green CI, not on any condition ([the details](#github-automation)). What it removes is the terminal babysitting, not you.

**`admin/README.md`** carries the identical opening sentence and is the npm facing page for the console, so it takes both sentences in its own pitch paragraph. It has no "When to use it" to hold them.

## Three places this could have overclaimed, and did not

* **Scope.** Both claims open with "On a forge". `SECURITY.md:275` says local folder jobs have no gate and no undo, no merge, no reviewer, no pull request to decline. Bleeding the promise into local runs would have been the same defect the issue was written to fix.
* **The gate is stated as write access**, not as "only collaborators can label". That reasoning is GitHub only: per `CONST-TRIGGER-AUTHOR-GATE`, a GitLab Guest can set labels at creation, which is exactly why GitLab, Forgejo and Azure resolve the actor's permission for every trigger type. `README.md:497` can lean on the label argument because it is inside the GitHub section. The top of the page cannot.
* **The merge claim is about the harness**, per `CONST-MERGE-NEVER-AUTOMATIC`, never that merging is impossible. `README.md:501` says plainly that the per job token *can* merge and that branch protection is the real control, so "pi-dispatch never merges anything" is the honest form and "it cannot merge" would have contradicted the page four screens down.

## Not done, per the issue's own exclusion list

No comparison section naming other tools, no softening of "while you are not watching" (it is accurate and it is the value, the fix is adding the other half), no restructuring, and the GitHub automation section stays where it is.

## Checks

Specs UNCHANGED, checked: `CONST-TRIGGER-AUTHOR-GATE`, `CONST-MERGE-NEVER-AUTOMATIC`. This states what already ships and changes no behaviour, so no spec file moves with it.

Both READMEs still contain zero dash punctuation (no em dash, no en dash, no spaced hyphen), which nothing in CI enforces. `#github-automation` verified as a unique heading slug. Suite green in the CI posture, 2327 tests, 0 skipped, live Valkey.

body: **Bug (devmcflyads post-approval smoke):** After Approve / **Open app**, the Admin iframe loaded the Mcfly marketing landing (`site/index.html`) instead of the desk Overview. **Cause:** App URL is `https://mcfly-analytics.fly.dev` (`/`). Production serves `site/` for public GET `/`. `express.static` ignores `?shop=&host=&embedded=1`, so Remix’s existing `/` → `/app` redirect never ran. **Fix:** If the request looks like an embedded Shopify session (`shop`, `host`, `embedded=1`, `hmac`, `id_token`, `session`), do not serve marketing HTML. 302 to `/app` with the same query. # Feature/support recent tabs

## Summary

Adds a persisted Recent Tabs view for ungrouped tabs, keeps its order synchronized with native tab activation and group changes, and supports moving entries into the main Tabs view. The change also validates restored workspace data and documents the new workflow.

### Changes

- Adds Recent Tabs ordering and persistence through a read-only tree contribution.
- Refreshes Recent Tabs on tab changes, supports selecting, closing, ungrouping, and dragging tabs into the main tree.
- Extends tree drag/drop MIME registration and guards no-op drops.
- Validates persisted group and tab records and filters invalid Recent Tabs IDs.
- Adds unit and extension-host coverage plus README, development, and testing documentation updates.

### Checklist

- [x] Code follows project structure and conventions
- [x] Unit tests added or updated
- [x] No secrets or sensitive data included
- [x] The PR is labelled

### How to test

- Run `npm run test:unit` for unit coverage.
- Run `npm run compile` for strict TypeScript compilation.
- Run `npm run test:e2e` for extension-host coverage.
- Manually open and activate ungrouped files, verify **Recent Tabs** ordering, drag one into a group, then ungroup it and confirm it returns to the list.

### Notes for reviewers

- Target branch: `main`.
- `npm run test:e2e` passes all 6 extension-host tests, and the new Recent Tabs and workspace-state suites pass.
- Full lint and unit runs are currently blocked by the empty [src/test/event.test.ts](src/test/event.test.ts) file in the branch: Prettier rejects its blank line and Jest reports that it contains no tests.

body:
## Wave 2 ownership
- Slot: **#144**
- Product: **SkyCredentialsWeb3**
- Lane: **12**
- Branch: `product/144-skycredentialsweb3-lane12`

Adds a dependency-free verifiable-credential metadata library: bounded HTTPS credential/schema/status references, bounded issuer/subject DID references, normalized credential types and JSON claims, deterministic SHA-256 metadata fingerprints, timestamp validation, and an explicit verification-plan contract.

Every credential result reports `proofVerificationPerformed: false`, `identityVerificationPerformed: false`, and `chainWritePerformed: false`. The fingerprint is a content identifier only—not a signature, proof, attestation, or chain commitment.

Integration target: `SkyDID -> SkyCredentialsWeb3 -> trusted verifier adapter -> SkyPolicy/consumer`. This product does not duplicate DID resolution (#143) and does not claim issuance, proof verification, status checking, identity proofing, wallet custody, blockchain execution, standards certification, or production deployment.

CI extends the existing Quality workflow with isolated syntax/tests and a production dependency audit while retaining frozen install, typecheck, application tests, and production build.

Merge only after exact-head required CI is green; use expected-head protection and squash merge.

author: fchecklist
body:
## Summary
R46 WPR cluster fix, T-WPR-15-1 ("No parent row accepts a directly typed progress figure").

Investigation found `WorkProgressClient.tsx` (the file the original UAT finding cited as having "ZERO awareness of BOQ line items") was already deleted in PR #113 (2026-08-24), superseded by `WorkProgressFormClient.tsx`, which **is** BOQ-line-item aware -- it has a `boqLineItemId` SELECT populated from every line item in the project's BOQ (`getBoq()` returns the flat, unfiltered list -- parents and children alike).

That surfaced the real, live gap: `createProgressEntry()` in `construction-progress-service.ts` validated that a supplied `boqLineItemId` resolves to a real line item this org owns, but never checked whether that line item is a **parent** (has hierarchical breakdown children). Confirmed live before this fix:

```
POST https://veridian-compliance-ai.vercel.app/api/v1/projexa/work-progress
boqLineItemId = ue03iu630ro2ytrxktofipce   (item 1.01 "Partition wall", 3 real children)
-> HTTP 201
```
(test row `zbpr7if7kbuwsrwqeaycdu6l` created, then deleted again immediately after confirming.)

That is exactly the failure mode WPR-15 forbids: "a parent figure must never be storable directly."

## Fix
`createProgressEntry()` now rejects (400) when the target `boqLineItemId` has at least one other line item pointing at it via `parentLineItemId` (i.e. it has children). This deliberately checks "has children" via a real query, not merely "parentLineItemId is null" -- a standalone leaf line with no breakdown of its own is a legitimate progress-tracking target and must keep working unchanged (confirmed unaffected: R-40's own weighted-sub-task progress tests post against child/leaf line items, none of which have their own children).

This enforces the same invariant already documented on the schema itself (`constructionBoqLineItems.parentLineItemId`'s "CANONICAL CHILD-RATE RULE" comment) and mirrored on the PROJEXA side by `applyWeightedParentRollup()`: a parent/root line's rate and percent are always DERIVED from its children, never independently entered.

## Testing
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` -- clean.
- `bun run lint` -- clean (0 errors; 3 pre-existing unrelated warnings, same ones already known in `data-table.tsx`/`VeriComposer.tsx`).
- Live retest plan (post-merge/deploy): repeat the exact POST above against the parent line item and confirm 400; repeat with a real child line item (e.g. Frame 01) and confirm 201, unaffected.

author: lbm364dl
body:
Closes #607. Refs #881.

**Classification: mechanical.** No coefficient, tolerance or default moves;
`data/livestock_coefs.rda` is untouched. The one thing that made this look like
an expert call — "only whoever ingested the tables knows which spreadsheet the
numbers were read from" — is settled by a checksum rather than by judgement, so
there is no defensible alternative to pick between. #607 was relabelled from
`needs-expert` to `mechanical`; the part that genuinely needs an expert was
split out as #881 and is *not* touched here.

## The defect

Four `gleam_*` topics cited `\doi{10.1088/1748-9326/aad4d8}`, which is the sole
`--as-cran` NOTE on `main` and the persistent CRAN blocker behind #190. The DOI
is **not registered at all**:

* `https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aad4d8` → `HTTP/2 404`
* `https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1088/1748-9326/aad4d8` → `Resource not found`

All fifteen GLEAM `@source` tags also attributed the tables to "MacLeod et al.
(2018) GLEAM 3.0 Supplement S1". That paper is real and irrelevant: Crossref
gives `10.1017/S1751731117001847`, *Animal*, "Invited review: A position on the
Global Livestock Environmental Assessment Model (GLEAM)", MacLeod, Vellinga,
Opio, Falcucci, Tempio, … — a position paper that publishes none of these
tables. The DOI was never a real reference; the commit that introduced it
(1ec4d197) has a truncated, tool-mangled message, and the citation looks
generated rather than looked up.

## Where the numbers actually come from

Established from the file rather than assumed. `data-raw/GLEAM_3.0_Supplement_S1.xlsx`
is **byte-identical** to the workbook FAO publishes:

```
149119 bytes, md5 207e3e928c176b2189e520bddcb0c5f6
https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/gleam/docs/GLEAM_3.0_Supplement_S1.xlsx
(HTTP 200, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
```

Its OOXML metadata names `FAO of the UN` as the company, `Monica Rulli (AGAL)`
as creator and `Giuseppe Tempio` as last editor, and is dated `2022-12-20`. Its
23 sheets are exactly `Table of contents`, `Tab. S.3.1` … `Tab. S.9.1`,
`Tab. S.A1-S.A2` — the table numbers the `@source` tags cite. The parent
document, "Global Livestock Environmental Assessment Model, Version 3.0 - Model
description", is dated 10/12/2022 on <https://www.fao.org/gleam/resources/en/>.

**Neither carries a DOI.** Crossref holds no GLEAM 3.0 model-description record
(searched by title, and across the whole FAO `10.4060` prefix), and the
FAO-style `10.4060/cd8425en` derived from the OpenKnowledge handle does not
resolve. So per CLAUDE.md the citation is title + URL, not a substituted
plausible-looking DOI.

## What changed

* The **twelve** tables parsed out of the workbook now read, e.g.

  ```
  #' @source FAO (2022) GLEAM version 3.0, Supplement S1 (an FAO
  #'   workbook; no DOI is issued for it), Table S.3.1:
  #'   \url{https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/gleam/docs/GLEAM_3.0_Supplement_S1.xlsx}
  ```

* A provenance comment at the top of `R/livestock_coefs.R` and in
  `data-raw/livestock_coefficients.R` records the checksum, the dates, and the
  fact that both candidate DOIs were checked and rejected — at the point of use,
  not only here.
* The **other five** GLEAM-labelled tables are not in that workbook at all.
  They are hardcoded `tribble()`s in `generate_gleam_pdf_tables()` with round
  placeholder values (MMS shares of exactly 60/30/10 %, cattle weights of
  exactly 650/1000/600/400 kg). Their `@source` now says they are untraced and
  unverified instead of naming a source they do not have. **`gleam_animal_weights`
  is consumed by `R/livestock_energy.R` as the fallback live weight for the
  Tier 2 energy calculation**, so that one is result-affecting — filed as **#881**
  (`needs-expert`), deliberately not "fixed" here by guessing a table.

No data object changes, so no published value changes.

## Evidence

`tests/testthat/test_livestock_coefs.R` (new) gates all three facts offline —
no network, no `WHEP_*` path — reading the checkout the way
`test_data_raw_freshness.R` does, and skipping where `man/`/`data-raw/` are
absent:

1. no `\doi{}` or `doi.org` citation of the unregistered DOI anywhere in `R/`
   or `man/`;
2. every one of the twelve workbook-derived topics cites the workbook URL — an
   invariant over the list, not a spot check, so a new table cannot arrive
   uncited;
3. the committed workbook still matches the md5 the citation was verified
   against, so the citation cannot silently outlive the file it describes.

Failing on unmodified `man/`, before `devtools::document()`:

```
Failure ('test_livestock_coefs.R:60:3'): no documentation cites the unregistered GLEAM DOI
`offenders` (`actual`) not equal to character(0) (`expected`).

    actual                          | expected
[1] "gleam_crop_residue_params.Rd"  -
[2] "gleam_dressing_percentages.Rd" -
[3] "gleam_energy_use_ef.Rd"        -
[4] "gleam_geographic_hierarchy.Rd" -

Failure ('test_livestock_coefs.R:97:3'): the workbook-derived GLEAM topics cite the FAO workbook
all(cites) is not TRUE
topics not citing the workbook: gleam_crop_residue_params, gleam_crop_residue_nitrogen,
gleam_dressing_percentages, gleam_energy_use_ef, gleam_feed_composition,
gleam_feed_conversion_ratios, gleam_feed_digestibility, gleam_field_operation_ef,
gleam_fracremove, gleam_geographic_hierarchy, gleam_mechanization_levels,
gleam_processing_transport_ef

[ FAIL 2 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 1 ]
```

Passing after: `[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 3 ]`.

### The NOTE, before and after

`rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = c("--no-manual","--as-cran","--ignore-vignettes"))`,
tests enabled, `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false`.

**Before** (`origin/main`, the only NOTE in the run):

```
* checking CRAN incoming feasibility ... [9s/37s] NOTE
Maintainer: 'Catalin Covaci <catalin.covaci@csic.es>'
Version contains large components (0.3.0.9000)
Found the following (possibly) invalid DOIs:
  DOI: 10.1088/1748-9326/aad4d8
    From: man/gleam_crop_residue_params.Rd
          man/gleam_dressing_percentages.Rd
          man/gleam_energy_use_ef.Rd
          man/gleam_geographic_hierarchy.Rd
    Status: 404
    Message: Not Found
```

**After**: the DOI block is gone. The NOTE
survives only as the two items no fix in this repo can remove — the maintainer
line and the development version string:

```
* checking CRAN incoming feasibility ... [9s/32s] NOTE
Maintainer: 'Catalin Covaci <catalin.covaci@csic.es>'
Version contains large components (0.3.0.9000)
Size of tarball: 7793209 bytes
```

No "Found the following (possibly) invalid URLs" block appeared either, so the
FAO workbook URL now cited in twelve `.Rd` files resolves for the checker as
well as for `curl` (HEAD 200, GET 200).

Also verified: `lintr` clean on both changed files, pkgdown parity clean (no
topic added or removed), `air format .` run.

author: zhebil
body:
## What and why

Closes #30. `layers.svg` and `round-trip.svg` carried arrow bends that were
dragged on the canvas and never written back into their sources. `npm run
diagrams` only reproduced them because it reuses a running `serve` and picks
the overlay up on the way past (#38); rendered from source alone, both came out
visibly worse. `<Edge bend>` (#42) exists now, so the numbers go in the source.

```
layers      app-usecases -> domain   bend="-42.8"
            infra-list   -> domain   bend="47.2"
            domain -> infra-list     bend="-105.4"
round-trip  committed -> source      bend="-288.6"
```

The two `-> domain` edges move out of the `<Edges>` block so they can carry a
prop.

Every ported value is roughly half the depth the router picks on its own
(`-42.8` against `-130.3`, `47.2` against `93.4`, `-105.4` against `-167.7`,
and `-288.6` against `-54.1` in the other direction). Most of that difference
was the router sagging an arc to pull two arrowheads apart. #48's face slots
separate them at the attachment instead, so each arc now only has to clear what
is actually in its way. That is why this had to land after #48 rather than
alongside it: ported against the old converged anchors, these numbers draw the
wrong picture.

Two commits follow from the same re-render:

- `pipeline.svg`, `cicd-pipeline.svg` and `kernel.svg` were already drifting
  from their sources, unrelated to any bend. A full `npm run diagrams` picks
  that up. With them committed, every SVG in the repo renders from source
  alone.
- `AGENTS.md` said those two SVGs cannot be reproduced without a running
  `serve`. That is no longer true, and left in place it reads as permission to
  leave a bend on the canvas, so it is replaced by the invariant and the way to
  keep it.

## How it was verified

`npm run check` passes (1013 tests, 76 files).

`npm run diagrams` run with no `tldx serve` up and no `*.overlay.json` anywhere
in the worktree, so every committed SVG here is a from-source render with
nothing merged in from a canvas.

I rendered `layers` and `round-trip` to PNG and compared them against both the
previous from-source render and the canvas state the overlay recorded. `layers`
now shows two clean arcs into `domain/` landing on their own slots instead of
two wide S-curves converging on one point, and the red `never` edge no longer
runs alongside `infra-list -> domain` for most of its length. `round-trip`'s
green `the loop closes here` sweeps clear of the whole column instead of
hugging the boxes it passes.

The bend values themselves came from `layers.tldx.overlay.json` and
`round-trip.tldx.overlay.json`, mapped back to their edges by matching each
arrow shape id against its start and end bindings.

## Notes for the reviewer

**Anchors were not ported, only bends.** The `layers` overlay also holds three
hand-dragged `normalizedAnchor` values. Two of the three were the author doing
by hand what #48's slot pass now does mechanically, and the third
(`app-usecases`' start at `0.747, 0.395`) is an interior point rather than a
face, which reads oddly as a source-level instruction. #30 is about the bends;
those anchors are better left to the router now that it separates them itself.

---

- [x] `npm run check` passes
- [x] The behaviour is pinned by a test at the layer that owns it (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/zhebil/tldx/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests))
- [x] One topic; commits are split by concern

author: rimioai
body:
## Context A `rimz remote connect` against an alias whose target path no longer exists on the server connected, attached, and birthed a broken room. Two failures sat behind that: Nothing validated the remote path. Remote `rimz start` accepted it because `WorkspaceResolver::resolve_with` never checked existence in `Create` mode: the chdir-`NotFound` from `git_output` mapped to `Ok(None)`, the marker walk found nothing, the bare-directory tier accepted the path, and `normalized_root` fell back to lexical absolutize. Room birth then ran with a bogus cwd, and the user saw only downstream symptoms — an "ignoring workspace pin with a vanished root" warning and later "no live RimZ room". Local `rimz start` had the same bug. The `connecting…` panel also lost its errors. Retry detail rendered only inside the alternate screen, which `LeaveAlternateScreen` discards, so on Ctrl-C the error vanished and only a terse "reconnect stopped" survived. Meanwhile the tracing fmt layer wrote straight to stderr with no terminal coordination, scribbling raw WARN lines over the live frame. ## Design choices **Two fail-fast layers, chosen for different reach.** A `test -d` preflight runs over the already-established ControlMaster inside `wait_for_master`'s `Connected` arm, before handoff — the socket is live, so it costs about one round trip, and the panel is still up to render the failure. It is gated to the initial connect. A version-independent `test -d … || exit 67` guard in the launch snippet covers what the preflight cannot reach: `--no-reconnect`, the interactive fallback, older remote RimZ versions, and a path that vanishes mid-session. **Preflight classification is deliberately conservative.** Only exit `1` means missing. Transport failures and unexpected exits proceed to the attach, which can report the real error, so a network wobble is never misdiagnosed as a missing path. **The root cause is fixed once, in the resolver.** `resolve_with` refuses a nonexistent `Create`-mode root rather than each caller checking. The guard sits below the `root_override` branch so it only fires when the starting path actually determines the root, and the four call sites that resolve a *persisted* task root — which legitimately outlives its directory — share one `WorkspaceResolver::persisted_workspace_id` boundary that resolves a live root and absolutizes a vanished one, so loop-task maintenance keeps working after a project is deleted. **Log capture is real, not suppression.** A `MakeWriter` in `rimz::tui` buffers tracing output while any `TerminalModeGuard` owns the terminal and replays the original bytes to stderr on restore. Warnings stay visible and formatted instead of being silenced or painted over, and every full-screen surface benefits, not just the connect panel. **On failure the panel holds.** A missing path repaints the panel as a red error frame carrying the fix and the five most recent captured warnings, waits for a keypress, restores the terminal, and lets the normal CLI report write the error to scrollback. ## Implementation The resolver refuses missing `Create`-mode roots; `delivery_target_alive`, `FireContext::resolve`, `newest_active_run_for_entry`, and `loop stop` route through `WorkspaceResolver::persisted_workspace_id`, which resolves a live root and absolutizes a vanished one, so the delivery reaper still reaps, a `Deliver` task still self-removes via `TargetGone`, and an active run is still stoppable. `stop_supervised_run` split out `cancel_supervised_run` so a vanished root cancels the run without the pane close that needs a workspace. On the remote side, `SshAttachPlan::path_preflight` compiles the probe for path targets only, `remote_path_guard` adds the snippet sentinel through the shared `remote_exec_snippet` — which also serves web prep, so web gets the guard too — and exit `67` joins the fatal sentinels. `fatal_session_message` dispatches on that code and rebuilds the message from the typed target path, so captured stderr never truncates the path or repeats the fix line; `run_web_prep` gained the same sentinel, which previously fell through to a bare exit-status message. `TuiLogWriter` routes tracing into a 64 KiB capped buffer while a guard is active. The session picker settles its handoff before re-entering the alt screen, keeping capture balanced and putting buffered warnings into scrollback. Interrupt paths now name the host and the last SSH error instead of a bare "stopped". Two deviations from the plan. The snippet guard applies through the shared helper rather than attach-only, because `remote_exec_snippet` also serves web prep. And `crates/rimz/src/remote` and `tui.rs` both sat exactly at their `refactor-target.toml` surface budgets: the first implementation traded away named API to fit, which produced string-matching on remote stderr, dummy-frame construction, and a bare `mem::forget` in place of a documented lifecycle method. Review rejected that trade. The budgets are raised by the items actually needed (`remote` 172→175, `tui.rs` 15→16), with the rationale recorded beside each entry. Covered by unit tests for the resolver guard, preflight argv and quoting, snippet contents, exit classification, sentinel message rebuilding, failure-frame rows, and bounded capture; by three vanished-root regressions in their owning modules; and by end-to-end tests driving a mock SSH shim that assert the tty attach never runs when the probe reports a missing path, that an existing path preflights before attaching, and that session targets skip the probe entirely. ## Advisories - A sibling family still hashes the persisted task root raw: `run_lock_path`, `fire.rs`'s ownership check, `loop run`, `loop run-report`, and task arming call `WorkspaceId::from_project_root` on `entry.resolved_root()` instead of the new boundary. This predates the change and is identical for an absolute normalized root; only a hand-edited relative or dotted persisted root splits the two conventions. Routing that family through `persisted_workspace_id` too would retire the class. - On the interactive-fallback attach, stderr is inherited, so the snippet's own echo reaches the terminal and the rebuilt message prints after it. Both now say the same thing; before, the second line was a generic status. Still duplicated on that path. - No PTY-driven test asserts the blocking keypress and alternate-screen teardown itself. Frame content, capture routing, and the process decisions are covered; the hold lifecycle rests on unit tests plus a manual smoke. - The live remote smoke could not be completed: SSH to the host timed out before reaching the path probe. The local refusal was verified directly, and the mock-SSH suite covers the remote preflight and no-attach guarantee. - The outage panel keeps its hard-coded crossterm colors. Migrating it onto the shared theme accessors is a follow-up, unrelated to the failure lifecycle. - `preserve_for_reexec` may drop a nonempty capture buffer at exec time; the upgrade path is noted in code.

body:
## Summary

Declares `0.10.13` as the next release version so the release train can cut an rc for it.

`v0.10.12` is already tagged — **both** `v0.10.12` and `v0.10.12-rc.1` exist — and the delta waiting on `develop` touches `internal/doctor/doctor.go`, under the `internal/*` publish_path in release-train's `repos.yml`:

- #563 `fix(release): retry the cosign call, bounded and transient-only`
- #564 `feat(doctor): measure disk, the dimension it never looked at`

With `VERSION` still reading `0.10.12`, the staging hop's version preflight refuses:

```
rc NOT tagged - v0.10.12 already exists and the delta DOES touch published files
(bump VERSION on develop before the next release)
```

**Measured, not inferred:** the `cli` leg hit this on the 2026-08-25 staging hop and `cli` sat the hop out while the rest of the fleet rode. It cannot ride any hop until this lands.

Same shape as #562 (the `0.10.12` bump) one day earlier. Worth stating the pattern out loud: **each hop that ships published files needs its own bump**, because the previous bump is consumed by the hop that shipped it. This is the second consecutive day the `cli` leg has been the only repo held for this reason.

Patch-level, matching the whole `0.10.x` series.

## Type

chore(release)

## Test plan

No behaviour change. `VERSION` is read by `release.yml` at tag time and by the release train's version preflight; nothing in the binary reads it at runtime.

Verified nothing else in the repo pins the old version:

```
grep -rn "0\.10\.12" --include="*.go" --include="*.sh" --include="*.md" --include="*.yml" .
→ VERSION:1 only
```

File shape is byte-exact — single line, trailing newline preserved (`0.10.13\n`), confirmed with `xxd` — which is what `release.yml` expects.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `develop`
- [x] One self-contained change (`VERSION`, 1 line)
- [x] Assignee set, one reviewer requested
- [x] No secrets, tokens or customer data

> **Low Risk**
> Single-line version stamp only; no application logic, security, or data-path changes.

> **Overview**
> Bumps the repo **`VERSION`** file from **`0.10.12`** to **`0.10.13`** so the release train can tag the next rc after **`v0.10.12`** is already cut.
> 
> This is a **release-metadata-only** change: it unblocks staging/version preflight when **`develop`** has deltas under published paths (e.g. doctor and release fixes queued after **`0.10.12`**), without altering runtime CLI behavior.

## Summary

Remediates CodeQL and security review findings identified following the PR #683 release sync:

### 1. Python Services (Stack Trace / Information Exposure)
- **`llm/benchmark` & `llm/rag-server`**: Replaced direct leakage of `str(e)` in HTTP responses (`dashboard_controller.py`, `migration_controller.py`) with `logger.exception()` and generic client error responses.

### 2. TypeScript / React Frontend (XSS, Open Redirects & Prototype Safety)
- **`app/src/components/common/ds/Link.tsx`**: Added `isSafeLinkHref` protocol validation (`http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`), default fallback to `#`, and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- **`app/src/components/workflow/WorkflowHeader.tsx`**: Validated `returnUrl` origin and pathname before navigation to prevent open redirects.
- **`app/src/components/workflow/utils/taskDescription.ts` & `KubernetesCreateAlert.tsx`**: Switched to explicit typed `switch` statements and `Object.create(null)` with `isSafeObjectKey()` validation to prevent prototype pollution.
- **`app/src/components/k8s/details/KubernetesTracesListing.tsx`, `KubernetesTracesGroupListing.tsx`, `KubernetesLogs.tsx`**: Fixed quote escaping order by escaping backslashes first before quotes.
- **`app/src/components/optimise-new/ResolveModal.tsx` & `useLiveResourceMetrics.ts`**: Tightened URL and provider hostname parsing.

### 3. Go Services (Argument Injection, Integer Bounds & Allocation Safety)
- **`llm/code-analysis/internal/git/client.go`**: Added `--` parameter delimiters to `git fetch origin -- <branch>` and `git remote set-branches --add origin -- <branch>` to prevent option injection from untrusted branch names.
- **`llm/code-analysis/tools/submit_analysis.go`**: Added integer bounds checking before casting float64 line numbers to int.
- **`llm/code-analysis/tools/repo_scope_guard.go`, `api-server/services/relay/service.go`, `llm/llm-server/tools/common_services_server.go`, `api-server/services/dashboard/table_columns.go`, `collector-server/cloud-collector/providers/aws/aws_cloudwatch_metrices_common.go`**: Fixed allocation arithmetic in `make()` slices and maps.

- **Link Protocol Filtering**: Any component relying on non-standard protocols in `<Link>` will now fall back to `#`. Only `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, and `tel:` are permitted.

author: bfrpaulondev
body:
## PX-AI1 — secure administrator AI core

**Task ID(s):** PX-AI1 / #285, coordinated with #284

**Base main SHA:** `b31da9b029013708869290cacd8413db8cca5559`

### User problem solved

Creates the server-side, advisory-only foundation for the Eutaktos administrator assistant. The browser can request a response, but it cannot supply trusted tenant, actor, role or capability values, and it never receives the OpenAI credential.

### What changed

- Added the official OpenAI SDK and a server-only Responses API adapter that explicitly reads `OPENAI_KEY_AGENT`.
- Centralized configurable model selection through `OPENAI_AGENT_MODEL`, with a verified Responses API default and a bounded server-side timeout.
- Added a versioned, repository-controlled agent policy that prohibits autonomous writes, secret disclosure, cross-tenant access and sensitive-trait inference.
- Added `POST /api/agent/respond` through the existing Netlify API adapter.
- Requires an authenticated session plus `tenant.manage` at the endpoint boundary; the request accepts only `message` and rejects browser-supplied identity/capability fields.
- Added narrow read-only tools for tenant-scoped people summaries, explicit availability summaries and approved static help. Each tool independently derives the server context, validates exact arguments and reapplies its own capabilities through existing application services.
- Added metadata-only allowlisted agent telemetry (`agent.requested`, `agent.tool_invoked`, `agent.completed`, `agent.denied`, `agent.failed`). It does not log prompt/response content, tenant/person identifiers, secrets or free-form errors.
- Defined, but did not persist, the tenant-safe administrator feedback contract.

### What intentionally did not change

- No frontend/UI changes.
- No hosting, DNS, Netlify secret or Supabase schema changes.
- No direct model access to SQL/Supabase.
- No write/action tools, no model-directed data mutations and no automatic fine-tuning or conversation memory.
- No duplication of Smart Assign, eligibility, scheduling or PX7 recommendation logic.

### Capabilities/security impact

- Tenant, actor and capabilities are resolved exclusively from the authenticated server session.
- The endpoint rejects caller-provided `tenantId`, `actorId`, `role` and `capabilities` as unknown fields.
- `tenant.manage` gates agent access; `people.read` and `availability.read` are independently rechecked within relevant tools.
- Tools use tenant-filtered database reads and existing application services; cross-tenant/malformed tool attempts fail closed.
- The OpenAI client uses `store: false`, disables SDK logs and keeps the custom API key only in server process memory.

### PII/privacy impact

- Current dynamic tools return only identifiers, display names, active status and explicit availability facts required for an authorized administrative answer.
- They do not return phone numbers, emails, addresses, emergency contacts, free-form notes or eligibility decision provenance.
- Audit telemetry is allowlisted metadata only.

### Tests added/updated

- Endpoint tests: no session, missing administrator capability, forged tenant/actor/capability fields, missing key and secret non-leakage.
- Agent tests: tenant-scoped tool reads, unknown tool/prompt-injection-style requests, malformed tool arguments, independent tool capability denial, zero write tools, abort signal and invalid model response.
- OpenAI adapter tests: custom key/configuration, configurable model, 429/5xx safe mapping and invalid upstream response.
- Router and observability tests remain green.

### Quality commands and results

- `npm run typecheck` — PASS
- `npx vitest run api/agent/*.test.ts api/_netlify.test.ts api/_observability.test.ts` — PASS, 24 tests
- `npm test` — PASS (repository gate, including adversarial regression)

### Remaining work / limitations

- This is the server core only; an authorized Ant Design assistant UI is intentionally deferred to the UI lane.
- Current real-time tools cover people, explicit availability and approved help. Scheduling conflicts, completed-history evidence and PX7 recommendations remain deferred until their existing application-service contracts are selected by the principal; no duplicate scheduling logic was added.
- Feedback persistence is a defined contract only because the repository does not currently expose a reviewed tenant-safe feedback-only storage boundary. It stores no prompts/responses.
- Responses are non-streaming in v1. The client has bounded timeout support; no streaming session is created, so there is no streaming zombie-session surface.

author: sbfnk-bot
body:
Adds the package hex logos to the software page, as a honeycomb index at the top and a logo beside each entry in the list below.

This PR closes #17.

## What changed

- `software.qmd` — `fetch_package_info()` now looks for `man/figures/logo.png`, falling back to `logo.svg`, resolving each repo's default branch rather than assuming one. A second pass over the same data emits the honeycomb.
- `_software-item.Rmd` — the description cell becomes `.pkg-body`, holding the logo beside the text. The contributors column is unchanged.
- `styles.css` — a plate and ring behind each list logo, and the honeycomb layout.

## Both themes

The site ships `flatly` and `darkly`, so no single background is safe: a sticker whose tone matches the current ground loses its edges. Rather than shipping light and dark variants of every logo, each one gets a `drop-shadow` ring that follows the alpha channel and traces the hex outline in whichever direction the ground needs. All the CSS is keyed to `[data-bs-theme="dark"]`, not `prefers-color-scheme`, because Quarto's toggle sets that attribute — a `prefers-color-scheme` rule would follow the reader's OS and ignore the site's own switch.

## Honeycomb

The logos are hex-shaped with transparent surrounds, so they tessellate without any positioning maths: rows overlap vertically by a quarter of the hex height, and alternating row lengths give the half-width stagger. Width is `clamp(46px, 6.4vw, 82px)` so it scales down on narrow screens instead of overflowing. The detailed list is kept below it — a wall alone would drop the description, language, last-updated date and contributor avatars.

Quarto's `link-external-icon: true` appends an icon to every off-site link, which broke the tessellation, so that is suppressed inside the wall only.

## Note

scoringutils will sit slightly proud of the honeycomb until epiforecasts/scoringutils#1225 merges — its logo has a transparent border baked into the file, so it renders smaller than the others at a common width.

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

Delta maintenance's watermark-persist step files an error tracking issue for a database failover it could have quietly retried past. It fired 2600+ times in one run in [this issue](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/error_tracking/01a03847-53da-7410-b247-1662c246d29c), spanning many unrelated schemas within the same short window — a shared-infrastructure blip, not a per-sync bug.

`DeltaMaintenance.run_scheduled` persists the vacuum watermark with `update_sync_type_config_keys`, which locks the schema row with `select_for_update()`. A brief primary failover leaves that lock unable to write, and Postgres raises `ReadOnlySqlTransaction` (SQLSTATE 25006). `is_transient_maintenance_error` already treats a DB connection blip (`OperationalError`/`InterfaceError`) as self-healing and just logs a warning, but psycopg classifies this specific failure under `InternalError`, a sibling class the check didn't cover, so it fell through to `capture_exception` instead.

## Changes

- `is_transient_maintenance_error` now also treats an `InternalError` caused by `psycopg.errors.ReadOnlySqlTransaction` as transient, matching how the same function already treats other DB connection blips.
- The match checks the wrapped psycopg cause, not the whole `InternalError` class, so unrelated internal errors (e.g. data corruption) still get captured.
- No retry logic changes: `run_scheduled` already treats a transient maintenance failure as best-effort and relies on the next scheduled pass to retry the same idempotent watermark update.

## How did you test this code?

- Added two cases to the existing parameterized `TestIsTransientMaintenanceError`: an `InternalError` wrapping `ReadOnlySqlTransaction` classifies as transient, and an `InternalError` wrapping an unrelated psycopg error (`DataCorrupted`) does not — guards against widening the match to the whole `InternalError` class.
- `pytest products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/core/delta/test/test_delta_errors.py` — 34 passed.
- `ruff check`/`ruff format` and `uv run mypy --cache-fine-grained .` (full repo) clean.
- Not run: a live Postgres failover, and `hogli ci:preflight` (not available in this sandbox).

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None — internal error-classification behavior with no documented workflow.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Investigated via PostHog error tracking MCP tools (issue details, sampled exception events with stack traces) and repo search to trace the raise site through `DeltaMaintenance.run_scheduled` → `update_sync_type_config_keys` → Django's `select_for_update()` → psycopg's SQLSTATE 25006. Confirmed via `gh pr list` that four other open PRs from the maintainer (#88295, #88296, #88297, #88299) fix the same `ReadOnlySqlTransaction`/failover root cause, but each patches a different, more generic layer (`posthog/temporal/common/db_errors.py`'s `is_transient_db_error` and `posthog/temporal/common/utils.py`'s retry helpers) that `run_scheduled`'s local best-effort handler never calls into — so this fix is additive, not duplicate.

Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

→ Postgres/ClickHouse/Redis/MinIO stack
→ public API readback
```

## Assertions

- one synthetic Hermes turn trace is actually ingested;
- one synthetic tool observation is actually ingested;
- public API readback returns trace/observation data;
- prompt/tool-argument/tool-result marker strings are absent from server readback in `metadata` mode;
- Langfuse remains observability only: no Evidence, Hindsight, CouchDB or Pantheon governed-state mutation.

## Boundary

```text
trace received != truth
trace received != Evidence
trace received != authorization
Langfuse unavailable != Hermes unavailable
```

No real dossier/client data or real production credentials are used.

author: sebastianschuetze
body:
Aktueller Stand

FounderOps veröffentlicht Grundwochen bereits atomar in Google Calendar und im Team. Bisher fehlte jedoch eine sichere Fortführung ab einem späteren Montag.

Problem

Eine neue Grundwoche darf weder vergangene Kalenderreihen verändern noch während einer teilweise fehlgeschlagenen Synchronisierung einen gemischten Teamstand erzeugen. Gleichzeitige oder veraltete Änderungen müssen stabil abbrechen.

Umsetzung

- versioniert Grundwochen unveränderlich ab einem Montag in Europe/Berlin
- beendet die vorherige Google-Serie per COUNT und ETag-Vorbedingung
- hält die bisher veröffentlichte Woche sichtbar, bis neue Serien und alle Übergänge bestätigt sind
- speichert Übergänge dauerhaft und nimmt verzögerte Läufe ohne Doppel-Schreibvorgänge wieder auf
- unterscheidet im privaten und im Team-Bereich zwischen aktuell veröffentlicht, vorbereitet und verzögert
- migriert bestehende Veröffentlichungen deterministisch, ohne bestätigte Google-Marker umzuschreiben
- hält Provider-IDs und Übergangsdaten eigentümerprivat

Warum das zählt

Damit lassen sich künftige Arbeitswochen vorbereiten, ohne Historie oder laufende Teamansicht zu beschädigen. Teilfehler bleiben reparierbar und werden erst nach vollständiger Bestätigung sichtbar.

Verifikation

- 850 Tests erfolgreich
- ESLint erfolgreich
- Next.js-Produktionsbuild erfolgreich
- Migrations-, Supabase- und lokale Datenbank-Sicherheitsprüfung erfolgreich
- Product-Update-Klassifizierung gegen den direkten Stack-Basisbranch erfolgreich
- Desktop- und Mobile-Ansicht geprüft
- Upgrade von zwei bestehenden veröffentlichten und zwei vorbereiteten Legacy-Versionen lokal geprüft
- keine produktive Datenbank-, Google- oder Deployment-Mutation

Closes #390

author: vandyckmed-droid
body:
A comprehensive UX/UI audit of the stock-detail chart, benchmarked against TradingView's mobile manipulation quality while preserving the app's Robinhood-style restraint. **Audit and plan only — nothing is implemented.**

## What this adds

- `docs/archive/2026-08-25-chart-ux-audit.md` — the ranked audit and phased implementation plan
- `docs/archive/README.md` — index row (the plan is explicitly marked **pending execution**)

## Method

Eleven parallel review passes across chart dimensions (gestures, zoom/pan mechanics, rendering, axes, integration, animation, performance, overlays, accessibility, test pins, TradingView benchmark) plus five interaction-design passes for the mandated capabilities; every current-behavior claim adversarially re-verified against source (one finding refuted and dropped, several corrected); and a live product session — the built web bundle driven with synthetic touch at iPhone geometry in both palettes, with measurements (vertical-spread zoom confirmed 56→25 bars; integer chip stepping recorded; 60fps / zero long tasks during the heaviest pinch on a 9–38-node SVG).

## Shape of the audit

- **A — Must fix (20):** pinch inverts below the 12-bar floor on 1W/early-YTD; vertical spread zooms the time axis; candles smear by paint order at 1Y+; the 1D hero and the list row disagree about "today" (session-open vs close-over-close baselines); hero mislabels stale data as 1D; the pulse outlives the market and bundles never revalidate; off-range MA lines cross the axis strip; morph ignores reduce-motion and pops on mid-flight retarget; every gesture frame re-renders the whole screen; the chart is invisible to screen readers; desktop has no zoom path at all; the gesture-claim layer has no test coverage.
- **B — Major upgrades (21):** continuous fractional view state with gesture-frozen y (the single largest feel gap); pan inertia and edge feel; long-press crosshair; a transient, never-persisted manipulable price axis; a fullscreen chart workspace (plus an immediate landscape-misfire fix); a four-class motion/continuity system; a self-documenting reset grammar with gliding resets; line-mode interaction-scoped disclosure; last-price axis tag; OHLC scrub readout; hollow up-candles; loading states that keep the chart mounted; and more.
- **C — Polish (16)** and **D — Do not change (20):** the protected strengths — the one-responder grammar, the integer onView payload, overlay causality, the node budget, the ink ladder, the anti-chrome discipline — each tied to its test pins.
- **§6** defines the single interaction system (grammar table, continuous view, axis handle, reset grammar, motion system, fullscreen, desktop pointer map, deliberate refusals); **§7** sequences it into eight dependency-ordered phases with per-phase test impact; **§8** describes the target feel.

## Verification

- `npm test`: all 35 suites passed — 947 checks (docs-only change).
- Every file:line citation in the audit was re-verified against source during the adversarial pass; verifier corrections are folded into the text.

author: singyichen
body:
## Purpose（目的）

為前端補上共用的 API 存取基礎建設：`api-client`、`query-client`、`QUERY_KEYS` 與手寫暫代型別，讓後續 feature slice 有一致的網路層可用（OpenSpec change `implement-foundation-core` 群組 6，任務 6.1–6.3）。

## Reason（原因）

群組 5 只落地了 Vite/React scaffold 與 ESLint 邊界規則，尚無任何呼叫後端的途徑。群組 7 的 `HealthCheckPage` 需要一個能解析 `ErrorResponse` 信封（FR-115）、傳遞 `X-Correlation-ID`（FR-046）、且 401 不重試（SC-020 第一子句）的用戶端；這些跨 feature 的共用件依 `shared/` admission rule 必須先獨立落地。

## Result（成果）

| 交付項 | 對應需求 | 說明 |
|---|---|---|
| `shared/services/api-client.ts` | FR-041 / FR-046 / FR-115 | `fetch` 包裝：解析 JSON、暴露 correlation id、非 2xx 丟 `ApiRequestError` |
| `shared/services/query-client.ts` | SC-020（第一子句） | `QueryClient` retry callback：401 不重試，其餘重試 3 次 |
| `shared/constants/query-keys.ts` | SC-019（前半段） | 集中式 query key 常數 |
| `shared/types/api.ts` | design.md 非目標「手寫暫代型別」 | 逐欄對照 `backend/app/schemas/common.py` 手寫 |
| `src/__tests__/eslint-boundaries.test.ts` | 任務 6.3 | 邊界規則回歸測試，已用 mutation 驗證（把規則關成 `off` → 3 測試中 2 紅） |

### 審查期間發現並修正的三個真實缺陷

| 缺陷 | 影響 |
|---|---|
| `expose_headers` 未設定 | `X-Correlation-ID` 不是 CORS safelisted response header，Starlette 的 `expose_headers` 預設為空 ⇒ 跨網域前端 `headers.get()` 讀到 `null`。MSW 不執行 safelist，所以前端測試不會揪出來，只能在後端補測試 |
| `credentials: 'include'` 硬寫死 | 後端 `allow_credentials=False` ⇒ 瀏覽器會整個扣住回應。同時 `Content-Type` 無條件設定會讓每個無 body 的 GET 觸發 preflight |
| 2xx 回應 body 壞掉會靜默變成 `undefined` | 截斷的串流／proxy 損壞與 `204 No Content` 無法區分，呼叫端拿到 `{ data: undefined }` 卻毫無訊號。已改為丟出保留 correlation id 的 `ApiRequestError` |

## Changed Files（變更檔案）

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `frontend/src/shared/services/api-client.ts` | 新增；`fetch` 包裝與 `ApiRequestError` |
| `frontend/src/shared/services/query-client.ts` | 新增；401 不重試的 `QueryClient` |
| `frontend/src/shared/constants/query-keys.ts` | 新增；query key 常數 |
| `frontend/src/shared/types/api.ts` | 新增；`ErrorDetail` / `ErrorResponse` / `PaginatedResponse<T>` 暫代型別 |
| `frontend/src/testing/{msw-server,setup}.ts` | 新增；MSW server 與 Vitest setup |
| `frontend/src/vite-env.d.ts` | 宣告 `VITE_API_BASE_URL`，堵住 `ImportMetaEnv` fallback index signature 造成的隱性 `any` |
| `frontend/vite.config.ts` | 加上 Vitest 設定區塊 |
| `frontend/package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` | 加入 `@tanstack/react-query`、`vitest`、`msw` |
| `frontend/src/**/__tests__/*.ts` | 新增 3 個測試檔（12 測試） |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `frontend-lint` job 補上 `pnpm test` 步驟 |
| `.gitignore` | 忽略邊界測試產生的暫時 fixture 目錄 |
| `backend/app/main.py` | CORS 加上 `expose_headers=[CORRELATION_ID_HEADER]`（一行） |
| `backend/tests/core/test_health.py` | 上述行為的 RED→GREEN 測試 |
| `openspec/changes/implement-foundation-core/{design.md,tasks.md}` | SC-020 第二子句延後說明、6.1–6.3 打勾、新增任務 7.3 |

## Test Plan（測試計畫）

前端（`frontend/`，`nvm use 20`）：

- [x] `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- [x] `corepack pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `corepack pnpm lint`
- [x] `corepack pnpm test` — 3 檔 / 12 測試全過
- [x] `corepack pnpm build`
- [x] `corepack pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` — 無已知漏洞
- [x] 以 CI 釘選的 pnpm 9.15.9 重跑 install + test，同樣綠

後端（`backend/`）：

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — 58 passed, 3 skipped
- [x] `uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=80`
- [x] `uv run mypy .` — 37 source files, no issues
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` + `uv run ruff format --check .`（先清 `.ruff_cache` 避免假綠）
- [x] `uv run --no-dev --with pip-audit pip-audit --desc`

OpenSpec：

- [x] `openspec validate --changes --no-interactive` — 1 passed

審查（`docs/sdd-workflow.md` §8 規則①）：

- [x] senior-code-reviewer 第一輪：REQUEST CHANGES（6 項全修）
- [x] senior-qa 情境驗收：ACCEPT WITH RESERVATIONS（逐項 mutation 驗證；唯一保留＝SC-019 強制機制目前僅靠「沒有違規者」成立，已轉為任務 7.3）

body: Merging a product PR to main should bump ApplicationVersion with no extra human steps (no Approve and run, no merging a bump PR, no approving bump-PR CI). ## Why #66 asked for approval `github-actions[bot]` opened PR #66. GitHub queued CI - Build & Test on pull_request with conclusion action_required and no jobs. That is the first-time contributor / bot workflow-approval gate: it fires at the platform before any job if. A maintainer must click Approve and run. Job-level skips cannot prevent that if the workflow is triggered. Separately, Increment could not squash-merge: required reviews. --auto failed because allow_auto_merge is false. Workflow YAML cannot override required reviews on main. ## What this PR changes - ci.yml: do not queue CI for Version.props-only bump PRs (paths-ignore). Belt-and-suspenders job skip for github-actions[bot], branch ci/increment-application-version-*, and title ci: auto-increment* (and the same commit messages on push to main). Product CI on main is unchanged. - increment-build-version.yml: open the GH006-safe bump PR with GITHUB_TOKEN (never git push origin main with that token), then squash-merge immediately — no wait for CI Complete, no --auto. If GITHUB_TOKEN cannot merge, use optional secret VERSION_BUMP_TOKEN with gh pr merge --admin. Unique max(Version.props, open bump PRs)+1 and CD dispatch are unchanged; skip guard still blocks increment loops. The job fails after CD if the bump did not land. ## Repo setting that must stay on Settings → Actions → General → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests — required so the bot can open the bump PR. ## Branch protection GitHub still requires (YAML cannot do this) On the main branch protection rule or ruleset, allow github-actions[bot] to bypass required pull requests, required reviews, and required status checks, OR add repo secret VERSION_BUMP_TOKEN for an actor that can bypass those rules. Without that, Increment will still open a bump PR and fail to merge.

body:
## What

Two things, both documentation only. No product code changes, so this does not
trigger an Xcode Cloud build.

### Filing

The three plans whose work has shipped move out of `docs/` and into `plans/`,
which already had the numbering convention and a status vocabulary:

| from | to |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/PLAN-M5-TAURI.md` | `plans/003-tauri-desktop.md` |
| `docs/PLAN-3.1.0.md` | `plans/004-shift-model-3.1.0.md` |
| `docs/PLAN-3.0.md` | `plans/005-product-3.0.md` |

`PLAN-MOBILE.md` and `PLAN-MSSTORE.md` stay in `docs/`. They are still being
executed, and `next.config.mjs`, `config/site.ts` and `AGENTS.md` cite them by
path as the reasoning behind decisions in the code — moving them would break
those anchors for no gain.

Every reference was rewritten and all 68 relative links re-checked. One dead
link in 005 predates this move (it points at a route file deleted in `9aa81a0`)
and is left as the record of what the plan said at the time.

`plans/README.md` becomes a general index rather than an animation-only one.

### The 002 roadmap

Adds `plans/002-records-life-focus.md`, covering recorded hours, the life view
and the pomodoro board. Its premise is that the app currently has **no memory at
all**: every "this week / this year" figure is projected from the schedule, and
the countdown's start time is not even persisted. So the first deliverable is a
recorder with no UI — hours that are not written down cannot be recovered later.

Delivery order, per the product decision:

```
P0  foundation: recorded hours + CloudKit + StoreKit + privacy copy/labels
P1  records + life view        <- same release
P2  todos and pomodoro         <- separate, last
```

Two load-bearing constraints the doc pins down:

- **Grandfathering paid users is not fixable after the fact.** Reading
  `AppTransaction.shared.originalAppVersion` has to be in the build *before* the
  subscription ships, so it can be written and tested now.
- **A lapsed subscription must never stop recording.** The paywall goes on the
  UI, never on the write path.

It also records that mainland-China iCloud is operated by GCBD, which caps how
strongly the privacy copy can be worded — "synced to your own iCloud, we have no
server" holds everywhere, "only Apple can see it" does not.

## Test plan

Documentation only. Relative links verified programmatically; no build or test
behaviour changes.

author: emilbon99
body:
# Issue Pull Request ## Linear Issue [SY-4736](https://linear.app/synnax/issue/SY-4736/prevent-one-hung-gap-read-from-blocking-all-telemetry-reads) ## Description Found replicating the v0.57 incident: the Feed's `Reader` holds one mutex across every remote gap fetch, and a fetch has no timeout. One remote read that never settles (for example a half-open socket) permanently blocks same-batch reads whose own fetches succeeded, every later batch on any channel, and `close()`. No error surfaces; only a clean TCP close recovers. The lock-across-fetch shape was inherited from the Pluto reader, where it guarded a shared live request set. The 0.57 rewrite replaced that set with per-window immutable entry arrays, so the reason no longer exists. The cache already tolerates interleaved writes: the streamer writes into it with no coordination, and the insertion planner trims or discards overlap. Changes: - Drop the mutex. Batches plan and write synchronously; fetches run unlocked. - Settle each read when its own fetches settle, so a hung fetch starves only the read that owns it. - `close()` rejects every pending read immediately and discards late fetch results instead of waiting for the batch in flight. - Bound each fetch with a deadline (`fetchTimeout`, default 30 seconds) that rejects the reads it serves with a freighter `Unreachable` error. ## Basic Readiness - [ ] I have performed a self-review of my code. - [ ] I have added relevant tests to cover the changes to CI. - [ ] I have updated user-facing documentation accordingly.

Greptile Summary

This PR removes global serialization from cached telemetry gap reads, adds per-read fetch tracking and deadlines, and makes reader shutdown reject pending operations promptly. - Allows successful reads and later batches to settle independently of a hung fetch. - Adds a configurable 30-second default fetch timeout surfaced as `Unreachable`. - Discards late results after close and adds focused timeout, concurrency, multi-gap, and shutdown tests.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with only a non-blocking test-helper naming issue to correct. The new concurrency, timeout, and shutdown paths preserve per-read settlement and allow later batches to progress independently; the only accepted concern is the fixture helper’s repository-inconsistent name. **Files Needing Attention:** client/ts/src/framer/cache/reader.spec.ts

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | client/ts/src/framer/cache/reader.ts | Replaces mutex-serialized batch reads with independent fetch tracking, bounded deadlines, and prompt close semantics; no blocking correctness defect was established. | | client/ts/src/framer/cache/reader.spec.ts | Adds strong coverage for hung fetch isolation, deadlines, close behavior, and multi-fetch reads, with one repository naming-convention violation. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant Reader participant Batcher participant Remote participant Cache Caller->>Reader: read(range, channel) Reader->>Batcher: enqueue gaps Batcher->>Reader: execute batch par Independent gap fetches Reader->>Remote: fetch gap A Reader->>Remote: fetch gap B end Remote-->>Reader: gap A result Reader->>Cache: write gap A Reader-->>Caller: settle reads served by A Note over Reader,Remote: Gap B may remain pending until its deadline Remote--xReader: gap B timeout Reader-->>Caller: reject reads served by B Note over Reader: close() rejects all tracked reads immediately ``` Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["SY-4736: Prevent one hung gap read from ..."](https://github.com/synnaxlabs/synnax/commit/9c93b04095556b1758c439caec925643cfb6667a) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=56604699) > Greptile also left **1 inline comment** on this PR. **Context used:** - Context used - CLAUDE.md ([source](https://github.com/synnaxlabs/synnax/blob/main/CLAUDE.md))
