body:
## Summary
- Added todo-specific mock data for the home page seed list.
- Replaced the placeholder home page with local-state add, toggle, delete, count, and empty-state UI.
- Updated the app shell test to assert the todo route content.
- Added React Testing Library coverage for seeded todos and todo interactions.
- Delegated root build/test scripts to the web workspace so the final gate runs the app checks.

<details>
<summary>Plan from XHawk</summary>

## Contents


- [Implementation checklist](#implementation-checklist)
- [The situation and the change](#the-situation-and-the-change)
- [Risks and things to watch](#risks-and-things-to-watch)
- [Design flow diagram](#design-flow-diagram)
- [The code changes](#the-code-changes)
- [How we'll know it works](#how-well-know-it-works)
- [Files changed](#files-changed)
- [Verify (final gate)](#verify-final-gate)


---


## Implementation checklist


- Add a todo-specific mock data module so the home page has explicit frontend-only seed data independent of the issue mocks.

- Replace the placeholder home page with a local-state todo UI that can add, toggle, delete, and summarize todos without backend persistence.

- Update the app-shell test so it validates the new home route behavior instead of the old placeholder heading.

- Add focused home page interaction tests so the required todo workflow is covered end to end in React Testing Library.


---


## The situation and the change


The web app currently has a placeholder home page, so it does not yet provide the frontend-only todo workflow the task asks for: add, delete, and mark-done behavior backed by mock data.


What happens today:


- `apps/web/src/main.jsx` mounts `App` inside `BrowserRouter`, so user-visible frontend behavior flows through the React app shell.
- `apps/web/src/App.jsx` renders the navigation and routes `/` to `Home` via the `Home` component.
- `apps/web/src/pages/Home.jsx` only renders a static `Home` heading, so there is no todo state, seed data, form, delete action, or done toggle.
- `apps/web/src/App.test.jsx` only checks that the navigation and placeholder home heading render.
- `apps/web/src/mocks/issue.js` shows the existing convention for local ESM mock utility modules, but it is issue-specific and should not be reused for todos.


Build the todo app as a client-only React page in `apps/web/src/pages/Home.jsx`, seeded from a new todo-specific mock module in `apps/web/src/mocks/todos.js`. The page should keep todos in `useState`, support adding non-empty items from a form, toggle completion from a checkbox or button, delete rows immediately, and render empty-state/count feedback so the UI always reflects the current in-memory state.


This deliberately does not add backend routes, persistence, routing changes, or global state management. The requirement is frontend-only mock data, and the existing app is small enough that local page state is the cleanest fit.


---


## Risks and things to watch


> **Watch out:** keep todos immutable and keyed by stable mock ids, or delete/toggle can affect the wrong row after additions.


| Risk | Why it matters | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Placeholder test drift | `apps/web/src/App.test.jsx` currently expects the old heading | Update it to assert the new default todo page instead of `Home` |
| Empty todo submissions | Blank items make the UI noisy and tests flaky | Trim input and ignore empty submissions |
| Duplicate ids | React keys and update/delete logic break when ids collide | Derive each new id from the current maximum todo id before appending |
| Mock data mutation | Mutating imported mock objects leaks state between renders/tests | Clone `mockTodos` into component state before editing |


---


## Design flow diagram


```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["main.jsx render"] --> B["App() routes"]
  B --> C["Home()"]
  D["mockTodos"] --> C
  C --> E["useState(todo list)"]
  F["Submit add form"] --> G{"trimmed text exists?"}
  G -->|Yes| H["append todo with next id"]
  G -->|No| I["leave list unchanged"]
  J["Toggle done control"] --> K["map todo.completed"]
  L["Delete control"] --> M["filter todo by id"]
  H --> N["render updated list and counts"]
  K --> N
  M --> N
  I --> N
```


---


## The code changes


1. Create `apps/web/src/mocks/todos.js` with an exported `mockTodos` array. Each todo should have an `id`, `title`, and `completed` boolean so the mock shape is explicit and independent from the existing GitHub issue mocks in `apps/web/src/mocks/issue.js`.

2. Replace the placeholder in `apps/web/src/pages/Home.jsx` with the full todo UI. Import React state support and `mockTodos`, initialize local state from cloned mock data, and render a clean todo card with a title, form input, add button, list rows, done controls, delete buttons, completed styling, counts, and an empty state when the list is empty.

3. Keep all todo operations local to `apps/web/src/pages/Home.jsx`. `handleAddTodo` should trim the input, ignore blank submissions, derive the next id from the current list, append a new active todo, and clear the input. `handleToggleTodo` should flip `completed` for the selected id, and `handleDeleteTodo` should filter the selected id out. Use functional `setTodos` updates so quick interactions apply to the latest state.

4. Update `apps/web/src/App.test.jsx` so the app shell test still verifies navigation but expects the new todo page content rendered at `/`, such as the `Todo App` heading and seeded mock todo items.

5. Add `apps/web/src/pages/Home.test.jsx` covering the behavior: seeded mock todos render, a user can add a new todo and see it in the list, empty input is ignored, toggling marks an item done in the UI, and deleting removes the item. Use React Testing Library events consistent with the existing Jest setup in `apps/web/setupTests.js` and `apps/web/jest.config.cjs`.


Do not modify `apps/web/src/mocks/issue.js` or `apps/web/src/__tests__/issueMock.test.js`; they are only useful as style references for local mock modules and tests.


---


## How we'll know it works


Run `pnpm --dir apps/web build` to confirm the Vite app still compiles after the React changes.


Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test -- --runInBand src/App.test.jsx src/pages/Home.test.jsx` to prove the initial mock todos render and that add, delete, and mark-done interactions update the UI without any backend.


---


## Files changed


| File | Action | Anchors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/mocks/todos.js` | create | — |
| `apps/web/src/pages/Home.jsx` | modify | `Home` |
| `apps/web/src/App.test.jsx` | modify | — |
| `apps/web/src/pages/Home.test.jsx` | create | — |


---


## Verify (final gate)


- **build**: `npm run build`
- **tests**: `npm test`

</details>

author: sndth
body:
A plain scalar which begins a line of its own can be continued by lines at the same indentation,
since nothing else on that line owns it:

```yaml
Warning:
  This is an error message
  for the log file
```

The continuation was measured against the indentation of the scalar's own first line, so a line at
that same indentation ended it. The scalar then broke into one token per line, and the deserializer
reported a misleading `The ":" mapping value indicator must be followed after a mapping key.`

A scalar which follows a key on the same line still requires more indented lines, because a line at
the key's indentation belongs to the parent mapping instead. The two cases are told apart by
comparing the scalar's column with the indentation of its line.

Lowering the bar also required naming the things which end a plain scalar explicitly, since the old
rule had been stopping scalars at column 0 as a side effect: a document marker, a `:` or `?`
followed by a space, and a flow collection. `- ` is deliberately not among them, because an indented
one is legitimate content (`AB8U`).

I ran tests and the YAML test suite failing cases go from 100 to 95 with no regressions: `4CQQ`, `NB6Z`, `RZT7` and
`XLQ9` now parse, and `DK4H` is now correctly rejected.

I also added `Deserializer_MultilinePlainScalarInBlockContext`, covering a scalar continued at the same
indentation, one following its key which needs deeper indentation, a document marker ending the
scalar, and `foo\n: bar` still being rejected. One existing expectation in
`LexicalAnalyzer_PlainScalar` changed: `"  foo\n   bar\n  baz"` is now a single token, which is the
same shape the suite requires in `4CQQ`.

---

## Pull Request Checklist

Read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/fktn-k/fkYAML/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) file for detailed information.  

- [x] Changes are described in the pull request or in a referenced [issue](https://github.com/fktn-k/fkYAML/issues).
- [x] The test suite compiles and runs without any error.
- [x] [The code coverage](https://coveralls.io/github/fktn-k/fkYAML) on your branch is 100%.
- [x] The documentation is updated if you added/changed a feature.

## Please don't

- The C++11 support varies between different **compilers** and versions. Please note the [list of supported compilers](https://github.com/fktn-k/fkYAML/blob/develop/README.md#supported-compilers). Some compilers like GCC 4.7 (and earlier), Clang 3.3 (and earlier), or Microsoft Visual Studio 13.0 and earlier are known not to work due to missing or incomplete C++11 support. Please refrain from proposing changes that work around these compiler's limitations with `#ifdef`s or other means.
- Please refrain from proposing changes that would **break [YAML](https://yaml.org/) specifications**. If you propose a conformant extension of YAML to be supported by the library, please motivate this extension.
- Please do not open pull requests that address **multiple issues**.

author: disseqt-tdogra
body:
## Summary

Turns ``@trace_function`` into a first-class traceable decorator for any user function — custom LLM call, retrieval step, business-logic step — with two enhancements on top of the existing decorator:

1. **Auto-capture the function's inputs and return value** onto the span (opt-out per-decorator; opt-out globally via the existing content-capture gate).
2. **Async function support** — the wrapper is chosen automatically based on the decorated callable.

Ships as a **v0.11.2** patch bump (additive; no breaking change).

## What the caller sees

```python
from disseqt_agentic_sdk import DisseqtAgenticClient
from disseqt_agentic_sdk.api.helpers import trace_function
from disseqt_agentic_sdk.enums import SpanKind

client = DisseqtAgenticClient(..., application_id="...")

@trace_function(client, kind=SpanKind.MODEL_EXEC, name="my_custom_llm")
def call_custom_llm(user_id: str, query: str) -> dict:
    return http.post("/llm", json={"q": query}).json()

call_custom_llm("u_123", query="hello")
```

Span now carries:

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| ``agentic.function.inputs`` | ``'{"user_id": "u_123", "query": "hello"}'`` |
| ``agentic.function.output`` | ``'{"answer": "hi"}'`` |

Named-key shape (via ``inspect.signature.bind_partial``) means dashboards can index into individual params (``inputs.user_id``, ``inputs.query``) without re-parsing.

## Design decisions

* **Content-capture gate honored.** Both new attribute keys added to ``_CONTENT_ATTR_KEYS`` — a deployment running ``set_capture_content(False)`` (HIPAA / GDPR / credentials-in-args) gets full redaction, no leak.
* **Truncation.** Values exceeding 20 000 chars are JSON-truncated with ``…[truncated]`` marker. Keeps a single span's wire payload bounded when someone accidentally decorates ``ingest_bulk(50mb_df)``.
* **Serialization.** ``json.dumps(..., default=str)`` covers datetimes / Decimals / UUIDs / pydantic ``__str__``; ``repr()`` fallback for objects json refuses (open sockets, thread handles, C extension types). Never crashes the decorated call.
* **Async detection at decoration time.** ``asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(func)`` is checked once, not per call. Returns async wrapper for coroutines, sync wrapper otherwise.
* **Exception path still captures inputs.** Inputs are stamped at span open (before execution); on exception, output is skipped, span is marked ERROR, original exception propagates. So you can debug a failing decorated call from just the inputs on the ERROR span.
* **Opt-out per-decorator:** ``@trace_function(client, capture_io=False)`` for functions whose args are large blobs or non-serializable handles.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| ``src/disseqt_agentic_sdk/api/helpers.py`` | New ``_serialize_for_span`` + ``_build_inputs_payload`` helpers; ``trace_function`` rewritten to auto-capture + support async |
| ``src/disseqt_agentic_sdk/semantics/agentic.py`` | New ``AgenticAttributes.FUNCTION_INPUTS`` + ``FUNCTION_OUTPUT`` |
| ``src/disseqt_agentic_sdk/instrumentation/_utils.py`` | Both new keys added to ``_CONTENT_ATTR_KEYS`` (gate honored) |
| ``tests/agentic/test_helpers.py`` | New ``TestTraceFunctionIOCapture`` class with 7 regression tests |
| ``CHANGELOG.md`` | ``[Unreleased]`` entry (Release workflow will stamp as ``[0.11.2]``) |

## Test plan

- [x] **7 new regression tests** covering:
  - named-key input capture from positional + keyword args
  - ``capture_io=False`` skips both attributes cleanly
  - ``set_capture_content(False)`` redacts both — including credentials in arg values that would otherwise leak
  - async functions produce the same span shape as sync
  - exception path still captures inputs and marks span ERROR
  - non-JSON-serializable arg (custom class) falls back to ``repr``
  - 100 000-char payload gets truncated (attr < 25 000 chars)
- [x] ``uv run pytest tests/agentic/`` — **299 passed** (was 292)
- [x] ``uv run ruff check .`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run black --check .`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run mypy src/disseqt_agentic_sdk/api/helpers.py`` — 0 new errors (8 pre-existing missing-return-annotations on sibling ``trace_*`` helpers, untouched)

## Release

Ships as **v0.11.2** (patch — additive). Standard flow:

1. Merge this PR — ``pyproject.toml`` stays at ``0.11.1``.
2. Dispatch **Release workflow** with ``bump: patch`` → bumps to ``0.11.2``, stamps CHANGELOG, tags, publishes to PyPI, backend picks up via registry polling.

## Related

- Sits on top of v0.11.1 (application_id required). Compatible with in-flight [#25](https://github.com/DisseqtAI/disseqt-python-sdk/pull/25) (ValueError-instead-of-TypeError for missing required args) — no file overlap.

author: sannguyen01
body:
Follow-up to #38, which merged at `cd1d577` while these three commits were still in flight. They are rebased onto the post-merge `main` — no content from #38 is repeated here.

## 🟢 The suite is green for the first time since 2026-08-22

**412 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed.** Two stale tests, neither a product defect.

### `contact.spec.ts` encoded a contract PR #32 deleted

#32 changed a missing `RESEND_API_KEY` from a fabricated `{success:true}` to an honest `503` — *"a missing key is a misconfiguration, not a reason to tell the customer their message arrived"* — updated `api-contact-route.test.ts` in lockstep, and **never touched this file**, whose last commit was 17 days earlier. Line 94 was the fossil:

```ts
// RESEND_API_KEY is not set in E2E env — API returns 200 via graceful degradation
```

`RESEND_API_KEY` appears nowhere in `.github/` or `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer.env`, so CI always takes the 503 branch. Four artifacts agree the error state is intended: the route, #32's unit tests, `api/health`'s doc comment, and `STATE.md`'s `RESEND-KEY-UNWATCHED` item.

**The consequence nobody noticed:** those two tests were the *only* e2e coverage of the success state, and they passed only because the route used to lie. That state has been unverified since #32 while appearing tested. So they're restored **honestly** via `page.route` interception — the technique this file already uses for the failure path — rather than flipped to expect an error, which would have lost that coverage permanently.

Added the assertion whose absence let the drift happen: with no interception, which is what CI actually runs, the form must show the error state, keep the submit button, and **not** show a success message. Verified non-vacuous — stub a 200 into it and it fails on `failed to send message`.

*Side effect:* the route rate-limits 5/hr/IP in-memory, shared across both Playwright projects. Two real submissions × 2 projects × CI retries could reach 8 and turn a 503 into a 429, so the failure mode itself drifted between runs. Now exactly one real submission per project.

### `product-detail.spec.ts:210` raced page render

CI on `cd1d577` failed **5**, not 4 — the fifth being the breadcrumb resolver for `disc-studs-titanium`, failing `expect(hrefs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` with `Received: 0`. The run before recorded the same test as `1 flaky` for `cable-cuff-titanium`. It passes locally every time.

**`evaluateAll` is the one locator method that does not auto-wait.** It resolves against whatever matches at that instant and returns `[]` if nothing does — and `[]` is exactly the value the assertion exists to catch. 418 tests across 2 workers against one `next start` is the load that surfaces it. The existing 30s `request.get` timeout was added for this symptom and guards the line *after* the race.

Fixed by awaiting the breadcrumb's first link before collecting.

## WS-3 — the photography premise became a check that can fail

ADR 008 names its own escalation: *"the right response is to promote the specific premise to a failing check, not to make all of them fail."* Zero coverage had been the reported state for weeks with nothing acting on it.

`productPhotographyPremise` is **removed**, not kept alongside. Its polarity was inverted — `holds: photoCount === 0` treated zero as the premise *holding* — so both would have printed `✗ coverage is zero` a few lines above `✓ premise holds` about the same number.

Follows PR #37's conventions: exported pure `classifyPhotographyCoverage` so both branches run in CI, a named `MIN_PHOTOGRAPHED_PRODUCTS` constant, `featuredImage` to match the numerator `collectPremises` used (**not** `featuredMedia`, which the neighbouring check reads — two numerators would let them disagree about one store), and the `everyProductPublishedToHeadless` zero-denominator guard.

Why it fails where `homepageStripsHaveEnoughProducts` deliberately only observes: a thin scroll strip is a *merchandising* choice, and turning someone's merchandising into a red build is how a signal becomes noise. Zero photography on a brand whose argument is implant-grade metal is the core claim unfulfilled — `STATE.md` already tracks it `blocking`.

**Stated, not buried:** it cannot run until #24 is fixed. `production-smoke.yml` has died at preflight for 30 consecutive runs, so the `0/22` on record is hand-entered, not measured. That's a reason to write it carefully, not loosely — an under-scoped token throws an unevaluable error, so it lands in *Could not be evaluated* and still exits non-zero. It cannot go quietly green (ADR 006).

## WS-4 — `main` is not branch-protected, and five documents said it is

Verified against the GitHub API: **every branch, `main` included, returns `"protected": false`.**

The merge record agrees. PRs #34–#37 were hand-merged with `E2E tests (Playwright)` red — **#34 merged 4m37s *after* that job concluded `failure`**; #35–#37 merged while it was still running. Required checks forbid both; auto-merge merges only after checks settle green. (#38 merged the same way.)

`docs/testing-strategy.md` **contradicted itself eight lines apart** — line 7 correctly said the repo enforces no required checks; line 280 said `main` requires both.

Two things make this worse than a stale doc:

1. **The safety argument depended on it.** `docs/safety.md` and `loop-constraints.md` permit auto-merge *on the grounds that* the gate decides safety. Real permission, no gate under it — ADR 006's shape with nothing underneath.
2. **The obvious remedy is booby-trapped.** `verify`/`e2e` are *job IDs*; GitHub publishes check runs under the job's `name:`. The real contexts are `Lint · Type-check · Unit tests · Build` and `E2E tests (Playwright)`. Requiring the documented strings would register two contexts nothing ever reports — every PR blocked forever, E2E still never gating.

So this adds **no** `vercel.json` `ignoreCommand`. A promotion gate sequenced *before* a merge gate is theatre: `main` auto-deploys with nothing in between, so the merge button already is the deploy button. Instead — ADR 015, all four editable documents corrected (each naming what it used to claim, since the false version was load-bearing in two of them), and `vercel.json` added to `gate.yaml`'s denylist: it holds `buildCommand`, is where any deploy gate would live, and was the one file in that neighbourhood a loop could rewrite.

## ⚠️ Two things for a human — I cannot do either

1. **`production-smoke.yml` line 11 still says "Branch protection requires `verify` and `e2e`".** Denylisted path (`loop-constraints.md`: escalate, don't autonomously edit), so it's named here rather than changed.
2. **Enabling branch protection is a console action.** The precondition the old paragraph correctly identified — *"only reasonable once a passing run existed to enforce against"* — is now met, by this PR. Use the two exact context strings above, **not** `verify`/`e2e`.

Plus the standing one: **issue #24**, which keeps the entire live tier dark.

## Type of Change

- [x] `fix` / `test` / `docs`

## Commerce Impact

- [x] **None** — test guardrails, a smoke-tier check, and documentation. No cart, checkout, pricing or Shopify mutation path.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check` pass
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run` — **1076 tests / 57 files**
- [x] `pnpm e2e` — **412 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed**
- [x] Unit tests for new utilities — `classifyPhotographyCoverage`, both branches plus the empty-store guard
- [x] No hardcoded hex; no secrets committed
- [x] Copy matches the brand identity and PROHIBITED list

## State Update

`STATE.md` gains a dated entry. `docs/adr/015-a-gate-that-was-only-ever-documented.md` is new; the premise removal is recorded as a tombstone note in `scripts/lib/premise-checks.mjs` so the promotion is traceable from where the function used to be.

## Notes for Reviewer

**Merging is deploying.** No promotion step exists. Per `loop-constraints.md` I have not merged and will not.

author: udaykondeti
body:
Two sections of CLAUDE.md described a deployment that no longer exists.

## Edge / TLS

**Was:** an nginx vhost at `nginx/fin.kirakon.com.conf` with Let's Encrypt SSL provisioned by `deploy.sh`.

**Actually:** `fin.kirakon.com` resolves to Cloudflare IPs, `cloudflared` forwards to nginx, and **nginx listens on `127.0.0.1:80` with no TLS config at all**. There is no certificate on the host to renew and nothing provisions one.

Replaced with the real request path plus two operational consequences that cost time today:

- The public URL is generally **unreachable from the Mac Mini itself** — requests hairpin out to Cloudflare and back. A `curl https://fin.kirakon.com` timing out from the box proves nothing. Test the vhost with `curl -H "Host: fin.kirakon.com" http://127.0.0.1/` instead.
- Confirming the site is genuinely up externally requires a browser or another machine.

Also records the **three concurrent `cloudflared` processes** and the `brew services` errors for both cloudflared and nginx as known-unresolved, rather than leaving them undocumented for the next session to rediscover.

## DB_PATH

**Was:** one line, `DB_PATH` (default `./data/finance.db`), with no hint that four separate sources resolve it or that they had drifted apart.

**Now:** a table of all four sources and their values, plus why it matters — `server/index.js` loads dotenv but **most scripts in `scripts/` do not**, so they land on the code fallback. When the fallback and configured path diverge, the app and the seed scripts open different databases and the app comes up healthy and empty while the real data sits elsewhere. That is what #146 fixed.

Adds the check to run after any `pm2 start` or `--update-env`:
```bash
lsof -p "$(pm2 jlist | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="fin-dashboard")|.pid')" | grep finance.db
```

## Smaller corrections

- `~/repos` recorded as the only location for repos
- Pippy's auto-deploy noted as unreliable — it silently missed #139 today, so verify `git log` on the box rather than assuming a merge landed
- Dropped "set secrets via the EC2 environment"; EC2 is decommissioned

## Verified

Every claim checked against the live files before committing — code default, `.env`, `ecosystem.config.js`, `.env.example`, the nginx conf, and `.gitignore` all confirmed to match what the doc now says.

author: realist2022
body:
## What this fixes
`CV_to_Job_Guestimator`'s fine-tuned `cv-guestimator` model was found to reject genuinely correct matches whenever CV evidence didn't literally repeat the requirement's wording (e.g. "Fully Registered Teacher (NZTC)" not recognized as satisfying "New Zealand Practising Certificate"). Traced to two problems in this repo's training data generation:

1. **Prompt/schema drift**: the three system prompts here had fallen out of sync with the consumer's `src/prompts/templates.py`, and — more importantly — training examples never included the JSON-schema suffix Instructor actually appends to every real request (`instructor/v2/providers/openai/handlers.py`). The model was trained on a different input shape than it's served in production.
2. **Literal-matching bias**: every `matched: true` label in the dataset was recoverable by a literal (or ESCO-alt-label) substring check against the CV text, so the model never saw a case where genuinely different wording still satisfies a requirement — and the "near-miss distractor" mechanism actively rewarded treating anything non-literal as false.

## Changes
- Synced the three system prompts to `CV_to_Job_Guestimator`'s current versions (v1.3/v1.2/v1.2).
- Reproduced Instructor's `Mode.JSON` schema-suffix byte-for-byte and appended it to training system prompts, so training input matches what's actually served.
- Brought `src/core/schema.py`'s `Field(description=...)` text in line with the consumer schemas (was previously missing, so the embedded JSON schema text wasn't fully byte-identical either).
- Added `SkillParaphraser` (OpenAI `gpt-4o`, structured outputs): generates and caches a genuinely differently-worded, real-world-equivalent CV phrase for a controlled fraction of matched skills, verified to not just restate the literal term.
- Added a data-grounded gerund-conversion table (~100 verbs, covering ~62% of ESCO's actual leading-word frequency) so literal/alt-label skill names read as natural noun phrases in CV bullets instead of colliding with the bullet templates' own leading verbs.
- Reworded 3 `SKILL_BULLETS` templates that collided with their own gerund forms ("Used" + "using" → "Leveraged", etc.).
- Added a `tqdm` progress bar (`python main.py 02` previously ran silently for ~15-50 min).

## Verification
Regenerated the full 3000-example `dataset.jsonl` twice (before/after the grammar fix), spot-checked rendered CVs and paraphrase quality by hand, confirmed schema-suffix text matches a live-captured production request from the consumer app.

## Known limitations / follow-up
- Gerund table covers ~62% of skill-name leading words by frequency, not exhaustive; rare compound skill names ("prepare and use X") only convert the first verb.
- `_build_experience_example`'s role-relevance labeling has the same literal-overlap pattern as skill_match did — not addressed here, flagged as a follow-up.

author: sileht
body:
The scopes snippets take `base` from the Mergify CI git-refs step and hand it
to a command where a leading `-`, or an embedded space, changes that command's
argument list.

- `migrate-partitions-to-scopes` interpolated `${{ steps.refs.outputs.base }}`
  straight into `run:`, so GitHub substitutes the value before bash parses the
  script. Route it through `env:` and quote it, like every other scopes page
  already does.
- `nx` and `others` left `$BASE` and `$HEAD` unquoted, so a value carrying a
  space splits into extra arguments, which is how the reported case turned one
  ref into three `nx` arguments.
- `bazel` quoted them, but `git diff` still reads a `-`-prefixed value as an
  option: the reported `--output=<path>` truncated a file on the runner.
  `--end-of-options` makes git parse both as revisions, so a `-`-prefixed value
  is a bad ref and git aborts.

Rejecting the ref is only useful if the reader sees it, and `$(git diff | tr)`
returns tr's status, so a rejected ref became an empty scope list behind a green
check. That is the failure the `bazel query` comment on this page already warns
about, so guard the pipelines too: `shell: bash` on the Actions step, an explicit
`set -eo pipefail` for Buildkite, and the same at the head of the shared Mergify
CLI script, which pipes a build tool into jq on every scopes page.

`--` is not the fix here: placed before the revisions it makes git read them as
pathspecs, and the diff comes back empty instead of failing. `--end-of-options`
needs git 2.24, noted inline; below that git ignores the flag and writes the
file, and the pipefail guard is what turns that into a visible failure rather
than a silent empty batch. Turborepo binds both values inside
`--filter="[$BASE...$HEAD]"`, so it needs no change.

Fixes MRGFY-8846

body:
2026-08-25 일일 수집 라운드(가설 우선 3일차)의 등록분입니다.

## 가설
무기한 선물의 펀딩비가 극단으로 오른 구간은 레버리지 롱 쏠림 상태이고, 그 구간은 강제 청산 연쇄에 취약하다. **강제 청산은 정의상 가격에 둔감한 매도**다 — 청산 엔진은 가격이 얼마든 팔아야 한다. 가설이 참이면 과열 구간을 비켜선 곡선이 낙폭에서 이기고, 거짓이면(과열이 그저 강세 신호라면) 오디션에서 진다 — 그 기각도 기록이다.

## 규칙
- 펀딩 > 과거 180봉 분위수(0.9) → 관망, 아니면 보유. 롱 전용.
- 문턱은 **자기 봉 제외 과거만**(shift 후 rolling) — 극단값이 자기 문턱을 끌어올려 자기를 감추는 함정 차단.
- `funding` 컬럼이 없으면(주식·수집 실패) 전부 관망 — "정상 펀딩"과 "몰랐다"를 같게 취급하지 않음.

author: masked-kunsiquat
body:
**Stacked on #98** — base is `test/inset-occlusion-harness`, not `main`. Merge #98 first and this retargets cleanly.

Hardens the harness ahead of #99, which is the work it exists to guard.

## Scroll-to-end replaces the viewport-bounds rule

#98 asserts that a scrolling viewport's bottom edge sits above the keyboard line. That is correct **only while the current padding strategy holds.**

A list that draws behind the system bars with bottom `contentPadding` — what #99 is about to do to every screen here — has a viewport extending past the inset *by design*, while its last row still clears the keyboard. The old rule would have failed that honest code mid-feature, looking exactly like a bug in the feature rather than in the test.

Scroll-to-end asks the question the user actually has. Reachable means *some* scroll offset clears the keyboard; the end of the scroll is the highest a control can get; covered there means covered everywhere. That is indifferent to how padding is arranged, so it survives #99 instead of fighting it.

Scrolling loops until the position stops moving rather than jumping to `maxValue`, because `LazyColumn` reports `maxValue` as an estimate that can be infinite before enough items have measured.

**All seven screens re-falsified individually** against the new rule — strip `contentWindowInsets`, confirm that screen's test fails, restore. All seven do.

## Positive control — from CodeRabbit's review of #98

Good catch, and generalised beyond the one test it was raised on. AGENTS.md §7 already requires asserting the expected thing is present, not only that the forbidden thing is absent, and this harness had been caught by *both* ways of violating it:

- a loading or empty fixture renders no controls and passes trivially;
- Add book's single-result fixture left the results list too short to reach the bottom of the screen, so deleting the inset handling changed no measurable bound.

`assertTheScreenCouldHaveFailed` now rejects both before any occlusion is measured. Verified by shrinking the Add book fixture back to one result, which now fails with the reason instead of passing:

```
This fixture's interactive content stops at y=828.0 px, well above the keyboard
line at y=1773 px, so nothing on it could be covered whether or not the screen
handles insets -- the test would pass either way.
```

Put in the harness rather than in the single test flagged, since every screen in the lane can fail this way and four of them already had.

It is necessary, not sufficient — a fixture can satisfy the precondition and still assert nothing, which is why the falsification sweep stays documented as mandatory.

## Testing

- [x] `./gradlew :shared:jvmTest :shared:testDebugUnitTest :app:testDebugUnitTest` — *CI runs this*
- [x] `./gradlew ktlintCheck :app:lintDebug` — clean
- [x] All seven screens re-falsified against the new rule
- [x] Positive control falsified against the degenerate fixture it exists to reject

No `app/src/main/` or `shared/` code changed.

author: vibechoom
body:
Closes #599.

Built under the settlement on the issue: **option (a), constrained** — generalise the service-side shape into `hytte-reactive`, additive only, give-up in the type's contract, migrate `displays` + Night light and nothing else.

## The survivor: the service-side model, as `hytte_reactive::Pending<T>`

```rust
pub struct Pending<T> {
    confirmed: T,             // the daemon's reading, never guessed at
    intent: Option<Request<T>>, // the user's not-yet-echoed request + its deadline
}
```

`displayed()` prefers the intent, `confirmed()` is the daemon, `is_pending()` drives the spinner. One value rather than a `Mutable<T>` beside a `Mutable<bool>`, so one emission moves both halves and a row can never render "off + spinning".

`NightlightState::{Off, Resolving, On}` maps onto it exactly (`Resolving` = confirmed `false`, intent `true`) and is deleted; the displays panel's `Rc<RefCell<HashMap<String, bool>>>` + 3 s `glib::timeout_add_local_once` is deleted.

### Why this one, on the three criteria

**1. Failure path — the deciding one.** `Pending` reverts, and the give-up is part of the *type*, not each call site's to remember: a request carries the deadline it will be abandoned at (`request(value, grace)` / `deadline()` / `expire(now)`). The two existing waits become two parameterisations — nightlight passes `FIX_WAIT`, displays passes `TOGGLE_GRACE`.

The widget-local model could not revert **at all**. Its 3 s timeout only erased the map entry; nothing re-rendered, and `displays::outputs()` is `PartialEq`-deduped, so a toggle niri never honoured produced *no emission* and left the switch pinned in the user's position indefinitely — until some unrelated topology change happened to rebuild the list. It also mis-handled a rapid double-toggle: each toggle armed its own 3 s timer keyed only by connector name, so toggle #1's timer disarmed toggle #2's intent early.

**2. Service pattern.** The daemon still owns the value (CLAUDE.md's system-daemon-as-state-store); the intent is shell-side optimism riding the same signal every consumer already binds to. So every monitor's drawer agrees, a drawer rebuild loses nothing, and a second surface for the same toggle needs no second copy. `Rc<RefCell<…>>` state private to one panel instance is invisible to the registry and dies with the widget.

**3. Churn — last, and it doesn't decide anything.** One call site either way.

### Additive only

New module `crates/hytte-reactive/src/pending.rs` + two re-export lines. **No change** to the `Service` trait, `Registry`, or any `bind*` contract.

## Migrated call sites

| Site | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/hytte-services/src/nightlight.rs` | `NightlightState` tri-state, `is_on()` / `is_resolving()` / `from_unit_active()` | `Pending<bool>`; `state()` emits it, `enabled()` projects `displayed()`; `announce_wait` calls `request(true, FIX_WAIT)` |
| `trollshell/src/panels/appearance.rs` | `state.is_on()` / `state.is_resolving()` | `*state.displayed()` / `state.is_pending()` |
| `crates/hytte-services/src/displays.rs` | `Output.enabled: bool` | `Output.enabled: Pending<bool>`; new service-side `intents` map, `record` / `merge` / `reconcile` |
| `trollshell/src/panels/displays.rs` | the pending map + `glib` timeout (deleted) | stateless rows: `*o.enabled.displayed()` on the switch, spinner + "Turning on/off…" subtitle on `is_pending()` |

One further file in the diff, `crates/hytte-services/src/networkd.rs`, is a single stale doc-comment sentence that named `NightlightState` as a live type — repointed at `Pending`, no code change.

The losing model is gone, not deprecated: `grep -rn "NightlightState" --include=*.rs` matches only two doc comments naming the retired type historically (`nightlight.rs`, and the `networkd.rs` line above), and `grep -rn "RefCell<HashMap<String, bool>>" --include=*.rs` matches only the two "this is what we removed" comments plus `plugins/pump.rs`'s unrelated per-monitor visibility map. No `NightlightState` declaration and no widget-local pending map survives.

**Not touched:** `trollshell/src/widgets/window_list.rs` (owned by #816) — checked, its `RefCell<HashMap>` is a button cache, not pending state, so no migration was needed there.

**Explicitly out of scope**, per the settlement: the five other silent-wait toggles the issue lists (wallpaper, keep-awake, fullscreen inhibit, bluetooth power, power profile). They can follow this pattern one-by-one without further design — `Pending<T>` plus a grace is all each needs.

## Two behaviour changes worth calling out

- **`TOGGLE_GRACE` is 6 s, not the old 3 s.** At one and a half poll intervals, 3 s could expire a toggle niri was about to honour; that only went unnoticed because clearing the widget-local map re-rendered nothing. ≥ 2 × `POLL_INTERVAL` is the first budget that cannot expire a healthy toggle, and there is a tripwire test on the constant.
- **Toggling back to the state the daemon already reports now cancels the outstanding request** rather than leaving a stale one behind. The old model had the same hole (its map entry survived the on/off/on sequence until its timer fired); `record` removes the entry instead.

## Tests

`Pending` (15 tests, `crates/hytte-reactive/src/pending.rs`) and displays (`crates/hytte-services/src/displays.rs`) cover the three edges the brief asked for, all hermetic — every intent is pinned to a deadline the test chooses and `reconcile` takes its `now`, so nothing reads a wall clock or needs a live niri:

- **confirm arrives** — `the_echo_retires_the_intent_and_the_row_goes_back_to_niri`, `the_derive_loop_retires_an_intent_the_snapshot_confirms`, `Pending::the_echo_retires_the_intent`
- **confirm never arrives (revert)** — `an_intent_that_is_never_echoed_expires_and_the_switch_reverts`, `the_derive_loop_expires_a_stuck_intent_on_its_own_tick`, `Pending::expiry_reverts_to_the_daemons_reading_and_only_at_the_deadline`, plus `a_poll_tick_does_not_extend_an_outstanding_intent` (the deadline belongs to the request, so re-running reconcile every 2 s can't push the give-up out forever)
- **rapid double-toggle** — `a_later_toggle_carries_its_own_deadline_not_the_earlier_ones` (pins the exact interaction the old timers had), `a_rapid_retoggle_cancels_rather_than_leaving_a_stale_request`, `Pending::a_second_request_replaces_the_first_and_brings_its_own_deadline`, `a_stale_echo_cannot_retire_a_newer_intent`

nightlight's #594/#597 supersession tests are all retained, replayed over the new state shape, plus `the_announced_wait_gives_up_exactly_when_the_coordinate_lookup_does`.

## Gates

All inside the devShell, foreground, `pipefail` set inside the `bash -c`:

| Gate | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features system-tests -- -D warnings` (`RUSTC_WRAPPER` unset) | `0` |
| `cargo test --workspace` | `0` (60 `test result: ok` lines, 0 failures) |
| `nix fmt -- --no-cache` ×2 | `0` / `0` — run 1: 2 changed in 2.312s; run 2: **0 changed** in 2.385s (not a cache hit) |

## Overlap with #820

#820 (`feat/633-spawn-supervised-handle`) was open when this was pushed and touches `crates/hytte-reactive/{supervisor.rs,health.rs,lib.rs}`. The only expected overlap is **adjacent `lib.rs` export lines** — this PR adds `pub mod pending;` and `pub use pending::Pending;` next to the `supervisor`/`health` entries #820 edits. Whoever merges second has a trivial resolution (keep both lines). No other file is shared; this branch is based on `main`, not on #820.

## Live-verify

Needs a running Niri session — CI can reach none of it (the niri IPC round-trip, the `wlsunset` user unit, a cold GeoClue).

**displays (Settings → Displays):**
1. Toggle an output off. The switch must stay off immediately, the subtitle must read "Turning off…" with a spinner, and within ~2 s (niri's next poll) the spinner must go and the row settle on "Disabled". Toggle it back on and watch the same in reverse.
2. **Revert path:** with a second output disconnected mid-toggle, or w

author: hannosirkel
body:
## The problem

The plan works in internal financial-account ids, so an instruction read:

```
2024-01-02 58.83 EUR — assign_general_ledger: debit 2 credit 260
```

Simplbooks never shows those ids. The UI shows **1020 Pangakonto** and **1021 PayPal**, so following the checklist meant translating every id by hand against a chart of accounts — 46 general-ledger rows plus every split part.

## The fix

The plan now carries the labels itself, taken from read-only discovery evidence (`discovery/financial-accounts.json`):

```
debit 2 (1020 Pangakonto) credit 260 (1021 PayPal)

part 1 -10.55 debit 52 (2310 Võlad tarnijatele) credit 2 (1020 Pangakonto) → purchase ...
part 4 -0.60  debit 141 (5350 Pangateenused)    credit 2 (1020 Pangakonto)
```

Labels live in the plan rather than being looked up at render time, so the checklist stays self-contained and reproducible — a plan renders the same way tomorrow, offline, as it did when built.

Degrading is deliberate: an account with no captured label renders its bare id, and a plan built without labels renders exactly as before. The labels make an instruction easier to follow; they are not part of what it means, so their absence must not fail a plan.

## Testing

TDD, watched failing first. Five tests, two of them controls for the degrade paths (unlabelled account keeps its id; unlabelled plan unchanged).

934 tests pass, ruff clean. Regenerating both real plans labels all 7 distinct accounts in use, with none left unlabelled.

author: maymun207
body:
`LENS-AUTHOR-SET-1-AG4-v1`, AG-4. The authorship lens returns a candidate **SET** where it used to abstain, and the set answers the only question the gate actually asks.

**AG-5 LANDS THIS. I land nothing.**

## The design is AG-3's

The lens is AG-3's and the reasoning that produced it is AG-3's. I hold the pen because its window cannot write — every AG-3 push refuses with `no ref refs/heads/lane/AG-3 on origin`. It carried nothing of mine this morning when the positions were reversed.

## Conflict of interest, stated before the argument

**#387 carries a report with my header**, so I am one of the two candidate authors in the tie this item resolves. I gain nothing actionable — I cannot land — but the tie-break makes a branch carrying my report landable. RULE-25 holds by AG-5 reading the printed classes **independently**, which is why the set prints unconditionally rather than only when it changes an outcome.

## Order F — invited to refute, and why I did not

The set is used **only to prove a negative**: the lander is not the author. For that, a **superset is the safe shape** — any lane wrongly *added* can only make the gate refuse more. The one error that could manufacture a wrong PASS is an **omission**, the true author missing from the set.

**That risk is not introduced here.** The existing single-lane path already trusts that a report header names its author; a branch touching only another lane's report already resolves to that other lane today. This inherits that assumption unchanged and, on a tie, is **strictly more conservative than any single-lane resolution of the same evidence.** Sound, with the residual risk named in the source rather than hidden.

## Order C — the loosening, measured

| lander | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **AG-5** | REFUSED `AUTHOR-UNKNOWN` | **PASS** `AUTHOR-SET-EXCLUDES-LANDER` |
| AG-2 | REFUSED `AUTHOR-UNKNOWN` | REFUSED `AUTHOR-UNKNOWN` |
| AG-4 | REFUSED `AUTHOR-UNKNOWN` | REFUSED `AUTHOR-UNKNOWN` |

**#387 becomes landable by AG-5 and by nobody else.** Candidate set `{AG-2 · AG-4}`, class still `AUTHOR-UNKNOWN`, author still unresolved — **the loosening resolves the LANDING, never the AUTHORSHIP.**

## Three places care was needed

**`candidates` is a separate field from `seen`.** `seen` is overloaded — lane *tokens* for the tie, *file paths* for "headers name no lane". A caller reading `seen` as candidates would compare a lander against filenames, find no match, and manufacture a PASS out of a type confusion.

**The set is carried out of `resolveAuthorLane`, not resolved inside it.** That function does not know the lander and must not: the set is a fact about the **branch**, whether it settles anything is a fact about the **landing**.

**`judgeReportOnly` takes a defaulted parameter**, so every existing caller keeps its exact behaviour, and the new reading lives only in the `author === null` branch.

## Constraint D is structural, not promised

Lens one resolving returns before reports are read. `mixed` gets no set. A resolved author **still self-land-refuses** even when the set would excuse it. All three are tests.

## A disagreement reported rather than absorbed

The card names a head for #387 that is no longer live. Its `ON-DISAGREEMENT` clause fires. I measured: the named head is an **ancestor** of the live head — moved forward, not rewritten — and ran the probe against **both**. Byte-identical results. Named *and* shown to be immaterial.

## Measured

| lens | result |
|---|---|
| `landScript.test.ts` | 123 passed (6 new) |
| `land --self-test` | classes=19 fixtures=21 reds=21 defects=0, control green |
| full suite | 694 files, 10101 passed, 4 expected-fail |
| `tsc` api + api.test | clean |
| `check:ground` | GREEN |
| `relayAudit` on the report | `[OK] kind=report grammar v1` |

**Falsifier planted in the SOURCE:** defeating the membership test makes the gate **pass a lander that is in the set** — the one direction the card called non-negotiable. Restored, green.

## Reported, not touched

**The gate from #401 is landed but not checked out.** The shared clone's working tree is one commit behind `origin/master` and its `mail-wait.mjs` has zero occurrences of `CARD_GATE` — so cards are still being read through an ungated reader. *Landed is not running.* I did not fast-forward it: every window's tick runs from that tree. One `git merge --ff-only origin/master` fixes it, and it is the foreman's call.

**No report was removed from any tree** (order E): the tie is a true fact, and deleting evidence to turn a refusal green is the one repair never available.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## What changed

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events` and the SSE stream stop publishing the opaque
provider replay state on reasoning artifacts. A reasoning part's `signature` and
`encrypted` payload no longer leave the server on any event read path; its
readable text, `item_id`, `provider` and `tokens` still do.

For callers this is a removal only, and only of fields that were never usable:
both are provider-internal blobs a client cannot validate or round-trip.

## Why

`Message::into_public` already stripped them from `GET .../messages`
(#3276), but the events read path returned stored rows verbatim — and
`output.message.completed` carries the very same `Message`. So one endpoint
withheld exactly what the other published. Found reviewing #3276 before merge and
filed as EVE-933 rather than widening that PR, since it is not a regression it
introduced: `main` already published `thinking_signature` on this endpoint and
persisted `encrypted_content` on `reason.item`, both of which #3276 removed.

The projection covers all three message-bearing variants, not just the one that
prompted it — `output.message.completed`, `input.message`, and `llm.generation`,
whose `messages` are the prompt replayed to the provider and carry the same
artifacts.

**Storage is deliberately unchanged.** Replaying a turn rebuilds the message from
the event log, so the replay state has to survive there. This is a read
projection, applied at the API edge.

## Before / After

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events` on a session whose assistant message carried a
signed reasoning block:

```
before   {"type":"output.message.completed","data":{"message":{"content":[
           {"type":"reasoning","provider":"anthropic","item_id":"rs_abc",
            "signature":"sig-…","encrypted":"enc-…",
            "text":{"kind":"plain","text":"visible reasoning"}}]}}}

after    {"type":"output.message.completed","data":{"message":{"content":[
           {"type":"reasoning","provider":"anthropic","item_id":"rs_abc",
            "text":{"kind":"plain","text":"visible reasoning"}}]}}}
```

`test_events_do_not_publish_reasoning_replay_state` asserts exactly this against
the real router. It was verified to fail before the fix: reverting the two
read-path call sites puts `sig-do-not-publish` back in the response body.

## Risk

- **Low**
- Breaking by intent for any client that read `signature` / `encrypted` off the
  events stream. Neither is usable by a client — they are opaque blobs the
  provider issued for replay — and the server keeps them for that purpose.
- The SSE path is hot. `needs_public_projection` gates the clone so the delta
  stream, which is almost entirely message-free variants, pays nothing; only the
  three message-bearing variants clone. A test pins that predicate against the
  `into_public` match so a newly added message-bearing variant cannot silently
  skip the projection.

## Security

- Threat categories reviewed: **TM-LLM** (provider artifact exposure, CoT
  retention), **TM-API** (published surface).
- Findings and resolutions: this closes the gap recorded in EVE-933 and narrows
  TM-LLM-034, whose entry is updated to name the events boundary alongside the
  REST one. No widening: nothing newly published, no authorization path touched,
  and retention is unchanged because storage still holds the artifacts.
- Checked the other surfaces that parse `OutputMessageCompletedData` —
  `app_api.rs`, `app_a2a.rs`, `fcp.rs`, `ag_ui.rs`. Each extracts text or reads
  `phase` and never republishes the raw message, so none leaks and none needed a
  change.

## Follow-ups

No follow-ups.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test -p everruns-core --lib` | 1056 passed, 0 failed |

body:
## What

Lockfile-only bump of `lru` 0.18.1 → 0.18.2, found during a security audit of
the workspace.

## Why

`cargo audit` (RustSec, 1226 advisories) over the 284 crates in `Cargo.lock`
reports one actionable advisory:

- **RUSTSEC-2026-0253** — `lru` 0.18.1, unsound: `LruCache::pop()` is not
  panic-safe, which can leave the cache holding a dangling entry and lead to a
  use-after-free. Patched in 0.18.2.

`lru` is a transitive dependency (`ratatui-core` → `ratatui` → `rinkaku-tui`).
0.18.2 is semver-compatible, so `cargo update -p lru --precise 0.18.2` resolves
it with no manifest change.

One `cargo audit` warning remains and is **not** addressed here: RUSTSEC-2025-0119
(`number_prefix` 0.4.0 is unmaintained), reachable only through `indicatif` 0.17.
Clearing it needs a major bump to `indicatif` 0.18, which is a manifest change
worth deciding on separately.

## Verification

- `cargo audit` — 0 vulnerabilities; warnings down from 2 to 1.
- `make test` — 1157 tests pass.
- `make lint` — clean (fmt + clippy `-D warnings`).

## Notes

The rest of the audit turned up findings in the source itself (most notably:
paths taken verbatim from a piped diff are read off disk without containment,
so a crafted diff can make stdin mode read files outside the repository). Those
are behavior changes that want their own ADR and PR, and are deliberately not
part of this dependency bump.

author: iainchesworth
body:
## Summary

Found this as an orphaned local branch (2026-08-23, never opened as a PR) while auditing branches for anything unmerged after the trunk-based-development cutover. The fix and its own tests/docs were already fully authored; verified it still applies cleanly against current `main` (548 commits later) and still builds/passes, then merged forward.

`wav_channel_order` wrote acmods 2/1 and 3/1 in bitstream order (L C R S) on the premise that no WAV convention covers a mono-surround slot. That premise was wrong: `WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE` defines `SPEAKER_BACK_CENTER` (`0x100`), and it's exactly the slot FFmpeg uses for both. Measured against FFmpeg 8.0.1 across every acmod it can encode, three more layouts turned out to diverge the same way once an LFE was added (3/0+LFE, 2/1+LFE, 3/1+LFE) — only 3/1 had a committed FATE sample exposing it.

`wav_channel_order` now sorts each coded channel by its `WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE` speaker bit instead of a hardcoded per-count table, so every acmod lands in the order any WAV consumer expects. 1+1 stays in coded order, unchanged: it carries two independent programmes rather than a soundfield, so there's no speaker position to sort by.

`millers_crossing_4.0.ac3` (AC-3 3/1) now decodes to the same channel order as FFmpeg's own decode, so `verify_fate_interop.py` flips it from decode-and-parse-only to a compared sample with a measured floor.

## Test plan

- [x] `ctest --preset test-linux-llvm` (Linux, clang-22): all tests pass, zero build errors, against current `main` post the mp4-reader and fuzz-classify fixes.
- [x] Merge-conflict resolution reviewed by hand (real content conflicts in `wav.cpp`/`docs/verification.md` from 548 commits of drift — `read_u16`/`read_u32` moved to `wav_format.hpp` since this branch was created; `ac3_layout_for` confirmed to be a distinct, still-used read-direction function, not touched by this fix).

author: bsvalues
body:
The stamp exists on HERMES. A separate observation found it. The grant that allowed it is already
revoked.

Executed under the owner's explicit 2026-08-25 decision. Branched from merged `main` `c3d822fa`
(post-`#1006`). Record: `docs/reports/WILLIAMOS-EXPERIENCE-V2-ORACLE-RESTORATION-003.md`.
`OWNER_COURIER_ACTIONS = 0`.

## One driver, four verdicts

`RS-00-settle-stamp-identity.mjs`, unmodified and digest-pinned, run four times with identical
arguments. Only the world around it changed:

| | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| before restoration | `BLOCKED_AT_AUTHORITY:AUTHORITY_UNREADABLE` |
| oracle republished, no grant | `BLOCKED_AT_AUTHORITY:AUTHORITY_NOT_GRANTED_NO_ROWS` |
| with `GRANT-0019` | **`SETTLED_MUTATION_EXECUTED`** |
| after revocation | `BLOCKED_AT_AUTHORITY:AUTHORITY_NOT_GRANTED_NO_COVERAGE` |

The fourth run left the ledger at the exact byte count the third left it at, and the stamp's digest
and mtime unchanged. Nothing happened, which is why it was taken.

## The oracle has an owner now

`williamos-postgres` was a hand-typed `docker run` from 2026-08-13 with its publish pinned to
`HostIp: 192.168.88.5`. When ATLAS's lease moved, Docker could not create the binding and started
the container anyway — no network, no `docker-proxy`, reachable from nowhere including the host it
runs on. `#1006` could not repair it because there was nothing to re-apply.

`deploy/atlas/williamos-authority-registry/` is that missing declaration. `0.0.0.0:15432` names no
interface on purpose; a literal re-creates the defect on the next lease change. Two layers make it
safe, neither optional, neither failing open:

- **`pg_hba.conf`**, mounted read-only via `hba_file` so it cannot drift inside the data volume. The
  server parsed five rules, no errors: one database, one role, one caller, `scram-sha-256`, and an
  explicit `reject` for everything else. It replaced `host all all all scram-sha-256` — every
  database, every role, from anywhere — which was harmless only while the publish was broken.
- **`DOCKER-USER`**, applied by `apply-network-policy.sh` and re-applied at boot by a systemd unit.
  `ufw` cannot be this layer and was `inactive` anyway: Docker's published ports are DNAT'd in `nat`
  PREROUTING and never reach the `INPUT` chain `ufw` filters.

`williamos_pgdata` is declared `external: true` so compose cannot create an empty volume beside it —
a fresh database that looks healthy and knows about no grants is the worst failure available here. A
`pg_dump` was taken before the container was replaced.

### The rule that looked right and blocked nothing

`--dport 15432` installed cleanly, `DOCKER-USER`'s counter climbed to 18 packets, and OMEN still
reached the Postgres wire protocol. Both rules read **0 packets**: `nat` runs before `filter`, so the
port had already been rewritten `15432 → 5432`. *A firewall that matches nothing is
indistinguishable from one that works* — the parent chain's counter even moves.

Fixed with `-m conntrack --ctorigdstport 15432 --ctdir ORIGINAL`. `--ctdir ORIGINAL` is equally
load-bearing: without it the DROP catches the reply direction of an allowed connection and breaks the
one caller the allowlist exists to permit.

Measured after, from both sides, with counters that move: HERMES is challenged for credentials, OMEN
is dropped silently, and ATLAS's four other published services (`5432`, `6379`, `27017`, `9001`) all
still answer. Nine refusal controls on the apply script, all exiting 1 with the port left as it was.

## `GRANT-0019`

Recorded through `app/actions/authority.ts` `createAuthorityGrantWithResult` — **no SQL**. That is
not pedantry: an INSERT produces a row and none of the advisory-lock-allocated ref, the content hash,
the `AUTHORITY_GRANTED` event, the register entry, or the Tier-2 ledger. A grant missing those is
identical in a `SELECT *` and invisible to every audit surface built on them. All four exist.

Narrow on every axis the machinery has: scope `#995`, `allowedActions ["node.stamp-identity"]`,
`A3_WRITE_SHARED` (not a choice — the route requires it by constant), `workOrderId null`, 16 blocked
actions. The recorder holds the grant as a **constant, not arguments**; a general-purpose grant
minter is the one tool this repository must not contain. It also refuses to run twice.

**The target restriction is not enforceable and is not claimed.** `authority_grant` has no target
column and `grantCovers` checks only level and action. What confines the mutation to one machine is
the route: the endpoint comes from the transport registry, not the request.

The 28 pre-existing grants hash to `dba0006c…` before and after — the same digest from `psql` on
ATLAS and from node-pg on HERMES, two tools over two transports. Exactly one row was added.

### The one honest gap

`getUserId()` reads `next/headers` and there is no request here. Two modules were substituted by a
literal whitelist: `next/cache` (no render cache exists in this process, and the real function throws
outside a request — *after* the grant would have committed) and `@/lib/session` (a named-actor
assertion, `ASSERTED_BY_OPERATOR_NOT_AUTHENTICATED`, refusing when unnamed). Fabricating a session to
satisfy an authentication check is the same class of act as minting a grant to satisfy an authority
check. Everything downstream is the canonical module unmodified, pinned to merged `main`.

## Three defects found by measuring rather than assuming

**`CONT-EXPV2-GRANT-EXPIRY-TZ-SKEW`.** `route.ts` reads `expiresAt` with raw `pg`, bypassing the
schema's `utcWallTimestamp` whose `fromDriver` exists to undo exactly that. A stored UTC wall clock
is read as local: on HERMES (UTC-7) the two-hour grant is one the route accepts for **nine**. Not
repaired here — the fix edits a module this proof digest-pins, mid-proof. It is why the grant was
**revoked** rather than left to lapse: revocation is checked by status, not by clock.

**`CONT-EXPV2-RUNTIME-CREDENTIAL-STALE`.** With both walls gone, the driver still hit `28P01`. The
resolver was ruled out first (the 64-character password is byte-identical through parse and
substitution). The live runtime's `.env.local` does not hold the `williamos` role's password —
established against the role's stored SCRAM verifier **arithmetically**, not by trying logins,
because a wrong guess is indistinguishable in the server log from someone else's. The deployed
WilliamOS runtime cannot read the authority registry even now. Invisible until the two walls in front
of it were removed.

**`CONT-EXPV2-ALLOWLIST-ADDRESS-BOUND`.** An L3 allowlist names addresses by nature. Declared once in
`fabric-callers.json`, rendered into both layers, with a test asserting they stay in step.

## What this may NOT be read as

**`CONT-EXPV2-AUTHORITY-REGISTRY-SINGLE-POINT` stays typed open** — by the owner's instruction and on
the merits. This makes the oracle *functional*, not *resilient*. It is still one Postgres, on one
node, on one LAN, and when it is unreachable every governed mutation refuses. That is correct
behaviour and still a single point.

**No standing `#995` permission remains.** Re-authorising is a new owner decision, not a re-run.

**`ufw` was never enabled** on ATLAS and enabling it would not have helped. Do not read "firewall"
here as "ufw".

## Boundary

This lane authored every commit on this branch and may not merge it. Pickup for the next merge sweep:
any coordinator lane that authored none of them. Re-gate at head. `#1007` is open on
`docs/reports/WILLIAMOS-EXPERIENCE-V2-RUNTIME-SETTLEMENT-001.md` and on
`scripts/lab-control/hermes/*`; this lane edited neither and ran the crossnode lane's
`sync-models-to-forge.ps1` read-only (`-ResolveOnly`) to verify `#1006`'s repair without touching it.

author: shubendu-assamdigital
body:
## What changed

Replaces the marketplace header stack (rotating gradient announcement → trust strip → logo-on-green-panel row with an "AI Search" button → category chips) with a calm three-band editorial navigation.

**Header** (`Header.js`, `Header.module.css`)
- Utility line → **masthead** (wordmark · search · thin-line icon actions) → **primary nav** under a 1px hairline, with the promises line capping the page below it.
- The light logo now renders **directly on the ivory** — the `.logoPanel` green box and its `--brand-logo-bg` background are gone. It reuses byte-for-byte the Cloudinary URL `index.html` already preloads, so the masthead paints from cache with no second request (`w_520` = ~3.7× the 44px render height, retina-safe).
- Nav is **API-driven** through `getMainMenuCategories()`: the seeded categories in `menuOrder`, a hairline tick, then New Arrivals / Bestsellers / Sale — plus **Today's Deals only while `useDealsConfig().enabled`**. Active state is a gold underline using the existing path+query matching.
- Hovering or focusing a parent category opens a restrained full-band **collection panel** of its sub-collections.
- **One honest search affordance**: an outlined field-button that opens `SearchModal`, icon-only at ≤1024px. The "AI Search" claim is dropped — nothing AI-powered exists behind it.
- Scrolled state deepens the hairline and adds `--sf-shadow-xs` with **no height change**, so nothing under it shifts.

**AnnouncementBar** — one calm ivory-on-ink band in tracked uppercase; the three `--sf-gradient-announce-*` backgrounds give way to a single treatment, and messages crossfade on opacity only. Dismiss + `localStorage` persistence, hover/focus pause, and reduced-motion behaviour all preserved.

**TrustStrip** — restyled as a hairline promises line (small gold glyphs, tracked uppercase). It paints no ground and no border of its own; each host draws the bounding rules, so it reads correctly both under the header nav and inside `SidebarMenu`'s bordered hero without doubling a hairline. Props `({ items, className })` unchanged.

## Why

Prompt 05 of the storefront redesign series. The old masthead was three loud, competing bands; the brief was a structurally different editorial navigation that keeps every existing behaviour identical.

## Reviewer notes

- **The sticky header is masthead + nav only (118px measured).** The announcement bar renders in normal flow above it and the promises line below, both scrolling away. Pinning all four bands would have run to ~200px, well past the ≤120px budget.
- **The "Mega Silk" / "Bridal" regex chips are retired.** `db.json` shows the reseeded catalogue promotes Mekhela Chador and Bridal & Occasion into the main menu proper, so the curated slots would have rendered them twice.
- **Announcement copy is now store-attested.** The banner claimed free shipping above ₹1,999 while `FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD` and the shipping methods both say ₹999 — it now reads from the constant so the two can't drift. The unbacked "Flash Sale — Extra 25% Off on the Premium Collection" line (no such collection survives the reseed, no coupon backs 25%) is replaced by the Sualkuchi origin note the store settings attest.
- **TrustStrip keeps its existing four items.** The labels are shared with `constants.js` and `Home.js`, and there's no documented support SLA to attest, so swapping money-back for a support claim would have meant inventing one.
- **The nav is `aria-label="Shop"`, not "Primary"** — `BottomNav` already claims that name, and two nav landmarks with the same label are indistinguishable in a landmark list.
- **Tab order is logo → search → actions → nav**, not the brief's logo → nav → search → actions, because the nav is a row *below* the masthead. DOM order matches visual order, which is what WCAG 1.3.2 / 2.4.3 require.

Two bugs surfaced during verification and are fixed here:
- The collection panel's links sat eight links away in the tab order — reachable only by mouse. The panel now renders inside its trigger's `<li>`, and the nav row wraps instead of scrolling so neither the panel nor a focus ring is ever clipped.
- The announcement rotated while the tab was hidden; browsers suspend rAF there, so each rotation queued an exit animation that could never finish and left every message stacked in the DOM. It now holds on `visibilitychange`.

## Testing

`CI=true npm run build` compiles successfully; ESLint clean on all three components. Verified at 1440/1280/1024/768/480/375 — no horizontal overflow from the header, nav fits without scrolling at every width, no label clipping anywhere. Exercised: full nav click-through, all four overlays (cart, sidebar, auth, search), login → avatar menu → logout, theme toggle (both modes resolve), deals gating (hidden on disable, restored on tab refocus), dismiss persistence across reload, keyboard paths, and `/admin` login + dashboard regression. `db.json` left byte-identical.

Verification was DOM- and computed-style measurement rather than screenshots — the browser pane wasn't compositing frames in this session.

Unrelated and untouched: `HeroSection` overflows the viewport at 375px (its slide is 377px wide and the category rail runs off-screen). That's prompt 12's territory.

author: zhengruifeng
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Replace the immutable Scala `Map[String, Int]` used by `CountVectorizerModel` for vocabulary lookup with a pre-sized `java.util.HashMap[String, Integer]`.

Build and broadcast the dictionary once, then dereference the broadcast value and its size once per document instead of once per token. Register `java.util.HashMap` with Spark Kryo so this remains compatible with `spark.kryo.registrationRequired=true`.

### Why are the changes needed?

`CountVectorizerModel.transform` performs one vocabulary lookup per input token. A local Java 17 benchmark with 262,144 String keys, 2 million lookups, and a 90% hit rate measured:

- Scala immutable Map: 69.5 ns/lookup
- Spark OpenHashMap: 38.3 ns/lookup
- java.util.HashMap: 20.7 ns/lookup

For the same vocabulary, Java HashMap used about 13% less deserialized heap than the immutable map, produced a 26% smaller JavaSerializer + LZ4 broadcast payload, and deserialized about 47% faster. OpenHashMap used less heap and deserialized faster than Java HashMap, but Java HashMap provides the best tradeoff for this lookup-heavy workload.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Added strict-Kryo coverage for `java.util.HashMap` and ran:

- `build/sbt "core/testOnly *KryoSerializerSuite -- -z \"basic types\""`
- `build/sbt "mllib/testOnly *CountVectorizerSuite"`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is **part 3 of 3** split from #24. It is intentionally opened as a draft and is currently stacked on #25 and #26, so GitHub shows their prerequisite commits too. The RGB implementation itself is commit `b074559`. I will rebase it onto `dev` after the prerequisites land and will not mark it ready before the resulting RGB-only diff is green.

## Context

This draft addresses #6 and is opened early so the architecture can be discussed before merge, especially the maintainer's concerns about scan-loop performance, current draw, and the difference between per-key RGB and underglow.

## Scope

- Optional portable RGB core and a small non-blocking backend API.
- Static, breathing, rainbow and rainbow-wave effects.
- A live mode where the host controls every LED.
- RAW HID capability negotiation plus frame/color/effect/brightness commands.
- Persistence for compact settings; live frames are deliberately RAM-only.
- First hardware backend: STM32F723, WS2812 on TIM2 channel 1 using DMA.
- Explicit logical-key, physical-chain and spatial LED topology in keyboard metadata.

## Performance concern

RGB is compile-time opt-in. A keyboard without an `rgb` metadata block does not compile the renderer/backend, allocate frame buffers, or schedule `rgb_task()`.

The portable layer never bit-bangs LEDs. `rgb_backend_submit()` must copy/queue a frame and return immediately; the STM32F723 backend uses timer DMA and completes asynchronously. Animation and transfer cadence are separate from matrix scanning. Host live frames are assembled in staging memory and become visible atomically only after every 60-byte chunk arrives, so partial/late packets cannot tear the active frame.

The draft has strict host tests for effect math and topology and has been built both with RGB enabled on KBHE and disabled on an existing HE60 target. Before ready-for-review, the rebased branch will be remeasured against the final prerequisite commits.

## Current-draw concern

Brightness is a board-owned setting applied in the core before submission. KBHE deliberately defaults to 50/255 rather than full output. Suspend sends a black frame and pauses animation. Live frames cannot bypass the global brightness scaling.

This draft does **not** claim to provide an electrical current measurement or a universal safe current limit: that limit depends on LED type, count, PCB power path and USB budget. I would like maintainer feedback on whether the schema should also require a board-specific hard maximum in addition to the conservative default before this leaves draft.

## Per-key versus underglow

The renderer is not tied to the KBHE serpentine chain. Metadata separates:

- host-visible logical LED order;
- physical chain order (`led_index_map`);
- spatial positions used by effects (`led_position`);
- optional key association (`key_to_led`).

KBHE uses one LED per key. The separation is intended to let an underglow board describe LEDs that have positions but no key association, without creating a second renderer/backend API. This is another point where feedback is welcome while the PR is draft.

## HID/API design

Hosts must first call `GET_RGB_CAPABILITIES` (`0x7F`) rather than infer RGB support from a firmware version. Basic effect and brightness commands are small fixed reports. Live per-LED control uses chunked 64-byte RAW HID reports and publishes only complete frames. No live frame is written to Flash, avoiding wear and input stalls.

## Validation completed on the isolated stack

- strict C host tests for renderer/effect behavior and topology mapping;
- deterministic metadata/schema generation tests;
- KBHE RGB build: 44,744 bytes Flash, 26,232 bytes RAM;
- existing HE60 non-RGB build: 38,936 bytes Flash, 14,420 bytes RAM;
- ELF inspection confirmed ADC and RGB DMA buffers are in DMA-accessible AXI SRAM, not STM32F723 DTCM.

## Dependency/rebase plan

1. #25 lands (STM32F723 + KBHE only).
2. #26 lands (independent HID gamepad).
3. Rebase this branch onto the new `dev`, resolve metadata migrations once, rerun host and both target builds, then replace the measurements above and mark ready.

Until then, please treat this as an architecture/RFC draft rather than a merge candidate.

## Why

`INTEGRATION_TEST_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` existed so the armada integration tests could read the MQTT credentials from `FlotillaTestsKv`. As of equinor/armada#100 those credentials are generated per test run and nothing is read from the key vault, so passing this secret does nothing.

Removing it here is what lets armada drop the declaration — GitHub rejects a caller passing a secret the reusable workflow does not declare, so the callers have to go first — and lets the secret and its service principal be retired.

No behaviour change: the workflow already ignores it.

## Depends on

equinor/armada#100 should merge first, so the workflow has stopped reading it.
