author: lucasmenendez
body:
## Summary

Documents the voter **memo** feature across the developers docs: the classic open "Other: ____"
answer, where a voter attaches a free-text note to their ballot. Nothing about this existed in the
docs before. It lands on four existing pages (no new page), covering the full lifecycle:

| Layer | Surface | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| Authoring | `choices[].openValue: true` marks the one free-text choice per question | `voting-types.md`, `voting-processes.md` |
| Casting | SDK `memo` option / React `memos?` / raw `VoteEnvelope.memo` | `casting-votes.md` |
| Reading | manager-only `memos: string[]` folded into question results | `results.md`, `voting-processes.md` |
| Optional auth | the "same 200, field absent" pattern, factored out once | `api-conventions.md` |

Upstream: server half is `saas-backend` #577; client half already shipped in `integrator-sdk`
(`memo` on `VotingClient.vote()`, `MAX_MEMO_BYTES`, `ElectionProvider.vote(ballots, memos?)`).

## Why the named-types correction is bundled

`voting-types.md` was already stale: `saas-backend` main has **four** named question types
(`singlechoice`, `multichoice`, `ranked`, `cumulative`) but the docs listed two and routed
ranked/quadratic through the raw `ballotProtocol` override. The memo docs cannot avoid this -
`openValue` is accepted on `singlechoice`/`multichoice`/`cumulative` and **rejected on `ranked`** - so
the docs must name the types accurately. The fix lands as its own commit
(`saas-backend #619`, which also covers the `uniqueChoices`/`minChoices` corrections) so it stays
independently revertable ahead of the memo prose.

## Two real hazards the docs call out (as warnings, not notes)

- **Memos are cleartext even on secret ballots.** The memo rides the vote *envelope*, not the encrypted
  vote *package*, so it is readable on chain even for a `secretUntilTheEnd` question.
- **Free text re-identifies voters.** The API attaches no voter to a memo, but the text ("as the
  treasurer, I think...") identifies its author. Documented as pseudonymous personal data.

## Testing

- `pnpm validate` (lint + 179 tests + all i18n/copy guardrails) - green.
- No em dash characters; sentence case; content-only change (no `lib/docs` or component touches).

## Open before merge

- [ ] **Chain availability.** #577 pins `dvote` to an unmerged node branch and its tests force chain id
      `vocdoni/TEST/1` so the `VoteMemoActive` soft-fork is active. Confirm memos are live on the
      staging and production chains; if not, add an availability note or land behind #577's deployment.
- [ ] **Staging end-to-end.** Once #577 is deployed to staging: create a process with an `openValue`
      choice, cast a vote with a `memo`, read `GET /processes/{id}/results` without auth (expect `200`,
      no `memos`) and with a manager key (expect the memo). This is the one step that can invalidate the
      prose, so run it before merging.

author: takazudo
body:
Epic: #2549

## Summary

- make Dev hydration publication transactional across client-script entries,
  worker/resource companions, islands, generated documents, and prunes
- keep readiness pending through exact entry-kind, document-write, rollback,
  and failed-prune obligations, then recover as soon as the matching publisher
  or request repair proves the served generation coherent
- make renderer discovery candidate-first and force every successful discovery
  refresh through the publication pipeline, including otherwise-empty plans
- serialize request-time lazy repair with active discovery while retaining
  sticky recovery proof after a blocked terminal, without requiring another
  watcher tick to return to ready
- publish authoritative generation/readiness headers on every Dev HTML response
  and prevent plugin or embed handlers from spoofing the reserved pair

## Implementation

### Transactional entries and documents

- prepare and collision-check the complete client generation before its first
  public write
- publish companions before stable entries with atomic writes and a reverse
  rollback journal for late failures
- persist the exact unsafe output names when compensation is incomplete; only
  a successful publication of that exact entry kind and output clears them
- separate entry-only pending state from partial-document uncertainty so
  zero-page and SSR-only generations can recover without weakening the
  document-write latch
- clear eager stale claims only after a document write completes and retain
  lazy fallbacks through client repair until a safe non-preserving boundary
- retry failed prunes on later unrelated publication ticks while revalidating
  against the complete current route namespace before deletion

### Discovery and request recovery

- boot a candidate V8 renderer and build its route tables before adopting it;
  route-table failure shuts down the candidate and preserves the live renderer,
  tables, content trace, and skip key
- distinguish a short-lived discovery `active` gate from sticky pending and
  document-boundary proof
- release request deferral after every explicit or Drop terminal attempt while
  keeping blocked recovery state available to an exact later request repair
- replay deferred repair after inherited-sticky pre-swap failures and safely
  reopen Pending when a newer discovery starts during a successful request
  commit
- treat a successful discovery renderer refresh as pipeline-worthy even when
  ordinary planning selected no pages or assets

### Readiness surface

- annotate ordinary pages and all framework/plugin/embed/security/static HTML
  responses in Dev with one authoritative `X-Zfb-Dev-Generation` /
  `X-Zfb-Dev-Ready` pair
- preserve the ordinary page renderer's single snapshot for islands selection
  and response metadata
- strip reserved readiness headers supplied by plugin and embed handlers before
  the outer Dev HTML layer fills the framework snapshot
- keep Preview/Embed and non-HTML responses header-free

## Regression coverage

- partial generation, companion-write, late-entry, and rollback failures
- exact client-vs-islands repair obligations and unrelated publication ticks
- entry-only, zero-page, SSR-only, request-time, and cold-bootstrap recovery
- persistent prune retry, resurrected lazy routes, and stale-write claims
- candidate renderer teardown and skip-key preservation
- CSS-only discovery filtering and otherwise-empty discovery apply
- request/discovery ordering, blocked-terminal request repair without another
  tick, inherited-sticky discovery failure replay, and request-first handoff
- plugin/embed attempts to supply deliberately stale readiness headers

## Validation

- `cargo test -p zfb-build --quiet` — 825 unit tests plus all integration suites
- `cargo test -p zfb-server` — 273 unit tests plus all integration suites
- `cargo test -p zfb --lib --quiet` — 1,086 passed, 6 expected ignores
- `cargo test -p zfb --test dev_bind_before_walk_e2e --quiet` — 10 passed
- `cargo test -p zfb --test ssr_reload_self_heal_e2e -- --ignored` — 2 passed
  with the staged pinned esbuild binary
- `cargo clippy -p zfb-build -p zfb-server -p zfb --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --no-default-features -p zfb --tests`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`
- final aggregate review — no actionable findings

## Residual risk

Portable filesystems do not provide a multi-file atomic swap for stable URLs.
Companions-first ordering and rollback cover surfaced failures, but a reader can
still observe a companion update before its stable entry during the short
successful commit window. If compensation fails and the exact output is absent
from later generations, readiness deliberately stays pending until that output
is republished or the Dev process restarts. The discovery/request concurrency
regressions are deterministic at the coordination seams rather than a long-run
stress test.

author: bnspopi
body:
## The bug

*"I did forgot password and now I cannot log in."* With **790 students** just told to use Forgot Password, that was aimed at everyone.

A student's password lives in **more than one document**:

| Document | Used by |
|---|---|
| `EcosystemUser` | what `/login` compares against for an **email** sign-in — which is what the portal tells students to do |
| `Student` | the legacy employee-ID path — and there can be **two** of these rows per person, since a student may enrol in two domains on one email and the rows deliberately share a password |

Every password-writing path updated only the `Student` row it happened to be holding:

- `server.js:8461` — the forgot-password reset ← **the reported bug**
- `routes/adminPortal.js:846` — the admin reset
- `routes/studentSecurity.js:147` — the student's own change

So the reset reported success and the next sign-in still checked the **old** hash.

## The fix

`utils/passwordStore.js` writes it to all of them. All three paths call it.

- **`updateMany`, not `findOne().save()`** — the two-domain case is exactly where a single-document write leaves half the account behind.
- **Case-insensitive email match, with the address escaped** — rows created before emails were lowercased hold `Name@Gmail.com`, and an exact match misses them. The escape matters too: an unescaped `.` in `a.b@example.org` would match `axb@example.org`.
- **Clears any outstanding reset token in the same write**, so a link issued earlier stops working.
- **Logs a reset that matched no account** — that's the failure this exists to prevent, and it is otherwise indistinguishable from a successful one.

## On the test that went red

`tests/routes/credentialReset.test.js` failed with `500`. Its `Student` double spoke only `findOne`/`findById`, and there was **no `EcosystemUser` double at all**, so the helper threw.

The gap was in the doubles, not the route — so the doubles were completed rather than the production code weakened. The `Student` double now applies the update to its fake row, so the existing assertions check what a real write would actually leave behind.

## Verification

`npx jest` — **98 suites, 1864 tests, all passing.**

New tests run the real helper and assert the **same bcrypt hash reaches both stores**, that every row for the email is updated, that capitalisation and dotted addresses match correctly, and that the reset token is cleared.

## After merging

```bash
cd ~/InternshipManagementSystem-Final && git pull && pm2 restart ten-portal-production --update-env
```

Then: Forgot Password → set a new one → sign in with the **email address**. That's the path all 790 students are on.

author: paulocpjunior
body:
**25/08, 09:15** — dentro da janela (08:00–12:00), com o SBC provado de pé pelo 🔌 (TLS 1.2, certificado público até 22/11, Asterisk respondendo SIP 200 OK), ícone visível e horário conferido:

> *"SP Assessoria não pode receber ligações do WhatsApp."*

As duas hipóteses anteriores caíram — **o certificado** (o 🔌 provou) e **o horário** (o relógio provou). E o painel continuava verde.

## 🚨 Porque ele olhava a coisa errada

A tela afirmava **"✅ Tronco gravado na Meta"** só porque `sip.servers[]` **existia**. Guardar o endereço do servidor **não é o SIP estar ligado**: `calling.status` e `sip.status` são interruptores próprios, e **nenhum dos dois aparecia na tela**.

Pior: a escrita manda `status: 'ENABLED'` e **ninguém re-lia** se a Meta guardou ligado. É **status passando por resultado dentro do nosso painel de diagnóstico** — a primeira regra permanente deste projeto, invertida no lugar mais irônico.

## O que passa a aparecer

`lerEstadoDaChamada` (núcleo puro) lê os quatro e devolve **impedimentos com a ação**:

| campo | quando acusa |
|---|---|
| `calling.status` | a chamada do número está desligada |
| `sip.status` | **servidor gravado com o SIP desligado** ← o verde falso |
| `sip.servers` | nenhum servidor: a ligação não tem para onde ir |
| `call_icon_visibility` | botão oculto para os clientes |

A tela imprime os quatro **com o nome do campo do lado** — é ele que se procura no WhatsApp Manager e é ele que vai num chamado à Meta.

⚠️ **Ausente nunca é ligado**: campo que a Meta não declara sai `nao-declarado`, nunca ENABLED por otimismo. Foi assumir o que não foi medido que fez este painel ficar verde enquanto o cliente ouvia a recusa.

⚠️ **E não inventa alarme**: com os quatro certos ele diz que a causa não está em interruptor nenhum daqui.

## 📌 Lição

Em três rodadas eu propus três causas — certificado, horário, agora os interruptores — e **as duas primeiras eram dedução**. A que sobreviveu veio de **ler o que a Meta guarda**. Sonda que mostra parte do estado é sonda que produz verde falso: ela mostrava **três campos de sete**.

author: jobordu
body:
Six workflows filtered `pull_request` on the **base** branch, so a PR based on anything but `main` (or the long-dead-looking `feat/ai-backend-matrix`) **ran no checks at all**.

Not a red we ignored, and not a green over nothing — **no checks section**, which reads as fine to anyone scrolling past.

### Measured
- **#130 merged to main with ZERO CI**, gated on "the named check". There was no check.
- **#139 has never had a CI run.**
- Every PR stacked on a non-main base had the same hole. This team stacks routinely.

### Fix
The filter is **deleted, not widened**. Adding each new base to six files goes stale the moment someone opens the next stack — and the allowlist had already rotted, still naming `feat/ai-backend-matrix`. `push` keeps its filter; that answers a different question.

⚠️ Retargeting a PR fires `edited`, which is **not** in `pull_request`'s default types. Changing a base does not start CI on its own — close/reopen, or push a commit.

### Guard
`scripts/check-pr-triggers.mjs` fails the build on any `pull_request.branches` filter, and **fails closed** on a workflow it cannot parse. Two vacuity guards: zero workflows, and workflows-but-no-`pull_request`, are errors rather than clean runs.

## Summary

- verify Partner Center credentials and QuiverDL product access on manual runs without publishing by default

body: ## FLASH NERA Les nouveautés publiées en boutique en ligne sont mises en avant automatiquement. Le client voit uniquement le **temps restant**. La durée interne (10 jours par défaut) n’est jamais affichée côté boutique. Conflits avec `main` (dashboard admin, PR #19) **résolus** : publication boutique, variantes/marques, et dates Flash coexistent. Le bouton Publier / Dépublier assigne le Flash à la première mise en ligne, sans le relancer ensuite. ### Architecture actuelle - Next.js App Router, Prisma / Postgres, stock unique `Inventory`, promotions via `isPromo` / `promoPrice` - FLASH NERA est une mise en avant temporaire, distincte d’une promotion prix - Le Flash se calcule : `flashStartAt <= maintenant < flashEndAt` **et** produit publié (`ACTIVE` + `onlineVisible`) ### Modèle Product - `flashStartAt` / `flashEndAt` (pas de `isFlash` stocké) - Durée admin : `flashDurationDays` dans les paramètres boutique (JSON `shop`), défaut 10 - S’applique uniquement à la **première publication** ; une modification ou une republication ne relance pas le compteur - Un produit non publié en boutique n’entre jamais en Flash - POS / ventes : le stock diminue, le Flash n’est pas touché ### Compteur client - ≥ 24 h : `⏳ Plus que XJ XXH` - 1 h – 24 h : `⏳ Plus que XXH XXMIN` - < 1 h : `⏳ Plus que MM:SS` (tick chaque seconde) - < 10 min : `🔥 Plus que MM:SS` - < 1 min : `🔥 MM:SS` - à `00:00` : sortie du Flash, produit toujours achetable en boutique ### Après merge ```bash npx prisma migrate deploy ```

author: tasaishogo
body:
## 何が起きたか（障害）

2026-08-25 の `deploy-spa.sh` 初回配信（`52bfece`）以降、**dev のログインが全滅**していました（Google もメール/パスワードも「処理に失敗しました。しばらくしてからもう一度お試しください」。Shogo さんの実機確認で発覚）。

原因: `frontend/src/features/auth/amplify.ts` は build 時に `VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID` / `VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_CLIENT_ID` / `VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN` を読みますが、`deploy-spa.sh` は Geolonia キーしか注入していませんでした。配信中バンドルを grep すると User Pool ID もドメインも 0 件（T028 時点の旧バンドルには両方あった）。Amplify が未設定のため `signInWithRedirect` が例外を投げ、Cognito へのリダイレクトすら起きません。PreSignUp トリガー（T014）とは無関係です。

これは #23 の私の実装漏れです。

## 修正

- `resolve_cognito_env`: 環境変数 `VITE_COGNITO_*` が 3 つ揃っていればそれを使い、無ければスタック Outputs（`UserPoolId` / `UserPoolClientId` / `CognitoDomain`。domain は `https://` を外したホスト名＝旧バンドルと同じ形式）から解決して export。deploy / dry-run の両方で build 前に呼ぶ
- build 後の検査に「バンドルに User Pool ID とドメインが埋まっていること」を追加（`keyring.apiKey=void 0` 検査と同型。未注入なら配信せず fail）

## 確認（host・`origin/main` のツリーで `--dry-run --app-url <dev>`）

```
==> Cognito 設定: スタック Outputs から解決（UserPoolId=ap-northeast-1_XVA4x96Pc domain=oriorimap-dev.auth.ap-northeast-1.amazoncognito.com）
==> Geolonia キー有効性検査: ... tiles.json 200
==> frontend をビルド ... → バンドルに pool id: 1 / domain: 1
```

`bash -n` / `lint-shell-vars` OK。実配信は pi ワーカー経由（マージ後、`auto/pi-q1` へ main を取り込んで再配信）。

## 再発防止メモ

- フロントが読む `import.meta.env.VITE_*` は現在 4 つ（`VITE_GEOLONIA_API_KEY` と `VITE_COGNITO_*` 3 つ）。今後増やす場合は `deploy-spa.sh` の解決処理と埋め込み検査に同時に追加すること（`git grep -oh 'import.meta.env.VITE_[A-Z_]*' frontend/src | sort -u` で一覧できる）
- 点検コメント（#22）の人手確認 S1〜S6 は、本 PR マージ → 再配信の後に実施可能になります

Report only. No code changed. The single file in this branch is reports/GA4_ANALYSIS_2026-08-25.md.

A genuinely fresh GA4 export landed in the Night Tasks folder -- 36 of 38 numbered CSVs now carry window 20260519-20260824, one day past the window the 08-23 and 08-24 reports both analysed -- so this is Prompt 9 (GA4 -> site improvements).

HEADLINE, and it has never been measured before: download (37).csv is a "Philly vs Lancaster" report that appears in no prior report. Philadelphia is 439 of 530 geo-identified active users (82.8%) and produced 6 key events and $59.98. Lancaster is 96 users (18.1%) and produced 16 key events and $108.96. CORRECTION TO LAST NIGHT: ads_conversion_About_Us_1 is NOT frozen. It read 97 on two consecutive exports and reads 99 tonight, with both new fires on 2026-08-24. It fires in rare bursts. author: aminulbd
body:
Closes #15.

## The part of the issue that cannot be done

> we need to scrap and grab pricing from all supported registry

There is no such price to grab. Registries do not sell domains retail — they sell
wholesale to accredited registrars under contract, and outside the ICANN gTLD
agreements (whose fee schedules are per-registry PDF exhibits, not a feed) they
publish no public price list at all. There is no price a registry charges *you*.
Most ccTLD registries publish nothing whatsoever.

So this PR does the achievable version: **more registrars**, which is who
actually sells you the name. I have not quietly redefined the issue — the
distinction is written into the harvest script's header, into `src/pricing.rs`,
and into a new *Where the prices come from* section in the README, so the next
person to read the file gets the same answer.

## Coverage

Against `main`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TLDs with a registration price | **569** | **870** |
| entries in `pricing.json` | 577 | 875 |
| distinct registrars | 1 | 3 |
| TLDs quoted by more than one registrar | 0 | 598 |

`ds` knows of ~1,650 TLDs it can actually look up, so this goes from ~34% priced
to ~53%. The remainder are mostly brand TLDs (`.abbott`, `.aarp`) that nobody
retails, and ccTLDs no registrar in the table carries.

The site's table grows from 1,684 rows to 1,800, because priced-but-unlookuppable
suffixes feed that union too; its "priced" column is the 870 above.

## Sources

| Source | TLDs | How | Currency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [101domain](https://www.101domain.com/pricing.htm) | 754 | one page per TLD, URLs enumerated from their `sitemap.xml`; the *Technical information* table gives Registration / Renewal / Transfer | USD, stated on the page |
| [Porkbun](https://api.porkbun.com/api/json/v3/pricing/get) | 634 | public JSON pricing endpoint, no key, one request | USD |
| Namecheap | 569 | **not re-harvested** — carried through from the existing file untouched | USD |

**101domain is the part that actually widens things.** 198 TLDs are priced by it
and by nothing else in the table, and they are precisely the long tail the issue
is about: `.ae .af .al .ar .at .bd .be .cl .cn .cz .dk .ee .eg .fi …`. That is
the single hardest gap to close and I found no other broad source that fills it.

Namecheap could not be re-harvested: their full price list page returns 403 to
anything without a browser fingerprint, and their pricing API needs an account
key plus an IP allowlist. Rather than invent or drop that data, the script leaves
offers from registrars it did not harvest exactly as it found them, and its
header says so.

**Sources I tried and rejected**, so nobody repeats the work:

- **NameSilo** — sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge. Getting the price
  list would mean defeating bot detection. Not doing that.
- **Cloudflare Registrar** — the TLD-policies table is rendered client-side and I
  could find no JSON behind it; coverage would also have been ~250 gTLDs already
  covered twice over.
- **Dynadot** — the only machine-readable prices on their price page are the
  promotional first-year figures (`.xyz` at $1.99), with no regular rate beside
  them. Fails the promo/regular test below.
- **Gandi** — every pricing endpoint requires an API key.
- **Hexonet / CentralNic Reseller** — shut down; the price list redirects to a
  shutdown notice.

## Currency

Every source above quotes USD at the source. **Nothing is currency-converted**
and no conversion code exists: the script takes only USD figures, and a row
quoting anything else is dropped rather than mixed in. That is also why the
EUR-denominated European registrars (INWX, Netim, EuroDNS) are not here — they
would have needed a recorded rate and a date, and 101domain covers most of the
same ccTLDs in USD already.

## Promotional vs regular

Worth being precise, because the answer is not flattering to the original data
either.

`prices.regular` has always meant *the registrar's published first-year list
price*, not the yearly cost. That was already true of the Namecheap data on
`main` — `.site` is `regular: 1.78, renew: 43.98`. I kept that meaning rather
than silently changing it, and instead made it explicit in three places: the
module doc in `src/pricing.rs`, the README, and the `/tlds` page, which now says
"Register is the first year, Renew is every year after" and points out they often
differ by a lot.

What I did **not** do is scrape anything time-limited:

- Porkbun's response carries a `coupons` array of discount codes alongside the
  standing price. The coupons are **dropped**; only `registration` is taken.
- 101domain's *Technical information* table is their standing price list. No
  banner or sale price is read; the pages carry no sale markup on the rows used.
- Dynadot was rejected outright because its page exposes only the promo figure.

So: standing shelf prices, promos omitted, and `renew` carried beside every one
of them so the reader can see the gap.

## Overlap with PR #20 — please read before merging either

I was told after finishing that PR #20 (issue #16) has independently rewritten
`pricing.json` and added `scripts/update-pricing.mjs`, merging Porkbun and
deserializing `register`. That means:

- **This PR overlaps PR #20 on `pricing.json` and on `scripts/`.** It will
  conflict, whichever merges first, and will need a rebase. I have not tried to
  resolve against that branch — I cannot see it, and sequencing is yours.
- **My Porkbun ingest duplicates theirs.** I harvested it before knowing, and
  kept it rather than tearing out working code. **101domain is the increment**:
  drop Porkbun from my side entirely and this PR still adds 198 TLDs that
  neither Namecheap nor Porkbun price.
- **The baselines differ.** My 569 → 870 is measured against `main`. PR #20
  independently moves that baseline to 950 entries; I have deliberately not
  quoted any number that assumes their work. Note their 950 counts ~273 names
  from Porkbun's feed that are **not in the IANA root zone** (Handshake names
  like `0zebra`, `3dom`, `4sale`). My Porkbun ingest filters on the root zone,
  which is why my Porkbun count is 634 rather than 907 — worth reconciling
  whichever way you merge, since `ds` cannot look those up.
- If PR #20 lands first, the sane rebase is to keep their file and re-run
  `node scripts/harvest-prices.mjs --sources 101domain` over it.

## Also in here

- **Means round to cents.** Averaging three registrars made `--json` report
  `"renew": 19.279999999999998`. `mean()` now rounds; new test covers it.
- **`/tlds` wording adapts.** The page detected the single-registrar case and
  said so explicitly. It now names all three registrars and says how many rows
  are a real mean (598) versus a lone quote — and still falls back to the old
  honest wording if the table ever narrows to one registrar again. The
  "neither RDAP nor WHOIS" note no longer claims those rows are mostly
  `.co.com`-style suffixes; with the ccTLD tail priced they are mostly country
  codes whose registry publishes no public lookup.
- **`build-tlds.mjs`** counts a registrar behind a row only if it quoted a
  registration price, so the site's count matches the CLI's `registrars` field.
- **README and `ds.1`** — the price column is described as first-year and as a
  mean over registrars; sample outputs updated to the prices the binary now
  actually prints.

## Cost

`pricing.json` 94 KB → 299 KB. Stripped release binary 4.18 MB → 4.38 MB (+5%),
since `include_str!` stores it verbatim. Noted in the README's Development
section so it is not a surprise.

## Politeness

The 101domain crawl is ~1,280 requests. `robots.txt` allows all agents with no
crawl-delay. Requests go out at a global 2.5/s ceiling across 3 workers, with an
honest `User-Agent` naming the project and a link to this repo, exponential
backoff on failure, and no retries beyond one. Full run takes ~20 minutes. The
Porkbun and IANA fetches are a single request each.

body:
## Summary

Three things the site did not have, none of which depend on anything outside the repo.

### Sitemap and robots.txt

Nothing told search engines what pages exist. Six pages is small enough that a crawler would find them eventually, but the site's job is to be found, and neither file costs anything to keep.

- `sitemap.xml` — every page, the top page first, its URL the origin itself rather than `/index.html`
- `robots.txt` — crawling allowed, and the sitemap's location, which is where crawlers look for it

Both are generated by `scripts/build_meta.py` rather than written by hand, so the page list cannot drift from what is actually in the repo and the public URL stays in one place.

### 404 page

An unknown URL showed the host's default error screen — a dead end with no way back into the site. `404.html` keeps the header, menu, lace and footer, so a visitor who mistypes an address or follows an old link lands somewhere that still looks like the shop and can carry on: every page is one click away, twice over.

It is deliberately outside the generated set — `noindex`, no OGP block, and `build_meta.py` skips it, so it stays out of the sitemap and out of shared-link previews. The number reuses the logo's white-fill, pink-outline treatment but takes the stronger pink, since the logo sits on white and this sits on the pink page.

### A default that was a footgun

The public URL now lives in a `DEFAULT_ORIGIN` constant. Running the script without `ORIGIN` set used to quietly downgrade every `og:image` and `og:url` back to a relative path — a bad default for a script whose documented use is "run this after editing a title". `ORIGIN=` still overrides it for a one-off, and moving to a custom domain is a one-line edit plus one run.

Running it produced no change to any page's tags, which confirms #15 landed correctly.

### Cleanup

`pull.txt` and `rating.txt` were empty files left from the repository's GitHub-practice days, unrelated to the site.

## Test plan
- [x] `sitemap.xml` parses as valid XML and lists exactly the six real pages — `404.html` is not among them
- [x] Both files are served from the site root with sensible content types (`text/plain`, `application/xml`)
- [x] Re-running `build_meta.py` leaves the six pages byte-identical — the tags were already correct
- [x] 404 page at 1280px and 390px: no horizontal overflow, 12 working links (6 in-body, 6 in footer), `noindex` present, no OGP tags, no failed requests

## One thing to check after deploy

Vercel is expected to serve `/404.html` for unknown paths on a static site, but that could not be verified from the build environment. Opening a made-up URL after this merges will show whether the new page appears or the default screen still does; if it is the latter, it needs a small config file and I will add it.

author: benskamps
body:
The first run in this estate against a **question** rather than an instrument.

The decision rule was committed at **12:10:02Z, before any real-target disposition was examined** (`4832d91`) — the condition `TRACKS.md` already sets for Track A's arrival, and the difference between an attempt and a fishing trip.

## Result — KILLED, on predeclared terms

| | |
|---|---|
| Null draws | **84,500**, max SDE 8.049 |
| Survey | 9,714 rows over **9,514 distinct targets** |
| Crossings at SDE ≥ 8 | **173** |
| — catalogued planets | **79** |
| — uncatalogued | 94 |

**Strongest uncatalogued: TIC 382028425, SDE 8.048.** Empirical FAP 1.18e-05 from a single null exceedance → expected background **0.113** against a pre-registered ceiling of **0.1**. Independently dispositioned `harmonic-alias`, so it dies twice.

**The claim that this survey already holds an undiscovered transit is killed.** The shelf's empty is no longer an absence of evidence — it is a measured empty with every exit counted.

### The load-bearing detail

**79 of 173 crossings are catalogued planets.** A null from a broken search is worthless, and a test now fails if that count ever reaches zero. The empty means something *because* the search demonstrably works.

The near-miss at 0.113 is the honest sting: a ceiling of 0.15 would have "found" something the vetting chain would then have killed anyway. Pre-registration earned its keep on the first run.

## Also in this change

**Triage.** `U-C01` and `U-I01` **RETIRED** — answered by the field in 2004; no instrument and no plan to get one. `U-M01` priced **out-of-reach at 0.3σ**: P(q) isn't stored per L, and even fixed, 34% error against a 13% effect needs ~62× more realizations ≈ **11 GPU-days**.

**Against my own interest:** retiring two unknowns flipped G01's `every_track_charted` from `False` to `True`. The lab did nothing; I removed the tracks that were failing. Both retirements are honest, the scoreboard effect is real, and it's recorded here rather than banked quietly. Steward warned this would be the failure mode on day one — it took one day.

**`_slug_for`** now recognises catalogue ids, so attempts are as findable in the archive as calibration rungs. The first ATTEMPT receipt in this estate was briefly named `run-2026-08-25-0810-run.json`.

## G01: MET

```
every_track_charted        True
a_field_unknown_attempted  True   ← U-A01
```

Set 2026-08-24 with a 30-day deadline, closed in one day **by a hypothesis dying exactly the way it said it would.** The goal was written so `killed` counts as much as `supported`.

Verified: 9 new tests; full suite **1956 passed, 7 skipped**.

body:
## What

`docs/eval.ja.md` had translated the quick-start `groove eval` transcript without its `Per-query` section (filed in `.dev/known-issues.md` during #229). Adding the three missing lines was not enough: the English example was not what the binary prints either, in four places at once — no `corpus:` line (every run has printed one since 0.15.0, `eval.rs:1236-1237`), a trailing `expected ... missing` phrase the formatter has no code for (`eval.rs:1356-1359` ends the row at the recall value), a `+09:00` timestamp where `DateTime<Utc>::to_rfc3339` writes `+00:00`, a placeholder row id where the real one is the first 32 characters of the query (`eval.rs:685-688`), and an aggregate that could not have come from its own row (one of two queries at `recall@10: 0.00` does not average to `recall@10 1.000`).

Both transcripts are now derived from the golden fence above them under one stated premise (first query hit at ranks 1 and 3, second query missed), and `grooveseek/tests/docs_eval_transcript.rs` builds that run from each page's golden and requires the untagged fence to equal `format_text`'s output character for character. The Japanese row id is the Japanese query, as the binary would print it. `eval::query_id` is now `pub` so the test does not carry a copy of the row id rule.

Same page, same PR: the Japanese hit rule gains the heading-omitted sentence its twin has, and the nDCG heading gets its expansion.

## What this cannot catch

The ranks are the example's premise, not a measurement — nothing runs a search. Every other untagged block on every other page is still unread; the twins guard's module doc now says so instead of saying the defect exists.

## Verification

- Red first: both tests failed on the current pages with the formatter's output in the diff; that output was pasted into the pages (nothing typed by hand, including the CJK padding).
- Probe after commit: `docs/eval.ja.md` `0.460` → `0.821` fails only the Japanese test, naming `docs/eval.ja.md:51`; reverted.
- `cargo test -p grooveseek --test docs_eval_transcript --test docs_commands_twins --test docs_commands_subset --test docs_commands_pinned --test docs_links_resolve --test docs_source_layout` and `cargo test -p grooveseek --lib eval::` green.
- CI block from `CONTRIBUTING.md:41-50` run locally on rustc 1.98.0, all seven green; `cargo test 2>&1 | grep 'test result' | awk` = 47 suites / 1699 passed / 0 failed / 58 ignored.

author: travisbergen2
body:
One cognitive prosthesis, every model. This adds `packages/vault-mcp` (`@rpcs1/second-brain-mcp`): a **local stdio MCP server** that exposes the Obsidian vault — or any folder of markdown — to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and any MCP-capable client, entirely on-device. Obsidian doesn't need to be running.

## The privacy law, one switch

- **OFF by default.** The server re-reads the plugin's `data.json` (`allowedFolders`, `writeBackFolder`) **on every tool call** — flip the setting in Obsidian and the server follows live, no restart. CLI `--allow` is an explicit override for plain-markdown users. Neither present → every tool refuses with opt-in instructions, and nothing (not even an audit file) is written.
- **Same scorer, same caps.** Search shares ≤6 snippets / ≤2400 chars per call via the exact selector the plugin uses — now lifted to `@rpcs1/core` (`vault-select.ts`) as the **single canonical implementation**, with `SELECT_CAPS` deriving from `CONTEXT_SNIPPET_LIMITS`. Plugin behavior byte-identical (default `minScore` 2.5 unchanged; server uses a documented 2.0 floor because MCP sessions have no active note — hop is always 3, so the graph-corroboration term the 2.5 assumed is structurally absent; bare recency/body still never ship).
- **Disclosure travels with the data**: every result lists exactly which paths shipped and how many chars; `Loop/mcp-audit.md` keeps the durable line-per-call log in the vault itself (`--no-audit` to disable; in-result disclosure never disables).
- **Writes are fenced**: `save_to_second_brain` is create-only (`wx`), confined to the write-back folder, and wikilinks its allowlisted sources — MCP saves land in the graph exactly like P3 loop sessions (`kind: mcp-note`, `via: <client from MCP clientInfo>`). Dot-folders (`.obsidian`, `.git`) are never readable, even if explicitly allowlisted.

## Tools

`search_second_brain` · `read_second_brain_note` (8000 chars/call + offset) · `list_second_brain` (metadata only) · `save_to_second_brain`

## Verification

- vault-mcp: **46 new tests** (gates incl. traversal/symlink/dotfolder refusals, OFF-state for all four tools, caps, audit, collision-suffix, no-leak assertions on fixture secrets)
- core: **360 passed** (scorer tests moved in as `vault-select.test.ts`); obsidian: **25 passed**, lint + esbuild green; web tests/lint/prod build green
- **E2E stdio smoke passed** against the built server: initialize handshake, tools/list, search disclosure, private-folder refusal without leaking, save with client identity + wikilink, audit line written
- Branch verified **byte-exact** against the locally tested tree before this PR

## Owner follow-ups (can't do these from here)

1. **CI**: `test-web.yml` path filters + steps don't cover the new package, and the integration token can't modify workflow files (403). Paste-ready 6-line diff is in the PR conversation below.
2. npm publish of `@rpcs1/second-brain-mcp` + MCP-registry listing — your call, later.

author: alexander-blessingmarketing
body:
Beim ersten echten Push im Testprojekt aufgefallen.

## Der Vorfall

`/qa` meldete **„Approved, Production Ready: YES"**. Die CI war rot:

```
src/app/(app)/page.tsx:50        loadLinks() im useEffect
src/components/link-sheet.tsx:61 setSlug(...) im useEffect
✖ 2 problems (2 errors)  react-hooks/set-state-in-effect
```

**Kein Umgebungsunterschied** — der Fehler war im Code und wäre lokal genauso gekommen. Er wurde nur nie gesucht, und lief so durch **vier Features**.

## Die Lücke

| | prüft |
|---|---|
| `/build` | „`npm run build` and `npm test` pass" |
| `/qa` | `npm test` |
| **Lint** | **kommt in beiden nicht vor** |

`.ai-eng-kit` führt `commands.lint` — benutzt wird es aber ausschließlich von `/deploy`, also ganz am Ende. `commands.typecheck` fehlte komplett, obwohl das Script existiert und die CI es ausführt.

## Die Änderung

**`CLAUDE.md`:** „Fertig" heißt `lint`, `typecheck`, `build` und `test` grün — alle vier, am Ende von `/build` **und** `/qa`.

Dazu explizit: **kein `eslint-disable`, um einen Fehler wegzubekommen.** Die Regel hat einen Grund; abschalten verschiebt das Problem in die Laufzeit. Begründete Ausnahmen mit `--`-Kommentar bleiben möglich, wie in `cookie-consent.tsx`.

**`.ai-eng-kit`:** `typecheck` in `commands` ergänzt, damit Skills es überhaupt finden. Nur dieser eine Schlüssel, JSON sonst unverändert.

## Warum das zählt

Ohne frühen PR fällt so etwas erst nach Stunden auf. Mit früherem PR fällt es beim ersten Push auf. Mit dieser Konvention fällt es **beim Bauen** auf — dort, wo es fünf Minuten kostet statt einen Nachmittag.

author: drudge
body:
## What changed

One CSS rule in `internal/web/assets/app.css`:

```css
html:has(dialog[open]) { overflow: hidden; }
```

## Why

A native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` blocks interaction with the page behind it, but it does not stop that page from scrolling. Reported against the dashboard rankings "View all" lists (Top Clients / Top Domains / Top Blocked): with one of those open, a wheel or trackpad flick over the backdrop slid the whole dashboard out from under the dialog.

## Notes for a reviewer

- **Scope is deliberately global.** Every modal in the console has this bug, not just the ranking dialogs. A rule scoped to `.top-stats-dialog` would leave the rest inconsistent. Say the word if you'd rather keep it narrow.
- **No layout shift.** `html` already sets `scrollbar-gutter: stable`, so hiding overflow doesn't reclaim the scrollbar's width or nudge the page sideways.
- **Dialog-internal scrolling is unaffected.** `.top-stats-list` has its own `overflow-y: auto` and lives inside the dialog, so the root clamp doesn't reach it.
- Every dialog in the console is opened via `showModal()`, so there are no non-modal `dialog[open]` elements that would get caught by the selector.
- Programmatic `window.scrollTo()` still works under `overflow: hidden` (that's spec behavior); only user scrolling is blocked, which is what we want.

## Verification

Ran the console locally and drove it in a browser:

- Dialog open, real wheel scroll over the background: `scrollTop` stayed at 0.
- Dialog closed, same wheel scroll: page moved to 600. Confirms the input was reaching the page.
- Opened a dialog with the page already scrolled to 600: background held position instead of drifting.
- Computed `html` overflow flips `hidden` → `visible` on open/close. No console errors.

author: slickg0ose
body:
## What

CI only ever ran `tsc --noEmit` against `client/`. `server/` and `shared/` both have tsconfigs and **neither was typechecked**, so a type error in either could reach `master` with every check green.

Surfaced while upgrading to TypeScript 7 (#103). Both zones were clean then and are clean now — this adds the gate, it doesn't fix a backlog.

```diff
       - run: npm test
         working-directory: server
+      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
+        working-directory: server
+      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
+        working-directory: shared
```

## Why these go in the existing `server-tests` job

Adding a job — or renaming one — renames the required status check. The `develop-policy` ruleset pins checks **by job name**, so a new required check needs an admin to update the ruleset first; until they do, every PR sits blocked on a check that never reports. CLAUDE.md flags this exact trap (the harness job rename in #66 was never re-verified against the ruleset).

So: no new job, and the display name stays `Server tests (vitest + supertest)` even though it now covers a little more than that. Slightly under-descriptive beats deadlocking the merge queue.

## Order

The server typecheck runs **after** `npx prisma generate` — `server/` types depend on the generated client, so it would fail spuriously ahead of it.

## Verification

Confirmed the steps actually gate, rather than assuming a green run means they work — a typecheck step that can never fail is worse than no step at all:

| Zone | Deliberate type error | Clean tree |
|---|---|---|
| `server/` | exit **1** | exit **0** |
| `shared/` | exit **1** | exit **0** |

Canaries removed afterwards; working tree clean. YAML re-parsed after the edit, and all job names verified unchanged.

## Harness ownership

Handled inline in the main session — single-file CI config change, no spec. Under the CLAUDE.md size gate: 1 file, no dependency, no data-shape change.

body:
Deux corrections de CI, toutes deux sur des fichiers qui **disaient autre chose que ce qu’ils faisaient**.

## 1. Les marges de mutation

`mutation.yml` annonçait « deux points sous la plus basse des mesures récentes ». Aucune des trois valeurs ne suivait cette règle :

| part | mesures relevées | seuil | marge réelle |
|---|---|---|---|
| `App\Services` | 58,74 / 58,74 / 79,17 / 80,05 | 80 | **0,05** |
| `App\Actions` | 64,49 / 64,49 / 66,47 / 67,88 | 66 | 0,47 |
| `App\Policies` | 94,28 ×4 | 94 | 0,28 |

La plus basse mesure de Services était **58,74** pour un seuil à **80**. La phrase ne décrivait rien, et pire : elle invitait à desserrer des portes serrées volontairement.

La politique réelle est de poser le seuil **juste sous la dernière mesure**, et le fichier justifie déjà pourquoi c’est légitime, deux lignes plus haut — le score est **déterministe en CI** : code identique, score identique au centième, ce que les 16 et 17 août montrent sur les trois parts à la fois. Une marge n’assure que contre du bruit, et il n’y en a pas.

Le commentaire dit maintenant ça, **et ce que ça implique** : un PR qui fait descendre le score d’un dixième bloque une livraison, et la réponse est de tuer le mutant, pas de baisser le seuil. Sinon il reste une porte de plus qui ne garde rien.

## 2. Le rafraîchissement automatique des avis hors-ligne

Le workflow de #1567 se contentait de prévenir, parce qu’une PR ouverte avec `GITHUB_TOKEN` ne déclenche pas `ci.yml` — GitHub supprime les évènements causés par son propre jeton.

Avec un jeton personnel en secret, il **ouvre lui-même la PR** et la CI tourne dessus normalement : elle arrive verte, il n’y a qu’à fusionner.

**Il te reste une chose à faire** — créer le secret `AVIS_HORS_LIGNE_TOKEN` : un PAT *fine-grained* limité à `kuasar-mknd/gym-tracker`, avec exactement deux droits — **Contents** (lecture/écriture) pour pousser la branche, **Pull requests** (lecture/écriture) pour ouvrir la PR. Rien d’autre, et surtout pas *Workflows*.

**Tant que le secret n’existe pas, rien ne casse** : l’étape se désactive d’elle-même (`if: env.JETON != `) et l’avertissement à 14 jours reprend son rôle. Le workflow reste utile dans l’intervalle.

Une seule branche, réutilisée et poussée en force : au plus une PR de rafraîchissement à la fois, portant toujours l’état le plus récent. Une PR par semaine en laisserait cinq derrière elle le premier mois, et personne ne les relirait.

## Vérification

- `actionlint` (même image Docker que le job `workflows`) : propre — il avait attrapé au passage un heredoc indenté qui ne se terminait pas, remplacé par du `printf`.
- Le script d’ouverture est **rejoué à blanc** avec `git` et `gh` bouchonnés, sur les deux chemins : verrou modifié (commit → push → `pr create`, message et corps vérifiés) et verrou inchangé (sortie immédiate, `ouverte=non`).

*Aucun changement de comportement sur la passe de mutation elle-même : les seuils ne bougent pas.*

author: tomerstarkware
body:
## The bug

`eval_circuit`'s failure branch and `circuit_failure_guarantee_verify` returned `llvm::undef` for the failure guarantee. The corelib walk that destructs it (`u96_limbs_less_than_guarantee_verify`) extracts the guarantee's limbs and branches on their comparison — so native branched on poison, while the VM branches on the real `(nullifier, modulus)` values its hint computes.

The walk stops at the first limb pair (most significant first) where the nullifier and modulus differ. In contracts (compiled with optimizations, so every arm carries a `redeposit_gas`), the stop position determines how much gas is refunded on the failure path. Native's poison walk folds to a fixed arm, so after any failing `circuit_inverse` — e.g. inverting 0, reachable by any modular-arithmetic contract with attacker-controlled input — its remaining gas diverges from the VM: 380 gas for the BLS12-381 modulus, 90 for secp256k1. Around the gas-exhaustion boundary this escalates to a hard divergence: the VM completes the transaction where native reverts with out-of-gas. Branching on poison is also UB regardless of the observed symptom.

## The fix

`CircuitFailureGuarantee` was a ZST in native (the VM's guarantee holds pointers into the builtin segments, which native doesn't have), so it couldn't carry anything. It's now a real value holding the nullifier and modulus limbs:

- `build_gate_evaluation` forwards the failing inverse gate's gcd (already computed by the egcd runtime call) to the error block.
- `eval_circuit`'s error branch materializes `nullifier = modulus / gcd(input, modulus)` — exactly the value the VM's hint computes (`0 < nullifier < modulus`, `input · nullifier ≡ 0 (mod modulus)`) — and stores `{nullifier, modulus}` in the guarantee.
- `circuit_failure_guarantee_verify` unpacks the carried limbs into its `U96LimbsLtGuarantee<4>` output instead of returning undef.

No verification is performed — the values exist solely because the destruct walk's branches consume them.

## The test

`test_data/programs/circuit_failure_guarantee.cairo` destructs the guarantee manually (the corelib-private walk API is importable in single-file programs) and returns the walk length as a first-class value, compared VM-vs-native. Two moduli with different expected lengths (secp256k1 → 2, `[7,0,0,0]` → 4) ensure any walk not steered by the actual limb values fails at least one case. Verified to fail with a return-value mismatch when the fix is reverted.

Note the existing `test_circuit_fail` couldn't catch this: its `[0,0,0,0]` modulus panics at `try_into().unwrap()` before ever reaching the guarantee path, and the precompiled test programs are built with `Optimizations::Disabled`, which emits no `redeposit_gas`, making remaining gas path-independent.

author: czunker
body:
Follow-up to #759. That fix got the bump PR opened and approved; the `Merge Pull Request` step is where [run 32846744040](https://github.com/mondoohq/installer/actions/runs/32846744040/job/97798092992) then stopped.

`gh pr checks --watch` only watches checks that **already exist**. The merge step runs about a second after the PR is opened, when none are registered yet, and gh treats an empty set as a failure rather than waiting:

```
Waiting for checks on PR #760
no checks reported on the 'automation/update-version-13.36.0' branch
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

It was a pure race. On that run the first check (GitGuardian) started at `12:17:25` — one second after the step gave up at `12:17:24` — and all eight checks passed by `12:18:40`. PR #760 was `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN` and approved the entire time, and merged cleanly by hand.

Poll for the first check to appear (up to 5 minutes) before handing off to `--watch`, so the bounded wait covers registration as well as completion. If nothing ever registers the step still fails loudly and fires the Slack alert, rather than hanging to the 20 minute `timeout-minutes`.

Verified by extracting the step body and running it under `bash -e` with a stubbed `gh`: the success path polls, breaks once checks appear, then watches and merges (exit 0); the starvation path runs the full 30 iterations and exits 1 with the `::error::` annotation. `actionlint` is clean.

author: sfc-gh-agedemenli
body:
## Description

Groundwork for authenticating to Iceberg REST catalogs whose authentication pg_lake has no built-in support for. Three independent pieces, none of which change behaviour for any catalog working today.

**Mutual TLS.** A catalog can sit behind a gateway that requires a client certificate on the connection even when the request itself is authorized by a bearer token, because the certificate governs *admission* rather than identity. Adds `pg_lake_iceberg.tls_ca_file`, `tls_cert_file` and `tls_key_file`, applied at the single libcurl setup point so every outbound request picks them up. Each is set only when configured: `CURLOPT_CAINFO` replaces the default CA bundle outright, so passing an empty path would leave the handle unable to verify any peer. Peer and host verification are stated explicitly rather than left to libcurl's defaults, which set the same values. No behaviour change when unset.

**A credential provider.** A catalog can be served by a provider in another extension, named by `pg_lake_iceberg.rest_catalog_auth_provider` as `"library:symbol"` and resolved on first use. Declining a catalog falls back to the built-in OAuth2 client-credentials grant, so one provider can claim some servers and ignore others. pg_lake keeps ownership of caching, refresh and header construction either way.

The provider is resolved by name rather than assigning a hook variable because a provider extension is typically loaded from `shared_preload_libraries`, whereas `pg_lake_iceberg` is loaded on first use of the extension: at the only point a provider runs init code, there is no pg_lake symbol to assign to. Resolving by name also keeps the dependency pointing from pg_lake to the provider, and only when one is configured, so load order stops mattering.

Three details in the contract are deliberate, so a provider can be written and changed without touching pg_lake again:

- the provider returns the whole `Authorization` header value rather than a bare token, letting it choose its own scheme. The three header builders and the retry path no longer hardcode `Bearer`.
- `expiresIn = 0` means "do not cache", which is what a provider needs when it reads a credential rotated underneath it rather than minting one with a known lifetime. This falls out of the existing expiry arithmetic rather than being a special case.
- the provider is handed a small `RestCatalogAuthRequest` rather than `RestCatalogOptions`. A provider lives in a separately built extension, so anything shared is an ABI contract, and `RestCatalogOptions` is an internal struct that will keep changing — and carries the client secret, which a provider has no business seeing. The request struct carries a version so a provider built against an older pg_lake declines rather than misreads it.

**Refreshing on 401.** The retry path already force-refreshes the credential when a catalog answers 419, which is what Polaris sends for an expired token. 419 is non-standard, though, and a catalog fronted by an OAuth2 token exchange answers 401 instead, so a credential that lapsed between minting and use failed the request outright.

401 does not distinguish an expired credential from one that was never authorized, so it earns a single refresh rather than every retry slot: a genuine authorization failure still surfaces on the second response instead of after three round trips. The credential request itself is excluded, since it has no credential to refresh and its own 401 is the authentication failure worth reporting.

No provider is configured in this repo, so with the setting empty every path behaves as before, apart from the `Bearer` prefix moving one layer down and 401 becoming retriable once.

## Test plan

`pg_lake_iceberg/tests/pytests/test_rest_catalog_auth_provider.py` drives a stub provider against a mock catalog that records the `Authorization` header of every request, counts token-endpoint hits, and can answer 401 on demand. The header and hit counts are what separate "the provider supplied the credential" from "pg_lake fell back to its own grant":

- the provider's value arrives verbatim, with a deliberately non-`Bearer` scheme, and no OAuth2 grant runs
- a credential reporting a lifetime is fetched once across two requests
- a credential reporting `expiresIn = 0` is fetched per request
- a declining provider leaves the built-in OAuth2 grant in charge
- a name that is not `"library:symbol"` is reported when a catalog is contacted, since that is when the name is resolved
- a single 401 is retried and re-fetches the credential
- a persistent 401 stops after one refresh, so the failure surfaces after two round trips rather than three

The stub is exported with `PGDLLEXPORT` and resolved through the same `load_external_function` path a real provider would use, since this library is built with hidden visibility exactly as a provider extension would be.

The pre-existing `test_token_refresh_on_retry.py` covers the 419 path and still passes, which is what confirms the Polaris behaviour is undisturbed. 36 tests pass across the provider, retry, catalog, vended-credential and Polaris connection suites. `make check-indent` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes and added tests if necessary
- [ ] I updated documentation if needed
- [x] **I confirm that all my commits are signed off (DCO)**

### Note on docs

The new GUCs are intentionally undocumented for now: they are `GUC_NO_SHOW_ALL | GUC_SUPERUSER_ONLY | GUC_NOT_IN_SAMPLE`, meant to be set by the platform rather than by users, and there is no in-repo provider to document yet. Happy to add a section if you'd rather have one now.

author: jwvanderstam
body:
DEL-2 says *"no sentiment: the eval decides"*. This builds the eval and reports what it found — which is **not** the verdict the ticket expected.

## The instrument

**`tests/eval/retrieval_cases.yaml`** — 20 question/expected-source pairs over this repository's own `docs/`. Your documents aren't available to CI and differ per install; 20 files of real prose about a real system are identical everywhere, which is what makes two runs comparable. An eval set over your own corpus is the natural second one — the harness takes any directory.

Each pair carries a `proof` string checked against the corpus **before** scoring, so a pair whose source was rewritten fails loudly instead of quietly dragging the number down. That check earned itself immediately: **two of my own twenty pairs were wrong** on the first pass, and six more had proofs too common to pin anything.

**`scripts/eval_retrieval.py`** — recall@1, recall@5, MRR, scored by *source file* rather than by chunk, because which chunk "should" have won encodes a judgement nobody made.

## Baseline

nomic-embed-text against the docs corpus: **recall@1 40.0%, recall@5 80.0%, MRR 0.563** over 20 questions.

## The verdict is not in, and that is the finding

Two comparisons came back at **exactly +0.000 on all three metrics**. That is not a null result — it is the absence of a measurement, and it took two guards to establish:

1. **The first ran against zero stored entities.** `GRAPH_RAG_ENABLED` governs extraction *at ingest* as well as expansion *at query time*, so a corpus ingested with it off leaves the "on" arm expanding against nothing.
2. **With 76 entities present, expansion still fired on 0 of 20 questions.** The entities spaCy finds in prose about software are codenames — `SEC-1`, `RBAC-1`, `PG-0`, `Flask` — and natural-language questions contain none of them.

The script now **refuses** both cases rather than printing a tie. A delta of zero from a feature that never ran is indistinguishable in the score from one that ran and didn't help, and that difference decides whether `src/graph/` gets deleted.

Without those guards I would have reported "GraphRAG does not improve retrieval" twice over, with numbers to back it, and been wrong both times.

## A defect found on the way

**`GRAPH_RAG_ENABLED=true` with spaCy's `en_core_web_sm` absent extracts nothing, logs at debug, and still reports a successful ingest.** Extraction is best-effort by design so it never fails an ingest — but the result is a feature you can switch on, that looks enabled, and does nothing. Chapter 12's shape: an absent signal reading as a positive one.

## What answering DEL-2 now needs

In order: install `en_core_web_sm`; then either write pairs whose questions contain indexed entity names, **or** accept the narrower finding that 1-hop expansion is inert for the questions users actually type over this corpus, and decide on that.

The second is a legitimate reason to delete `src/graph/` — but it's a different claim from "it doesn't improve retrieval", and the ticket shouldn't record one as the other.

## Not in CI

Against a stubbed model the numbers measure the stub. This is a `bench_concurrency.py`-shaped tool: run it either side of a change to the RAG path, an embedding model, or the reranker, and record both numbers.

That also makes it the guard for the open `sentence-transformers` 6.0.0 question — every reranker test mocks `CrossEncoder`, so nothing else would notice a ranking shift.

author: ogsai
body:
Fixes the bug reported in [Weird things on interactive puzzle page](https://forums.online-go.com/t/weird-things-on-interactive-puzzle-page/60697): after navigating backward with the new move-number slider, entering the correct solution still showed the red "Incorrect" banner.

## Root cause

The slider and its step buttons route through `GobanController.checkAndEnterAnalysis()`, which switched the goban from "puzzle" mode into "analyze" mode on any navigation. Answer detection, the `puzzle-correct-answer` / `puzzle-wrong-answer` events, and the opponent's automatic responses only run in "puzzle" mode, so one touch of the slider silently disabled the puzzle: later moves became plain analysis variations, no events fired, and the stale banner never cleared. The same switch also broke Joseki exploration after slider use, since Joseki keeps its goban in puzzle mode and relies on `puzzle-place` events.

## Changes

- `GobanController.checkAndEnterAnalysis()` now navigates without leaving puzzle mode, matching the puzzle view's left-arrow/undo path. The puzzle editor's keyboard navigation still enters analyze mode explicitly through `PuzzleNavigation`, which is unchanged.
- The Puzzle view clears the "Correct!" / "Incorrect" banner on any backward navigation (via the goban's `cur_move` event), so slider navigation behaves like the undo shortcut instead of leaving a banner that describes a position the user has left.
- Comment update in `MoveNumberSlider.tsx`; new regression test asserting backward navigation keeps the goban in puzzle mode.

## Testing

- `yarn type-check`, `yarn lint`, jest (472 tests), and `yarn build` all pass.
- Verified in the browser against the beta backend (puzzle 1555, same shape as the reported 99499 scenario): wrong move shows red "Incorrect"; stepping back with the slider clears the banner and stays in puzzle mode; playing the correct move shows green "Correct!" and fires the solution POST. Before the fix, the banner stayed red. Also confirmed the slider still cannot scrub forward into the unplayed solution after a reset.
- The "Try again returns to move 1" behavior discussed in the same thread was left as is, per the thread's conclusion that it is intentional.

author: davetashner
body:
## Summary

[ADR 0013](https://github.com/davetashner/sandtable/blob/main/docs/decisions/0013-chapter-index.md) built the pack's table of contents and printed **no dates in it**. PR #98 said why, and it was a statement about the data rather than about tables of contents:

> `1914:origins` and `1914:july-crisis` sit in a clamped 2–4 August window that is not when they happened, and the data cannot tell the component which windows are real. Their beats carry the true dates in `dateLabel`; the index stays silent rather than lying.

[ADR 0015](https://github.com/davetashner/sandtable/blob/main/docs/decisions/0015-chapter-windows.md) (#113) made the data able to tell it. **The index speaks.**

### The whole pack, by category

Twelve levels, and the two obvious cases are not the whole picture — three of the five chapters have windows that are perfectly real, so "chapter" and "no date" were never the same question. Only `window` separates them, which is exactly what 0015 exists to say.

| `window` | Levels | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _(absent)_ — a real window inside the campaign | `1914:liege`, `1914:lorraine`, `1914:frontiers-north`, `1914:belgium-antwerp`, `1914:guise`, `1914:marne` (zoom-ins); `1914:ardennes`, `1914:grand-couronne`, `1914:tannenberg-east` (chapters) | the span: `4–17 Aug 1914`, `18 Aug – 14 Sep 1914`, `5–12 Sep 1914` … |
| `"outside"` — a real window the campaign does not hold | `1914:meanwhile-epilogue` | the span, from its own clock: `1915–1919` |
| `"placed"` — where it sits on the strip, not when it happened | `1914:origins`, `1914:july-crisis` | **`dates inside`** |

Nine dated from their own windows, one dated from a clock the campaign does not contain, two that cannot be dated at all. `1914:tannenberg-east` is worth naming because it looks like a special case and is not: it is a routeless chapter about the far end of the same war, and its 20 August – 14 Sep window is genuinely when those two corps left the line and arrived, so it is dated like any zoom-in.

### What a `placed` chapter shows, and why

A `placed` window must not be printed — that is the lie 0013 refused, and it is still a lie. But a blank is not the alternative it looks like. In a column where ten of twelve entries carry a date, an empty one does not read as a silence anybody chose; it reads as data that failed to load, which is a worse thing for a page about evidence to say about itself.

So the slot says **why** it is empty and **where** the answer is:

```
The July Crisis: from Sarajevo to the Belgian frontier
CHAPTER · dates inside
```

Inside is `1914:beat-july-crisis`, whose `dateLabel` reads `28 June – 4 August 1914`. The words are the same for every pack, because `placed` is the only thing the engine knows about such a level — and the accessible name carries them too: *"Open the chapter The July Crisis, dates inside"*.

### What was rejected

Written up in full as an **amendment to ADR 0013** (this record's own follow-up, per 0015's consequences); in order of how nearly each one worked:

- **The real span, derived from the chapter's beats' `dateLabel`.** The obvious answer, and it does not survive contact with the field. `1914:origins`'s nine beats carry `1871–1894`, `1891–1905`, `The French frontier after 1871`, `December 1905`, **`The argument since 1956`**, `1906–1914`, `1911–1914`, `1839–1914` and `The plan as a machine`. Two are not dates; one is a date in the 1950s about historiography. A min/max over them prints `1839–1956` — a false span stated with confidence, which is worse than silence. `dateLabel` is authored prose for a reader (`docs/content-model.md` says so), and parsing prose to fill a data slot is how a pack starts lying by accident. It would also mean handing the index the pack's 74 beats to compute a wrong answer.
- **Nothing at all, as before.** Right while the data could not tell the two kinds apart. Once it can, an unexplained gap is the only remaining ambiguity in the column.
- **A word like "Prologue".** True of both of this pack's `placed` chapters and false in general: `placed` means "somewhere on the campaign strip", not "before it", and an interlude placed mid-campaign is as legal. Deriving the word from where the window sits relative to `pack.timeRange` would be inference dressed as data, which is the thing 0015 removed.
- **A new field, `Battle.dateLabel`, in the author's own words.** The fully informative answer and the right one eventually — it is the only way the July Crisis gets to say `28 June – 4 August 1914` in the index. It is also a content-model change (schema, JSON Schema, validator, every pack) two days after 0015 settled the field that says what a window means, and 0015 explicitly rejected a second string beside it. **Filed as a follow-up, not smuggled in behind a chrome bead** — see below.
- **Dates on the breadcrumb trail once you are inside a level.** The trail says where you are, and the timeline under it is already showing that level's window at full width. A second answer to a question nothing asked.

### The shape

`labelSpan` in `src/engine/ticks.ts` writes a span the way a person writes one: drop the month when both ends share it, the year when both ends share that, and write a run of whole calendar years as years — so the epilogue is `1915–1919` and not `1 Jan 1915 – 31 Dec 1919`. Tight dash between bare numbers, spaced between phrases, which is the typography the packs' own `dateLabel`s already use.

The kind tag moves from beside the title to **under** it, with the date, as one mono eyebrow. Beside the title, the longest span the pack has — `18 Aug – 14 Sep 1914` — takes half a 280px column and shreds the long titles into four lines. Under it both are whole, and the title has gained the width the kind tag used to occupy, so several entries that used to wrap now do not.

### Constraints

- **ADR 0006.** The **closed** control is untouched: one pill, one count, no dates. The resting chrome above the map is still a single thin row; the dates live in the disclosure, which was already a wrapped line of its own.
- **ADR 0010.** `--fs-xs` (11.5px, the floor) for the eyebrow, `--fs-sm` for the title, `--space-1` for the gap. No literal sizes.
- **Targets.** Every entry got **taller**, not smaller: a two-line entry is ~44px against the old ~28px, and `min-height: 28px` is unchanged. Nothing in this diff touches `button.card__chip` or any other component's metrics, so the 24.000px measurement in `sand-pmz.15` is exactly where it was.
- **Visual gate.** Green, `scripts/visual-baseline.json` **unchanged — no row retired and none added**. The gate's twenty scenes are URLs and the app's index rests closed, so no app scene renders the list at all; the one cell that does is `gallery`, whose `Chapter index — open` specimen now shows twelve dated entries in both themes. `tiny-text` reports 4 findings across 1 element, as it did before — the authored SVG label ADR 0010 leaves alone.

### Verification

```
format:check     All matched files use Prettier code style!
lint             clean
typecheck        clean
test             62 files, 437 passed (+4 new: three on labelSpan, three on the index; four call sites moved to a prefix matcher now the accessible name carries the date)
validate:content 1 pack — 12 battles, 74 beats … content valid (3 warnings, pre-existing)
build            ✓ built in 788ms
visual:check     84 cells walked, ✓ every scene rendered, no console errors, no structural defect off the baseline
```

**Review artifact: `/gallery.html` on this PR's preview, section "Chapter index — open"** — the twelve entries in both themes on the real pack, with the closed control above them in the breadcrumb specimens.

### Follow-up filed

- **`Battle.dateLabel` for a `placed` chapter's real span** — so the July Crisis can print `28 June – 4 August 1914` in the index instead of pointing at where it is written. Content-model change, its own bead, after this lands.

## Beads

Closes sand-neh.23

author: systemwright
body:
### Wat

Golf 4, fase 2: V17 (kentekenprecisie) en V27 (creditcard-recall), samen omdat beide de
regex-laag raken en samen zijn gemeten.

**V17 — `Licence_Plate` over-maskeerde gewone woorden.** Spatie was toegestaan als scheidingsteken
en het patroon draaide met IGNORECASE, dus "twee letters, twee letters, twee cijfers" matchte op
tweeletterwoorden. In het synthetische corpus waren **7 van de 8** kenteken-matches vals:

| was | nu |
|---|---|
| `zeker 60 reed <Kenteken>-zone` | `zeker 60 reed in de 30-zone` |
| `<Kenteken>, ik sta machteloos` | `ze is 84, ik sta machteloos` |
| `niemand neemt <Kenteken>.30` | `niemand neemt op na 16.30` |
| `artikel <Kenteken> een andere route` | `artikel 12 Sv of een andere route` |

De lay-outs staan nu één keer (`_PLATE_SEP` / `_PLATE_NOSEP`) en worden twee keer gebruikt:
streepjes-gescheiden kentekens blijven hoofdletter-ongevoelig (`ab-12-34`), spatie-gescheiden en
aaneengeschreven kentekens vereisen hoofdletters. Alle echte kentekens (`AB-12-34`, `12-ABC-1`,
`AB 12 34`, `AB1234`, `12ABC1`, `AB-CD-1234`) blijven gemaskeerd; kleine-letter-productcodes
(`ab1234`, `12ab34`) niet meer. `Number` is bewust ongewijzigd (beleidskeuze, geen bug).

**V27 — `Credit_Card` lekte bij een aangrenzend cijfer.** De greedy reeks van 13–19 cijfers slokte
een los cijfer op, de Luhn-controle faalde op 17 cijfers en de kaart bleef **volledig** staan:

| invoer | vóór | na |
|---|---|---|
| `Kaart 4539 5787 6362 1486 2 keer gebruikt.` | ongemaskeerd | `Kaart <Credit_Card> 2 keer gebruikt.` |
| `Kaartnummer 4539-5787-6362-1486-1 ingevoerd.` | ongemaskeerd | `Kaartnummer <Credit_Card>-1 ingevoerd.` |
| `Kaart 4539 5787 6362 1486 gebruikt.` | `Kaart <Credit_Card>gebruikt.` | `Kaart <Credit_Card> gebruikt.` |

Het patroon kent nu expliciete groeperingen (4-4-4-4 met optionele 3-cijferstaart, 4-6-5, 4-6-4,
13–19 aaneengesloten); de Luhn-callback controleert bij een opgeslokte staartgroep het kaartdeel
apart. Luhn-validatie (1.1.3) blijft de wachter: `1234567890123` en `1234 5678 9012 345` blijven
ongemaskeerd. Versie 1.1.10 en CHANGELOG-entry als tweede commit.

### Verificatie (staging-harness, baseline `main @ ea71be0`, v1.1.9)

- Recall-gate `--full`: OK, alle categorieën 1,00, residu-PII 0 (het echte kenteken in de gold
  blijft gemaskeerd).
- Regex-snapshot: **7 records verschillend, alle 7 gereviewd** — uitsluitend herstelde tekst,
  geen enkel echt kenteken geraakt. De snapshot wordt na de merge bewust herschreven.
- 37 gerichte zinnen; een nieuwe red→green-regressiewachter in de harness is rood op de oude
  code en groen op deze.

### Bekend en buiten scope

- Gegroepeerde Amex/Diners/Maestro (`3782 822463 10005`) worden vóór en na door `ID_Number`/`Phone`
  opgevangen omdat die in het order-contract vóór `Credit_Card` staan — deels gemaskeerd, verkeerde
  tag. Apart item (V35), hoort bij het order-contract.
- 17+ aaneengesloten cijfers zonder herkenbare groepering (`45395787636214862`) blijven
  ongemaskeerd, zoals vóór.

### Na de merge

Harness her-ijken op de nieuwe `main`-sha, inclusief snapshot-herschrijving.

author: jayhesselberth
body:
Two of the three defects #213 found but deliberately left alone. Stacked on
`fix/audit-sweep` — both fixes build on that branch's `iter_chunk_columns` and
`ChunkNpzWriter`. **Merge #213 first.**

The third (negative `seq_to_sig_map` entries) is not here: I went looking for a
live trigger and could not find one. The crop is `ref_to_sig_map -
ref_to_sig_map[0]` over a monotonic array, so the minimum is 0 by construction;
zero negatives across all 34 fixture alignments. It is a robustness gap in the
exported `compute_signal_levels`, not a production bug, and it deserves its own
issue rather than a speculative fix.

## `None` written as the string `"None"`

`chunk.get("label", "")` returns the default only when the key is *missing*, so
a key present with the value `None` reached `np.array(..., dtype=str)` and was
stringified.

Two ways in, both routine:

```
prepare with no --label (the default, and what the quickstart shows):
  labels        : ['None', 'None', 'None']
  source_groups : ['None', 'None', 'None']

save/load round trip, which `data merge` performs:
  source_group ''  ->  load -> None  ->  save -> 'None'
```

The second is the nastier one: `save(load(x)) != x`, so merging a corpus
*renamed* its empty source groups to a group called `"None"`.

That bucket then behaves like a real one — `--balance-groups` gives it equal
per-epoch weight with the actual amino acids, and pairwise relabelling (which
matches on the stored label) matches nothing, leaving `label_int` at -1 so
`LeechDataset` drops those chunks silently.

Fixed in `_text()`, in the one place both write paths share. The round trip is
idempotent again.

**Corpora written before this keep their `"None"` strings.** The readers are
deliberately *not* changed to reinterpret them — a source group legitimately
named "None" would then be destroyed silently, which is the same class of bug
pointing the other way. Check with `np.load(f)["source_groups"]` and re-prepare
if affected.

Note the reader convention is not uniform and the test pins that rather than
papering over it: `label` and `source_group` come back as `None`,
`reference_name` deliberately comes back as `""`. Both round-trip cleanly.

## `run_inference` deadlock

The sequential path shut its three `ThreadPoolExecutor`s down with
`wait=False`, leaving worker threads alive past the return; the parallel path
then forks an `mp.Pool`. A fork inherits the memory of a process with running
threads — including any lock those threads hold — but not the threads
themselves, so nothing ever releases it.

`num_workers=0` then `num_workers>0` in one process hung forever, with no error
and no timeout. The CLI never hit it (one predict per process); anyone
scripting the exported `leech.run_inference` twice did.

The pools are drained by that point anyway (`_drain_gpu` and
`_wait_for_bam_write` run above), so `wait=True` costs nothing.

## Tests

7 added; **5 fail on the parent branch**. The 2 that pass both ways are
deliberate guards — one asserts a real label still survives, the other
demonstrates the fork-after-threads mechanism (it exercises the pattern, not
the module, so the source guard is the one that would catch a regression).

Full suite: `1308 passed, 30 skipped in 91.57s`. `ruff format`, `ruff check`
clean.

One note on running this locally: `uv pip install -e '.[test,rust,pod5]'` can
resolve a stale cached `leech_core` (I got 0.6.7-rc.1 against a 0.6.7 source
tree). `tests/test_rust_version_pairing.py` catches it; `bash rust/build.sh`
fixes it.

body:
assembly/pom.xml declares spark-avro at compile scope in <dependencies>, but the `connect` profile re-declares it with <scope>provided</scope>. bigtop's do-component-build activates -Pconnect for spark3, so the profile definition wins and spark-avro never reaches assembly/target/scala*/jars -- which is what make-distribution.sh copies into the distribution. Result: format("avro") is unusable on the shipped spark3 build:

  AnalysisException: Failed to find data source: avro. Avro is built-in but external data
  source module since Spark 2.4.

spark3_3_5_1 ships the jar precisely because its bigtop goals omit -Pconnect, which is the clearest evidence that the profile scope is the cause rather than the module being absent (connector/avro has been in the reactor since ODP-756, 2024-04-18).

author: rhcarvalho
body:
## Summary

While working on #289, I noticed that the API / `/docker` UI may return image tags that were never successfully pushed to Docker Hub.

If downstream code would come across such tags, it would be confusing to handle the "ghost" image tag on the client side. Careful clients would need to query the Docker Hub API or attempt a pull, which is exactly the thing that tends to fail because of transient availability issues and why those clients want to rely on Bob instead of Docker Hub.

---

When `priv/scripts/docker/elixir.sh` and `priv/scripts/docker/erlang.sh` exhaust their 5 retry attempts pushing to Docker Hub, they ended with `(exit 0)`.

Because the scripts returned exit status 0, `Bob.Script.run/3` treated the execution as successful. The calling job (`BuildDockerElixir` or `BuildDockerErlang`) then proceeded to invoke `Bob.RemoteQueue.docker_add/3`, registering the tag in the PostgreSQL `docker_tags` table despite the image never landing on Docker Hub.

This caused several issues:
1. Phantom tags: The Public API (`/api/docker`) and LiveView (`/docker`) advertised images as available when they did not exist on Docker Hub.
2. Suppressed retries: `Bob.Job.DockerChecker` relies on existing tag records to determine what has already been built; registering an unpushed tag prevented `DockerChecker` from re-enqueuing the build job until nightly reconciliation.
3. Incomplete manifests: Subsequent `Bob.Job.DockerManifest` jobs either built single-arch manifests or skipped manifest publication entirely.

History & Evolution:
- In May 2020 (98a64c9, "Cool it with the docker pushes"), `(exit 0)` was added to `elixir.sh`, `erlang.sh`, and `manifest.sh` to prevent transient Docker Hub push errors from failing build jobs.
- In May 2023 (a9afd5b, "Fail manifest"), `manifest.sh` was updated to `(exit 1)` so that failed manifest creation would surface as an error, while `elixir.sh` and `erlang.sh` retained the `(exit 0)` fallback.

Why change to `(exit 1)` and consequences for future jobs:
- Changing `(exit 0)` to `(exit 1)` ensures that when all push attempts fail, the shell script terminates with a non-zero exit code.
- `Bob.Script.run/3` will raise a `%Porcelain.Result{status: 1}` error, failing the job and logging the failure in `Bob.Runner`.
- `Bob.RemoteQueue.docker_add/3` is never reached, preventing the tag from being inserted into PostgreSQL.
- On subsequent runs, `Bob.Job.DockerChecker` will see the tag missing and automatically re-enqueue the build job.


## Testing

These shell scripts depend on live Docker daemon operations and external Docker Hub network pushes, so push failure paths are not directly exercised by the unit test suite. Verified via script analysis, shell exit code behavior, and running `mix test --warnings-as-errors`.
