body: ### Summary Adds scroll-triggered reveal animations across the site sections and unifies button hover/interaction styling with fully rounded, "depth" hover effects. ### Problem The page felt static as users scrolled, with sections appearing abruptly and no motion feedback. Buttons across the site also had inconsistent shapes (some square, some pill) and hover styles, unlike the fully rounded look used in the header nav. ### Solution Introduced a reusable `useReveal` hook backed by `IntersectionObserver` to detect when sections enter the viewport, and paired it with new CSS motion utility classes for fade/rise/stagger reveal effects. Updated all major sections to use these utilities. Standardized button styling by adding a shared `button-depth` class (hover lift + shadow) and switching buttons to `rounded-full`, matching the nav's rounded pill look. Also updated the Storefront SVG text from "PORTFOLIO" to "RESTAURANT" and made the marquee pause on hover. ### Key Changes - Added `src/hooks/use-reveal.ts`: IntersectionObserver-based hook returning `ref` and `isVisible` for scroll-triggered reveals - Added new motion CSS utilities in `styles.css`: `motion-hero-rise`, `motion-hero-scale`, `motion-reveal` (with delay variants), `motion-stagger`, `motion-band-underlay`, `motion-band-content`, `motion-card`, `motion-image`, `motion-sway`, and `button-depth` - Wired `useReveal` into `CollageGrid`, `CraveMarquee`, `FeaturedSection`, `FlavorCta`, `IconBand`, `NewMeal`, `Reviews`, `SiteFooter`, and `TypeSpiral` sections - Applied `motion-hero-rise`/`motion-hero-scale` entrance animations to `Hero` and `Nav` - Standardized buttons to `rounded-full` with `button-depth` hover/active lift effect in `Hero`, `Nav`, `KhidaSection`, `FeaturedSection`, `Reviews`, `SiteFooter`, and the shared `ui/button.tsx` variants - Updated `Marquee` to pause animation on hover via `group-hover:[animation-play-state:paused]` - Changed Storefront SVG label text from "PORTFOLIO" to "RESTAURANT" with adjusted font size and text length - Added `prefers-reduced-motion` overrides to disable all new animations/transitions for accessibility ---    > [!TIP] > This PR wasn't reviewed by Quality Agent. author: tomasmbrito
body:
Slice A of #134, the first of five. Planned in `.claude/plans/recruitment-and-onboarding.md`.

⚠️ Schema (migration **019**) + auth change. Approved 2026-08-25 along with retention, manual membership, and coordinator-level decisions.

## It replaces a dead link

`JoinsUs.tsx` had `const joinUsLink = "https://google.com"`. The "Candidata-te" button on the public site pointed at Google. That shipped.

## The modelling problem: the outcome is per team

Someone who applies to Dev-Team, Visuais and Fotografia may be accepted by one and rejected by another. So it cannot be a status column on the application — it is a row per `(application, department)`, keyed by `departments.name`, the same key `internal_events` and `tasks` use, so `canForTeam` authorizes each decision with **no translation step** (the #180 lesson).

Verified end to end against a running app:

```
Fotografia coordinator accepts        200
…tries to decide Visuais' part        403  "Insufficient permissions"
outcomes afterwards                   Visuais=pending, Fotografia=accepted
```

## Three access decisions

**The form is public.** Asking someone to authenticate to a system they have no relationship with, in order to apply for one, is the wrong order. It is therefore the only unauthenticated write in the workspace family — so **every rule lives in `submit_application`**, not the route: there is no caller to check. Submission verified with no session at all.

**Reviewing needs `team.recruitment.decide`, not `team.workspace.view`.** Every other workspace panel lets any member of the team look. These rows hold names, phones, emails and motivations belonging to people who may never join NEIIST, so reading them is a narrower act:

```
coordinator of Fotografia   200
MEMBER of Fotografia        403   ← sees the rest of the workspace, not this
coordinator, other team     403
```

It is **not grantable**. A two-week borrowed scope should not read that pile, nor decide somebody's year.

**Retention: 6 months after decision**, enforced by `purge_old_applications` rather than by anyone remembering. Importing Notion's GDPR exposure into the website would defeat the point of the whole migration (#126). Undecided applications are never purged — they have not been dealt with.

## Two traps worth recording

**`/candidatura` had to be added to `publicRoutes`, and the reason is the mirror image of #97/#117.** `canAccess` is only consulted for an *authenticated* request, so an unlisted public page works fine logged out and redirects **logged-in** visitors to `/unauthorized`. A member sharing the form with a friend would have hit exactly that. Caught by the planner, not by me.

**"One open round at a time" cannot be a partial unique index.** `NOW()` is `STABLE`, and Postgres refuses it in an index predicate — correctly, since an index whose membership changes with the clock is not an index. It is a trigger.

## Proven

18 tests. Mutations, all killed:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| a decision applies to every team, not just this one | 5 failed |
| the reader ignores the department | 2 failed |
| applications accepted with no round open | 2 failed |
| the purge deletes undecided applications too | 2 failed |
| *(restored)* | 18 passed |

One test-hygiene fix found the hard way: a mutation run died before `afterAll` and left a test edition behind, which the overlap trigger then used to block **every** later run — presenting as a broken suite rather than stale state. The fixture clears its own leftovers first now.

Browser: the form shows only the seven teams (admin bodies are elected, not applied to), states the multi-team rule in the copy, and the review panel expands to show contact details plus *"Candidatou-se também a: Visuais"* — the other team named without leaking its decision.

```
yarn type:check   PASS
yarn lint         PASS
yarn format:check PASS
yarn test         PASS  356 tests (18 new)
yarn build        PASS
fresh schema.sql  clean; 3 recruitment tables
```

## What is NOT here

Slices B–E, deliberately: **interview scheduling** (creates an `internal_event` — #129 is already merged and will be reused, not duplicated), **the acceptance email and its token**, **the onboarding page** (phone, `@neiist.pt` address, WhatsApp links), and anything touching Google Workspace.

The acceptance email is the one I most want landing on its own — sending is irreversible, and a token that authenticates a specific applicant is credential-adjacent. It deserves its own diff and its own review.

`@neiist.pt` generation is **#213 / PR #214**, already open and independent.

author: yashmhatre
body:
The repository went public today carrying no licence at all, which left it all-rights-reserved by default: nobody could legally use, fork, or contribute to it.

## Why Apache 2.0 rather than MIT

- **Section 6 withholds the trademark grant.** The code licence and the project name stay separate without needing a second document. MIT is silent here, which is why MIT projects end up writing a standalone TRADEMARK policy to cover the same ground.
- **Section 4(d) gives `skills/NOTICE` a formal role.** The vendored third-party skills are MIT and their attribution has to propagate downstream. Apache 2.0 is what makes that file load-bearing rather than decorative, and MIT vendors into an Apache 2.0 project cleanly.
- **Section 3 grants patent rights.** Enterprise review expects that from a tool that shells out to vendor CLIs, and enterprise data engineering is the stated target.

## What is here

- `LICENSE` is the canonical text from apache.org, byte-identical through END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS. Only the appendix placeholders were filled in with a copyright line, so licence detection and scanners still identify it as stock Apache 2.0.
- `pyproject.toml` declares the licence as an SPDX expression per PEP 639, which raises the setuptools floor to 77. `license-files` carries both `LICENSE` and the vendored `skills/NOTICE` into the wheel.

Verified: a built wheel reports `License-Expression: Apache-2.0` with both `License-File` entries present, and the suite is 238 passed.

## Open item, not addressed here

`skills/MANIFEST.yaml` flags that `theclaymethod/unslop` states its MIT grant only in prose, with no LICENSE file and no named copyright holder, and asks that this be resolved before AgentForge is distributed publicly. That has now happened. Tracked upstream separately; the grant itself is unambiguous, so it does not block this.

author: roozbehshafiee
body:
## Summary

UBI-186: three real changes extending the existing Smithy path so AWS can get data sources, mirroring what UBI-178/181 already built for the other five providers.

- Add `List` to `readVerbs`. Roughly doubles the real candidate pool (2,420 to 4,924 raw, confirmed live against all 430 real AWS Smithy models from `github.com/aws/api-models-aws`). Naive addition changed 34 of 1,420 existing resource read pairings (S3's own `Bucket` resource silently repointed from `GetBucketAcl` to `ListBuckets`, a real correctness break). Fixed via `bestMatchExistingResource`, which tries Get/Describe first and only falls back to List; verified live to change zero existing pairings.
- Add `DiscoverDataSources`, the inverse of `Discover`: every real read-verb-prefixed operation not already claimed as a resource's own read op.
- Add `FetchCatalog`: enumerates all real service model files in `github.com/aws/api-models-aws` via the git Trees API's own recursive mode, one real HTTP call. `schema_url` resolves one file at a time today; AWS-wide coverage needs all of them. Live-tested (`UBX_LIVE_VALIDATION=1`), gated the same way this repo's other live tests already are.

Real, live-verified counts: 429 of 430 real services parse (one blocked on an unrecognized protocol trait, `partnercentral-revenue-measurement`); 4,924 raw data-source candidates, 4,545 survive UBI-181's own five filter rules applied fresh to this corpus.

Discovery only, matching Checkpoint 1's own established scope split: no schema translation or naming resolution for data sources yet, and no config-expansion (the `sdk/providers/.ubx/config` entries a real AWS-wide rollout would need) -- naming agreement between this path and the CFN-derived resource side needs to be settled first (see the linked report).

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` clean, including the new `datasource_test.go` and `resourcemap_test.go` regression cases
- [x] Live test against the real `github.com/aws/api-models-aws` repo passes (`UBX_LIVE_VALIDATION=1 go test ./internal/smithy/... -run TestFetchCatalog`)
- [x] Verified live against all 430 real downloaded service models that the List-verb fix changes zero existing resource read pairings

author: mudream4869
body:
## 目標

一次匯入數十本書時，`useImportBook.submit()` 是逐檔 for 迴圈，`ImportBookModal` 只列出每檔文字狀態——沒有彙總進度、沒有百分比、也不能中止（`onClose` 在 `submitting` 時直接 return，modal 完全鎖死）。42 本 EPUB 的匯入看起來就像卡住。

這張票補上「第 N / M 本」進度與中止，並把 submit 的「來源」抽象成 executor，讓下一張票（desktop）能重用同一套進度與中止邏輯。

## 變更

- **抽象化 submit**：`submit(units, executor)` 成為與來源無關的核心，負責進度統計與檔案邊界中止；`File` 上傳改為其中一種 executor（`submitFiles`）。匯入單元不再綁死 `File`。
- **中止語意**：新增 `abort()`——進行中的檔案跑完後，在檔案邊界停止；剩餘檔案標為可辨識的 `cancelled` 狀態（不與 `failed` 混淆），且不再送出任何 import request。中止後若已有成功匯入，沿用既有的 `results.partial` 文案。刻意對齊 `taskutil` 的 `partially_completed` 心智模型。
- **UI**：`ImportBookModal` 顯示 `ProgressBar` 與「第 N / M 本：\<檔名\>」以及「中止」按鈕，僅在多檔批次時出現；單檔匯入的行為與文案完全不變（不多出進度條或確認）。
- **i18n**：`en.ts` 與 `zh-Hant.ts` 同步補上 progress／abort／cancelled 狀態與 cancelled 結果文案。

## 不在範圍

依票面保留：byte 級上傳進度、匯入中背景化（state 提到 store）、server-side import taskchain。

## 測試

新增 `useImportBook.test.ts`，涵蓋 (a) 進度遞增 (b) 中止後停止送出且剩餘標為 cancelled、非 failed (c) 部分成功的彙總結果，另加單檔文案不變與 executor 解耦兩案。

- `npm --prefix frontend test` — 1128 passed（含新增 5 案）
- `npm --prefix frontend run build`（`vue-tsc --noEmit` + build）— 通過
- `npm --prefix frontend run check-boundaries` — 通過

未跑：Go 測試（本次無 Go 變更）、e2e。

author: marynes0111
body:
## Objective
Replace plain-text logs with structured JSON, and add a correlationId that lets a single request be traced end-to-end across filter, handler, and controller — the missing piece the existing runbooks already reference but that didn't exist yet.

## Summary
- Added `logstash-logback-encoder` and `logback-spring.xml`: all log output is now structured JSON (`@timestamp`, `message`,  `logger_name`, `level`, `app`), instead of Spring Boot's default  plain-text format.
- Added `CorrelationIdFilter`: generates a UUID per request (or reuses an incoming `X-Correlation-Id` header if present), puts it in MDC, and echoes it back in the response header. MDC is always cleared in a `finally` block to avoid leaking across requests on reused threads.
- Registered via a dedicated `FilterRegistrationBean` with `Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE` in `LoggingConfig`, so the correlationId exists before the entire Spring Security filter chain runs — not just within it.

## Verification (live, not just unit-level)
- Confirmed console output is valid structured JSON after startup.
- Sent an unauthenticated request to a protected endpoint (`GET /api/references` without a JWT): response returned `x-correlation-id: be21a51d-...` header, and the corresponding
  `AuthEntryPointJwt` log line included the exact same `"correlationId":"be21a51d-..."` field — confirming the ID survives  through a path that runs entirely outside the normal controller/service flow, which is the hardest case to get right.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Logs are structured JSON in dev (test/prod use the same logback-spring.xml, no profile-specific divergence)
- [x] Every log line within a single request shares the same correlationId
- [x] correlationId present even for requests that fail before reaching a controller (confirmed via 401 case)
- [x] `mvn verify` passes

closes #184

The local full-suite red that held #483's merge up **was load, not the change.** Two local runs
failed a *different* 1 and 3 specs (`meal-label`, `food-logging-complete`,
`tabs-instant-paint (More)`); none reproduced alone or in a 15-test subset. **CI E2E passed all of

**It took 11m16s.** A docs-only PR's E2E job ran just as long, so that is the job's cost here, not
something this change caused. Two things follow, and both are now in the baton:

- A long-running E2E is not a hang. I read one as stalled for a while because

author: hihancioglu
body:
### Motivation

- Operators need actionable diagnostics when External ACS or Hikvision ACS HTTP deliveries fail so background retries are visible in logs without exposing credentials. 
- The manual "Test Door Action" flow currently drops error details; surface a sanitized connection/validation error on the device page to aid troubleshooting.

### Description

- Add `_log_delivery_failure(kind, action, device)` to record sanitized warning logs for asynchronous ACS failures and call it on both HTTP non-2xx responses and exceptions in the External ACS and Hikvision ACS delivery paths (in `app/acs.py`).
- Preserve secrecy of credentials while logging actionable context: action id, device serial number, attempt count, queue status, HTTP status and sanitized error (in `app/acs.py`).

## What

`IDM_MEASURE_SAT_ALL_LEVELS` ("All colors at all stimulus levels") was reusing the plain `measure-sat-all` glyph, so it looked identical to `IDM_MEASURE_SAT_ALL` in every place both appear. It now uses the new `measure-all-sat-stim` artwork.

Three call sites:

- `Views/MainView.cpp:6576` — sat-mode all-levels button, idle state restored after a sweep ends.
- `Views/MainView.cpp:7590` — same button, initial creation.

- **Light-theme `measure-sat-all` for the toolbar set.** `toolbar/light` and `toolbar/dark` were byte-identical for this glyph, i.e. the toolbar had no light variant at all and served the dark line art to both themes. (`menu/light` already had a distinct one.)

author: kadsa-mxzi
body:
Closes #225

## Summary

너클을 요청대로 개편했습니다.

1. **머리 위 게이지 바** (`scripts/gauge_bar.gd`) — 너클을 들었을 때만 뜹니다.
   `Player.gauge` 값은 있었는데 **그리는 곳이 없어서**, 게이지로 세기가 갈리는 유일한 무기인데
   그 세기가 화면에 없었습니다.
2. **충전을 "맞은 횟수"에서 "받은 데미지"로** — `gauge_fill_damage`(40)만큼 받으면 100%입니다.
   출혈처럼 무적을 무시하는 지속 데미지도 함께 셉니다.
3. **강펀치를 부채꼴로** (150px · 80도) — 한가운데 **10~40**, 가장자리는 그 **45%**.
   감소가 거리가 아니라 **각도**입니다: 코앞에서 내지르는 것이라 조준이 값이어야 합니다.
4. **게이지 75%부터 오라** — 젤리에 자홍 오라가 돌고, 게이지 바 색이 바뀌고,
   강펀치 연출이 **다른 디자인**으로 나갑니다(`scripts/heavy_punch.gd` — 청록 결정 조각 + 고리).
   세 곳이 `Player.is_charged()` 하나를 봅니다.

| 항목 | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 게이지 표시 | 없음 | **머리 위 바** (너클만) |
| 충전 | 피격당 +10 | **받은 데미지 × 100/40** |
| 스킬 판정 | 단일 근접 | **부채꼴 150px · 80도** |
| 데미지 | 게이지 비례 10~40 | 한가운데 10~40, 가장자리 45% |
| 오라·연출 | 없음 | 75%부터 오라 + 전용 연출 |

게이지는 **맞았는지와 무관하게 비워지고 쿨타임도 늘 돕니다** — 헛치면 게이지만 날아가는 것이
이 무기의 무게입니다. 부채꼴이 되면서 **크게 들어 올린 방패가 정면에서 막습니다**(#222와 같은 판정).
근접 특수였을 때 `is_blocked()`(사거리 비교)에 막혔던 길이 사라지므로 같은 규칙을 이었습니다.

## Verification

Godot 4.6.2 헤드리스 `--script` 하네스, **24항목 전부 PASS**.

- **무기 표** — `gauge_max` 100 / `gauge_fill_damage` 40 / 한가운데 10~40 / 부채꼴 150px·80도 /
  가장자리 45% / 오라 75%, 그리고 `gauge_per_hit`이 사라진 것까지 확인
- **씬 로드** — `heavy_punch.tscn`·`player.tscn`·`main.tscn`
- **게이지 바** — 너클에서 보이고 검에서는 안 보인다
- **충전** — 10 데미지 → 25% / 누적 30 → 75%(여기서 `is_charged()` 켜짐) / 누적 50 → 100%에서 멈춤
- **부채꼴** — 게이지 100% 한가운데 **40.0** / 가장자리 **18.5** / 게이지 0% 한가운데 **10.0** /
  사거리 밖 0 / 각도 밖 0 / **정면 방패 0**
- **소모** — 쓰면 게이지 0, 오라도 꺼짐
- **연출 실물 확인** — 창을 화면 밖에 열어 프레임을 PNG로 뽑아 눈으로 확인했습니다.
  게이지 100% 젤리에 자홍 오라와 가득 찬 바, 40% 젤리에 보라 반 바(오라 없음),
  충전 강펀치는 자홍 부채 + 청록 결정 + 고리, 평소 강펀치는 호박색 부채로 확실히 다릅니다.

## Residual risks

- **연출 디자인의 근거가 스크린샷 2장뿐입니다.** 함께 주신 mp4 2개는 이 작업 환경에서
  열 수 없었습니다(영상 디코더가 없고 ffmpeg 도 없습니다). 영상에서 본 것과 다르면
  그 장면을 캡처해 주시면 맞추겠습니다.
- **한가운데 40은 근접 특수 중 상위권**입니다(망치 16 + 기절, 양날 도끼 28 + 충격파 14).
  다만 40 데미지어치 받아야 도달하는 값이고, 그동안 이미 밀리고 있다는 뜻이기도 합니다.
  너무 세면 `gauge_max_damage`, 너무 자주 나오면 `gauge_fill_damage`를 손댑니다.
- **부채꼴 150px는 근접(약 86px)보다 넓어** 닿지 않을 거리에서도 들어갑니다.
  기획서의 "단거리"와 어긋나면 줄일 곳은 `punch_cone_range`입니다.
- 전용 서버와 내보낸 실행 파일을 함께 갱신해야 합니다.

author: vib-adhoc
body:
Fixes #1209.

`checkCredentials()` treated an expired access token as a lost login. The token lives
~12 hours and the CLI refreshes it with the refresh token the next time it runs, so a
session left idle overnight reported as disconnected while the login was intact.

A present `refreshToken` now counts as still logged in.

**To reproduce:** log in with `claude /login`, leave the CLI unused until
`claudeAiOauth.expiresAt` passes, then open Settings → Agents → Claude → Account.

author: profindecom-alt
body:
## Why

The phone number in the code did not match the Google Business Profile, and the Sanity CMS had drifted from the code on several identity fields. `app/seo.ts` already documented itself as the single source of truth for NAP — this makes that true and removes Sanity from the metadata layer entirely.

## Contact details

- **Phone** `+212667680937` → `+212666566865` (matches GBP). The `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD reads `BUSINESS.phoneE164` directly with **no CMS fallback**, so structured data had been publishing the wrong number while the visible site showed the right one.
- **WhatsApp** fallback → `212665417683` — a genuinely separate line, now commented so it isn't "aligned" with the phone later.
- **Five WhatsApp buttons** built their `wa.me` link from the *phone* number rather than the WhatsApp line. Pre-existing bug, now fixed.
- **Hours** → `00:00`–`23:59` all week (Google's encoding for open 24/7), matching GBP.

## Hardcode identity / drop Sanity from meta

- Removed every `settings?.x || BUSINESS.x` fallback; phone, email, address, social links and analytics IDs now live in `app/seo.ts`.
- **Fixes a live bug:** the CMS held `contact@amnay-gency.com` (typo — missing the `a`), which won over the correct code value in the footer `mailto:` on every page.
- `SOCIAL_LINKS` drives both the footer icons and JSON-LD `sameAs`, so they cannot drift.
- Dropped the `google-site-verification` tag — the stored value was the HTML-*file* method string, not a meta token, and was being emitted verbatim. GSC verification is unaffected (verified by another method).
- `RootLayout` no longer touches Sanity; removed 14 dead `siteSettings` fetches left across the app.
- Removed the now-unused fields from the Sanity query, types and schema. **Stored data is untouched.**

## SERP metadata

- Homepage title gains the brand — Google was rewriting the title link on brand queries because neither `<title>` nor `<h1>` contained "Amnay".
- Meta description 165 → 141 chars so it stops truncating; extracted to `SITE_DESCRIPTION` (was duplicated in four places).
- Added a `WebSite` JSON-LD node linked to the existing Organization `@id`. No `SearchAction` — there is no `/search` route.
- Service JSON-LD `PostalAddress` now matches the root layout's.

## Verification

Checked against the **built HTML**: `tel:`/`mailto:`/`wa.me` links, JSON-LD phone, email, `sameAs`, hours, title and description. `tsc`, `eslint` and `next build` all clean.

author: huina017
body:
## 개요 🔎

최고 관리자가 탈퇴한 회원을 일정 기간 내에 복구할 수 있도록 회원 복구 API를 구현했습니다.

회원 탈퇴 후 7일 이내에만 복구할 수 있으며, 같은 회사의 회원에 대해서만 최고 관리자가 복구할 수 있도록 권한 및 상태 검증을 추가했습니다.

## 작업사항 📝

* 회원 복구 API 추가

  * `PATCH /api/users/:userId/restore`
* `SUPER_ADMIN` 전용 복구 권한 적용
* 같은 회사 소속 회원만 복구 가능하도록 검증
* `WITHDRAWN` 상태의 회원만 복구 가능하도록 처리
* `withdrawnAt` 기준 탈퇴 후 7일 이내 복구 가능하도록 제한
* 복구 시 회원 상태 변경

  * `status: WITHDRAWN → ACTIVE`
  * `withdrawnAt → null`
* 회원 복구 관련 에러 코드 추가

  * `USER_ALREADY_ACTIVE`
  * `USER_CANNOT_RESTORE_SUPER_ADMIN`
  * `USER_INVALID_RESTORE_STATE`
  * `USER_RESTORE_PERIOD_EXPIRED`
* 복구 기간 관련 상수 공통화
* 회원 목록에서 `ACTIVE`, `WITHDRAWN` 회원을 모두 조회하도록 수정
* 회원 목록 응답에 `status`, `withdrawnAt` 추가

## 테스트 ✅

* 정상 회원 복구 성공
* 이미 ACTIVE 상태인 회원 복구 차단 확인
* 복구 기간 7일 초과 회원 차단 확인
* USER / ADMIN 권한 접근 시 `403` 확인
* 다른 회사 SUPER_ADMIN의 복구 요청 차단 확인
* 존재하지 않는 회원 복구 시 `USER_NOT_FOUND` 확인
* `WITHDRAWN`이지만 `withdrawnAt`이 없는 비정상 상태 차단 확인
* 복구 후 DB에서 `ACTIVE`, `withdrawnAt = null` 반영 확인

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes user lifecycle and listing behavior (withdrawn users visible again) with authorization checks; incorrect date or status logic could restore wrong accounts or leak withdrawn members past the window.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **member restore** for company super admins via `PATCH /:userId/restore`, mirroring withdrawal guards (same company, not `SUPER_ADMIN`) and only allowing `WITHDRAWN` users whose `withdrawnAt` is within **7 days**.
> 
> Restore uses a conditional `updateMany` in the repository (`WITHDRAWN` → `ACTIVE`, clears `withdrawnAt`); the service maps failed updates to new error codes (`USER_ALREADY_ACTIVE`, `USER_CANNOT_RESTORE_SUPER_ADMIN`, `USER_RESTORE_PERIOD_EXPIRED`, `USER_INVALID_RESTORE_STATE`).
> 
> **Member list** now returns recently withdrawn users (still inside the recovery window) alongside active members, with `status` and `withdrawnAt` on each row. Shared constants live in `src/constants/user.ts`. `package-lock.json` only drops `dev: true` on optional `@typescript/*` platform packages.

body:
# First Merge Request : Estrutura Inicial do Domínio

## Descrição
Este *merge request* implementa a modelagem inicial das entidades base e dos *enums* fundamentais para a base de dados do sistema.

### Novas Entidades

author: akeemphilbert
body:
Closes #520

Stacked on #527 (story #519) ← #526 (story #523).

## What

The house vocabulary moves to the domain WeOS owns: `mp:` → `https://weos.io/vocab/meal-planning#`, `mem:` → `https://weos.io/vocab/memory#`, `ag:` → `https://weos.io/vocab/agents#`, including the ten memory/agents terms that spell the namespace out in full. No file under `application/presets/` references `weos.org` (a source guard and a registry-wide sweep enforce it). Nothing is retargeted to another ontology.

- **Fresh install:** every class, reference predicate and literal predicate lands on `weos.io`; every reference property still reverse-maps to its own name.
- **Existing install:** the boot HOLDS each prefix (and each full-IRI term) at its stored definition and reports it on every boot; every existing edge and every write made while held stays readable; an additive change beside a held prefix still lands; a plain `preset install` never overwrites it. Adopting the held Conflict is story #518 (six scenarios wait `@wip @needs-518`).
- **`normalize-edge-keys --restamp`** (decided today; #521 reuses it): a reprojection replays payloads verbatim, so a resource written before a term, prefix or class moved keeps the old IRI in its own embedded `@context` forever. `--restamp` brings every document's embedded `@context` and entity `@type` up to what a fresh write embeds now — from the type's **stored** context — and moves the aggregate's `Triple.Created`/`Triple.Deleted` predicates with it (otherwise a reproject folds the old predicate back in as a second edge). `--type` scopes it. Dry run by default, idempotent, batches never split a transaction, a document with a declined edge keeps its context.
- **Memory recall** accepts both the current and the legacy Fact class and confidence predicate (COALESCE, DISTINCT), so an install mid-migration does not go blind.
- Docs: the how-to gains the re-stamp procedure and its limits (held context → nothing to move until adopted; the triples table is upsert-only so the old row lingers).

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/features/house_vocabulary_domain.feature` — 60 scenario rows in the default gate over the REAL presets (a new world whose "old build" is the default registry with `weos.io` rewritten back), plus 6 `@wip @needs-518`.
- `application/edge_key_normalization_db_test.go` — the IRI-keyed document + `Triple.Created` shape moves together in one run and is idempotent.
- `application/presets/house_vocabulary_domain_test.go`, `application/memory_recall_sparql_test.go`, printer tests.

## Decisions Akeem made

- `--restamp` instead of "historical resources keep the old class"; assertions on the stored document (what the graph store ingests) rather than the tag-gated oxigraph store.
- Four re-stamp scenario amendments (fixture scope, prefix mapping in the literal outline, Triple.* move, triples table follows).

## Noted, not done

- Downstream copies of the old IRIs: `services/mini-me-weos/cmd/mini-me/food_preset.go` and its e2e support — file in `wepala/mini-me-weos` (and check finexity) after this merges.
- The `kg_*` tools list two Fact classes until the graph is rebuilt; `RemoveSubject` clears only the current class's ontology triples.
- The `context terms diverge` warning has no remedy until #518; #518 should make the line name it.

body:
Closes #810.\n\nTreats recursively provable empty literal dictionary unpacking as incapable of overriding a selected key, while retaining conservative fallthrough for dynamic unpacking. Adds both positive and negative regressions.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to static literal dict subscript resolution in the type checker; dynamic unpacking behavior stays conservative.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#810** by allowing static dict subscript lookup (e.g. `{"x": target, **{}}["x"]`) when literal unpacking is recursively provable as empty, so empty `**{}` no longer blocks resolving a concrete callable on a static key.
> 
> Callable resolution in `check.rs` previously required every dict entry to have an explicit key; the new `literal_dict_is_provably_empty` / `literal_dict_has_only_static_items` helpers treat only `**{...}` literals that cannot add keys as safe, while **dynamic** unpacks like `**mapping` still skip static resolution. Regression tests cover nested empty unpacks and the dynamic decline path.

author: nmc192-ux
body:
Every TikTok post died on this, and the error message contained the proof:

```
TikTok token refresh failed: {"access_token":"act.i2Nzw…","expires_in":86400,
"open_id":"-000oiy5…","refresh_expires_in":31214061,…}
```

**A valid token, printed inside a failure.**

TikTok's v2 `/oauth/token/` returns the fields **flat** at the top level. Only v1 nested them under `data`. This client read `body.data?.access_token` — the v1 shape — so a perfectly successful refresh evaluated to `undefined` and threw.

Both shapes are accepted now, so a future move back isn't another outage. `expires_in` defaults to 24h rather than producing `NaN` if absent.

## The pattern worth naming

This is the **third** TikTok defect in a row where the *check* was wrong rather than the credential:

1. `isTikTokConfigured()` demanded the access token this very function mints
2. the credentials were never on the VPS at all
3. and now the parse

**Nothing was ever wrong with the account.** Every failure was our own gate misreading a working setup — and each one produced a message ("not configured", "refresh failed") that pointed away from the real cause.

Found by posting a real short through the deployed client, not by reading code.

Suite **1047 pass / 0 fail**.

author: samsmithyeah
body:
Part 2 of the app-reset work (stacked on #210). Plan: declared isolation (#210) → **daemon `ResetApp` + Android deep-link fix (this)** → persistent UI worker → readiness/speculation → `@tapsmith/react-native` warm reset.

## Why
After #210 the declared policy still ran as a sequence of individual RPCs from the SDK, and the iOS "soft reset" hard-coded a cold relaunch at every file boundary (7–13 s/file). Android `openDeepLink` also burned a full 10 s whenever the destination screen looked like the current one — every same-screen deep link in CI showed `10.4–10.7s`.

## What
**Daemon**
- New `ResetApp` RPC (+ `AppResetMode` enum; proto additive, `buf breaking` clean). `app_reset.rs` holds the pure logic — hooks-marker wire format + parser, the cold-policy decision (retry / failed-warm streak / `cold_every_n_resets` valve, each with a human `reason`), and the `warm → restart → clear` ladder over a `ResetOps` trait — with 18 unit tests against a mock.
- `open_deep_link` → thin wrapper over `deliver_deep_link`, shared with the ladder so declared resets get the same warm/cold/reboot handling, acknowledged by the in-app marker epoch (`ackEpochGreaterThan`) rather than a hierarchy diff. `__reset` URI sniff removed.
- **Android settle fix**: judge navigation by "target app is the resumed activity" (or the epoch ack), 3 s cap, one intent re-fire at 1.5 s only if not resumed, 2 s idle wait.

**iOS agent**: `openDeepLink` honours `ackEpochGreaterThan` on warm and cold paths, returns `epochAfter`, surfaces `err=` from the marker. (Builds clean against iPhone 16 sim.)

**SDK**
- `device.resetApp({ mode, fallback, target })` → `AppResetResult` — public, documented; runner uses `_resetApp`. Recorded as a `resetApp` trace row with a `detail` line naming the rung/reason (traced actions can now carry `detail`).
- `executeAppReset` delegates warm/restart/clear to the daemon; the runner no longer forces cold at file boundaries — `appResetColdEvery` (default 10) bounds the warm window, so `resetAppDeepLink` users get genuinely warm between-file resets.

## Expected effect on e2e timing
iOS between-file gap 7–13 s → ~1–3 s (warm deep link, cold only every 10th file / on retry); Android same-screen deep links 10.5 s → < 1 s. The e2e workflows on this PR are the measurement.

## Verification
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test` (345), `buf lint` + `buf breaking`; iOS agent `xcodebuild build-for-testing`; `npm run typecheck/lint/knip/test` (2146) + `npm run build` + web-tests (202).

author: pjordanandrsn
body:
Prereg + decision calculator only — committed **before any implementation exists**. (Re-opened off `main`: the original #243 was auto-closed when its stacked base branch was deleted by #242's squash-merge; content identical.)

Registers the narrower unresolved question: *what does speculative verification cost when repeated expert selections across the window actually share their packed-weight read?* S2's 47.71 ms singleton bound disables that reuse by construction; S2's own controlled data shows **3.28–4.91 route assignments per loaded expert** in real windows.

**Mechanism (registered, not built):** fully device-side T>1 grouping — flatten (expert, row, slot) → device sort/bin → fixed `counts[E]` + prefixes → expert-major gather → each expert executes **once** over its `M_e` rows via the **existing M-tile kernel** fed device-built `(t_row0, t_rows, t_group)` at a static tile budget `ceil(R/BM)+E` with `rows=0` masking → inverse-permutation scatter preserving route-weight semantics. No `.item()`, no `unique_consecutive`, no host sync; the active-expert count never returns to Python. A new GEMM is not licensed unless the existing kernel provably cannot express the fixed-shape captured form.

**Gates before any timing:** device-vs-host grouping parity (CPU-checkable, exact, incl. zeros and `M_e > BM`); numeric parity vs the eager grouped path with identical greedy verify tokens; post-rewind continuation identity; the S2 sequential-oracle gate through the new path.

**Measurement:** same anchor + A/A; K ∈ {16,32,64} with accepted tokens from the committed table only; per-K distinct-expert counts, full `M_e` occupancy histograms, grouping/scatter overhead timed separately; and the three-way **singleton vs eager-grouped vs captured device-grouped** comparison at K=16 so the reuse-disabled artifact inside 47.71 ms is quantified.

**Adjudication fixed now** (16 self-test cases): GO ≥1.5×, INCONCLUSIVE-LIMITED 1.2–1.5×, REFUTED <1.2× — and only after a grouped receipt exists is the composed ceiling recomputed and any statement about 425 made. The negative hypothesis is registered as live: perfect grouping still touches 5.19× ordinary decode's distinct experts for 2.948 tokens at K=16 (6.73× for 3.447 at K=32).

> **Overview**
> Adds **pre-registration only** for the S3 benchmark cycle: a spec for CUDA-graph-capturable, fully device-side T>1 expert grouping (reuse existing M-tile kernel; no host sync) and the measurement/adjudication plan before any code or timing exists.
> 
> **`PREREG-s3-grouped-verify.md`** frames the question left after S2’s reuse-disabled singleton bound, lists ordered correctness gates (grouping parity, numeric parity vs eager grouped path, continuation identity, S2 oracle), defines what to record at K ∈ {16,32,64}, and fixes GO / INCONCLUSIVE / REFUTED / REFUSE rules tied to committed acceptance rates.

author: owolabenjade
body:
Fixes #171.

Security audit records require canonical serialization, append-only storage controls, cryptographic hash chaining, and offline verification capabilities. Prior to this fix, audit log entries were formatted without deterministic key ordering and did not retain parent-child hash signatures, making historical audit records vulnerable to undetected modifications or deletions.

This pull request introduces RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme - JCS) key-sorted serialization via `canonicalJsonStringify` and parent-child SHA-256 hash chaining ($\text{hash}_n = \text{SHA256}(\text{previousHash}_{n-1} + \text{canonicalJSON}(entry_n))$) anchored to a genesis state (`'0'.repeat(64)`). The delivery audit service in `src/lib/delivery/audit.js` automatically computes and persists the hash chain in MongoDB, and exposes `verifyDeliveryAuditChain()` to detect tampered, reordered, or deleted records. `scripts/verify-backup.mjs` has been updated to probe and validate audit trail integrity during database archive verification.

### Changed
- `src/lib/api/audit.js`: Implemented `canonicalJsonStringify` for RFC 8785 deterministic JSON formatting and `computeRecordHash` for SHA-256 hash chaining. (Fixes #171)
- `src/lib/delivery/audit.js`: Updated `recordDeliveryAudit` to compute parent hash links and export `verifyDeliveryAuditChain` for append-only tamper-evident verification. (Fixes #171)
- `scripts/verify-backup.mjs`: Added automated delivery audit log integrity probe during backup verification. (Fixes #171)

### Testing
- Executed backend test suite: `npm run test:backend`
- Executed unit tests for audit hash chaining & tamper detection: `node --test tests/backend/issues_fix.test.mjs`

### Scope Notes
Backend logging, telemetry, and backup verification only; no frontend UI redesigns or database schema breaking changes.

### Push Command
`git push origin feature/audit-append-only-integrity`

author: hello-vendoraph
body:
Promotes #73. **Time-critical:** `registrations:prune` fires at **03:30 Asia/Manila** (the app timezone the scheduler follows, not the box's UTC clock). This must be on the boxes before then.

## Why

The command was validated against binhs-coop production only, where it found one clean candidate. The **portfolio** box would have pruned **nine** — four of them holding **9 loans, 30% of that database's loan book**. binhs-coop has zero pending-with-loans, which is the only reason the original check looked safe.

`loans.borrower_id` is `restrictOnDelete` so those four throw, but `purge()` unlinked files **inside** its transaction and filesystems do not roll back: **3 real borrower photos** would have been destroyed with the rows restored around them, leaving dangling `photo_path`s. Plus 4 audit rows claiming a prune that never happened. All silent — root cron discards output and exit code alike.

## Changes

- Exclude borrowers with `loans`, `share_capital_ledger` movement, or a `gcash_transactions` row. **Not the pledge** — every borrower has one, so gating on it prunes nothing forever.
- Collect file paths in the transaction, unlink in `DB::afterCommit`.
- One transaction around the audit row and the purge; `Log::warning` on failure.

## Verification

Five new specs, **each confirmed to fail with its guard removed** — including the inverse case where *adding* a pledge guard fails a test, catching the silent no-op the obvious fix creates.

Full suite **564 passed** (was 559), Pint clean, `pest` green on #73 in 17m45s.

**Expected `--dry-run` after deploy:** portfolio **5** (was 9), binhs-coop **1**, other three **0**, none of `BRW-000016/17/18/23` listed. I will confirm this on the boxes rather than assume it.

author: copilot
body:
Builds the haircut scheduling app from scratch on a previously empty repo. Replaces the localStorage-only approach with Firebase Firestore for cross-device shared state, and wires up EmailJS for email delivery — all free-tier, fully static, GitHub Pages compatible.

## Core app (`index.html`)
- Single-file static app; no build step
- Month calendar: Mon/Sun closed, Tue–Fri 10+10 slots (7:30am–12pm / 1pm–5pm), Sat 30-min slots, current day highlighted blue, next-month nav
- Booking form: name, people count (default 1), phone, email — all required

## Shared persistence & double-booking prevention
- Firebase Firestore stores appointments; doc ID is `{date}_{slot}` — Firestore `create` rule rejects writes if doc already exists (atomic, server-enforced)
- Pre-write freshness check in JS as a UX guard before the Firestore write
- Calendar re-fetches live slot counts per month render

## Appointment lifecycle
- Every confirmation email includes a `?appt=<docId>` management link
- Link opens a management modal: view details, **reschedule** (mini inline calendar with live availability), or **cancel**
- Cancel/reschedule each send update emails to both client and `contact@tituspaine.com`

## Email templates (EmailJS)
Three templates wired up: `template_confirm`, `template_notify`, `template_mgmt_update` — params documented in `SETUP.md`

## Config placeholders

author: smileygames
body:
Closes #1808

brake 2（L1 根本基準評価者）を廃止し、L1 Model Layer 変更のマージゲートを brake 1 に一本化した。評価者は両ポートとも削除し、根本評価基準5項のうち L1 に無かった第3項・第4項のみ `rules/model/foundational-invariant.md` へ畳んだ。

## 版数

**patch。** `.claude/agents/` は Create-only ミラーであり、マージは既存 workspace へ伝播しない。既存インストールから agent ファイルが消えることはなく、user/system 観測可能な影響を持たない。`rules/operations/release-version-rule.md` により、構造規模が大きくても観測可能な影響を伴わない governance / spec 変更は patch に留まる。

## 判断が必要だった点

**execution-mode の L1 override をどう畳むか。** 選択肢は「削除して execution-mode 規定どおりに戻す」と「brake 2 の座を人間チェックへ差し戻す」の二つ。issue の purpose が「brake 1 + 実行モード規定に一本化」であること、および Master literal「鳥かごをもっと大きくしてよい」から前者を採った。L1 の patch は他の patch と同じく per-PR exception で waive される。AI 単独起点の L1 変更に対する律速は `skills/evolution-l1-update-gating` の観測閾値として残っており、そこは不変である。

**carve-out が寄りかかっていた「対」の扱い。** `skills/evolution-l1-update-gating/SKILL.md` は human-directed な L1 変更について「起点の human 判断 + brake 2」の対が観測閾値の役割を担う、と書いていた。書き直した結論は、その対はそもそも対ではなかった、というもの。brake 2 自身の射程 literal が証拠の充足度を軸から除外していたため（wiki `brake2-scoped-to-content-not-evidence`）、観測閾値の役割を担い得なかった。carve-out を解除するのは human 自身の directing 単独であり、下流のゲートは荷重を持たない旨を明文化した。

**節名 Two-stage brake の改称。** 一段しか残らないため `Merge brake` へ改めた。全参照側（rules / skills / adapter / docs）を同じ編集で直している。一方 **brake 1 の序数は残した** — 改名は issue の target files を超え、wiki entry 名（`brake1-*` 4件）にも及ぶ。`rules/evolution/initiator-autonomy.md` Merge brake に「これは序数ではなく名である」旨の1文を置いて、読者が brake 2 を探しに行かないようにした。改名の可否は別軸。

**既存 workspace に残る agent ファイル（issue 制約の明示要求）。** 残置が既定。`Li+update.md` 4c.6 / 4x.5 の stale 非削除は「ソース側が削除された target」も覆うことを明文化し、削除はユーザーの手に残ること、および残置されたファイルが不活性である理由（agent ファイルは名指しの spawn でしか到達されず、rules / skills / adapter のどこもそれを名指さなくなった時点で到達路が無い）を書いた。

## 契約テスト

削除ではなく更新した。`tests/test_agent_sentinel_contract.py` は sentinel 区画機構そのものの契約であり、実カリアが無くなっても機構は `Li+update.md` に残る。実カリア集合が空になると per-source の形状アサーションは vacuous になるため、branch (b) の置換意味論だけは synthetic fixture（md / toml 各1）で実行し続ける形にした。空になり得ることは docstring に明示している。

## target files 外に触れた1点

`skills/task-subagent-delegation/SKILL.md` — `Two-stage brake` を名指す参照1行の修復のみ。節名変更に伴う dangling 参照であり、参照側を同じ編集で直すのは wiki `rules-hold-criteria-not-provenance` の規律。issue の target files 列挙には無いため明示する。

## wiki

新規 entry `brake2-removal-l1-gate-unified-on-brake1` を立て、`l1-brake2-root-criteria-evaluator` / `brake2-scoped-to-content-not-evidence` / `brake2-deviation-overridden-by-human` の3件に supersede edge を張った（削除せず）。`docs/Decision-Structure.md` の index にも追加済み。

## 検証

`python -m unittest discover -s tests` = 79 tests, OK。

author: benlinton
body:
## The rule, stated once

> **ALL CAPS names a file that speaks for the thing containing it. Lowercase names one of the things contained.**

`BUNDLE.md` speaks for its Bundle; `LOG.md` for its directory's history. A Type Definition at `_types/bundle.md` does not — it describes what a Bundle *is*, living inside one thing while being about another. A template at `templates/bundle.md` is a pattern for making one. Both are content and both stay lowercase. **The rule excludes them rather than exempting them**, which is why it needs no list of exceptions.

## What the casing is for

**A gate on participation, not decoration.** Nobody types all caps by accident, so a file joins the format's machinery only when somebody deliberately made it so — and getting it wrong fails in the safe direction: a `bundle.md` is an ordinary Document, ignored rather than silently treated as a manifest. Somebody who writes lowercase either isn't using these tools or doesn't want that file wired up, and both are cases where wiring it up anyway would be wrong.

**It is the inverse of why `README.md` can carry no rules.** People edit a README without knowing any exist — universal permission semantics no specification overturns. So this makes explicit what was previously only implied: **a consumer MUST NOT depend on the content or structure of `README.md`.**

Directories stay outside the rule. `_types/` already says *structural rather than content* with its underscore, and a second signal for one meaning is worse than one.

## `index.md` is withdrawn

Not renamed — **released**. Its structure was never specified, nothing implemented it, and the name is one static site generators resolve in lowercase, so keeping it would have been this rule's only exception. A future reservation for derived navigation should take a name of its own.

## Also

An idea recorded, not acted on: whether `_types/` should be named for the thing that reserves it. The underscore says *structural* but not *whose* — worth deciding alongside a second reserved directory rather than before one exists.

author: oleksii-debug
body:
## Mission

Run the longest scientifically useful LOCAL_FREE approximately 100K Base experiment currently justified by live repository identities, without retuning architecture/tokenizer/data/optimizer simultaneously.

## Exact incumbent

Ancestry-preserving composition now includes the current RESEARCH06 PR #183 exact head `832130e36e251f776287b9832be3e5879859b285`. Current TRAIN-41 exact head is `9129421d2a3f71d8792b5003bc4891141907ee22`; compare against the RESEARCH06 head is exactly four additive TRAIN-41 files and zero behind.

The run preserves RESEARCH06's first controlled candidate exactly: 95,568 parameters, vocab 256, context 256, d_model 48, 3 blocks, 4Q/4KV heads, head_dim 12, SwiGLU d_ff 128, tied embeddings, InitSpec v1, strict aligned causal-pair accounting, canonical byte tokenizer, project S0 train/validation split, FP32 AdamW lr=3e-4 betas=0.9/0.95 weight_decay=0, constant LR, clip=1.0, seed 1337, batch4 x seq64.

TRAIN-33 optimizer experiments are not treated as authority because their current exact-head matrix did not execute past D08 verification. The promising repeatable BPE-472 artifact is also not substituted because the live DATA-10 contract keeps it not frozen on representative data and changing vocabulary would alter the ~100K geometry.

## Long-run contract

Maximum budget: 2,097,152 exact optimized causal targets (~21.95 target tokens/parameter).

Held-out evaluations are dense early and progressively spaced later: 1K/2K/4K/8K/16K/32K/65K/131K/262K/524K/1.048M/1.573M/2.097M plus random-init baseline.

Telemetry records train/validation BPB, LR, pre-clip global gradient norm, clip rate, sampled relative L2 update ratio, per-step throughput, cumulative training/end-to-end throughput, evaluation time, checkpoint save/load overhead, optimizer/model bytes and peak RSS. Step telemetry is every update through step 64, every 8 through 512, every 32 through 2048, then every 128 plus evaluation boundaries.

Greedy generation snapshots use fixed raw-Base prefixes `The `, `Україна ` and `def ` at 0/16K/65K/262K/1.048M/1.573M/2.097M targets.

## Retained checkpoints and real resume

Full D05 checkpoints are retained at 65K, 262K, 1.048M, 1.573M and 2.097M targets when reached.

The first process must stop exactly at 1,048,576 targets. A separate Python process verifies/restores that checkpoint, requires held-out validation drift <=1e-12 and exact greedy generation-token parity at the resume point, then continues. The Actions artifact retains complete checkpoint directories, not only manifests.

## Early stop

Clean early stop is allowed only for explicit fail-closed criteria:
- pre-clip grad norm >100 for eight consecutive committed updates;
- validation loss > random-init validation by >2.0 nats;
- at/after 1,572,864 targets, <1e-4 nats best validation improvement across the latest four scheduled evaluations.

Non-finite training remains an error, not a successful stop.

## Current data truth boundary

The S0 train fixture is only 1,920 UTF-8 bytes and validation 406 bytes. DATA-10 mechanics corpus is 1,454 bytes; approved external training sources are zero. Therefore this run can provide strong optimization/memorization/held-out-fixture/resume/systems evidence, but not representative Ukrainian/English/code language-model quality evidence.

No canonical config is modified, no tokenizer/corpus is frozen, no paid compute is used, and no capability/promotion claim is introduced.

Exact-head `TRAIN-41 Long 100K Base` workflow is the execution authority.

author: christianspliid-ui
body:
Stage 1 of the six-stage effect-vocabulary activation program. Plan doc: [`Docs/plans/2026-08-25-effect-vocabulary-activation.md`](https://github.com/christianspliid-ui/threadbare/blob/main/Docs/plans/2026-08-25-effect-vocabulary-activation.md) (merged in #1614).

## The executors were never broken

`getReactiveTrigger` has mapped `entered_hex` and the combat pair to reactive triggers since the primitive architecture landed, and `processEffectEvent` has always known how to dispatch them. What never existed was a **producer** — outside a single `encounter_outcome` raise inside the orchestrator, **no site in the engine ever constructed an `EffectEvent`**. So the whole executor family (teleport, spawn, compel, cascade, …) was unreachable in normal play while every part of it read as fully wired.

That shape is why the ledger found 53 union members and ~21 executing: the dead half was not dead code, it was live code nobody was calling.

## What changed

- **`raiseEffectEvent`** (new, `src/engine/effects/effectEventDispatch.ts`) names the raise sequence once — process → apply → instantiate transforms → execute reactives → emit. The orchestrator's inline copy was **migrated onto it** rather than left as a second copy, so hand-rolled dispatch blocks went 1 → 0 while producers went 1 → 4.
- **`entered_hex`** at movement arrival — **final arrival only**, not per hex step and not on same-hex sublocation moves (per-step firing is ≈4× the event volume for no design gain).
- **`combat_started` / `combat_ended`** at battle create/resolve. Audience is **participants only**, which resolves to the two commanders: an army is an `actor` node carrying a headcount, not a roster of agent nodes. `combat_ended` fires **before** `applyAftermath` — a `killed` commander is removed from the graph there, and the raise fail-softs on a missing agent, so raising after would silently drop the loser's `leave_combat` expiries.
- **The `never` guard.** `executeEffect`'s `default` arm was answering `success: false` / "Unknown effect type" for **13 union members** — the whole query/tick-layer family — every one of them working exactly as designed elsewhere. They joined the modifier fallthrough, and `default` became `const _exhaustive: never = effect`.
- **Consumable charges deplete.** `chargesRemaining` had a reader, an initialiser and a destroy-at-0 branch and **no decrement anywhere**, so every "3 charges" item in the reward catalogs was in fact unlimited. One charge per completed encounter step whose reach matches `onUse.reach` — step granularity, not action.
- **`resource_manipulate` one_shot fires.** `effectTick` documented it as "handled by the event handler", and that handler had no case for it; the mode was dead in both places. It is now spent even when it cannot land, so a solo-encounter `other_agent` shot does not retry forever.
- **Two dotted trace categories** registered at all four sites. A raise traces **even at `reactivesFired: 0`** — "live and nothing listening" vs "never wired" being indistinguishable is precisely how this sat unnoticed.

## Verification

```
npm test
  Test Files  1072 passed (1072)
       Tests  17720 passed (17720)

npm run check:typecheck
  check-typecheck-ratchet: OK — 3012 error(s), unchanged from baseline.
  (baseline refreshed 3014 → 3012 and committed; re-run LAST per THR-976)

npx vite build
  ✓ 3623 modules transformed.
  ✓ built in 10.27s

printf "tick 30\nstatus\nexit\n" | npm run cli -- --seed 42 --map medium
  ✓ Tick 30  |  42 events  |  phase: playing
    Agents: 384 · Locations: 738 · Doom stage: 1
    Outcomes (N=14): clean 29.4% | at-cost 35.7% | fail 21.4% | crit-succ 11.8%

check-generated-freshness: OK — 34 generated artifact(s) match HEAD.
check-wiki-freshness: OK (exempt)
check:impediment-ids: OK — 761 table rows, every # unique.
```

**Live raise, not just unit-tested.** Same seeded run with `traces 5000`: **10 × `[effect.event_raised] entered_hex raised at movement_arrival`** by tick 30. The `site` string only exists at the `phaseMovement` call site, so the trace cannot appear unless that wiring is live.

**The charge-spend call site is proven by falsification.** With the call site disabled, **5 of the 6** tests in `consumableChargeSpend.integration.test.ts` go red (the 6th is the negative case, which correctly still passes). That test exists because the CLI cannot settle it either way: only **1 of 13** charged artifacts in a seed-42 medium world has a bearer at all, so a natural matching-reach step inside 60 ticks is a long shot, not a guarantee.

## One gate caught this and was right to

The THR-1065 emitTrace cast ratchet went 107 → 109 on two new casts in the new module. Fixed the way the ratchet asks rather than by raising the ceiling: legacy-shaped payloads funnel through a single cast site, and migrating the orchestrator removed two more — **final count 106**, below where it started. Its "New sites" message misattributed the cause to two untouched files; logged as impediment **#760**.

Impediment **#762** also logged: a Python write that throws while encoding truncates the target to zero bytes first, which emptied a 217-line canon page mid-session (restored from HEAD, redone with Edit).

`Browser-verify exempt: engine-only change, no UI-pillar files touched.`

Fixes THR-1239

body:
## Le bug (signalé par F4GLD)

Le panneau **« départements À FAIRE »** (#270) était **structurellement incomplet** dès qu'un **chasseur inédit** (jamais loggué) apparaissait sur un département manquant — un bug qui ne se voit qu'**en live** et sape la confiance dans la feature.

**Cause** : `department_targets()` **jetait le locator porté par le spot** (le cluster le donne souvent) et ne résolvait le département d'un indicatif inconnu que par un **lookup callbook réseau** (plafonné, cache d'échec) — qui échoue hors ligne / en zone blanche / en plein contest THF (le pire moment pour dépendre du réseau).

## Le fix

On **conserve le locator du spot** et on résout le département du plus fiable au moins fiable :
1. **historique** (log / calldb / archives) ;
2. **le LOCATOR DU SPOT → `dept_from_locator`, EN LOCAL, sans réseau** ← corrige la cécité (ta remarque : « on retrouve le département avec le locator de la station ») ;
3. **lookup réseau** en repli, uniquement pour les spots **sans** locator.

Réservé aux indicatifs **français** (cohérent avec `dept_for_qso` : le département REF est un découpage français). **Zéro requête réseau** quand le spot porte déjà un locator.

## Tests

`test_dept_targets_spot_locator.py` : station jamais logguée résolue par le locator du spot **sans réseau** ; pas de cible fantôme sans locator ni réseau ; indicatif non-français non rattaché. TDD + contre-épreuve par mutation. **Non-régression départements verte (53).**

author: 1102huynh
body:
New module: /v1/promotions and /v1/promotion-thresholds, per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md 3.5.

Business-risk decision (matches the 3.3 precedent - asked rather than guessed): TT22/58 promotion criteria are officially expressed via xep loai hoc luc, which isn't computed yet (deferred in 3.3), and the exact diem/hanh kiem/nghi hoc cutoffs are a regulation/policy detail. Asked the user how to handle the preview's auto-suggestion; chosen approach: ADMIN/PRINCIPAL-configurable thresholds (PromotionThresholdConfig, no defaults seeded - same pattern as GradeComponentConfig in 3.3), applied to data that already exists reliably.

Key design choice beyond what was asked: the threshold compares against the LOWEST of a student's per-subject diem TB nam, not an invented overall/blended average across subjects - TT22/58 define criteria per-subject-plus-conditions, not one blended number, so a cross-subject average would itself have been an uncredentialed formula invention. This floor-based comparison is grounded in the actual regulation shape without needing classification. Documented as an approximation, not the official calculation, in Javadoc/Swagger/README.

Entities: PromotionThresholdConfig (minSubjectAverage, minConduct, maxAbsenceRate, scoped by appliesFrom), PromotionRecord (one per student per academic year, snapshots lowestSubjectAverage/conduct/ attendanceRate frozen at confirm time so later corrections don't silently change a decision already made, decision enum LEN_LOP/O_LAI/ TOT_NGHIEP/RA_TRUONG).

Endpoints:
- GET /v1/promotions/class/{classId}/preview?academicYearId=... (ADMIN/ PRINCIPAL/TEACHER) - live, unsaved suggestion per student in the class: suggests TOT_NGHIEP for graduating grades (9, 12) that meet thresholds, LEN_LOP otherwise, O_LAI if not met, null if no threshold config applies yet. RA_TRUONG is never auto-suggested - always a human choice.
- POST /v1/promotions/confirm (ADMIN/PRINCIPAL only) - persists the final decision, "ghi de hang loat": confirming again for the same (student, academicYear) updates the existing record rather than erroring.
- GET /v1/promotions/student/{id} (+STUDENT, self-only) - decision history, same object-level ownership pattern as 3.3/3.4.
- POST/PUT/GET/DELETE /v1/promotion-thresholds (ADMIN/PRINCIPAL only).

Migration V7__promotion_records.sql: no default threshold rows seeded (ADMIN/PRINCIPAL must configure before any suggestion is computed) and no backfill (nothing pre-3.5 represented this data).

Self-reviewed with the code-review skill before committing (same practice as 3.3/3.4) and fixed what it found:
- previewClassPromotions never verified the requested classId actually belongs to the requested academicYearId - the same className/section can exist across multiple years (SchoolClass's own unique constraint spans all three), so a mismatched pair would silently mix one year's roster with another year's grading/attendance window. Now checks academicYear.name against the class's own academicYear field first and rejects a mismatch with 400. Live-verified: created a second, unrelated academic year and confirmed the mismatched classId/academicYearId combo is rejected before touching any data.
- Documented (not changed) two lower-severity findings: decidedBy is accepted as given rather than pinned to the caller's own staff profile (unlike ConductRecordService's evaluatedBy check) - deliberate, since /confirm is already ADMIN/PRINCIPAL-only and a xet len lop decision is recorded "on behalf of" a Hoi dong, not as one teacher's individual act; and previewClassPromotions does one lookup per roster student (no batching) - fine at class scale, would need work for a whole-school report.
- Extracted the "leading year" parsing (the exact logic that had a real bug fixed in the 3.3 review) into a new shared util.AcademicYearMatcher and switched GradeRecordService's resolveWeight to use it too, instead of introducing a third private copy for PromotionService.

Live-verified against local MySQL/Tomcat (port 8081) with real JWTs and seeded dev accounts: preview with no threshold config shows no suggestion with an explanatory reason; classId/academicYearId mismatch -> 400; created a threshold config (duplicate -> 409, malformed appliesFrom -> 400); gave a student qualifying grades (9.0 MIENG both semesters), HK2 conduct TOT, and attendance (4 present/1 absent = 80%, exactly at the 20% max-absence threshold) -> preview correctly returned meetsThresholds=true, suggestedDecision=LEN_LOP; confirmed it, then re-confirmed with a different decision and verified the SAME record id was updated in place (not duplicated); TEACHER can preview (200) but not confirm or configure thresholds (403 both); STUDENT can read their own promotion history (200) but not another student's (403). Cleaned up all test-created rows afterward.

New PromotionIntegrationTest (12 tests, real Spring context + local MySQL, @Transactional rollback) covering the same scenarios, including the graduating-grade-level (9) TOT_NGHIEP suggestion branch and the ghi-de-hang-loat (overwrite, not duplicate) confirm semantics.

Full suite: 80/80 passing (68 pre-existing + 12 new) against local MySQL.

README: added Promotion Thresholds/Promotions module rows, V7 migration entry, object-level authorization note extended to /v1/promotions/student/{id}, Future enhancements updated (3.5 marked done) with a note on the lowest-subject-average approximation and the preview's per-student lookup cost.

author: zer0ken
body:
The release workflow has been failing validation ('workflow file issue') on every push since #105, because `if: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN != '' }}` uses the `secrets` context inside an `if` condition.

Per the [official context-availability table](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/learn-github-actions/contexts#context-availability), `secrets` is **not** available in `jobs.*.if` or `jobs.*.steps.if` (only in env/run/etc). Verified empirically: GitHub rejects both step- and job-level secrets-in-`if` with 'workflow file issue'.

Fix: inject the token via `env:` (where secrets is allowed) and gate `cargo publish` on the injected env var in the shell.

Verified with actionlint: release.yml is now clean.

author: brunolabbe
body:
Folds the fifth orchestration session's lessons into the skill, following the
pattern of `ea52f8b` (#95). One file, four entries, **+59 lines** — against the
previous fold-in's +438, deliberately, since two of the entries are about the
cost of verbosity.

Two are about correctness, two about cost — the latter because the session's own
output was **266 non-documentation lines against 1,113 of documentation**, and
its wall clock went to verification rather than to writing.

- **Point every verification run at the narrowest thing that can fail.** The page
  has told gates to reproduce and to run controls for five sessions and never said
  what to run them *against*. Measured here, warm: one spec **2 s**, its directory
  **41 s**, the tool's project **~50 s**, rebuild **12 s** — a five-mutation sweep
  is 1.2 minutes or 4.4 for identical evidence.
- **Restore from a `trap`, not the next line** — the next line does not run when
  you are killed. Written from the orchestrator doing exactly this to itself and
  stranding a mutated tree with a security-relevant lookahead deleted.
- **A snapshot of a live worktree is a moment, not a state.** Both handover
  captures were wrong within minutes. Capture pointers, re-read the tree, and push
  what exists nowhere else.
- **Long form on the pull request, short form in the ticket** — and the bloat is in
  the Log (753 lines) rather than the gate record (303, of which 294 lines were
  posted a second time).

**Gate 1: CONCERNS**, five findings, all applied. The one worth naming: I wrote
*"whole output was 104 lines of source"* in the entry about cost discipline, which
excluded 162 lines of tests. Tests are output. The real ratio is **4.2:1, not
10.7:1** — precise and false, on the sentence the preamble calls the session's real
lesson, which is the exact defect class this page devotes a section to. The gate
also falsified a timing figure (`>60 s` → ~50 s, re-measured twice), caught that
the new `trap` bullet had been inserted between two `dist` bullets joined by *"the
same trap running backwards"* and broken that antecedent, and found five loose-list
blank lines.

Three contradiction checks came back **clean** and are worth recording: the new
targeting rule does not fight *"enumerate, never sample"* (that rule governs what
you mutate, this one which suite runs per mutation); the `trap` bullet is
complementary to the `dist`-staleness pair rather than redundant; and
*"capture pointers, not content"* names the reviewer-report rule as its explicit
exception.

`.claude/` is in `.oxfmtrc.json`'s `ignorePatterns`, so `npm run check` cannot see
a broken table or an unclosed code span here — the page says this about itself, and
I broke a `**` span once while editing it. Structure was verified with a
per-paragraph checker run against `origin/main` as a control (0 and 0); a per-line
check is useless here, since bold spanning two lines is this page's dominant style.

No ticket, matching #95. There is no ticket for the gate record to live in, so the
full report is posted below — which is what the new Records guidance prescribes.

author: fredabood
body:
## What

`.claude/hooks/pre-commit-tests.sh` consumes the same `discover-test-suites.sh` output as
`tests.yml`. Discovery grew a `rust` kind (homelab#1548) and CI grew an arm for it; this
dispatch did not — it was `bash` arm, `node` arm, everything else → pytest. A rust suite
therefore fell into the pytest arm, `pytest --collect-only` exited 5 because pytest does
not collect `.rs` files, and the gate printed:

> `could not be COLLECTED here (usually missing deps) — SKIPPED, not passed.`

The LAB-1455 defect, one kind over: a suite silently skipped by the gate that exists to
enforce it, under a reason that was not the reason.

## The dispatch change

```sh
  elif [ "$kind" = rust ]; then
    if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "[pre-commit-tests] cargo not available for $dir — SKIPPED (not a pass)." >&2
      ...
      continue
    fi
    if [ ! -f "$dir/Cargo.toml" ]; then ... status=1; continue; fi
    if ! out="$( cd "$dir" && cargo test 2>&1 )"; then ... status=1; fi
```

**Absent toolchain vs failing tests.** `cargo test` exits non-zero for a compile error and
for a failed assertion alike, and a shell running a binary that is not installed also exits
non-zero. Reading "cargo is missing" out of an exit code would make an un-toolchained
machine look like a repo full of broken tests; tolerating that exit code to fix it would
make broken tests look like a missing toolchain. So the toolchain question is settled by
`command -v` **before** cargo is invoked and never revisited after — the same split as the
pytest arm's `--collect-only` probe and the node arm's `node_modules` check. Missing cargo
skips loudly and allows; a failing `cargo test` blocks.

Two smaller things, both mirroring `tests.yml`: a rust `dir` with no `Cargo.toml` means
discovery and the runner disagree (loud, not skipped — the bash arm's stance on a missing
`tests/*.test.sh`), and `ignore` is pytest's `--ignore` with no cargo equivalent, so it is
warned about rather than dropped on the floor.

## Tests

`pre-commit-tests.sh` had **no** suite, which is how it acquired this defect twice. It has
one now — `hooks/tests/pre-commit-tests.test.sh`, **24 assertions**, harness modelled on
`docker-safety-check.test.sh` (synthetic PreToolUse payload on stdin, exit-code and stderr
assertions) over a `worktree-gate.test.sh`-style sandbox repo, because this hook reads a
real git index and a real discovery script.

Two things the fixture controls deliberately:

1. **Discovery is a stub** emitting the `suites.json` each case writes. The unit under test
   is the dispatch; discovery lives in the parent repo and is tested there.
2. **PATH is rebuilt from an explicit tool list**, so `cargo` is absent by construction
   rather than by luck. It is absent on this laptop and present on `ubuntu-latest`, which
   runs this suite in CI — a missing-toolchain test that only tests anything on one of the
   two machines is LAB-1425 (21 assertions vacuous on Linux) with the platforms swapped.
   The fixture asserts its own preconditions and hard-fails if cargo is still reachable.

Every one of the 24 assertions was observed **red** against a reintroduced defect before
being kept: rust arm removed (12 red), cargo-check inverted (14), failing `cargo test`
swallowed (4), `Cargo.toml` check removed (3) and inverted (11), the `cd $dir` dropped (1),
the `ignore` warning removed (1), the bash arm removed (2, the regression control), the
git-commit guard removed (2), and the fixture's green bash suite made red (2).

Verification: 24/24 green; all 11 `*.test.sh` suites in this repo exit 0 (`docker-safety-check`
still 48/48); `bash -n` and `shellcheck` clean on both files.

Scope: this repo only. The `rust` kind in `internal/scripts/discover-test-suites.sh`,
`tests.yml`, and the submodule gitlink bump are handled in homelab#1548 / separately.

Refs fredabood/homelab#1437

author: genesispray
body:
this pr closes #669 
this pr closes #670 
this pr closes #671 
this pr closes #672 

Four issue reports, all traced to real bugs:

- Mobile overlap on the credentials page (<375px): the credential list row packed a full 64-char hex ID plus type/status badges, expiry text, and two buttons into one non-wrapping flex row. On a 320-375px screen the unbreakable ID text pushed everything else off-screen, overlapping and hiding interactive elements. Wrapped the row, truncated the displayed ID (full value kept in `title`), and added a `@media (max-width: 375px)` block tightening badge/button sizing.

- Expired credentials showing a green "Valid" badge: the actual bug was in the SDK, not the UI. CredentialClient.verifyCredential()'s simulation-error branch only recognized "not found" contract errors and silently defaulted revoked/expired credentials to reason: 'unknown', so the UI never got a chance to distinguish them. Now decodes the on-chain error code via ContractError.extract and maps CredentialExpired/CredentialRevoked/CredentialNotFound correctly. Also gave the credentials list a dedicated yellow "Expired" badge instead of reusing gray.

- resolveDid returning 404 immediately after createDid: the retry loop only retried on transient network errors (429/503/timeout/etc.) and explicitly excluded "not found," so a DID that hadn't yet propagated to the RPC node serving the read failed immediately instead of self-correcting. resolveDid now also retries the DID-not-found contract error, bounded by the existing retry budget (default bumped to 5 attempts / ~500ms-8s backoff) so it self-heals within the propagation window instead of surfacing a false negative.

- CredentialClient memory growth under repeated calls: CredentialsPanel was constructing a brand-new CredentialClient (each with its own RequestQueue and an unawaited health-check request) on every verify/search/issuer-check call and never disposing it. Switched to a single client instance reused for the component's lifetime and disposed on unmount.

Also cleaned up merge-conflict leftovers in the SDK that were blocking verification of the above and would have broken any real build: sdk/src/errors.ts and sdk/src/index.ts had duplicate parseContractError declarations/re-exports, and sdk/src/credentials.ts had duplicate CredentialInput/BatchOptions/BatchResult interfaces plus references to undefined identifiers (CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOUND_CODE, CREDENTIAL_REVOKED_CODE, AjvCtor). Removed the duplicate local Credential type in CredentialsPanel.tsx that shadowed the SDK's type and caused a separate compile error. Fixed a missing Account mock in credentials.test.ts that was masking 20 test failures unrelated to this change, and updated identity.test.ts's resolveDid retry tests to reflect the corrected not-found-retry behavior.

author: copilot
body:
There was no way to tell how long a Postgres, MongoDB or Redis round trip took, or which operation dominated database time. This adds wall-clock timing to every datastore round trip, aggregates it per operation (split read vs write) on `GET /metrics`, logs slow queries to the server console, and pulls the same table into the Android **Export Logs** file.

### Timing primitive — `server/src/lib/queryTiming.ts`
- `timeQuery({ backend, operation, kind, target }, run)` measures with `performance.now()`, reports to a settable sink, and re-throws untouched so no call site changes behaviour.
- The sink is process-global (the instrumented modules are built without a `state` handle) and `setQueryTimingSink` returns a disposer that only uninstalls its own sink, so tearing one server down cannot blind others.
- Slow (≥ threshold) and failed queries log a warning; everything else goes through the existing redacting `verboseLog`. Only query *shape* is ever recorded — never statement parameters, filter documents or message bodies.

### Instrumentation seams
- **Postgres** (`server/db/client.ts`): wraps `pool.query` and each checked-out client's `query`, so every Drizzle-generated statement — including ones added later and those inside transactions — is measured without touching a query. Operation/table/read-write are parsed from the statement text.
- **Mongo** (`server/src/messageStore.ts`): wraps the eight store methods so labels stay business-meaningful (`listConversations` vs a point lookup). `connect()` is awaited *before* the timer starts, keeping one-time index creation out of the first query's latency.
- **Redis** (`server/src/cache.ts`): `get`/`set`, plus one timing for the whole `delByPrefix` scan-and-delete sweep. The memory backend is deliberately untimed.

### Aggregation and surfacing
- `telemetry.ts` gains `db_*` counters, `{pg,mongo,redis}_query_duration_ms` histograms on finer buckets (1–5000 ms; the call buckets start at 100 ms), and a bounded `dbQueries` table keyed `backend:kind:operation`, sorted by total time so the costliest operation is row one.
- `mobile/src/diagnostics.ts` fetches that snapshot (2.5 s timeout, never rejects) and appends it to the exported log file.

Console output and `/metrics` shape:

```
[db-timing] SLOW backend=mongo op=listConversations kind=read target=messages durationMs=482.1
```

```json
"dbQueries": [
  { "backend": "mongo", "operation": "listConversations", "kind": "read",
    "count": 42, "slow": 3, "totalMs": 5120, "meanMs": 121.9, "maxMs": 480.2 },
  { "backend": "pg", "operation": "insert", "kind": "write",
    "count": 190, "slow": 0, "totalMs": 812, "meanMs": 4.27, "maxMs": 31.5 }
]
```

### Configuration
`DB_QUERY_TIMING` (default on), `DB_SLOW_QUERY_MS` / `MONGO_SLOW_QUERY_MS` / `REDIS_SLOW_QUERY_MS` (default 100 ms each), documented in `SETUP.md`. Env vars are read per query so thresholds can be tuned without a restart.

### Notes for reviewers
- Request-to-query correlation via `AsyncLocalStorage` is deliberately deferred; the current labels answer read/write cost and worst-operation without it.
- `reviews/log-sql-mongo-db-query-times-review.md` contains a self-review of this diff and the resolution of each finding.

## Summary by Sourcery

Instrument SQL, MongoDB, and Redis operations and surface their latency and per-operation cost through server metrics, console logs, and Android diagnostic exports.

New Features:
- Add end-to-end wall-clock timing for Postgres, MongoDB, and Redis datastore operations, including read/write classification and slow or failed query logging.
- Expose bounded per-operation datastore timing summaries and backend-specific latency histograms through GET /metrics.
- Include the server query-timing snapshot in Android diagnostic log exports with graceful handling of unavailable metrics.

Enhancements:
- Support live configuration of query timing and backend-specific slow-query thresholds while redacting query details to preserve sensitive data.
- Aggregate query counts, errors, slow operations, total, mean, and maximum durations with costliest operations listed first.

Documentation:
- Document query timing metrics, console logging, Android log export behavior, and related environment variables in SETUP.md.

Tests:
- Add server coverage for timing behavior, thresholds, failures, SQL classification, telemetry aggregation, overflow handling, Mongo instrumentation, and Postgres instrumentation.
- Add mobile coverage for formatting, fetching, failure handling, and writing query timings to exported logs.
