author: adamforrester
body:
Closes #1010.

`field-message` built an **FPO placeholder** where its status icon belongs: one `kind: 'slot'` part nominating an `INSTANCE_SWAP` target, wrong size, no per-status glyph. The 39-glyph set landed in **#920** and this def bound none of it.

Three `presentWhen`-gated `vector` parts replace the slot, each at `icon.size.xs` inking its semantic role:

| tone | glyph | enclosure | ink |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | *(none)* | — | `color.text.secondary` |
| `error` | `warning-triangle` | exclamation in a **triangle** | `color.icon.danger` |
| `warning` | `error-circle` | exclamation in a **circle** | `color.icon.warning` |
| `success` | `check-circle` | circled check | `color.icon.success` |

## Why nothing caught it, which is the half worth reading

**A placeholder is a structurally valid child.** Every value resolved — the slot resolved, the size resolved, the paint resolved. There was no wrong value anywhere; there was a *right* value pointing at scaffolding whose reason had expired. Nothing in the repo relates "this def declares a placeholder" to "the thing it stands in for now exists", and no gate can, because a dependency landing elsewhere is not a change to this file. The def's own `codeOnly` entry said it "cannot bind WHICH glyph each tone shows" — true when written, false by the time it was read.

## The default tone projects no glyph

Read off the Prism2 reference's `standard` row (*no icon, gray text*), not its `info` row (*a circled information mark, blue*). This tone paints `text.secondary`/`icon.secondary`, so it is gray — matching it to `info` would be matching by **position in a list** rather than by what it paints. It also agrees with the def's pre-existing prose, which already documented `props.icon` as optional on the default tone while every Figma member shipped a glyph.

`default.icon` is **kept**, because the code path still needs it (`props.icon` may supply a domain-specific mark), and named in `lint-paint.ts`'s `UNREACHED_EXPLAINED`. That register now holds **two categories**: five `<def>|focus-ring` nominations (no stroke field, #740) and this one. Membership no longer implies the category, so the entry states *why this one* is unreachable — the paint is code-only because the projector enumerates members while the node is optional per instance.

## `FigmaProperties.footprintVaries` — the reusable half

The footprint cohort reported **three misses on a correct build** (`tone=error measures 126x24 but tone=default measures 102x0`). Its key is `size=` + `leading=` + `trailing=` — the axes that legitimately change *Button's* box, authored for Button and never revisited for `presentWhen` (#910). `checkbox` and `radio` gate a mark **inside** a size-bound `control`, so their box holds still and they never met this; `field-message` is the first def where a gated part is a flow child of the row.

**Declared, not derived from `presentWhen`.** Deriving it would exempt `checkbox` along `selection` and silently delete a cross-variant comparison that is doing real work. Validated as (a) an axis this def projects and (b) an axis some part's `presentWhen` gates, so neither half can be satisfied by accident. What the exemption costs is stated at the declaration rather than assumed: `tone` is this def's only axis, so each member becomes its own cohort and the footprint rule checks nothing here — two named arms measure the box directly instead.

## Verified at the NODE, not the plan

The issue was explicit that a plan-level check sees nothing wrong, *"which is how it shipped"*. `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` runs the real component set through the shim and reads back: member names, per-tone artboard counts `0,1,1,1`, one non-zero `VECTOR` per icon tone, **three distinct subpath sets**, both size axes bound to `icon/size/xs`, ink per tone, zero `INSTANCE` nodes, no surviving `INSTANCE_SWAP` property.

**The first fingerprint was the ink BOX, and it was wrong in both directions at once.** It failed on correct code (`20.3x19.5, 20.0x20.0, 20.0x20.0`) and could not have caught two tones sharing one glyph — `error-circle` and `check-circle` are the same 20px ring, so their bounding boxes are identical, live as well as in the shim. Replaced by modelling `vectorPaths` in the harness shim and comparing subpath **data** pairwise.

## The mapping reads transposed and is not

`warning-triangle` is an exclamation in a **triangle** (triangle + bar y9–14 + dot y16–18); `error-circle` is the same exclamation in a **circle** (ring 2→22 + bar y7–13 + dot y15–17). A glyph name describes the **enclosure**, not the tone. Confirmed by measuring the artwork, because reading the names gives the wrong answer.

`lint-glyph-geometry.ts`'s `FIXED_GLYPH` is where that belongs — a **second author** of the pairing, in a different file. So the single most likely future edit to this def, somebody "correcting" the mapping to agree with the names, now fails as a stale record. Without it that edit draws correct ink on a correct artboard at a valid coordinate and **passes every geometric arm in that file** — the same reason `checkbox.dash` is in the table.

## The sweep the issue asked for

- **String.** Zero `FPO` in `packages/engine/out/` and `packages/engine/schema/`. All twelve remaining source hits are the caller-supplied `swapTarget: 'FPO-default-icon'` argument or a comment about it. **Those are correct and stay** — a slot means the consumer supplies the content, so `button.leadingVisual` genuinely does not know what goes there and a named placeholder to swap against is right.
- **Structural, and this is the one that would have found it.** Four `kind: 'slot'` parts existed repo-wide (`button` ×2, `icon-button`, `field-message`); three remain. `field-message`'s was the only one whose slot content was **determined by the def's own axis** — the only one where the def knew exactly what belonged there and declined to draw it. One grep plus one question.

## Mutations — all fire by name

| | mutation | fails as |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | drop `footprintVaries` | plugin misses arm + both new engine arms |
| M2 | payload ignores the shipped list | **only** the new parity arm — the pre-existing focus-ring parity arm stayed **green**, which is the `docs/34` proof it was blind to the new segment rather than redundant with it |
| M3 | delete the shipped const | 22 failures, incl. `payload THREW -> FOOTPRINT_VARIES is not defined` |
| M4 | `footprintVaries: ['bogus']` | `is not an axis this def projects [tone]` |
| M5 | `['intent']` on button | `gates no part (presentWhen)` |
| M6 | two tones share a glyph | `4,4,4 subpaths, 2 distinct` |
| M7 | `icon.size.sm` | both halves — engine `20` in all five brands, plugin `icon/size/sm` |
| M8 | ungate `iconError` | `explained as unreachable but IS now reached` |
| M9 | transpose the glyph in the def | `FIXED_GLYPH records 'warning-triangle'… Nothing below can see this` |
| M10 | move the recorded coordinate | the `at` mismatch, same explanation |

The parity arm extracts `const FOOTPRINT_VARIES=` out of the payload and prepends it to the compiled body rather than injecting it as a parameter — deliberately, so a chunk that stops declaring the const goes red instead of passing.

## Versions

`ENGINE_VERSION` **0.21.0 → 0.23.0**. Minor, not patch: the artifact content a consumer observes changed. **0.22.0 is taken by the open #1016**, hence 0.23.0 rather than a second 0.22.0 entry the later merge would have to reconcile. `CONTRACT_VERSION` stays **5.3.0** — no token name and no `$type` moved, and the baseline diff is the `engineVersion` stamp alone (accepted via the CLI, not hand-edited).

## Judgment call: "copy needs updating" has two readings, and I did one

The **words** are rewritten — `description`, `props.icon`, four `codeOnly` entries and the notes, several of which made claims #920 had already falsified.

The reference's **bolded message** is not done, and my first reason for that was wrong so it is worth stating the rea

author: lilyshen0722
body:
Fifth in the reviewer-checklist stack: #1209 → #1219 → #1172 → #1237 → **this**. Based on #1237, not `main`.

## The rule

> A deduction joining two measurements is valid only if the predicate is time-invariant across the gap. Age predicates never are.

Wording and the find are @sprint-review's; I'm writing it up because the stack is mine and a five-deep chain owned by two people is the merge-order problem rule 20 exists for.

## Why it isn't covered by "verify your inputs"

The dangerous shape is two *good* measurements. Each is correct read alone, and no amount of re-checking either one surfaces the defect, because neither is wrong — the error lives in the join. A predicate containing `NOW()`, `Date.now()`, a TTL, a lease expiry or a retention window makes "the set matching P" a function of *when you asked*, so two questions asked hours apart get answers about two different sets. Nothing throws.

## Earned

On the #1208 retention question, in this pod, today:

- 20 nights of `[pg-retention] done: totalDeleted` prove the cron deletes (`08-06`→`08-25`, no zero nights, no gaps).
- A same-day count showed 885 rows past 30 days across 19 non-exempt pods.
- `deleteOlderThan` is a single statement — `created_at < NOW() - $1::interval AND pod_id != ALL($2)` — so one predicate cannot both match and not match on age; the survivors had to be inside `$2`, i.e. Pro-protected.

Valid in form, and it over-reached. The count was taken **~3.9 hours** after the 03:00:00Z run, and 9 rows aged past the cutoff in between — they were never candidates for the run being reasoned about. Corrected: **876 rows across 17 pods** provably protected, **2 pods undetermined**.

@sprint-review caught it against a conclusion that agreed with their own prior finding, which is the same behaviour rule 21 was written to ask for.

### The citation demonstrates its own rule

The first draft of this entry gave the gap as "~11½ hours" — derived from when the 885-row count was *read in conversation*, not when it was *taken*. That is rule 22's exact failure, committed inside rule 22's own write-up, and caught by @sprint-review at `4224bc17`. `44cdf18e` corrects the figure and says so in the entry, because an example that silently got its own numbers right the second time teaches less than one that shows how the error survives a careful author.

## Rider

The leftover rows are *undetermined by the argument*, not refuted by it. Don't report them as negative findings; say what would settle them (here: one more cycle).

## Verification

- Rules **1..22 contiguous and distinct** at this tip.
- Diff vs #1237's head is additive on the one file — zero real deletion lines at `4224bc17`; `44cdf18e` is a one-line correction to rule 22's own text and touches nothing else.
- Rule 19 byte-identical between #1219's head and this tip (verified independently by @sprint-review; my own first attempt at that check produced a false alarm because the extractor was anchored on a `20.` landmark that #1219's head does not have — see 58636).
- Docs-only. No code, no tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: aivsomkar
body:
## In plain language

Two things a bot can now do for itself, both **off by default**, both under
Settings on any bot.

**Auto-review** answers the approval cards you would obviously have allowed.
Right now every tool call that nothing granted becomes a card, including
`git status`. With this on, a model reads the request and settles the routine
ones with a reason attached, and everything else still comes to you.

It ships with a middle setting — **Watch** — that answers nothing and only
records what it *would* have done. That is the mode to run first: compare its
verdicts against what you actually clicked, then decide whether to trust it.
A feature that decides things on your behalf should have to earn it.

**Self-remembering** writes durable facts into a bot's memory without being
asked. Every bot already has a MEMORY.md that loads into its prompt each turn
and that it is told to curate with its own file tools — which works when the
agent remembers, and it usually does not. The useful fact arrives mid-task and
the turn ends without it being written down. This is the host doing it
instead.

## The two design decisions worth reviewing

**Where auto-review sits.** It is consulted at exactly one point: where
`autoVerdict` already returned `no-grant` — nothing granted the request, and
just as importantly no guard stopped it. The destructive, sensitive,
unattended and local-computer guards exist precisely to outrank grants, and a
classifier does not get to join that hierarchy. `shouldReview()` is an
**allowlist** over `AutoVerdictSource`, tested against every member, so a
source added later must opt into review deliberately rather than inherit it.

The worst thing this can do is approve something routine a person would have
clicked Allow on. It can never widen a grant, and it never sees a request a
guard already stopped.

**The card is shown first and settled after**, rather than holding the fold
for the classifier. Blocking would stall the whole event bus, and a person
staring at nothing for eight seconds is worse than one watching a card answer
itself. A human click always wins: `respondToRequest` reports `unavailable`
and nothing is written.

**The fenced block.** MEMORY.md is a file the user owns and hand-edits — that
is the whole reason it is plain markdown. Synthesis owns only what sits
between `<!-- maus:synthesized -->` and its close. Two sets of markers, a
half-open block, or a close before an open, and it refuses to write at all. A
rewrite that eats a line someone put there by hand is far worse than a fact
that never got recorded.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `server/helper-instance.ts` (new) | `generateText` is optional on `ProviderInstance` and only claude, antigravity, grok, minimax and openai-compat implement it, so a bot on codex or an ACP engine borrows a sibling. Everything fails to null: a feature built on this degrades to *off*, never to a guess. |
| `server/auto-review.ts` (new) | Classifier prompt and verdict parser. Prose, broken JSON, a non-boolean `allow`, or a missing reason all return null — and null means show the card. An approval must carry a reason because that reason is the decision-log row. |
| `server/index.ts` | `reviewCard()` at the fold; `runMemorySynthesis()` debounced 15s off `turn.completed`; `firstHandTurns` records whether a turn came from the keyboard. |
| `server/memory-synthesis.ts` (new) | Fenced-block reader/writer, prompt, and output parser. A fact containing a marker is stripped so it cannot forge a second block. |
| `server/auto-approve.ts` | `AutoVerdictSource` gains `auto-review` and `auto-review-shadow` — decision-log values only; they never appear in an `AutoVerdict`. |
| `server/store.ts`, `SettingsPanel.tsx` | `autoReview` (off/shadow/enforce) and `memorySynthesis`, both default off, both validated server-side rather than copied through — the same discipline `autoApprove` gets. |

## Fail-closed inventory

Every one of these leaves the card standing, or the file untouched:

- no helper instance available (a codex-only fleet gets neither feature)
- the classifier times out (8s for review, 30s for synthesis)
- the answer cannot be parsed
- the verdict is a refusal
- the user answered the card first
- the provider no longer has the request
- MEMORY.md is ambiguous, or the result would blow the budget
- the turn's origin was a webhook, listener, connector resume, or another bot

## Testing

191 test files, 1968 tests green, plus broker / updater / desktop-viewer /
packaged-server. `pnpm typecheck` clean. `oxlint` counts per touched file
identical to `origin/main`.

New coverage: 11 on helper resolution and querying (including that a slow
engine yields null instead of hanging), 21 on the review prompt and parser
(every malformed-answer shape, plus `shouldReview` against all nine verdict
sources), and 20 on synthesis (hand-edited file, no block, two blocks,
half-open block, backwards markers, a fact that tries to forge a marker,
oversized body, round-trip).

Settings round-trip verified against a live fleet: both fields save, and an
invalid `autoReview` is refused with a 400.

author: paolovalletta-exelab
body:
## What

Forward-ports the **v1.0.1 hotfix** (WhatsApp Twilio API Key authentication, released from `main` via #277) onto `develop`.

`main` was never back-merged into `develop` after v1.0.0, so `git merge main` conflicts in ~509 files. This is a `cherry-pick -x` of the 24 feature/test/doc commits instead — 22 cherry-picked, 2 re-applied by hand where a literal pick was structurally impossible (noted in those commit messages).

**Deliberately not ported:** the version bump and the CHANGELOG entry. `develop` is already at 1.1.0 with its own release in preparation, so those belong to that cycle — see the open question below.

## Conflict resolutions worth reviewing

Each of these was a place where taking the wrong side loses something silently:

- **`CHANNEL_CONFIG_KEYS.whatsapp` kept the six-key list** (`authMode` included). `develop`'s legacy three-key list would have failed *silently*: `authMode` ignored by the merge handler, and every API-Key save either 400ing on the discriminated union or quietly persisting Auth Token mode.
- **Both log protections compose**, rather than one replacing the other: `sanitizeForLog(instanceSlug)` and `sanitizeForLog(redactWebhookPath(webhookUrl))`. `develop` had the sanitizer; `main` added the path redaction.
- **`develop`'s `hasOwnProperty` prototype-pollution hardening was preserved** through every subsequent refactor of the allowlist walk. `main` used the weaker `in` operator there, so this is one place `develop`'s version won on purpose.
- **The shared `buildEventSourceWebhookUrl` replaced `develop`'s inline `buildWebhookUrl`**, verified to produce a byte-identical URL — an operator's already-configured event-source URL must not change.
- **`create-logger.ts` kept `develop`'s copy** (byte-identical to the one `main` backported); only the WhatsApp controller call sites came across.
- **The web part was re-applied at `develop`'s tenant path**, not `main`'s. `develop` deleted `(admin)/instances/[slug]/`, and its channels tab is a different shape (one channel per page with a shared save action, versus `main`'s all-channels-on-one-page). The card and its wiring were adapted to that, not pasted; a naive cherry-pick would have created dead files at an unroutable path while the live tab kept rendering WhatsApp through the generic loop.
- **`CLAUDE.md` follows `develop`'s convention**, not `main`'s: a one-line rule in Key Conventions plus the full reasoning in `references/channels.md`. `main`'s flat "Important Caveats" block does not exist on `develop`.

## Testing

Baseline established on a fresh `origin/develop` before the first pick, then re-run after:

| | baseline | after |
|---|---|---|
| engine | 223 files / 2714 tests, 0 fail | **231 / 2800, 0 fail** |
| web | 58 / 607, 0 fail | **59 / 622, 0 fail** |
| typecheck | 0 errors | 0 errors |
| lint | 0 errors | 0 errors |

24/24 commits carry the DCO trailer.

## Open question for the reviewer

The **1.0.1 CHANGELOG entry is not in this PR**. `develop` carries a `## [1.1.0]` section dated the same day. Whoever owns the 1.1.0 release should decide whether to add a `## [1.0.1]` section below it (it is a released version, so arguably yes) or to fold this content into the 1.1.0 notes. Deliberately left alone rather than guessed at.

The stderr object only had one unit test, printing a single fixed string. This adds a dozen more cases covering the shapes of input it's likely to see in practice: an empty string, a multiline string, unicode text, emoji, a very long string, a single character, a string with no trailing newline, a whitespace-only string, tabs and quotes, and a Windows-style carriage return.

It also checks the return value directly with an explicit `eq.` comparison to `true`, and adds two tests around calling stderr more than once: one confirming a sequence of writes still succeeds, and one confirming the same string produces the same (successful) result across repeated calls.

Since stderr writes to the real file descriptor 2, these tests can only exercise that the call completes and returns `true` for each input shape, the same limitation as the existing stdout/console tests.

author: justinwlin
body:
## Problem

Fixes #365 · Internal: CON-1230

An `Endpoint` declared in client mode (`image=...`, no decorated functions) produced a build manifest with an empty `resources` map. `flash deploy` uploaded the artifact, created the app and environment, printed `✓ deployed to production`, and exited 0 — provisioning nothing. `flash env get production` then showed `no resources. run flash deploy --env production`, pointing the user back at the command that had just run.

## Fix

The build now discovers top-level client-mode `Endpoint(image=...)` objects during scanning and registers each as a function-less manifest entry marked `client_mode: true`. Deployment config — `imageName`, `gpuIds`/`instanceIds`, workers, scaler, env, volumes, datacenter locations — comes from the Endpoint's own `_build_resource_config()`, the same object first-`run()` provisioning uses.

From there the existing deploy path (`reconcile_and_provision_resources` → `create_resource_from_manifest` → `ResourceManager.get_or_deploy_resource`) provisions them like any other resource and persists endpoint URLs into the state manifest. So `flash env get` lists them, and re-deploys reuse the same endpoint unless config changed.

The first commit on this branch (f36fa48) shipped an honest "no deployable resources" message instead. That short-circuit remains, but now only fires for projects declaring neither decorated resources nor client-mode endpoints.

## Verified

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/unit/cli --no-cov` | 587 passed |
| `pytest tests/unit --no-cov` | 2575 passed, 3 failed (pre-existing) |
| `ruff check` + `ruff format`, touched files | clean |
| Offline end-to-end chain | provisionable objects produced |

<details>
<summary>The 3 failures are pre-existing</summary>

`test_load_balancer_sls_stub.py` ×2 and `test_regressions.py` REG008 reproduce identically with these changes stashed — order-dependent pollution on the base commit, not introduced here.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Offline end-to-end chain</summary>

Real `RuntimeScanner` → `ManifestBuilder.build()` → `create_resource_from_manifest()` over a client-only project (GPU `vllm-openai` + CPU `whisper`) yields provisionable `LiveServerless`/`CpuLiveServerless` objects carrying the user image, GPU/CPU config, workers, and env. Verified with `FLASH_IS_LIVE_PROVISIONING` unset (concrete class names) and `=false` (normalized to `Endpoint`, still provisionable).
</details>

## What changed

**`build_utils/scanner.py`** — `RuntimeScanner` collects top-level `Endpoint` instances with `image=` set and `id` unset (those attach to existing endpoints) into `scanner.client_endpoints` during module import. Re-exports (`from defs import ep` in a second file) are tolerated when the image matches; the same name with a different image fails the build with a "defined in multiple files" error.

**`build_utils/manifest.py`** — `ManifestBuilder._add_client_endpoints` registers each client endpoint into `resources` with `functions: []`, `client_mode: true`, and config extracted by re-importing the source module and calling `_build_resource_config()` (same `_extract_config_properties` path as decorated resources). `resource_type` records the concrete class only when the deploy-time provisioner can rebuild it; otherwise it falls back to `"Endpoint"`, which `create_resource_from_manifest` resolves to GPU/CPU via `gpuIds`. Name collisions with decorated resources raise.

**`cli/commands/deploy.py`** — the empty-resources message is reworded to "no deployable resources found; nothing was deployed" and only triggers when the manifest has no resources at all.

<details>
<summary>Four supporting changes</summary>

- **`cli/utils/deployment.py`** — `_FLASH_SOURCE_FINGERPRINT` env injection skips `client_mode` entries, so code-only deploys don't trigger pointless rolling updates of external-service endpoints. Reconciliation is otherwise unchanged, which is what keeps re-deploys idempotent (state-manifest compare + `get_or_deploy_resource` reuse).
- **`build_utils/handler_generator.py`** — skips `client_mode` resources; no functions means no handler to generate.
- **`cli/commands/preview.py`** — local preview skips `client_mode` resources; they run user-supplied images and are provisioned remotely.
- **`runtime/resource_provisioner.py`** — supported class list is now a module-level `PROVISIONABLE_RESOURCE_TYPES`. Behavior unchanged.
</details>

## Live testing

2026-08-25, real Runpod account. Client-mode-only app:

```python
Endpoint(name="con370-live-1248", image="runpod/serverless-hello-world:0.4.1",
         gpu=GpuGroup.AMPERE_16, workers=(0, 1), idle_timeout=60)
```

- `flash deploy` created app `con370-live` + `production` env and **provisioned and printed the endpoint**: `con370-live-1248  https://api.runpod.ai/v2/4kuwiutqisjt2f/runsync`. On `main` the same app yields empty `resources` and a false success.
- `GET /v1/endpoints/4kuwiutqisjt2f` → `workersMin: 0`, `workersMax: 1`, `idleTimeout: 60`, `gpuTypeIds: [A4000, A4500, 4000 Ada, 2000 Ada]` (the AMPERE_16 pool), flashboot on. Deployed config matches the request.
- `flash env get production` lists the endpoint. On `main` it printed `no resources`.

## Out of scope

- **`workersStandby: 1`** on the live endpoint is expected here and addressed in #372.
- **Idempotency** is covered by the mocked tests (state-manifest carry) rather than a second live deploy; the single live deploy above was the missing piece.

author: colewesterveld
body:
## What this fixes

Importing a shared program has to work out which local exercise each of the sharer's exercise ids means. It did that by exact SQL title comparison, and dropped anything it could not resolve. Three problems fell out of that.

### 1. Matching was case sensitive, so it made duplicates

`where: 'exercise_title = ?'` is case sensitive in SQLite. A program shared as `barbell bench press` did not match the local `Barbell Bench Press`, so the importer created a second, near identical library entry. The user's history, goals and PR detection then split across two exercises that look identical in the list.

Matching now uses a normalised key (trimmed, lowercased, runs of whitespace collapsed), read from one query over the library instead of one query per exercise.

### 2. Exercise creation was outside the transaction

New exercises were inserted with `db.insert` before `db.transaction` opened. If the program insert then failed, those exercises stayed in the library with nothing referencing them. Everything is now in a single transaction.

### 3. Unresolvable rows were dropped silently

`if (newExerciseId == null) continue;` and two siblings dropped exercise instances and planned sets, then returned success. `exercise_order` was left with a hole in it, and the user had no way to tell a lift was missing from their new program.

A file that refers to rows it does not contain is damaged. The import now aborts, the transaction rolls back, nothing is written, and the user is told.

A dangling `superset_group` is deliberately **not** treated as damage. Deleting the first exercise of a superset leaves the others pointing at an id that is gone ([program_provider.dart](../blob/main/lib/providers_and_settings/program_provider.dart#L721) uses the first instance's id as the group id, and `deleteExerciseInstance` does not clean up). That is a normal program, so those import as ungrouped, unchanged from before.

## Also in here

- **Blank exercise details are filled in from the shared file.** If the sharer recorded the muscles worked and this device left it blank, take theirs. Anything already filled in locally is never overwritten.
- **The snackbar reports what was added**, since the user's exercise list quietly grew: `"Shared Plan" imported. 3 new exercises added to your list.` Unchanged when nothing new was needed.
- **`PRAGMA foreign_keys` in the full backup import was a no-op.** SQLite ignores that pragma once a transaction is open, so the OFF/ON pair around the wipe did nothing. That import only worked because its delete and insert ordering happened to be FK correct. Replaced with `defer_foreign_keys`, the transaction scoped equivalent, which actually takes effect.

## Tests

New `test/program_import_test.dart`, 11 tests over the real code with `sqflite_common_ffi`. Four of them fail on `main`, covering exactly the behaviour changed here:

| Test | On `main` |
|---|---|
| case and spacing differences match the existing exercise | creates a duplicate |
| a blank local field is filled in from the shared file | stays blank |
| a damaged file writes nothing at all | reports success, writes a partial program |
| a planned set with no exercise fails the whole import | reports success, drops the set |

The rest pin down behaviour that must not regress: the custom exercise case that started this, its planned sets, re-importing the same file, superset round trip, dangling groups, and that all three starter programs still import (they go through the same code path).

## Not in here

Exercises are still identified across devices by their title. That leaves two gaps this PR does not close:

- **Two different lifts sharing a name silently merge.** If one person's custom "Row Machine" is a chest supported row and another's is an erg, importing merges them onto whichever already exists, and the history panel then shows the wrong numbers. Normalised matching makes this slightly more likely, not less.
- **`assets/exercises.txt` is only read in `_onCreate`**, so a user's library is frozen to whatever the seed list said on the day they installed. Editing that list post release (commit `013ffd5` already renamed `Pull-Up` to `Pullups` once, pre release) permanently fragments the user base, and sharing between the two halves creates duplicates that normalisation cannot fix.

Both need stable identity rather than text: a `source_key` column, fixed slugs for the seeded exercises and generated ids for custom ones, behind a schema v4 migration. Worth doing before the next edit to `exercises.txt`, not needed for the bug this PR fixes.

body:
<!-- Write all pull request text in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100): short sentences, one instruction per sentence, simple approved vocabulary, and the active voice. -->

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - This fork runs a PR review GitHub Action that mints a short-lived App installation token
> - Upstream wires that gate to the paperclipai App `commitperclip` (id 3718661)
> - A fork cannot hold upstream's App private key, so signing as 3718661 always fails
> - Tangent-Forge already owns `tfrm-review` (id 4541043) with repo vars and `REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`
> - PR #80 wired those vars; an upstream adopt later replaced the script and workflow with the hardcoded upstream copies
> - PR #105 only fixed the secret name; JWT still used iss=3718661 and GitHub returned 401 undecodable JWT

## Summary
In `packages/core/src/runtime.ts`:
`dynamicPromptExecFromState` builds targeted retry contexts from validated extractor fields, truncating field contents longer than 500 characters using `${content.slice(0, 497)}...`.

When structured field values contain multi-byte UTF-16 surrogate pairs (e.g. emojis or astral plane characters), slicing at index 497 can split a surrogate pair in half and produce orphaned surrogate characters (`\uFFFD`).

body:
## Description

- **Cause racine du gel de la prod**, trouvée dans une alerte du sonar restée sans suite : « Deploy hook prod a répondu **304** » (`#02_vitrine_sonar`, 24 août 8h12).
- Deux circuits déclenchent les builds à quelques minutes d'intervalle — le **sync Athena de la minute :10** et la **publication de l'illustration de la Une** (`art.ts`, actif depuis le 23 août). Cloudflare répond `304` au second : « un déploiement est déjà en file pour cette branche ». **Ce n'est pas un échec**, c'est la preuve que le premier appel a été pris.
- Le code levait dessus. Et comme `prod` est appelé **en premier**, l'exception emportait **aussi le build `dev`** : plus rien ne rebâtissait le site, ni prod ni dev.
- Correctif : `304` journalisé comme succès ; chaque hook a sa chance (échecs collectés, rapport unique à la fin) ; la fonction déménage dans son propre module pour être testable sans tirer Neon dans la compilation racine.

## Type de changement

- [ ] Nouvelle fonctionnalité
- [x] Correctif
- [ ] Refactorisation
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Outillage (CI, scripts, gardes)

## Surface touchée

- **Raffineurs / scrapers / pipelines** : aucun
- **Tables et colonnes (créées, modifiées, supprimées)** : aucune
- **Outillage (CI, scripts, gardes, infra)** : `workers/api/src/deploy-hooks.ts` (nouveau, extrait de `sync-athena.ts` qui le réexporte — aucun appelant à changer), `tests/sync-athena.test.ts` (+3 cas)

## Dépendances

- [x] Aucune — cette PR se merge seule
- [ ] Dépend de #… — à merger après **son merge**
- [ ] Dépend de #… — à merger après **son DÉPLOIEMENT**

Complémentaire de #581 (filet 6×/jour côté Actions) : celle-ci répare le chemin **autonome** (Worker → hooks → Pages), #581 garantit le repli. Les deux peuvent vivre ensemble ; si ce correctif suffit, #581 pourra revenir à une cadence plus basse.

## Déploiement

- [ ] DEV suffit — le changement n'a pas à agir en PROD
- [x] À graduer en PROD — le Worker se déploie par `wrangler` (voir `workers/api/README.md`) ; le correctif n'a d'effet qu'une fois le Worker redéployé

## Tests effectués

- `npx vitest run` : **26 fichiers, 393 tests verts**, dont **3 neufs** sur les trois cas exacts — `304` sur prod (dev est quand même appelé, aucune erreur), échec réel sur prod (dev tenté quand même, puis signalé), hook absent (les autres partent).
- `npm run type-check` : propre — c'est précisément ce que l'extraction du module protège (importer `sync-athena.ts` depuis un test tirait `@neondatabase/serverless` dans la compilation racine et cassait toutes les PR ; le piège est documenté en tête du fichier de test).

**Non exécuté :**

- Le comportement réel face à Cloudflare (le `304` est reproduit par un `fetch` simulé, pas par un vrai hook). À vérifier au premier cycle après redéploiement du Worker : un build `prod` doit partir même si l'illustration a déjà déclenché le sien.

## Impact méthodologie

- [x] Aucun impact métho — ne change ni horaire, ni collecte, ni liste de médias, ET les 3 docs restent exactes (justification, en nommant les 3 : `public/methodologie/index.html` ne décrit pas la mécanique de publication ; `public/docs/horaire-refiners-2026.html` — l'horaire des raffineurs est inchangé, ce correctif est côté site ; `public/docs/workflow-vitrine-2025-swimlanes.html` — ni table, ni raffineur, ni modèle touché)

## Note de journal

Le site pouvait rester affiché sur une édition ancienne pendant des heures, même quand les nouvelles analyses étaient prêtes : deux mises à jour lancées à quelques minutes d'intervalle se gênaient l'une l'autre et la publication était abandonnée. Chacune suit désormais son cours, et la page se renouvelle comme prévu.

## Apport de l'IA

- [x] IA impliquée — provenance en français fournie (trailer sur les commits + « 🤖 Assisté par … » dans ce corps de PR)
- [ ] Aucun apport d'IA

author: maho7791
body:
Schließt Issue #3 (beide Teile). **Basiert direkt auf snapshot** (nach Merge von #21 rebased — der Diff ist nur noch der MQTT-Commit).

## Teil 1: Java-MQTT-TCP-Drahtnachweis (Harness Szenario D)

- `broker.mqtt`/`client.mqtt` liegen schlummernd (configurationPolicy REQUIRE) in den Standard-Launches; die neuen Launch-Varianten `broker-mqtt.bndrun`/`client-mqtt.bndrun` wecken sie über das Config-Bundle `org.eclipse.fennec.services.itest.mqtt.config`.
- Bewusst ein Bundle statt `configurator.initial`: die Property wird geparst, bevor das jakarta.json-Provider-Bundle gestartet ist („Invalid JSON"), und `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` strippt die Anführungszeichen, die Inline-JSON braucht.
- Szenario D assertet REGISTERED + UNREGISTERING über echten Mosquitto-TCP, mit Ordnungskontrolle: der letzte Stream-(Re-)Open vor den Events muss die MQTT-Subscription sein.
- **SDK-Fix (Nebenbefund):** ein per `service.ranking` besser gerankter EventSource übernahm einen bereits offenen Stream nicht — `transportAvailable()` schließt jetzt und öffnet neu; der Reopen triggert das Re-Snapshot (Transport-Handover verliert keine Events, FR-Sync-Reconnect).

## Teil 2: MQTT-Service-Flavor (Harness Szenario E)

- Eingefrorene Request/Response-Konvention (`mqtt-rpc.ts`, dokumentiert in ARCHITECTURE §3 + WIRE_CHANNELS §5 als umgesetzte TOPIC_BASED-Strategie): MQTT-3.1.1-tauglich — `correlationId` + `replyTo` reisen im JSON-Envelope, ein Reply-Topic pro Request, QoS aus dem Flavor-Paar, nie retained; Handler-Fehler antworten mit dem error-Envelope statt eines Timeouts.
- `MqttFlavorPlugin` (Consumer: pending-Map über correlationId, Timeout, Verbindungs-Pool pro Broker-URL) und `MqttOperationServer` (Provider-Dispatch pro Operation-Topic).
- Der TS-Beispiel-Provider annonciert mit `MQTT_URL` zusätzlich den `MqttFlavor` auf derselben Implementation (DoD-Szenario: *same interface, different transports*) und bedient beide Transporte aus demselben Zustand; MQTT-Endpoint lauscht **vor** dem Publish (nie einen toten Endpoint annoncieren).
- Die Harness-Probe ruft `getBalance` über den **annoncierten** Flavor auf — die Broker-Adresse kommt aus `MqttFlavor.brokers`, nichts ist out-of-band konfiguriert. Der DDSR-Broker ist an der Invocation unbeteiligt (Discovery/Acquisition only).

## Tests

- 6 neue RPC-Tests (Roundtrip über In-Memory-Broker-Fake, error-Envelope, Korrelation unter Nebenläufigkeit, Timeout, canHandle, Topic-/QoS-Ableitung) — TS 91 gesamt grün
- Voller Java-Build grün; Podman-Harness lokal **A + B + C + D + E** grün

author: pinfada
body:
## Type de changement

- [x] Implémentation ou correction conduite en TDD
- [ ] Spike reproductible
- [ ] Documentation ou ADR
- [ ] Audit ou revue externe

## Résultat

`isolation-probe.mjs` vit désormais sous `src/spike/isolation-probe.mjs`. Il est chargé par trois
contextes — la page coquille du spike #35, son Worker runtime et le document applicatif — et ne
reçoit donc plus que l'intersection des globals page ∩ Worker au lieu de tout le jeu navigateur.

Concrètement : un `document` écrit dans ce module passait le lint sans un mot et n'aurait cassé que
le Worker, à l'exécution. Il est maintenant refusé par `npm run lint`.

Le déplacement ne change aucun comportement d'exécution. Les trois importateurs passent du chemin
relatif `./isolation-probe.mjs` au chemin absolu `/src/spike/isolation-probe.mjs`, racine que
`tools/serve.mjs` sert déjà — pour les deux rôles de serveur, coquille et territoire applicatif.
**Aucune modification de `tools/serve.mjs` n'a été nécessaire** : l'issue anticipait un ajustement
des racines servies, mais `resolveRoot` traite `/src/` depuis le spike #2 et le document applicatif
importait déjà `/src/spike/origin-topology.mjs` par cette voie.

Closes #49

## Critères d'acceptation

- [x] Le module est analysé avec l'intersection page/Worker (bloc `src/**` de `eslint.config.mjs`).
- [x] Les trois importateurs sont ajustés (`shell.mjs`, `runtime-worker.mjs`, `app-probe.mjs`).
- [x] Les racines servies par `tools/serve.mjs` sont correctes — vérifié, déjà le cas, sans
      changement.
- [x] Les tests du spike #35 restent verts (`npm run test:spike:origin`, 15 épreuves).
- [x] `docs/development.md` ne mentionne plus cette limite et donne le module en exemple de la règle.

## Preuve adaptée au type

### Implémentation — rouge, vert, refactorisation

#### Rouge

**1. Démonstration directe du défaut.** Sur `main`, avant tout changement, un usage DOM est ajouté
au module tel qu'il vivait sous `public/` :

```js
// TEMOIN ROUGE : usage DOM interdit dans un module chargé par le Worker runtime.
export const titreDocument = document.title;
```

```sh
npx eslint public/spike/origin/isolation-probe.mjs
```

```text
code de sortie : 0
```

Aucune sortie, aucune erreur : le linter accorde `document` à un module que le Worker runtime
importe. C'est exactement le silence que l'issue #43 signalait en fermant sa propre tranche. Le
témoin a été retiré avant le commit.

**2. Test versionné.** Commit du test seul : `ee608e0 test: exiger qu'un module partagé page/Worker
reçoive l'intersection`.

L'épreuve ajoutée à `tests/unit/eslint-config.test.mjs` ne code pas en dur l'emplacement souhaité :
elle **localise** `isolation-probe.mjs` sous les deux racines servies au navigateur (`public/` et
`src/`), exige une occurrence unique, puis lint deux sources témoins sous son chemin réel. Elle
échoue donc tant que le module est mal rangé, et elle échouerait à nouveau si on l'y remettait.

```sh
node --test tests/unit/eslint-config.test.mjs
```

Sortie sur `ee608e0`, module encore sous `public/` :

```text
✔ le code servi au navigateur n'a pas accès aux globals Node (133.1585ms)
✔ le code Node n'a pas accès aux globals du navigateur (9.6313ms)
✔ un module Worker n'a pas accès au DOM mais garde ses globals propres (10.5063ms)
✔ un module partagé de src/ ne reçoit que l'intersection page et Worker (4.4478ms)
✔ un module de page garde le DOM et un module Node garde les globals Node (10.546ms)
✖ un module réellement partagé est rangé là où il reçoit l'intersection (7.1346ms)
✔ les spécifications Playwright cumulent Node et navigateur (27.7676ms)
ℹ tests 7
ℹ pass 6
ℹ fail 1

✖ failing tests:

test at tests\unit\eslint-config.test.mjs:154:1
✖ un module réellement partagé est rangé là où il reçoit l'intersection (7.1346ms)
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: public/spike/origin/isolation-probe.mjs reçoit le DOM :
  il est analysé comme un script de page, pas comme un module partagé
  + actual - expected

  + []
  - [
  -   'document'
  - ]
```

L'échec nomme le fichier fautif et sa cause. Les six épreuves déjà vertes sont les témoins positifs :
le test n'échoue pas parce que tout serait refusé.

#### Vert

Commit d'implémentation : `23910ab chore: ranger le module de mesure d'isolation sous src/ (#49)`.

```sh
node --test tests/unit/eslint-config.test.mjs
```

```text
✔ le code servi au navigateur n'a pas accès aux globals Node (139.4525ms)
✔ le code Node n'a pas accès aux globals du navigateur (9.5838ms)
✔ un module Worker n'a pas accès au DOM mais garde ses globals propres (10.5772ms)
✔ un module partagé de src/ ne reçoit que l'intersection page et Worker (4.6035ms)
✔ un module de page garde le DOM et un module Node garde les globals Node (10.8853ms)
✔ un module réellement partagé est rangé là où il reçoit l'intersection (8.6902ms)
✔ les spécifications Playwright cumulent Node et navigateur (24.838ms)
ℹ tests 7
ℹ pass 7
ℹ fail 0
```

**Le même témoin DOM, au nouvel emplacement**, est maintenant refusé :

```sh
npx eslint src/spike/isolation-probe.mjs
```

```text
C:\...\src\spike\isolation-probe.mjs
  32:30  error  'document' is not defined  no-undef

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)

code de sortie : 1
```

C'est la démonstration symétrique du rouge n° 1 : même code, même commande, verdict inversé. Le
témoin a été retiré ; il n'est pas versionné.

**Le spike #35 reste vert**, ce qui prouve que les trois importateurs chargent réellement le module
à son nouveau chemin — la coquille, le Worker runtime et le document applicatif exposent tous les
trois une mesure d'isolation lue par les épreuves :

```sh
npm run test:spike:origin
```

```text
Running 15 tests using 2 workers
```

author: gjgilbert
body:
## Summary

  32 commits, 43 files, +3040 / −1904 against `kpf-next`.

  Fills out the science-chain quality-control suite
  (`kpfpipe/quality_control/{diagnostics,qc_flags}`) and settles the division of labor
  between its stages: **Diagnostics measure and write header keywords; QC reads those 
  keywords and writes 0/1**. Most of the volume is new L0 metrics ported from v2.12.

  ### Framework

  - **`ISGOOD` is gone.** The cross-level AND aggregate is removed from `QC.run`, the
  registry, the architecture doc, and the science run summary. `Checkpoint.qc_flags` now
  warns with the list of failing flags instead; `RAISE_FLAGS` still raises per level.
  - **Diagnostics and QC no longer abort the pipeline.** A diagnostic that raises is logged
  at ERROR and its keyword simply isn't written; a QC check that raises is logged and
  counted as a fail (writes 0). `NotImplementedError` from a placeholder writes nothing.
  Halting stays the checkpoints layer's job.
  - **Defensive header accessors removed** (`QC._hdr_float`, `QC._hdr_bool`). Checks read
  headers directly, so an absent or malformed card surfaces rather than silently reading as
  `None`/`False`.
  - Registry CSVs now accept `#` section banners (`pd.read_csv(..., comment="#")`), and the
  generic `QC` populator tag is dropped — every QC row is `QCL{n}`.

  ### Keywords

  | Level | Added | Removed |
  |---|---|---|
  | L0 | 78 | 6 |
  | L1 | 12 | 2 |
  | L2 | 64 | 15 |

  **L0** — pointing offsets (`TCSOFF`/`OBJOFF`/`GAIAOFF`), dead/saturated pixel fractions,
  24 per-amplifier percentiles, exposure-meter channel metrics and per-band cumulative
  counts, guider metrics (RMS/bias, saturation, FWHM/flux statistics, Moffat-fit seeing),
  and CCD/etalon temperature offsets. New QCs consuming them: `READOK`, `CAHKPR`, `EMSCIPR`,
  `EMSKYPR`, `GREENL0`, `REDL0`, `NTPOK`, `TARGETOK`, `GTEMPOK`, `RTEMPOK`, `GUIDEROK`,
  `ELEVOK`, `ETATMPOK`, `AGITOK`.

  Renames: `TARGOFF`→`TCSOFF`, `RADECOK`→`TARGETOK`, plus the L0 QC keyword pass in
  `d0074ea0`.

  **L1** — per-chip flux percentiles (`FFI{G,R}{10,50,90,99}P`); `FFIOK` replaced by
 `L1NANOK`, `L1SNROK`, `L1VAROK`.

  **L2** — chip-level SNR and flux ratios replaced by per-band equivalents at
  452/548/652/747/852 nm across orderlets; `ZEROFRAC` replaced by per-orderlet `ZERO*`
  counts.


  ### Elsewhere

  - `scripts/quality_control/{qc,qlp}.py` deleted with their regression tests — the recipe
  drives all three stages through `CheckpointL{n}.run()`.
  - `AstroQuery` no longer writes the `WMKOCR`/`GAIACR`/`SIMBADCR` presence flags; an
  unresolved source is simply a missing `CATALOG_RECORD` row.
  - `ImageProcessing` writes `FLATDIV` alongside `BIASSUB`/`DARKSUB`.
  - `BaseMasterModule._load_frame` runs `DiagL0` before `QCL0`, so the flags that consume
  diagnostics have their inputs.
  - Architecture and style guides updated,
  
  ### Testing

  `make test` — 1950 passed. Test files carry roughly half the diff.

author: mereithhh
body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring production bug where an archived ordinary session disappears locally and returns after reload. The production trace showed that `/archive` committed, but session-scoped `killSession` registration had been rejected by the machine-only RPC scope and a later heartbeat wrote `active=true` again.

This replaces the kill-first UI workaround with a server-owned lifecycle:

- add a durable nullable `Session.archivedAt` tombstone and make delayed presence writes conditional on it
- commit archive in the server first, reject/reap archived session sockets, and broadcast a lifecycle command to session clients plus machine daemons
- restore exact session-scoped RPC registration without allowing user-scoped or cross-scope registration
- reconcile missed archive commands when a daemon reconnects, and safely re-adopt persisted live Happy PIDs after daemon restart
- route archive termination through every runner (Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenClaw, ACP), with SIGTERM → SIGKILL escalation and exit verification
- make resume an explicit unarchive transition with awaited archive compensation if spawn fails
- make terminal deletion succeed only after exact-target `tmux has-session` confirms the tmux session is gone

The design, compatibility matrix, release order, rollback boundary, and production acceptance steps are captured in `specs/2026-08-session-archive-lifecycle.md`.

## Verification

- Server: typecheck; 76 files / 499 tests
- Web V2: 125 files / 1,559 tests; production build; typecheck
- CLI: build; 135 files / 1,264 tests; runtime `--version` smoke
- Real tmux integration: 2 files / 19 tests
- Secret scan: no leaks

## Deployment note

This PR is not deployed. Required order is additive migration → server → Web → CLI publish → `vh-update`; then perform the production archive/reload/heartbeat/resume acceptance sequence from the spec.

author: ayinde38
body:
Closes #781
Closes #782
Closes #783
Closes #784

Four frontend fixes, batched into one PR since they touch overlapping files.

## #781 — token expiry during an active session

`AuthGuard` checked the token once, on mount. A token that was valid at page load and expired while the user sat on the dashboard left them with rendered UI whose every request 401s, and nothing on screen explaining why.

**New `src/lib/session.ts`** owns the expiry decision. It deliberately imports nothing from `api.ts` or `auth.ts` — those already import each other, so a third edge would close the cycle. It decodes the JWT `exp` (for *scheduling* only; the server remains the authority on validity), and `handleSessionExpired()` clears storage, toasts `"Your session has expired. Please log in again."` and redirects to `/login` preserving where the user was. A once-only latch stops a burst of concurrent 401s stacking toasts and redirects.

- `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 branch now routes through that handler. It previously cleared the token and redirected inline, with no message — the user just found themselves back at login.
- `AuthGuard` schedules a refresh **60 s before expiry** and re-arms against the new expiry on success. `scheduleAt()` chunks delays past `setTimeout`'s 32-bit ceiling; a 30-day token would otherwise overflow and fire immediately.
- `refreshAccessToken()` exchanges a stored refresh token at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`, handling the backend's token rotation.

**One thing worth knowing:** `refreshAccessToken()` returns `null` when there is no refresh token to spend, and today that is the common case — `/api/merchants/login` returns only `token`, never `refresh_token`. When that happens the guard ends the session cleanly at expiry rather than refreshing it. That still fixes the reported bug (the user is told and redirected instead of sitting on a dead page), and `LoginForm` now stores `refresh_token` when the response carries one, so the proactive path lights up the moment the backend starts supplying it. Wiring the merchant login endpoint to return one felt like a separate change.

## #782 — checkout widget under a strict CSP

The widget reads `data-nonce` from its own `<script>` tag via `document.currentScript`, cached at load time since `currentScript` is null by the time any callback runs. It falls back to a `data-fluxapay-widget` tag, then a `src` match, then `window.FLUXAPAY_CSP_NONCE`, so async loaders work too. The nonce is applied to everything injected, and exposed as `FluxaPay.nonce` plus `createNoncedElement()` for host code injecting alongside the widget.

**The substantive fix is the styling.** Every element was styled with `element.style.cssText = ...` — inline style *attributes*. A nonce **cannot** whitelist a style attribute; CSP nonces apply only to `<style>` and `<script>` elements. So under a strict `style-src` the widget rendered completely unstyled no matter what nonce was configured, and adding nonce support without touching this would have satisfied the letter of the issue while leaving it broken.

All styling now lives in a single nonced `<style>` element with class names on the elements. `style-src 'nonce-…'` works and merchants do not need `'unsafe-inline'`. A test asserts no inline style assignment survives anywhere in the source, so this cannot regress quietly.

Also swapped `innerHTML` for `textContent` on the close button, and added `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal` and a label to the modal while I was in there.

`docs/CHECKOUT_WIDGET_CSP.md` covers the directives to allow, async loading, verification and troubleshooting.

## #783 — VirtualizedTable with no rows

The issue says an empty array crashes. It doesn't, quite — `[].length` is `0`, the slice comes back empty, and the component renders nothing at all. The crash it describes (`Cannot read properties of undefined`) happens when `data` is **undefined or null**, which is exactly what a table bound to an in-flight or failed request receives.

Both cases are handled: `data` is normalised once at the top, and an empty result renders `EmptyState` with optional `emptyMessage` and `emptyIcon` props.

One wrinkle worth flagging: `EmptyState` only emitted `<tr><td>`, and `VirtualizedTable` renders `<div>`s — dropping it in as-is produces invalid DOM and a React nesting warning. It gained a `variant="block"` that renders a `<div>`; the default stays `"row"`, so all six existing table call sites are untouched. A test asserts no `<tr>` escapes into the div tree.

The props are named `data`, not `rows` as the issue says.

## #784 — PII in the invoice draft

`saveDraft()` serialised the whole form to `localStorage`: unencrypted, readable by any script on the origin, and surviving the tab. Customer name and email are the merchant's *customers'* personal data, not the merchant's own — a shared device or a single XSS foothold would expose people who never used this app. Losing an autosaved name costs a retype; leaking one is a breach.

`PII_DRAFT_FIELDS` is stripped before anything is written, with the reasoning documented at the constant. Restore defaults those fields to empty, which also means **the next save purges PII written by an older build** — existing drafts on users' machines clean themselves up. Everything describing the invoice rather than a person still persists, so the autosave keeps doing its job.

The test asserts the PII *values* appear nowhere in the serialised draft, not merely that the keys are absent — a rename or a nested copy would otherwise slip through.

## Tests

Four new test files, ~90 cases: widget nonce discovery and injection, session expiry and JWT decoding, the 401 interceptor and refresh flow, and VirtualizedTable's empty and non-empty paths.

**They have not been run.** The npm registry is unreachable from my environment, so `node_modules` could not be installed and `vitest` could not execute. `public/fluxapay-widget.js` is syntax-checked with `node --check`; the TypeScript is reviewed by reading only. Please lean on CI.

author: monkdim
body:
Two real exports, one of a fight with a module (Titan Hard) and one without (Alexander), exposed three problems.

## Moduled fights got the worse analysis

The good analysis — mechanic shapes, cast-time positions, spread, movement — lived inside the whole-recording dump. So a duty **nobody has covered** produced that, while a duty **somebody had written a module for** produced a flat list of mean positions relative to a derived arena centre and nothing else.

That is exactly backwards. Moduled fights are the ones with role assignments worth reporting.

Both exports now use one implementation. The caller supplies who counts as the party, how to label them, and which actions are in scope, so the encounter export scopes to each pull and labels rows by role, while the recording dump covers everything and labels by name.

## Knockbacks fell outside the sampling window

Alexander's Super Cyclone is described as a heavy room-wide knockback. The export reported players travelling 3 to 6 yalms between cast and resolution:

```
PLD Rune Novalke    cast d= 4.34 NE  spread 0.43y  |  hit d= 1.45 N   moved 3.80y
MNK Akira Gremorie  cast d= 3.66 SE  spread 1.14y  |  hit d= 1.20 E   moved 4.55y
```

That was people repositioning **during** the cast. A knockback deals its damage first and shoves a moment later, so the resolution sample is still pre-displacement and the shove never appeared at all.

There is now a third sample two seconds after resolution, reported as `after`, which is where displacement actually shows up.

## A column ran into the next one

```
VPR Ozrin N'vero   cast (  -0.00,  -0.02) d=   0.02 on topspread    0.00y
```

The compass column was padded to six characters, which is exactly the width of `on top`.

## Worth noting from the same data

Spread at cast time is very tight — 0.43y for the tank, 1.14 for the monk — which is the signal a positional hint needs and was invisible while only resolution positions were recorded.

body:
## Summary

Sonar key `AaA57a9zVV1QfOFj-9qY` — rule **go:S2077** (VULNERABILITY / MAJOR) at
`internal/contracts/comments.go:22`: *"Make sure using a dynamically formatted SQL query is safe here."*

**Verdict: real SQL injection.** `AddComment` assembled the INSERT with `fmt.Sprintf`,
interpolating `contractID`, `author` and `body` into single-quoted SQL literals. All three
come straight from `r.FormValue` in `(*Server).Comments` (`internal/web/comments.go`), which
serves `POST /contracts/comments` — the public *"Comentarios de seguimiento"* form linked from
every contract detail page. Nothing validates, escapes or allowlists that input.

Exploit path: `/contracts/C-1001` → *Comentarios de seguimiento* → comment form → `AddComment` → `db.Exec`.

Typing this into the `Comentario` field breaks out of the value tuple and appends an
attacker-controlled row, so one submission writes **two** comments:

```
hi'), ('C-1001','INJECTED','pwned via SQLi in comment form
```

![exploit: injected row appears](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..m6UUNKtT4FsHe3fgtN8CRfexvJDZVSLFW_nXBdRnRyI)

Full statement control also allows writing to other contracts or pulling values out of
`api_keys` via subselects in the injected tuple.

### Fix

Parameterize the statement so the driver binds the values as data, matching `ListComments`
and `CountByRegion` which already use placeholders:

```diff
-	query := fmt.Sprintf(
-		"INSERT INTO comments (contract_id, author, body) VALUES ('%s', '%s', '%s')",
+	_, err := db.Exec(
+		"INSERT INTO comments (contract_id, author, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
 		contractID, author, body,
 	)
-	_, err := db.Exec(query)
```

### Evidence it is fixed

Same payload, same form, patched build — a single row is created and the payload is stored
verbatim as text; no `INJECTED` row:

![after fix: payload stored as literal text](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..zj-dIXcI1izR_7YqFoKAQ0eg47K-y5rmmlkqUHj2iOc)

Legitimate flow still works — a normal comment saves and the seeded thread renders:

![after fix: normal comment still works](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..BxBGAKGjsJiPBLchFJ-wsohprvAJ1dDg5aDXPqk0A4A)

`go build ./...` and `go test ./...` both pass (`TestAddAndListComments` included).

### Notes

`sonar/remediation` does not yet contain the comments feature (it lives only on
`feature/contract-comments`, PR #1), so this branch is `feature/contract-comments` + the
one-file fix; the diff against the remediation branch therefore also carries that feature commit.

Out of scope, deliberately untouched: `internal/web/comments.go` renders the body via
`template.HTML` (stored XSS) and `avatarColor` uses `math/rand` — separate findings.

author: branarakic
body:
## Summary

This adds a small, controlled way to fetch named Knowledge Assets from another node. It uses the RFC64 exact-asset sync path, so the receiving node does not have to scan or replace the complete Context Graph.

- Add the node-admin route `POST /api/context-graph/fetch-assets`.
- Accept 1-10 exact Knowledge Asset UALs and up to five optional peer IDs.
- Prove that every UAL belongs to the requested local and on-chain Context Graph before network work starts.
- Fetch only assets that are not already present.
- Verify the latest on-chain Merkle root before reporting success.
- Keep the Context Graph reconcile watermark unchanged.
- Recognize an independently confirmed exact VM copy when a mutable workspace head is corrupt.

## Why

The existing graph-wide catch-up route is too expensive when only one asset is missing. In two production checks, the source node timed out while it read the first page of a complete graph. No asset data was fetched. This exact route avoids that full-graph read.

## API

```http
POST /api/context-graph/fetch-assets
```

```json
{
  "contextGraphId": "sports",
  "uals": [
    "did:dkg:base:8453/0x.../1"
  ],
  "peerIds": [
    "12D3KooW..."
  ]
}
```

If `peerIds` is not present, the node selects up to five suitable peers. The response reports each asset as `already-present`, `materialized`, `fetched`, or `unresolved`.

## Safety limits

- A node-admin token is required. Agent tokens are rejected.
- One request can name no more than 10 assets and five peers.
- The node validates the network, Knowledge Asset ID, Context Graph binding, publisher, and latest Merkle root.
- An older peer can return more data, but the requester keeps only the named assets within the RFC64 bounds.
- The route does not start background reconciliation, scan the complete graph, replace the graph, or advance its watermark.

## Validation

- Agent focused tests: 102 passed.
- CLI and API focused tests: 101 passed.
- Agent build and type checks: passed.
- CLI build and package checks: passed.
- The exact RFC64 transport fetched and authenticated one selected production asset during the investigation.

The first endpoint prototype could not classify that asset because the local mutable workspace head was corrupt. This PR includes the exact confirmed-VM fallback and a regression test for that case. A complete post-fix endpoint test on a live node is intentionally left for `testnet-canary`; no custom build remains active on production nodes.

author: testlabauto
body:
Adds e2e coverage for the Packages pane's security advisory (CVE) indicators, for Python and R.

### Summary

The interpreter images are rebuilt monthly from `test/e2e/test-files/requirements.txt` and `test/e2e/test-files/DESCRIPTION`, so a test that asserts "some installed package has an advisory" changes meaning with every rebuild. That approach also does not work today: of the 50 latest-version packages I queried against Package Manager (including every package in `DESCRIPTION`), **none** has an open advisory, and the entire OSV CRAN database is 14 records across 10 packages.

So each test installs a package whose *installed version* is permanently vulnerable:

- **Python** — `bottle==0.12.19`, affected by CVE-2022-31799 and fixed in 0.12.20, so the advisory cannot age out from under the test. Zero dependencies, pure-Python wheel, and nothing in the image depends on it, so installing and removing it perturbs nothing else. Covers the scored/banded rendering (Critical, with a CVSS score on the badge).
- **R** — `widgetframe` at its latest version. Its advisory RSEC-2026-0 has no fixed version, so the current release is affected and no version pin (and no source build) is needed. That matters because R cannot install a historical version through the pane at all — `searchPackageVersions` returns only the current version from configured repos, with a `TODO` for archives. Every CRAN advisory is also unscored, so this covers the "Severity unknown" rendering path.

Badge assertions read the accessible name and match the score loosely (`CVSS \d+\.\d`), so an NVD rescore within the same severity band will not break them.

### Page object changes

`test/e2e/pages/packages.ts` gains badge, row, detail-view and Security-tab helpers, plus two fixes to existing methods that the new tests exercise:

- **`installPackage({ version })` was broken.** No test had used the `version` option. It typed the version, pressed Enter (accepting whichever quick-pick row was active), and then called `selectQuickInputElement(0)`, which waited on a picker that had already closed. It now filters and clicks the exact version row.
- **`searchPackages` now scrolls the list to the top,** working around #15714: filtering a scrolled Positron list renders an empty pane, because `PositronListInstance.setEntries()` does not clamp the grid's vertical scroll offset when the row count shrinks. The helper carries a comment explaining why it exists so it can be deleted when that issue is fixed.

The list bug was found by this work: the advisory data was correct throughout, the matching row was simply never rendered.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:packages-pane @:web

Both new tests pass locally on Electron, as do the six pre-existing packages-pane tests — the latter being the check that matters, since this PR touches two shared page object methods:

```
✓ Python - Flags an installed package with a known CVE (54.0s)
✓ R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory (9.6s)
✓ Python - Install, search, and uninstall package (python) (34.1s)
✓ Python - Install, search, and uninstall package (pythonAlt) (14.2s)
✓ R - Install, search, and uninstall package (8.9s)
✓ R - Opens package help in Help pane (1.6s)
✓ Python - Opens package help in Help pane (2.7s)
✓ Python - Shows external link for a package with a homepage (2.0s)

8 passed (2.9m)
```

The new tests reach a real Package Manager instance (the public one at packagemanager.posit.co unless the environment configures its own), so they need network access — as the installs themselves already do.

seed-top.

3/5 `e627b96a` lc-gfni-plane2 (two independent byte-planes per
`gfni_fold_tile` inner pass): **1,457,147.44**, p10 **0.178568 s**,
**−6,778 (−1.69%)**. That restacked a priced two-plane GFNI tile
(`b8fce96`, −1.92%). Reverted before this edit. Do not restack plane2
/ extra-ZMM GFNI interleaving.

This 4/5 is a **different dest, different function, different phase**.
Not seed. Not seed-top. Not lincheck GFNI. Not open-mul-diet.

## One mechanism

Ranked Ligerito open starts with DirectFold8
(`materialize_direct_fold8`). The f-side of a block is

```
fold16_banked(f_in[64n], m4[4n], fold16_weight)   # 64 → 4, L1 mid
fold4_nested(m4[4n], f_out[n], r4, r5)            # 4 → 1, dest
```

in 256-slot sub-blocks. `m4` is a per-job `LocalBuf` the next
`fold4_nested` **reads immediately**. `f_out` is a slice of the
prove-sized `folded_f` pool buffer. This task never reloads `f_out`.
The next consumer is remaining sumcheck after the rayon join that
finishes every block.

The incumbent published `f_out` with `_mm512_storeu_si512`. Regular
stores write-allocate: each dest line is filled from DRAM before the
store retires. That hidden read is pure waste when the line is not
read again on this core.

This archive publishes those same four F128 lanes with XMM `MOVNTDQ`
(`_mm_stream_si128` of each 16-byte lane extracted from the result
ZMM). Same butterflies. Same twiddles `r4, r5`. Same even/odd
permute body. Same `ghash_mul_x4`. The live set does not grow: the
result ZMM already exists; only the store opcode changes.

`fold16_banked` is untouched. Mid `m4` stays temporal `storeu`. The
ordinary-basis b-side fold4 (dead on the ranked path, which has no
ordinary basis) stays temporal. The GFNI b-side is untouched.

Kill switch `FLOCK_NO_DF8_FOLD4_NT=1` restores `storeu` in the same
binary. Ranked env is cleared, so NT runs.

XMM, not ZMM stream: large pool allocations on this lineage land **16
mod 64**, and a 64-byte gate in front of `_mm512_stream_si512` would
silently never fire — the same trap seed-top `publish_row_nt` and
open-phase `publish_f128_row_nt` already documented. Every F128
element offset preserves the base's 16-byte alignment; the caller
checks that residue once per dest pointer (`nt_ok`). Unaligned dest
falls back to `storeu` (same bytes).

A per-task `_mm_sfence` after the slot loop drains WC buffers on the
producing thread. The rayon join of `par_chunks_mut(block_len)` is
the later sumcheck's happens-before. Distinct blocks write disjoint
`f_out` slices, so no two workers NT-publish the same line.

## Why this dest is not seed-nt / open-nt-reg-pub / fold16-then4

`f54aaf0f` NT-published recursive **RS codeword rows** (~43 MiB of
`seed_layers_pair_from_msg` destinations). That opcode is priced.
This dest is `folded_f` of DirectFold8, an 8 MiB (2^19 F128) open-phase
buffer produced **after** the witness is already committed. Different
allocation, different later reader, different function
(`fold4_nested` vs `butterfly_fused_2layer_row_from`).

`85b0943` open-nt-reg-pub deleted the 32 KiB L1 **stage bounce** of
`fold_and_msg_chunk_nt_x86` by register-publishing four dest lanes.
That bounce is priced (−0.67%). This archive does not touch
`fold_and_msg`. Mid `m4` (the 4 KiB sub-block scratch) stays a
write-before-read temporal buffer, because the very next instruction
in the same task loads it.

fold16-then4 (`073c8d3`, −2.13%) retuned the **live set** of
`fold16_banked`. This archive does not change how many banks, how
many accs, or the 64→4→1 schedule. The 16-bank deferred fold still
writes `m4` with `storeu`. Only the 4→1 publish of `f_out` changes
opcode.

Not fold16 T0 prefetch. Not dual-acc fold16. Not 16-acc. Not four-bcast.
Not DF8 serial-4 / msg-tile / fb-overlap. Not glue-x8. Not open-mul-diet
(no CLMUL split of a broadcast scale; `ghash_mul_x4` is the incumbent
6-CLMUL product). Not TNT 5-CLMUL. Not add_scaled.

## Ranked geometry

Ligerito Fast, m=32, DirectFold8 `initial_k = 6`. Packed witness
length 2^25 F128. Folded f-side length `2^25 / 64 = 2^19` F128 =
**8 MiB**. `SUB = 256` slots × 16 bytes = 4 KiB of dest per inner
iteration. `block_len` is `eq_lo.len()` of the DirectFold8 claim;
the parallel grain is one `eq_hi` block of `block_len` outputs.

Eight mebibytes of write-allocate RFO per prove on a buffer whose
next reader is remaining sumcheck after a join — the same *class* of
waste 1/5 deleted on the recursive RS dest, at a different size and
a different point on the Fiat–Shamir chain. If the 8 MiB stays in
the 105 MiB SPR L3 until that reader, NT trades an L3-resident
temporal write for a later DRAM reload and the row is noise-or-loss.
If other traffic (witness views, remaining glue, Merkle upper
levels) evicts it, NT saved the RFO. 1/5 at +0.10% on 43 MiB said
the class can move the median; this row asks whether the 8 MiB
DirectFold8 dest is in the same class.

`m4` is at most `4 * 256` F128 = 16 KiB, L1-hot by construction. NT
on `m4` would force the immediately following `fold4_nested` loads
to miss. That is why `m4` stays `storeu`.

## Exactness

`fold4_nested_impl<true>` computes the identical ZMM `out` as
`<false>`. Lane order of the four `_mm_stream_si128` extracts is
`extracti32x4_epi32::<0..3>`, which is the memory order of
`_mm512_storeu_si512` of the same vector. The scalar tail (when
`dst.len()` is not a multiple of 4) writes one F128 with
`_mm_set_epi64x(hi, lo)` into `_mm_stream_si128` — F128 memory
layout is little-endian `lo` then `hi`, matching `dst[t] = v`.

`nt_ok` requires 16-byte dest alignment. `take_f128` / `alloc_uninit_vec`
hand back F128 slices; F128 is `repr(C, align(16))`. A sub-slice
`f_out[slot..]` at `slot` multiple of 256 preserves that alignment.
If a dest were 16-mod-8, the arm falls back to `storeu` and the
bytes are still the incumbent's.

`_mm_sfence` after the slot loop does not change values. The later
sumcheck reads `folded_f` only after the `par_chunks_mut` join.
Proof bytes unchanged. The trusted verifier is the authority.

## SPR accounting

`MOVNTDQ` is a 16-byte WC store. Four extracts per 64-byte dest
group is four store uops versus one `VMOVDQU32-zmm`. That is extra
uops in exchange for skipping the RFO of each dest line. The four
extracts are independent. No extra ZMM live: `out` already exists.

Not 16 named fold16 banks. Not 64-ZMM

author: jackjennings
body:
#606

## Summary

`ur review` had no way to see ticket metadata — title, URL, phase, status, scope, approvals, worktrees, PRs, body — without leaving the TUI. The only tabs shown were phase output files (intake, enrichment, spec, etc.).

This adds a `ticket` tab prepended before all phase tabs. It renders the already-loaded `TicketState` as Markdown: title as H1, URL, phase/status, scope entries, approvals with compact timestamps, worktrees, PRs (only when non-empty), and the full body after a horizontal rule. The initial view still opens at the most recent phase tab; the ticket tab is leftmost but not the default. Switching to it hides the editor, consistent with how non-last tabs behave.

The implementation extracts a pure `renderTicketTab(ticket: TicketState): string` function and prepends a ticket `TabContent` (with `headings: []` and `totalSourceLines: 0` to disable the TOC sidebar) to the parallel `allTabs`/`allTabContents` arrays, replacing the `tabs`/`tabContents` references throughout the TUI event loop. No existing tab behavior is affected.

Issue: https://github.com/jackjennings/urras/issues/606

## Changes

- `src/review.ts`: Export `renderTicketTab`; build `allTabs`/`allTabContents` with ticket tab prepended; update all TUI references
- `src/review_test.ts`: 10 unit tests for `renderTicketTab` covering each rendered field and the conditional PRs section

author: asmundg
body:
Provisioning Seriestevne 7 end to end surfaced five bugs, each of which either blocked the run or would have shipped a wrong printout to the meet crew.

## Cloudflare blocked every browser command

OpenTrack sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that Playwright's bundled Chromium never clears, so `admin create` and everything after it hung on the login form. Real Chrome with the automation switches removed passes on the first load, and a persistent profile keeps the clearance cookie and the login between runs. `playwright-stealth` turned out to be part of the problem rather than the fix, so it is gone.

## The athlete upload was raced

Uploading queues a server-side task with no progress banner, so Process was clicked while still disabled. It now waits for the button to go live.

## Hurdle lanes ignored the hurdle setup

The lane draw sorted every track heat by seed time alone. Seriestevne 7's 80m hekk came out with J15 at 76.2 cm in lane 4 next to G14 at 84 cm in lane 5, with no gutter between them — a heat the crew physically cannot rig.

The gutter logic already existed in the hekkeplan, so the scheduler now exports those lanes and `admin seed --track-lanes` applies them.

## Block starters sat next to standing starters

Athletes start from blocks from 13, so a sprint heat merged across that line puts a standing starter right beside the blocks the crew has to reach. The layout guide asked for an empty lane there, but only as something to say out loud during handover.

Lane assignment now works in bands — athletes sharing a hurdle setup and a start type, with one empty lane between adjacent bands. That subsumes the hurdle gutters, so the export covers flat sprints too. Lanes within a band stay interchangeable, so the start list still seeds them by performance.

## Merged heats printed under one category's name

Seriestevne 7 went out as "J12 60 meter" for a heat G13 and G14 also ran in. The name is applied during `admin schedule`, but seeding rebuilds the heats afterwards and nothing re-checked, so the reset shipped silently. `admin seed` now re-asserts the combined names as its final step.

## Seeding also wipes the implement weights

Same mechanism, worse symptom: the weights live in a browser-only editor with no API field, so the failure surfaces as an empty Vekt column — one discus sheet covering six categories at four different weights, none of them printed. Nothing can read them back to verify, so `seed` names the throwing events it just cleared and gives the command to restore them. The README now pins the order: `schedule → update-pbs → seed → set-implements → reports`.

## Verification

All of it was driven against the live Seriestevne 7 competition and checked back over the API and in the generated PDFs: 37 events timed, 5 heats merged and correctly named, both gutters in place, and every implement weight printing on the field cards.

127 tests pass. The new ones cover the lane bands, including one that asserts the old unsafe draw is what you get *without* a plan, so the regression cannot sneak back.
