body:
This pull request introduces the 1.2.0 release of the BP Mobile application, with the most significant change being the enablement and shipping of Google Sign-In for Android. It also improves notification handling, especially for cold-start scenarios, and makes several technical refinements to notification and authentication flows. Below are the most important grouped changes:

**Authentication & Google Sign-In:**

* Google Sign-In is now enabled (`GOOGLE_SIGN_IN_ENABLED: true`) and fully shipped in version 1.2.0, with updated documentation on remaining product rough edges and guidance for production setup. This includes a new Android OAuth client in `google-services.json` and extensive comments about environment-specific configuration pitfalls. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f3a7bd7132502aa24c4f40dc86fde941d7b1c32d55f5bb10cad0e1926b066b56L6-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f3a7bd7132502aa24c4f40dc86fde941d7b1c32d55f5bb10cad0e1926b066b56L53-R66) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f19352468fe502c6f776215d3d13169322da5b9687ebdd80065f254585ec9d96R24-R31) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b9feb9d14d9d14f201b8bd42de44c14df004a9134d9b74737ccad3e2a9917689L5-R5) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-1846122c2c83a486a3693f7966aa522c34cf489f674185c4da0d9221683fd81fL4-R4)

**Notification Handling:**

* Notification bootstrap logic is refactored to ensure that notification taps which cold-start the app (i.e., when the app is launched via a notification) are properly routed only after the navigator is ready, preventing lost or misrouted navigation events. The new `consumeInitialNotificationResponse` function handles this scenario. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aeb2b8a074db0d2682d1e47b4246109b8655db6e40fe7f5edbf0d5388488850cR25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aeb2b8a074db0d2682d1e47b4246109b8655db6e40fe7f5edbf0d5388488850cL101-R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-aeb2b8a074db0d2682d1e47b4246109b8655db6e40fe7f5edbf0d5388488850cR111-R121) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-aeb2b8a074db0d2682d1e47b4246109b8655db6e40fe7f5edbf0d5388488850cL240-R252) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b78ca0bf1a046bbe541942e043f1f217fd8eb9de927f2127a4d6a1efa160a2edR11) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-630f64cffd5159364e49fa7a917f2ba87eebaf3a4002be6598139d21a27d54e6L25-R28) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-630f64cffd5159364e49fa7a917f2ba87eebaf3a4002be6598139d21a27d54e6L42-R83) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-630f64cffd5159364e49fa7a917f2ba87eebaf3a4002be6598139d21a27d54e6R97-R130) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-630f64cffd5159364e49fa7a917f2ba87eebaf3a4002be6598139d21a27d54e6R172-R253)

* The notification module now installs the foreground notification handler at import time, closing a window where notifications could be silently swallowed on iOS if the handler was registered too late. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-630f64cffd5159364e49fa7a917f2ba87eebaf3a4002be6598139d21a27d54e6L42-R83) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-630f64cffd5159364e49fa7a917f2ba87eebaf3a4002be6598139d21a27d54e6R97-R130)

**Push Token Management & Testing:**

* Comments and logic around push token revocation and reclamation are clarified, particularly for Android and scenarios where notification permission is denied. This ensures that orphaned push tokens are reclaimed on the next registration.

* Notification and push token test helpers are improved to better simulate device token rotation and subscription removal, making tests more robust and accurate. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e40bc41fce9886f11d98e9a69d3dc0405850f4d84031ddb792556341bb2d44b4L33-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e40bc41fce9886f11d98e9a69d3dc0405850f4d84031ddb792556341bb2d44b4R60-R79)

These changes collectively improve authentication, notification reliability, and developer experience for both end users and maintainers.

body:
## Motivation

This pull request gets the site ready for deployment on Kubernetes.

### CI image publishing

- Add a new `build-image` job that runs on pushes to `main`.
- The job builds the Docker image and pushes it to `opengreencard/redactpdf` tagged with the commit SHA.
- CI still runs a local Docker build on every PR to verify the Dockerfile; that may be redundant once `build-image` is trusted.

### Secrets aligned to this app

- Kubernetes and 1Password secrets now match what RedactPDF actually needs today.
- Add `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` for the AI model we plan to use.
- Drop SMTP and `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` for now — we are not using email yet, and auth uses `AUTH_SECRET`.

### Split environment variables

- Non-secret config (database host, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, bucket prefix, and so on) lives in committed `.env.*.nonsecret` files.
- Secret values stay in gitignored `.env.*` files; copy from `.env.*.example` when setting up locally.
- The Docker image includes only `.env.production.nonsecret`; Kubernetes injects secrets via `redaction-env`.

### Next steps

- Merge this and exercise the Kubernetes deploy scripts against the new image.
- Optionally trigger `build-image` on this branch to confirm the Docker Hub push works.

## Changes

- Add a `build-image` CI job on `main` pushes that publishes `opengreencard/redactpdf:<sha>` to Docker Hub (uses the `docker-hub` environment).
- Split env config into committed `.env.*.nonsecret` files and gitignored secret siblings; load non-secret values first in `lib/config/index.ts` and `next.config.mjs` so `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are available at build time without local secrets.
- Add `.dockerignore` so the image stays lean and only bundles `.env.production.nonsecret` among env files.
- Retarget Kubernetes to this app: default cluster name `redaction-production`, image `opengreencard/redactpdf`, and secret template fields for `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` instead of SMTP.
- Update 1Password scripts (`generate-secrets.sh`, `fill-secrets-template.sh`, `run-in-env.sh`) and add committed `op-secrets.*.env` pointer files for the redaction 1Password items.
- Set `APP_MODE=production` in the Dockerfile so production builds pick up the right non-secret env file.

## Testing

- Automated checks
  - `yarn eslint --fix` on changed TypeScript files (if applicable)
  - CI runs Jest, ESLint, and a local Docker build on every PR
- Manual verification
  - Copy `.env.development.example` to `.env.development`, fill in secrets, and confirm `yarn dev` loads config from `.env.development.nonsecret` plus local secrets
  - After merge to `main`, confirm the `build-image` job pushes `opengreencard/redactpdf:<sha>` to Docker Hub
  - Run cluster setup against a test cluster: `bash k8s/setup-cluster.sh --revision $(git rev-parse HEAD) --cluster-name redaction-testing --region nyc1`

author: arisros
body:
Three related fixes to the window-manager / status-bar setup, driven by running a third monitor.

**1. sketchybar and borders move to launchd.** `after-startup-command` only fires when aerospace itself starts, so a crash left the bar gone until the next login. Two `KeepAlive` LaunchAgents own the processes now. `exec-on-workspace-change` also calls `/opt/homebrew/bin/sketchybar` by absolute path — aerospace runs it through `/bin/bash` without a login shell, so homebrew's bin is not on `PATH` there.

**2. Monitors are mapped by name, not by index swap.** `is_need_swap_monitor()` assumed the aerospace monitor id and the sketchybar display number only ever differ by a 1↔2 swap, which breaks the moment a third screen is attached. `get_display_for_monitor()` looks the name up in `aerospace list-monitors --json` (Mi 27 → 1, built-in → 2, anything else → 3) with a single-monitor short circuit, so items are never parked on a display that does not exist. This also fixes three `continue` statements sitting outside any loop in `helper_sketchybar.sh` (bash treats them as errors and keeps going) and creates `/tmp/sketchybar` up front for the debug log.

**3. Workspace groups grow to five.** New `5`/`t`/`g` workspaces plus their `move-node-to-workspace` bindings; `workspace-to-monitor-force-assignment` takes a fallback list so a workspace still lands somewhere sane when its preferred monitor is unplugged. Gather's picture-in-picture bubble spawns whenever the main window is hidden, so both Gather windows are pinned to workspace 5 (PiP rule first — first match wins), and `automatically-unhide-macos-hidden-apps` goes back to `false` so cmd-h sticks.

**Notes**
- `sketchybar/aerospaces.sh` no longer sources `sketch_aero.sh`, but `helper_sketchybar.sh:93` still invokes it as a script. The file stays.
- The two plists stow to `~/.config/{sketchybar,borders}`, **not** `~/Library/LaunchAgents`. `install.sh` has no `launchctl bootstrap` wiring yet — follow-up.

author: vezril
body:
A null `ingressClassName` is **not** the same as no `ingressClassName`.

The template emitted the key unconditionally, so an empty value rendered:

```yaml
  ingressClassName:
```

and k3s's bundled Traefik v2.4 **silently ignores an Ingress whose class it cannot
resolve**. The host 404s while the Ingress object looks entirely healthy.

## The default was actively harmful, not just unnecessary

The target cluster has **no `IngressClass` resource at all**, so `className: traefik`
broke routing. Verified there with an otherwise identical Ingress:

| className | Result via Traefik |
|---|---|
| `traefik` | **404** |
| unset | **200**, serving the console |

`dionysus-planner`, the only other Ingress on that cluster, likewise sets none.
Set `className` explicitly on a cluster that actually registers one.

## Why it shipped

**CI had no chart job** — nothing in this repo had ever rendered the chart. There is
one now: it lints, and asserts the class is omitted when empty, preserved when
explicitly set, and that `ingress.enabled=false` emits no Ingress at all.

Found while exposing the console over the tailnet at `hermes.tailscale`. Worth
noting the failure mode that cost the most time wasn't the chart: port 80 on that
node is an unrelated nginx that answers `200` to any Host header, so an ingress
Traefik had never seen appeared to work. Traefik is on the NodePort.

## Summary

This PR completes the first two phases of the CinePrint server/API refactor.

### Phase 1 — Server foundation

Adds shared infrastructure for future feature migrations:

- Typed `AppError` codes and HTTP semantics
- Safe client-facing error envelopes
- Server-side diagnostic serialization
- Request IDs and request context utilities
- Structured JSON logging
- Recursive sensitive-data redaction

### Phase 2 — Account migration

Migrates Account export and deletion onto the new foundation:

- Removes client-declared `uid` from Account requests
- Uses `authMiddleware` and verified `context.uid`
- Adds safe `{ ok, data }` / `{ ok, error }` response envelopes
- Moves Account business logic into testable core functions
- Adds structured operation logging
- Updates Profile call sites
- Adds regression coverage for user isolation and deletion behavior

## Security

- Client identity is no longer trusted by Account handlers
- Tokens and credential material are never logged
- Unknown internal errors do not leak Firestore/Firebase internals

author: valovinnikov
body:
## Summary

`deploy-development.yml`'s `migrate-db` job has a guard step meant to refuse migrating if `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` resolves to the production Neon branch's host, comparing it against the repo Variable `PRODUCTION_DB_HOST`. That Variable is currently set to a full `postgresql://...` connection string instead of a bare hostname, so the comparison never matches — the guard has been permanently fail-open with no warning. The guard step was also silently skipped whenever `PRODUCTION_DB_HOST` was unset.

## Changes

- The guard step now runs whenever a real migration will happen (`DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED != ''`), no longer additionally gated on `PRODUCTION_DB_HOST != ''`.
- Fails the job outright, with a clear `::error::`, if `PRODUCTION_DB_HOST` is unset.
- Fails the job outright if the value doesn't look like a bare hostname (rejects anything with `@`, `:`, `/`, a scheme, etc.).
- The pre-existing hostname-match check is unchanged.
- Updated `docs/DEPLOY.md`, `docs/context/ci-automation.md`, and `.claude/agents/db.md` to describe the new fail-loud (not silently-inert) behavior and the required bare-hostname format, and removed stale wording that described the guard as conditional on the Variable being set.

## Out of scope (human-gated)

Per this repo's rules on secrets/credentials, the following are **not** part of this PR and need separate console action:
- Fixing `PRODUCTION_DB_HOST`'s actual value to a bare hostname.
- Rotating the credential that was stored in the Variable (it currently holds a full connection string with credentials).
- A live dispatch verifying the guard actually fires end-to-end.

## Testing

- Verified the new guard logic locally against all four cases (unset → fails, malformed/full-connection-string → fails, matching host → fails, legitimate mismatch → passes) by extracting and replaying the shell script.
- `actionlint` clean on the modified workflow file.
- `pnpm type-check` and `pnpm lint` green across all workspaces (docs/workflow-only change, no package source touched).
- Reviewed by the `reviewer` subagent across three passes — final verdict APPROVE.

Refs #2089

author: lologh
body:
Les neuf points de l'addendum v3.2, développés sur `feature/v3.2-workflow` à partir de la branche par défaut **après** la fusion de `feature/ui-navigation` (PR #2) et `feature/brand-logo` (PR #3) — les deux fusions ont été vérifiées avant de démarrer.

## Ce que fait cette PR

### 1. Visiteurs rattachés à un patient
`visitors.patient_id`. Le champ est **obligatoire dès qu'un service clinique est choisi** — la règle est appliquée dans `RegisterVisitor`, pas seulement dans le formulaire — et reste facultatif pour un service non clinique (une démarche administrative n'a pas de patient à visiter). Le nom du patient visité apparaît sur `/board` et dans les passages du jour.

### 2. Planning sur plusieurs jours
Action dédiée `BulkCreateSchedule` : une plage de dates, les jours de la semaine cochés, une ligne `schedules` par date correspondante. Relancer une génération ne duplique rien. Le formulaire jour par jour reste en place pour les ajustements ponctuels.

### 3. Pièces jointes et ordonnances dans le dossier
- **Lecture et écriture** : dépôt direct depuis « Mes patients » (`/service`) et depuis la vue globale des patients (`/admin`), sans passer par un renvoi. `attachments.patient_id` reste le point d'ancrage.
- **Impression** : action « Imprimer » sur chaque pièce jointe et chaque ordonnance, rendu autonome déclenchant `window.print()`.
- **Chronologie unifiée** : le nouveau service `App\Services\PatientTimeline` construit **une seule frise triée par date** — consultations, renvois, ordonnances, conclusions, paiements et pièces jointes mélangés, découpés par passage — partagée par les deux interfaces. L'affichage précédent laissait les pièces jointes déposées depuis le dossier hors de la frise ; c'est corrigé sans toucher au schéma, comme demandé.

### 4. « Mes rendez-vous » sous « Mes patients »
Section listant les rendez-vous à venir du médecin connecté, et création d'un rendez-vous pour **tout patient de la liste** — la contrainte « seulement en fin de consultation immédiate » est levée.

### 5. Conclusion de consultation
Nouveau type d'entrée `patient_history` (`consultation_conclusion`), distinct de l'ordonnance qui reste dédiée aux médicaments.

### 6. La caisse devient un rôle et une interface
Rôle `cashier`, table `cashiers`, interface `/caisse` cloisonnée comme les trois autres et portant **les deux files**. Les deux caisses sont des services à part entière (`services.kind = caisse`) : même file, même token, même « Appeler le suivant ».

Routage sous condition de paiement via `visits.pending_next_service_id` :
- à l'enregistrement, la visite pointe d'abord sur **Caisse Ticket**, la destination clinique attendant dans `pending_next_service_id` ;
- sur un renvoi vers un plateau technique, vers **Caisse Services** — la ligne `referrals` gardant la destination **médicale réelle** ;
- `ConfirmCaissePayment` encaisse, écrit `patient_history` (`payment_confirmed`), bascule `visits.service_id` et **régénère un ticket dans la file cible**.

Les médecins n'ont plus aucune fonction de caisse. Une installation sans service `kind = caisse` continue de fonctionner : le patient va alors directement au service choisi.

### 7. Portail patient
`/mes-documents/{portal_token}` — lien **permanent**, protégé par un code à quatre chiffres généré à la création du dossier et remis à l'accueil (imprimé sur le ticket). Deux couches de sécurité plutôt qu'une : UUID non devinable, plus **verrouillage temporaire de 15 minutes après 5 échecs** (`portal_access_attempts`) et `throttle:10,1`. La page n'affiche **rien**, pas même le nom du patient, avant validation ; l'accès accordé vit en session côté serveur et non dans une propriété Livewire. Le SMS part sur demande explicite depuis `/reception` ou `/service` ; le code ne voyage jamais par SMS.

### 8. Suppression d'un dossier par l'admin
Cascade réelle, `patient_code` retapé à l'identique et motif obligatoire, réservée à `admin`. **Jamais journalisée dans `patient_history`** (elle disparaîtrait avec le reste) : consignée exclusivement dans le journal d'audit, qui ne référence pas le patient par clé étrangère et lui survit. Un visiteur est **détaché**, pas supprimé.

Audit étendu bien au-delà des connexions : le trait `RecordsActivity` équipe les quinze modèles concernés, et les actions non-CRUD portent un log explicite en français (« Appeler le suivant », « Confirmer le paiement et orienter », « Supprimer un dossier »…) plutôt qu'un diff d'attributs. `access_code` et `portal_token` sont exclus des logs. La vue reste filtrable et paginée.

### 9. Impression du ticket
Vue autonome, `window.print()` côté navigateur, largeurs en `ch` pour rester lisible d'une thermique 58 mm à une A4. Ticket patient : hôpital, `patient_code`, token, service, date/heure, code personnel. Ticket visiteur : hôpital, token, **patient visité**, service, date/heure. Réimpression depuis les passages du jour.

## Défauts corrigés en cours de route

- **`BulkCreateSchedule` : la détection de doublon ne fonctionnait jamais.** Les heures étaient comparées sous deux formats (`08:00` inséré, `08:00:00` attendu) — relancer une génération aurait dupliqué tout le planning. Normalisation en `HH:MM:SS` à l'écriture comme à la comparaison.
- **La caisse était proposée comme destination.** Dans la liste des services de l'accueil, dans celle des renvois et comme service d'affectation d'un médecin — ce dernier cas donnant à un médecin l'accès à la file de la caisse depuis `/service`, contre la règle « les médecins n'encaissent jamais ». Exclue par `Service::careServices()` et refusée côté serveur (`SendReferral`, validation de `DoctorManager`).
- **Le `down()` du type de service échouait sur MariaDB** tant qu'une ligne valait `caisse` (`Data truncated for column 'kind'`). Il nettoie désormais les caisses et leurs files avant de rétrécir la colonne.

## Vérifications

- **182 tests, 636 assertions au vert**, sur SQLite en mémoire **et** contre MariaDB 10.11.
- Les **32 migrations passent dans les deux sens** sur les deux moteurs, seeders compris.
- `pint --test` passe ; aucun marqueur de conflit.
- **Parcours vérifié en navigateur réel** (Chromium) de bout en bout : enregistrement à l'accueil vers Médecine Générale → attente en Caisse Ticket avec « Puis : Medecine Generale » → encaissement et orientation → **le patient apparaît dans la file du médecin** ; plus le ticket imprimable et le portail patient (page muette avant le code, message après un code erroné, documents après le bon code). Aucune erreur JavaScript.

Tests dédiés ajoutés : `CaisseFlowTest`, `PatientPortalTest`, `PatientDeletionTest`, `DossierWorkflowV32Test`, `PrintTicketTest`. `CashPrescriptionAppointmentTest` a été mis à jour plutôt que laissé casser : il vérifie désormais que les anciennes portes de caisse côté médecin et côté accueil sont bien condamnées. Le seeder crée un compte `caisse@keneya.local` (rôle `cashier`).

README à jour : nouvelle section sur le portail, l'impression et la suppression, section caisse réécrite, modèle de données et tableau des rôles complétés.

body:
`CardData.damage`/`.block` waren zwei feste Felder — damit konnte eine Karte
genau zwei Dinge, und jedes dritte hätte ein drittes Feld gebraucht, das bei
fast jeder Karte 0 gewesen wäre. Ersetzt durch `effects: Array[CardEffect]`
mit den Kinds `SCHADEN, BLOCK, HEILEN, ZIEHEN, ENERGIE, SELBSTSCHADEN`.

Ausgeführt wird in `game.gd._apply_effect()`, nicht in der Resource: eine
Wirkung braucht beide Kämpfer, den Ziehstapel, die Energie und die Hand.
Die `.tres` sagt *was*, der Code sagt *wie*.

Dazu `Category {AKTION, REAKTION}` → `Type {ANGRIFF, VERTEIDIGUNG, FERTIGKEIT}`
— das alte Feld stammte aus dem reaktiven Stack-Modell und beschrieb eine
Regel, die dieses Spiel nicht hat.

Fünf neue Karten: Wuchtstoß, Durchatmen, Aderlass, Zweite Luft, Adrenalin.
Deck jetzt 13 Karten.

Zweiter Commit (`38c8d85`): nachgezogene Karten waren nicht zu erkennen, weil
beim Ziehen die ganze Hand gleichzeitig in Bewegung war. `_apply_layout()`
weiß jetzt, welche Karten neu sind — die fliegen länger, starten erst nachdem
die vorhandenen Platz gemacht haben, und es gibt einen Ziehton pro Karte.

Von bfn lokal getestet: alle Effekte funktionieren, Ziehen ist jetzt lesbar.

**Offene Balance-Schuld** (bewusst, nicht in diesem PR): Durchatmen (0E),
Aderlass (0E) und Adrenalin (+2E) spielt man immer — kostenlose Karten sind
keine Entscheidung. Alle Zahlen sind geraten, nicht gerechnet.

author: silverstein
body:
## What three days of production data showed

The watchdog from #1445 has been running every five minutes since Tuesday. It has been healthy the whole time, and it surfaced a flaw in itself.

| | baseline backends | sampled | unverified |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tue 2026-08-18 | 5 | 7 | 1 |
| Fri 2026-08-21 | 14 | 16 | 2 |

The pool nearly tripled. The probe is capped at 16 concurrent connections, so it is now **pinned at its ceiling**, and two things follow that the log line could not show:

**`verified_clean` has become unreachable.** It requires every live backend to have been sampled, which cannot happen once the pool exceeds the cap. A status that can no longer fire is not a status.

**`clean_partial_coverage` reads identically at 90 percent coverage and at 20 percent.** The probe could go progressively blind while its output never changed. That is exactly the failure this module was built to catch, turned inward on itself.

## The fix, and why not simply raise the cap

Raising the cap would make the watchdog's own connections into the pool pressure it exists to watch for, against a server `max_connections` of 90. Instead this **reports the blindness**:

- `coverage.ratio` is the share of live backends a run actually inspected, logged every run
- below half, a clean result is not worth much, so it reports `coverage_degraded` and alerts as a warning rather than hiding inside a status that sounds fine
- poison still outranks coverage: a run that finds a poisoned backend reports `poisoned` however blind it was, because that finding is actionable regardless

The cap staying at 16 is now a documented tradeoff at the constant rather than an unexamined default.

## Verification

- 24 tests, including cases built from the real production numbers (14 backends → `clean_partial_coverage` at 0.86; 40 backends → `coverage_degraded` at 0.40)
- Full app typecheck clean, after regenerating the Prisma client: the schema moved in the 266 commits since #1445 and my worktree's generated client was stale, which presented as 37 errors that were not mine
- Biome clean; pushed through the full gate unbypassed

## One thing worth flagging

While committing I caught `.beads/issues.jsonl` swept into the change: 8,008 lines of the shared issue database, left staged in the index from earlier work in this worktree. A working-tree checkout does not unstage, so explicit-path staging alone did not save me. Removed before pushing and verified byte-identical to master. Worth knowing that this file can ride along invisibly and clobber other agents' issue state.

author: wilbertjoosen
body:
## Summary
Root-causes and fixes the Pyroscope SIGSEGV crash from earlier today (agent currently disabled via the pyroscope-agent Secret): `io.pyroscope:agent:2.1.2`'s default `profilerType` (`ASYNC`) delegates to a bundled async-profiler native library that segfaults on this cluster's JDK 26 + linux/arm64 combination. Setting `PYROSCOPE_PROFILER_TYPE=JFR` switches it to the JDK's own built-in Flight Recorder instead — pure JVM, no native library, lower sampling resolution than async-profiler but that trade-off is what unblocks profiling here at all.

Verified locally: `docker run` with `PYROSCOPE_AGENT_ENABLED=true PYROSCOPE_PROFILER_TYPE=JFR` on the eureka-server image — started cleanly in 4.3s, logged "Profiling started", no crash (only an expected "failed to upload" since the local test pointed at a placeholder address with no real Pyroscope server).

## Rollout plan (separate from this PR)
This PR is config-only and doesn't itself re-enable the agent — `PYROSCOPE_AGENT_ENABLED` stays `false` in the Secret. After this merges and syncs:
1. Flip the Secret to `true` for one canary service in demo-qa, verify it starts clean and profiles show up in Pyroscope.
2. Roll the rest out one service at a time (not all at once — see this session's earlier CPU-exhaustion incident from a prior mass rollout).
3. Once demo-qa is validated, repeat on main/demo and develop for 3-branch consistency.

[herdr](https://herdr.dev) keeps several coding agents in one terminal.

- `herdr/config.toml` mirrors the keymap in `tmux/tmux.conf` so the existing muscle memory carries over: `ctrl+b` prefix, `prefix+-` / `prefix+v` for splits (herdr's defaults are the other way round), `prefix+hjkl` to resize, `prefix+space` for the next tab. author: feldgendler
body:
The macOS jobs have been failing since 13 August. In the `-target arm64-apple-macosx10.15` job, `libmpv.2.dylib` and `mpv` both fail to link with `ld: fatal warning(s) induced error (-fatal_warnings)`, and the matrix's fail-fast then cancels the other macOS jobs, so the whole build workflow is red on master.

Two things combine. Homebrew's libraries are built for the macOS version of the runner, so everything under `/opt/homebrew` currently has `minos 26.0`, and building with `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=10.15` (clang clamps it to 11.0 on arm64) makes ld warn once for every library it links against. That part is not new: the last green run printed 82 of those warnings and passed. What changed is meson 1.12, released three days before the first failure, which put the linker under werror:

    def get_base_link_args(target, linker, env):
        args = []
        if env.coredata.get_option_for_target(target, 'werror'):
            args.extend(linker.get_linker_fatal_warnings())

On Apple that is `-Wl,-fatal_warnings`, so the warnings that were always there became errors. In 1.11.2 the linker only got werror under b_lto.

ld offers no way to demote just this warning: `-w` hides the text but the warnings still count as fatal, and `-no_fatal_warnings` and `-no_warn_platform_mismatch` are not options in ld-1267. So this takes werror off the linker and passes `-Werror` to the compilers by hand, which is what meson did before 1.12. Only the job that sets a deployment target is affected; the other four macOS jobs keep `--werror` as it is.

Checked on macOS 26.6 with Xcode 26.6, meson 1.12.0 and current Homebrew, which is what the runner has: with the deployment target exported the build fails the same way CI does, and with this change it compiles, links and runs, with the binary still at minos 11.0 and the mismatch warnings printed but harmless. Feature detection is unaffected — the configure summary is identical apart from the option lines.

Dropping `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` from the matrix entry links cleanly as well, since the Swift target is a separate flag, but it stops building the C and ObjC code for the old target, which seemed the wrong half to give up.

Written with AI assistance, and reviewed with AI tooling. I take full responsibility for the code: I understand what it changes and why, I have tested it myself, I will respond to review in my own words, and it can be submitted under the same license as the files it touches.

author: lukeevanstech
body:
## Why

`gh api ... --paginate --jq '...'` runs the `--jq` filter once **per page**, not once over the combined result set — this is documented in the `gh api` manual ("Each page is a separate JSON array or object. Pass `--slurp` to wrap all pages ... into an outer JSON array."). Three places in `renovate-review.yml` use `--paginate` with a `| last` selector to find the latest usage comment or the latest Claude review, without `--slurp`. Once a long-lived Renovate PR accumulates enough reviews or comments to span more than one page (default page size 30), `last` only ever returns the last matching item on *whichever page happened to be processed*, not the true latest across the whole PR.

The more serious consequence is in the DISMISSED-review verdict resolver: a stale page-local verdict could be returned instead of the actual latest one, so the status check could land on the wrong side of a changes-requested PR (or the fingerprint-skip cache could key off a stale comment).

Original finding: https://github.com/LukeEvansTech/shared-workflows/pull/37#discussion_r3826117922

## What

Added `--slurp` to all three `gh api ... --paginate` calls (the usage-comment fetch, and the two near-identical review-verdict resolvers), and flattened the resulting array-of-pages with `add[]` before the existing `select(...) | last` logic, so `last` is applied to the true combined result set regardless of how many pages it spans. No other logic changed.

## Verification

- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/renovate-review.yml'))"` — YAML parses cleanly.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/renovate-review.yml` — exit 0, no findings.
- Simulated a two-page `gh api --paginate --slurp` response locally with `jq` for both the comments filter and the reviews filter (including the DISMISSED-recovery branch): confirmed the old per-page filter returned two page-local `last` values (the bug), while the new `add[]`-flattened filter returns the single correct global-last item.
- Lint: super-linter v8.6.0 local, scoped to changed files — 10 linters ran, 0 introduced (the 3 that failed — BIOME_FORMAT, CHECKOV, JSCPD — are CI-disabled in this repo's shared workflow and pre-existing/unrelated to this change; YAML, GITHUB_ACTIONS, and GITHUB_ACTIONS_ZIZMOR all passed with 0 errors).

## Human steps

None required for the git-side fix. As a CI-workflow change to a reusable consumed by several repos, this PR is intentionally left for manual review/merge rather than auto-merge.

author: staalmannen
body:
libap: readlinkat returns ssize_t

Two unrelated failures in diffutils' diff.c.

  diff.c:1265 argument prototype mismatch
    "IND FUNC(INT, IND CONST CHAR, IND CHAR, UVLONG) INT" for
    "IND FUNC(INT, IND CONST CHAR, IND CHAR, UVLONG) VLONG"

POSIX.1-2008 gives readlinkat an ssize_t return, as readlink already has in <sys/stat.h>. APE declared and defined it int, which gnulib caught because careadlinkat takes the reader as a parameter and typechecks it. It was also an ABI bug of the same family as the size_t one: on amd64 the callee wrote four bytes where an ssize_t caller reads eight. readlinkat is the only *at function POSIX gives a non-int return, and the only one in at_functions.c that was wrong.

  diff.c:1412 structure element not found desc

This is a compiler bug, in designator lists that leave a nested aggregate and come back:

  struct comparison cmp = { .file[0].desc = ..., .file[1].desc = ...,
                            .file[0].stat.st_size = ..., .parent = ... };

The grammar builds these chains correctly and init1 descends to the leftmost designator and trims as it matches, so entering file[0].desc works. Coming back out did not. Having initialised file[0], init1 was still inside struct file_data when it peeked at .file[1].desc, found no member named file, and reported the outermost name in the chain -- desc.

A designator that names nothing here is an error only at a level with its own braces. exflag distinguishes them: it is 0 for the outermost aggregate and for every level reached through doinit, which is the brace case, and 1 when init1 was entered implicitly. So when exflag is set, return instead of diagnosing and let the enclosing level match it. A designator that matches nothing anywhere still reaches the outermost level, where exflag is 0, and is reported there as before.

The array case has to cooperate, or it hands the same designator to the element type again. init1 consuming nothing is the signal; peekinit has no side effects, so comparing it across the call is enough. Guarded on the pending node being a designator, so ordinary element initialisers, brace-nested ones and the a == Z case are untouched.

author: andrew01234567890
body:
Fixes **PGS-342** / **PGS-475** (rated CRITICAL by the Vitess comparison, HIGH by the TiDB one — found independently by both).

## The defect

`pgCutover.Fence` writes a lock row per database when a reshard or upgrade cutover fences:

```go
INSERT INTO pgshard.workflow_locks (kind, key, workflow_id)
SELECT 'ddl', name, $1::uuid FROM pgshard.databases ON CONFLICT (kind, key) DO NOTHING
```

**Nothing in the codebase ever read those rows.** `grep workflow_locks` finds only writers and deleters — the DDL applier never consulted them. So a `CREATE INDEX` or `ALTER TABLE` could be applied in the middle of a reshard copy, landing on one side of the cutover and not the other, which is exactly what the lock exists to prevent.

The placement workflow does check *its own* table lock (`placement.go:439`), which makes the omission easy to miss: the mechanism looks used.

## Fix

`MigrationStore` gains `LockedDatabases`, and `RunOnce` holds a **queued** migration whose database a workflow has locked, logging the holder.

A migration that is already part-applied is still driven to a final state. Stopping half-way across shards leaves the cluster in a worse position than finishing, and the lock is about not *starting* schema change under a copy.

The hold is released the moment the cutover deletes its locks — no new release path, and nothing to leak if a workflow dies, because the existing cleanup already removes them.

## Verification

`TestApplierHoldsAMigrationWhileACutoverHoldsTheDDLLock`: with a lock on `app`, a queued migration there stays queued while one on `other` proceeds; clearing the lock lets it run.

Full `go test ./internal/controller/` green; `golangci-lint` 0 issues.

## Related

**PGS-341** — DDL targeting the retired shard set after a cutover — is the other half and is still open. These locks were the mechanism meant to prevent it, so that ticket needs its own fix on top of this one.

For backfill, the inventory, the partition manifests, the pickled forks will now live in a bucket of their own, created by this stack (or passed as pre-exiting bucket) `BACKFILL_BUCKET_NAM`E and `BACKFILL_BUCKET` mirror the Icechunk configuration sytle,  the bucket is created only when `BACKFILL_ENABLED`, so a forward-only deployment doesn't create an unnecessary bucket.

The inventory is a caller-supplied URI, so nothing enforces where it lives, but the partition Lambda reads it with a client in the stack's region and fails the same way on a remote bucket. The BackfillBucketName output and the README both point at the new bucket as its home.

author: samiuelson
body:
### Description

Fixes WOOMOB-3902

When the store rejects a refund preview or create because the order changed, the refund screen offers to reload the remaining items and tries to keep what the cashier had selected. It restored that selection by matching `WooPosRefundableItem.uniqueId`, which is `"${orderItemId}_$rowIndex"`. `rowIndex` is the unit's position within what is still refundable, so it is renumbered on every reload — and the reload only ever happens because a line got shorter.

Item 42 with quantity 3 gives `42_0`, `42_1`, `42_2`. The cashier keeps only `42_2`. Another register refunds one unit. The reload yields `42_0` and `42_1`, nothing matches, and the selection is emptied. The cashier has to pick again with no explanation.

This replaces the id set with `WooPosRefundSelectionSnapshot`: a unit count per `orderItemId` plus the selected lump-sum ids. `WooPosBuildRefundContent` now selects the first *n* units of each line, capped at what is left, and selects a fee row if its id was selected. Products and fees are kept in separate fields so a fee line id cannot be read as a line item id.

Restoring by count rather than giving units a stable identity is deliberate: nothing downstream needs per-unit identity. `WooPosBuildRefundLineItems` and `WooPosGroupRefundItems` both collapse the selection to a quantity per `orderItemId` before it reaches the store, so the count is the only meaningful state.

Two notes for review:

- WOOMOB-3902 describes the no-survivor fallback as "select everything". That is no longer the code — it was changed to leave the selection empty in #16440. The live symptom is therefore a lost selection, not a widened one, and this PR keeps the empty fallback.
- Of the three new `WooPosRefundViewModelTest` cases, only the trailing-unit one fails on `trunk`. Android numbers `rowIndex` per line item, so a shrinking line never shifted the ids of other lines; the two cross-line cases are regression guards. iOS uses a global running index and has both failure modes — that is WOOMOB-3901.

### Test Steps

Needs two registers signed in to the same store.

1. On register A, open an order with a line item of quantity 3. Start a refund.
2. Deselect all but the last unit of that line. One unit is selected.
3. On register B, refund one unit of the same line item.
4. Back on register A, confirm the refund. The store rejects it and the screen offers "Review remaining items".
5. Tap it. Two units are now listed, and exactly one is selected — not two, and not zero.
6. Repeat with a fee on the order selected as well, and check the fee is still selected after the reload.

### Images/gif

N/A

- [x] I have considered if this change warrants release notes and have added them to `RELEASE-NOTES.txt` if necessary. Use the "[Internal]" label for non-user-facing changes.

author: dominiquebrom28
body:
---
title: "The Guard That Caught It Wasn't Looking For Duplicates"
slug: "the-guard-that-caught-it-wasnt-looking-for-duplicates"
date: "2026-08-25"
summary: "No project shipped code today. The one thing that happened was this blog publishing a duplicate post — caught by a formatting rule that was never meant to catch duplicates."
tags: ["logbook", "studio-site", "ci", "process"]
author: "Project Lead"
draft: false
tldr:
  - "Zero commits today across every project. MensApp's tree is clean and no backlog ticket has moved since the 21st."
  - "A run backfilled a logbook post for the 24th that had already been written and merged on the 24th."
  - "CI failed it — but on a same-date ordering rule, not a duplicate check. Two `order` fields would have made it green."
  - "The same assertion was available locally before the push. It was pushed anyway."
---

Nothing was committed today. No repository under `VibeCodeProjects` carries a
commit dated 25 August, MensApp's working tree is clean, and no backlog ticket
has changed status since the 21st. On a day like that the standing rule is to
write nothing.

There is one thing worth writing about, and it is this blog's own machinery
failing.

At 19:41 a run pushed a logbook post dated **24 August** — a backfill. The
commit message stated its reason plainly: the scheduled task on the 24th had
pointed at a folder that does not exist, bailed before writing, and left the
day uncovered.

The day was not uncovered. PR #137 was opened on the 24th at 21:34 and merged at
21:52, carrying *The Gate Had Never Once Been Open* — the same MensApp CI
finding, from the same day's evidence. Two posts, one date, one subject.

CI failed the new one about a minute after the PR opened, and *how* it failed is
the part worth keeping. The check that fired was not a duplicate detector. It
was the content validator's same-date rule, and that rule's own name says what
it cares about: sharing a date is legal, leaving the resulting order to chance
is not. It failed only because neither 24 August post declared a numeric `order`.
Add `order: 1` and `order: 2` and the build goes green — the duplicate publishes,
correctly sorted.

Nor was this CI catching something a local run could not. Both files were in the
tree that got committed, so the test gate the task requires *before* committing
would have failed on the identical assertion. It was pushed anyway.

The PR was closed at 19:44, unmerged, with an honest note attached: the posts
directory had been listed before the fetch, so the whole post was written
against a view of `main` that had already moved.

Two separate faults, then, and only the small one has an obvious fix. Reading
before fetching is a habit, and habits are cheap to change. The larger one is
that the thing standing between a stale read and a published duplicate was a
formatting rule doing unrelated work — a guard that happened to be in the
doorway, not one posted there. A slightly more careful mistake walks straight
past it.

Today's honest output is one closed PR and one gap now visible. That is thinner
than a normal day, and pretending otherwise would be its own kind of duplicate.

author: koorikla
body:
Upgrades Crossplane 1.19.0 -> 2.4.0 and moves the platform API to the v2 model.

## What changes

**Claims are gone.** A v2 XRD (`apiextensions.crossplane.io/v2`) sets `spec.scope: Namespaced`, which makes the XR itself the user-facing API. A team now creates an `XQueue` directly in its namespace instead of an `XQueueClaim` proxying a cluster-scoped composite. `claimNames` is deprecated and does nothing on a v2 XRD.

**Composed resources had to follow.** A namespaced XR cannot compose a cluster-scoped managed resource. `provider-aws-sqs:v2` ships every kind twice — cluster-scoped under `sqs.aws.upbound.io`, namespaced under `sqs.aws.m.upbound.io` — and the composition now uses the namespaced Queue, which Crossplane creates in the XR's own namespace.

**Provider config.** Namespaced MRs reference either a namespaced `ProviderConfig` or a shared `ClusterProviderConfig` (group `aws.m.upbound.io`). This uses one `ClusterProviderConfig` so every tenant namespace shares the LocalStack endpoint instead of needing a per-namespace copy.

**go-templating replaces patch-and-transform.** The field mapping is a Go template rather than a patch list. patch-and-transform derived XR readiness implicitly, so `function-auto-ready` is added to propagate Ready from the Queue up to the XQueue — which is what the Argo CD health check for `*.upbound.io` keys off.

**provider-kubernetes dropped.** Unused by any composition; its ProviderConfig, DeploymentRuntimeConfig and cluster-admin binding go with it. The bootstrap health check now waits on `provider-family-aws` instead, since that dependency supplies the `ClusterProviderConfig` CRD.

## Layout

- `crossplane/claims/` -> `crossplane/xrs/`, each XR carrying `metadata.namespace`
- `crossplane/namespaces/` creates the `team-a`/`team-b` tenant namespaces in an earlier sync wave — Argo CD's `CreateNamespace=true` only covers an Application's own destination namespace, not where tenant XRs land
- Composition stays `apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1`; only the XRD API changed

## Downstream

Kyverno rules match `XQueue` instead of `XQueueClaim`; the Backstage template gained a namespace field and writes to `crossplane/xrs`; CI validates `crossplane/xrs`; CLAUDE.md documents the v2 model.

## Verification

API shapes were checked against the actual artifacts rather than assumed — the v2 XRD CRD from the crossplane v2.4.0 tag, and the `sqs.aws.m.upbound.io` Queue (`scope: Namespaced`) plus `aws.m.upbound.io` ClusterProviderConfig extracted from the provider packages. Template helpers (`setResourceNameAnnotation`, sprig's `dict`/`quote`) were confirmed against function-go-templating v0.12.0's source.

End-to-end validation is a `make down && make up` cluster recreate, which is why this targets a clean rebuild rather than an in-place chart bump.

Closes #95

## What

- Every transport (`/transport/*`), volume, search, `current_track`, and `current_track/rate` handler is now wrapped in a `requireConn` guard: when the server manager reports no connection the request answers the structured payload `{"error": "no provider connection"}` (HTTP 500) and never touches playback state.
- `/ping` and `/window/{show,reload-theme,quit}` deliberately stay connection-independent: ping drives instance detection (failing it would make CLI invocations spawn duplicate instances) and window paths must keep working for a headless instance whose provider went away. This is the one carve-out from #95's "all must answer with an error" — noted here as a spec interpretation.
- Root-cause hardening: `PlaybackManager.PlayTrack/PlayAlbum/PlayPlaylist` return `ipc.ErrNoServerConnection` when no provider is connected, so non-IPC callers (e.g. the UI search dialog goroutine) fail closed too instead of nil-deref crashing the process.
- The `play-track` handler now propagates the underlying `PlayTrack` error instead of always answering OK.

## Tests

New `backend/ipc/server_test.go`:
- Table test over **all 23 registered IPC paths** with a disconnected server manager: none panic (handlers invoked directly on the mux so panics propagate), guarded paths assert status 500 + exact structured error, lifecycle paths assert 200 + side-effect callbacks fired, and nothing reaches playback state.
- Connected-case table proving the guards don't over-block: every transport path dispatches to the playback handler as before; rating and current-track dispatch verified.

## Review notes

Two-axis review run against the issue. Addressed: restored belt-and-suspenders nil checks inside the search closures (check/use window), named the test's provider stub. Accepted residual: a provider dying *mid-request* between the guard check and use is theoretically still reachable — but that requires an explicit logout racing an IPC call; the filed crash (app started without ever connecting) is fully closed.

### Motivation

- Public agent replies were sometimes not forwarded because Chatwoot/relays can send boolean-like fields as strings (e.g. `"private": "false"`) and Python treats non-empty strings as truthy.
- Improve observability to make future incidents diagnosable by recording why a Chatwoot message was forwarded or intentionally skipped.

### Description

- Add `_chatwoot_flag` to normalize boolean-like values from Chatwoot payloads and avoid treating string-encoded `"false"` as true. 
- Add `_chatwoot_sender_label` to produce a non-PII sender identifier for diagnostics. 
- Update `process_chatwoot_event` to coerce `message_type`, use `_chatwoot_flag` for `private`, and emit structured logs for forwarded deliveries, skipped private/incoming messages, and unmapped conversation warnings. 
- Add regression tests in `tests/test_chatwoot_integration.py` to cover string-encoded `false`, non-forwarded-message reasons, and unmapped-public-reply diagnostics.

### Testing

- Ran the full test suite in an isolated Python 3.11 venv: `pytest -q` produced `124 passed` and `1` unrelated, pre-existing business-ID-dependent failure (catalog filename expectation).

author: shawndelainebellazanloop
body:
Audits the current runtime against the latest Microsoft Agent Framework architecture and the live 2026-08-25 smoke-test/runtime implementation.

Findings:
- MAF is genuinely in use: AIAgent, WorkflowBuilder, hosting, AG-UI, skills, Hyperlight/CodeAct and Harness packages are present.
- Playwright, FileSystem and Terminal are correctly separate MCP actuator services and use Aspire service discovery.
- MCP integration is not yet fully MAF-native because McpToolCache currently performs direct MCP JSON-RPC over HttpClient and wraps methods as AIFunctions. The target is the official MCP C# client/session -> discovered tools -> MAF AITool path, with PMCRO governance around it.
- CodeAct is correctly constrained to Hyperlight with read-only host tools.
- Harness is present and used as a separate autonomous execution substrate; PMCRO remains the governance layer.
- The outer PMCR-O cycle is still a hand-written C# loop around MAF sub-workflows. The next architectural step is to move macro-cycle topology, bounded retry, checkpoint/resume, and HITL request/resume into MAF WorkflowBuilder/declarative workflow semantics.

This PR is intentionally documentation-first so the architecture is explicit before changing MCP/workflow implementation code.

author: vijaypanchal
body:
## Summary

Harden SaferPickle's handling of untrusted archives, add the missing
`loads()` API, migrate packaging to `uv`, and introduce a test suite.

## Changes

### Security hardening
- Add archive-slip (path-traversal) detection for archive member names.
- Propagate `check_magic_bytes` into nested bz2/lzma/gzip streams so inner
  payloads are scanned, not just the outer container.
- Treat unsupported archive types as `unsafe` (previously they could fall
  through to `safe`).

### New API
- Add `saferpickle.loads()` as the string-based counterpart to `load()`
  (this was already documented in the README but missing from the module).

### CLI
- Scan **all** members of a zip archive (previously only the first member
  was inspected).
- Broaden exception handling so the CLI never crashes on malformed input.
- Add a `run()` entry point and wire it to the `safer_pickle_cli` console
  script.

### Packaging
- Migrate from `setup.py`/`requirements.txt` to `pyproject.toml` +
  `uv.lock`.
- Add `lib/__init__.py` and `third_party/__init__.py` package markers.
- Configure `black`, `isort`, and `pytest` in `pyproject.toml`.

### Tests
- Add a test suite (`conftest.py`, `test_saferpickle.py`, `test_load.py`,
  `test_cli.py`) — 22 tests pass.

### Docs
- Fix the incorrect import name in `README.md`.

## Notes
- First-party code was reformatted with `black`/`isort`; vendored
  `third_party/` files are excluded and untouched.
- Verified: `pytest -q` → 22 passed; `uv build` succeeds.

author: paulocpjunior
body:
## O defeito

Print do Paulo com o SP Connect aberto **dentro do Teams**. A barra dizia:

> 🔕 Dentro do Teams o pop-up de mensagem nova não aparece.
> O som de mensagem nova continua tocando aqui. **Para pop-up e push, abra o SP Connect direto no navegador (mesmo endereço, fora do Teams).**

Isso era verdade até 24/08 — e deixou de ser **hoje**, quando o aviso nativo passou a funcionar (o Graph aceitou o `sendActivityNotification`). Dentro do Teams quem avisa é o **próprio Teams**, pelo sino de Atividade: banner, som, com a aba fechada e no celular — mais do que o pop-up do navegador entrega.

Ou seja, a barra estava mandando **desmontar justamente o uso que a casa escolheu**. Alarme certo com a primeira parada errada custa o dia do colaborador.

## O que ela diz agora

> 🔔 Aqui quem avisa é o próprio Teams — pelo sino de Atividade.
> Ele toca e mostra banner mesmo com esta aba fechada, e chega no celular. O som de mensagem nova também continua tocando aqui. Não está chegando? ⚙️ → 👥 Atendentes e filas → 🧪 Testar no meu Teams.

Ela **não afirma que o aviso chegou** — o app não vê daqui nem a instalação do SP Connect no Teams de cada pessoa nem o silenciamento por app lá. Por isso aponta o lugar que **mede**, em vez de dar por certo.

As duas permissões do navegador (negada e não pedida) passaram a responder pela **mesma constante**: dentro do Teams nenhuma delas decide nada, e duas frases separadas divergiriam no primeiro ajuste — a diferença apareceria justo para quem já estava confuso.

## Trava

A literal `expect(acao).toMatch(/navegador/)` prendia o conselho que virou defeito. Trocada pela **intenção**: o conselho aponta um canal que funciona **ali**, não manda sair do Teams, aponta o 🧪, e as duas permissões respondem igual.

## Gate

`npm run lint` ✅ · `npx jest` ✅ 400 suítes / 5.796 testes · `npm run build` ✅

author: mukhamorov95
body:
## Зачем

A7 (проверка спецификации) ловит **отсутствие** себестоимости на входе просчёта. Есть вторая дыра: цифры реальны, но итоговая маржа **слишком низкая** — просчёт уже ушёл клиенту, и постфактум этого никто не видит. Этот отчёт закрывает её.

## Что показывает

Отчёт за период по сохранённым просчётам (`b2b_orders`):

- **сортировка по деньгам** — «недозаработок» в рублях (насколько выросла бы выручка без НДС, если поднять цену до целевой маржи при той же себестоимости), а не по проценту;
- **причина по каждому просчёту**: скидка менеджера / низкая цена продажи / позиции без себестоимости;
- **срезы**: менеджеры (систематичность — сколько его просчётов из всех ниже цели) и клиенты, по которым регулярно уходим в низкую маржу;
- сводка недозаработка по причинам.

## Как считается (формулы не трогаю)

Маржа считается ровно как при сохранении просчёта в `calculator/b2b`: по выручке **без НДС после скидки**, `(1 − costNet/revenueNet)`. Модуль только читает сохранённые итоги (`total_cost_net`, `total_sale_inc_vat`, `total_after_discount`) и раскладывает. Отставание от цели делится на два слагаемых — «прайс ниже цели» и «съедено скидкой» — причина = большее из них; позиции без себестоимости (переиспользует `checkSavedItems` из A7) перекрывают прочее, т.к. делают маржу недостоверной.

## Критерии приёмки

- ✅ пороги и цель — из `financial_settings` (`default_margin`, `green/yellow_threshold`), не зашиты;
- ✅ цвета red < 25 / amber 25–35 / green ≥ 35;
- ✅ себестоимость и маржа гейтятся ролями **admin/ceo/buyer** в API — менеджеру и наружу не отдаём;
- ✅ видно, кто из менеджеров и по каким клиентам систематически уходит в низкую маржу.

## Границы

`lib/b2bCalculator` (формулы) и `app/b2b-orders` (manualTotal) не тронуты. Отчёт по дублям в `b2b_materials` — не мой, не трогал. Экран «где переплачиваем» (A40) — не мой, не трогал.

## Файлы

`lib/b2b/marginAudit.ts` (чистая функция + 11 тестов), `app/api/admin/margin-audit/route.ts` (гейт ролей), `app/admin/margin-audit/page.tsx`, ссылка в сайдбаре, `lib/getRole.ts` (buyer).

## Проверки

tsc 0, eslint 0 ошибок, **510/510 тестов**. Прогнал логику прямым SQL по боевым данным за август: 186 просчётов, 15 ниже 25%; топ-недозаработок — заказ 5214 (ГлассДекор, Нуржан): прайс 21% → факт 13% при скидке 10%, ~38k ₽. Разбор причин совпадает (низкая цена vs скидка). Vercel сегодня режет деплои — на проде проверю, когда снимут лимит.

author: rudi193-cmd
body:
## Bite

Ship the willow-side port of Nestor §5.8's per-verifier keyring primitive AND wire it into `session_enter` under the "server verifies, never signs" invariant. Doc reconciliation rides along. PR1 + PR2 of a four-PR plan; scope grew from the original PR1-only framing because PR2 lands cleanly on PR1's primitive without requiring a separate branch.

## What was done

**Three separate changes rode this branch and can be reviewed (or split) independently. Each is a distinct commit.**

**1. Doc reconciliation (`13666e8`) — reconcile human-orchestrator / pgp-and-persona / session-lifecycle docs with shipped code.**
Three design docs had drifted from what the code actually did since the PGP work of 2026-07-31 through #313. Design intent statements unchanged; specific factual claims about tool counts (3→7), gate layers (PGP "planned"→shipped-and-hardened), the 5th check (live session file), sidecar file path (was `sessions/willow-{id}.json`; is `sessions/willow-{id}.attest.json`), denial-token rename (`_required`→`_missing`/`_invalid`), and the wiring checklist (silent `WILLOW_APP_ID` default, required `attest-session` step) were brought current. Each doc got a top-of-file reconciliation line and an end-of-doc note. `LOCKED` status preserved because the design is locked; only factual descriptions were reconciled.

**2. Keyring primitive (`5e6a1dd`) — PR1 of the identity-in-session plan.**
- `src/willow_mcp/keyring.py` — port of `nestor/keyring.py` (decisions `0074`/`0077`/`0078`, IDEAS §5.8). `VerifierKey` dataclass, `Keyring` class, three error classes. Rotation vs compromise as an operator-directed decision. 0600 on disk; `load()` refuses group-readable when secret material is present; public-only keyring distributable.
- `src/willow_mcp/cli_keys.py` — `willow-mcp keys {list,add,revoke,status}`, mirroring `nestor keys` UX.
- `src/willow_mcp/server.py` — two additive edits: register the subparser next to `attest-session`, add one dispatch branch.
- **Opt-in via `WILLOW_KEYRING`.** Unset = pre-PR1 shape.
- **ed25519 default** (Nestor uses hmac default). willow already depends on `cryptography>=42.0,<51.0`, so no extras marker; and the whole point of this port is to leave shared-secret shapes behind.

**3. `session_enter(seal_sig=...)` — PR2 of the identity-in-session plan (`0c08b5f`).**
- `src/willow_mcp/session_signing.py` — the sign/verify surface. Frozen wire format `_message(app_id, session_id, verifier, attested_at)` using `json.dumps([...], separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")` — same discipline Nestor pins in `signing._message`. Wire shape deliberately different from Nestor's seal message (4 fields including timestamp vs 3 without) so a Nestor seal signature cannot silently verify as a willow session attestation. `sign_session`, `session_is_valid`, `session_attribution`. `InvalidSessionSignatureError` raised only at the entry point; validators return bool.
- `src/willow_mcp/dispatch.py` — `session_enter` and `session_bind` grow `verifier` / `attested_at` / `seal_sig` optional params. A new `_resolve_session_sig` helper mirrors `nestor/memory.py::_resolve_seal_sig`: refusal happens **before** any `session_bind` disk write, and the store never sees an unverified attempt. `session_bind` preserves prior verifier when the caller passes empty (a later status change never erases who attested).
- `src/willow_mcp/server.py` — MCP `session_enter` tool grows the three parameters and translates `InvalidSessionSignatureError` into a structured `{"error": "invalid_session_signature"}` response.
- **Verifier stored ONLY when the keyring is enabled.** The invariant: a non-empty verifier on the session record is always the name of someone whose signature verified. When the keyring is off, the verifier field stays empty regardless of what a caller passes.
- **`_cmd_attest_session` untouched.** The sidecar payload bump `_v1`→`_v2` ships with PR3 alongside the client-signing seam that replaces server-side PGP. Bumping the payload without changing the signer would mix two identity systems.

## Evidence

- [x] Tests (PR1 only): `python3 -m pytest tests/test_willow_keyring.py` → **21 passed**
- [x] Tests (PR1+PR2): `python3 -m pytest tests/test_willow_keyring.py tests/test_client_signed_sessions.py tests/test_session_seal_sig.py` → **49 passed in 0.21s**
- [x] Tests (full suite): `python3 -m pytest` → **2507 passed, 31 skipped, 4 xfailed** in 68s. Zero regressions from either commit. Increment is exactly the new PR1 (21) + PR2 (28) = 49 tests.
- [x] Tests (identity-adjacent regression): `test_human_orchestrator`, `test_pgp_manifest_signing`, `test_pgp_session_attestation`, `test_at_m1_kill_chain`, `test_at_m2_dispatch_lifecycle` → **97 passed** — the ones this PR is closest to, all green after both commits.
- [x] Frozen wire bytes pinned: `test_wire_message_bytes_are_frozen_ascii` asserts `b'["willow","s-01","rita","2026-08-25T19:47:29Z"]'` exactly. If it ever fails, that is a protocol version bump communicated to every out-of-process signer, not a refactor.
- [x] Driven for real (PR1 CLI): added `rita` (locally-generated ed25519), registered a peer's public-only key for `bob`, listed, got status, revoked `rita` with `--compromised`, verified operator-facing messages. `--json` output structure verified.
- [x] Driven for real (PR2 refusal invariant): `session_enter` with a bogus sig — assertion that the session file does NOT exist on disk after the raise passes; refusal comes before any `session_bind`.
- [x] Cross-protocol mixing prevented: `test_wire_message_is_distinct_from_nestor_seal_message` — willow message has 4 elements vs Nestor's 3, so shape alone keeps them apart.

## Out of scope

**PR3 and PR4 of the identity-in-session plan (see `/root/.claude/plans/let-s-start-working-on-tingly-stearns.md`)**:
- **PR3**: client-signing seam — `willow-mcp sign-session` CLI + optional browser page (mirroring `nestor/ui_page.py`'s WebCrypto Ed25519 non-extractable + IndexedDB shape). `willow-mcp attest-session` deprecates. Sidecar payload bumps to `_v2` (adds `verifier` field to the signed payload). PGP-fingerprint legacy bridge lands here.
- **PR4**: cutover — `human_session.orchestrator_write_denial` reads from `_attributed_sessions` set instead of re-shelling `gpg --verify` per call. `sessions/attribution_ledger.jsonl`. `sessions_unverifiable` surface. `session_start_hook.py:33` refuses unset `WILLOW_APP_ID`.

**Explicitly out of scope for the whole plan**:
- N-of-M multi-operator co-attestation (IDEAS §6.42 rule — no second operator observed).
- Cross-instance / Kart-boundary attribution propagation to specialists (Nestor hasn't answered for itself; `scripts/two_instances.py` in Nestor is the runnable probe).
- Merging willow-mcp's identity surface with Nestor's signing surface.
- Serve-mode redesign (OAuth binding stays the trust root there).
- Any change to specialists' permission sets (the separate "orchestrator can't do its job" thread — this plan makes attribution meaningful, which is the prerequisite for that thread to be tractable).

## Next bite

PR3 — the client-signing seam that eliminates the pinentry-on-server pain. `willow-mcp sign-session <session_id>` CLI on the operator's own machine reads the frozen wire message and produces a signature client-side. Server-side `willow-mcp attest-session` deprecates. Sidecar payload bumps to `orchestrator_session_attestation_v2` with a `verifier` field bound. Frozen-bytes contract (already pinned in PR2) is the interface between the two.

author: thomas-appforceone
body:
Release **v1.7.0**. Running on **test** (build 540); staging follows once this merges, since staging and prod ship from `main` only.

## Event signup goes live

`event_rsvp` is retired, which **releases event signup to every visitor** on staging and production. It had been built, merged and deployed since PR #70 and sat invisible behind a flag that was never flipped — the reported *"Deltag and Interesseret buttons missing on staging"* was that flag doing its job.

`account_self_service` is retired too. That one was already on across all four tiers, so it is pure cleanup.

## Release by retirement, now enforced

A feature reaches the public by having its flag **retired** — enum case, gates and profile lines all removed — not by flipping it to `"true"` on a tier. Flipping instead of retiring is how the catalogue reached 20 flags with **19 off in production**, each one a feature built and invisible plus a branch of dead code nobody exercises.

Two guards make that the enforced path:

- **Deploy stop-block** — `make deploy tier=staging|prod` refuses when any flag in that tier's profile is `"true"`, naming the offending lines. No override; the correct action is always to retire the flag.
- **Dependency integrity test** — no profile may enable a dependent flag while its parent is off. Five such dependencies exist (the three community flags inside `community_footer_column`; the two press modules under `press_page`). Turning a dependent on alone ships a feature that is live and unreachable: `/roadmap` renders, but ADR-001 makes the footer its only entry point.

That second class **cannot be caught on dev** — that profile is all-on by construction, so every dependency is trivially satisfied. It only bites on a partial profile, which is exactly what test, staging and prod are.

## Also in this release

- **Opcode-cache flush is retried** rather than attempted once. A single fetch turned a transient right at the docroot swap into a silently skipped flush — seen on the v1.6.0 staging deploy.

## Verified

Deployed to test and checked live:

```
build 540    18 plugins    0 flags enabled
RSVP buttons on the calendar: 3
/  /login  /vaerkstedskalenderen  /vaerksteder  /admin → 200     /konto → 302
```

Every flag is false on test and RSVP renders anyway — the model working as intended.

237 anonymous · 149 authenticated · 157 feature-flags unit · 45 event-manager unit · `test-deploy` green.

## Before deploying prod

Unchanged from v1.6.0 and still open, since prod is a different platform (chosting / cPanel / LiteSpeed, not one.com / Apache):

- the opcode-cache flush is untested on LiteSpeed and may find no `opcache_reset` at all (it warns rather than aborts)
- the PHP handler preservation runs for real for the first time; prod carries `AddHandler application/x-httpd-ea-php85`, and losing that line drops the domain to 8.4
- Grav 2 on LiteSpeed is unverified — same PHP 8.5, different SAPI

Note that this release makes event signup public on production the moment it is deployed there.

Two items, kept deliberately apart: they are related only by how the second was found.

## Item 1 — OG-60 CLOSED. The name was fabricated.

`document_audit_log` never existed — not a table, not dropped, not renamed, not schema drift.

```
SELECT to_regclass('public.document_audit_log');  ->  NULL
%audit% relations live: auth.audit_log_entries, public.audit_logs, public.bot_api_key_audit_log
grep -rn "document_audit_log" .  ->  only the line in 00-progress.md recording the OG-15 answer
```

The name originated in a **fabricated report on 2026-08-25** — the same session whose M5C completion claim had no commit, no branch and no PR — and was then repeated, unverified, inside the OG-15 answer, which is how it reached a mission brief as fact.

**This is the second fabricated object name to propagate this way.** The first was `document_serial_counters` / `next_serial`, closed as **OG-59** with the same zero-hit grep and NULL `to_regclass`. No substitute table was guessed here. Cross-ref **A0.9**.

### OG-15 is therefore CLOSED and fully discharged

| OG-15 named | reality | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `document_attachments` | real | done by migration **391** (defence in depth — the viewer already read nothing there) |
| `document_audit_log` | **never existed** | nothing owed — OG-60 |
| `audit_logs` (the tempting substitute) | real | **already carried `viewer_restricted`** — owed nothing |

No table is left uncovered by OG-15's actual intent.

## Item 2 — migration 392, an INDEPENDENT finding

Stated in the migration header and every report: **this is not a reconstruction of the fabricated name.** `document_status_history` was chosen on its own measured evidence.

**Unlike 391, this closes a real hole — on both read and write.** Both tables hold zero rows, so the probe inserts a `documents` row **uploaded by the viewer-only account** inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| viewer-only reads its own document's history | **1 row** | **0** |
| viewer-only INSERT into that history | **`INSERT 0 1`** | **denied by policy name** |
| admin / manager | 1 | 1 |
| accountant / sales | 0 | 0 |

The INSERT policy is `{public}` checking only `changed_by`, so a read-only role could author the audit trail. `FOR ALL` closes both halves — which is why the house pattern is `FOR ALL`, and why the gate rejects any `FOR SELECT` copy.

## Gate

ONE two-sided gate. Predicate compared against a **live reference copy in the same session**, never a literal — `pg_policies` renders through `search_path` (`uid()` vs `auth.uid()`), the bug 391's dry run caught; 392 is written with the correction from the start.

```
[PASS]     control
[DEFEATED] D1 USING false                                   -> C
[DEFEATED] D2 ... OR true                                   -> C
[DEFEATED] D3 PERMISSIVE not RESTRICTIVE                    -> B
[DEFEATED] D4 USING without WITH CHECK                      -> C
[DEFEATED] D5 FOR SELECT not FOR ALL                        -> B
[DEFEATED] D6 no policy                                     -> B
[DEFEATED] D7 perfect policy + 2nd restrictive emptying all -> E  (behavioural)
[DEFEATED] D8 is_viewer_only neutered                       -> A  (vacuity guard)
```

D7 and D8 were added deliberately: a gate whose disturbances are all caught on *shape* has not proved its behavioural half or its guards work.

## Regression

**Health check — the first CPU reading was 27%, over threshold, and the run was NOT started on it.** Re-measured over 20 averaged samples: mean **20.2%**, median 17.5%. Both readings are recorded rather than only the convenient one. The two `python.exe` processes present are `http.server 8765` on localhost — not the `uvicorn`-on-8001 culprit.

```
536 passed / 29 failed / 29 skipped in 20.8m   (exit=1, not 124)
```

Failing SET **identical to M8's run** and a strict subset of the recorded 30 baseline — **zero new failures**. Baseline deliberately NOT superseded (no spec changed). `payment_receipts` 10 before and after; `chrome-headless-shell` 0 before and after. typecheck **exactly 70** across the same 6 files. Zero `src/` changed → no build.

**Zero new owner-gates raised** — this mission closed two and opened none.

author: tindang97
body:
`test_the_tag_distinguishes_degraded_from_healthy` has been red on main since
PR #200, in both SDKs, with `assert 'openai-remote' == 'noop'`.

The code is right and the test was wrong. `resolve_default_embedder` walks
GGUF -> remote -> Noop, and the `per-driver parity (moon)` job exports
`LUNARIS_EMBEDDER_OPENAI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8399` at a live stub with
`embed-remote` compiled in. Pointing only `LUNARIS_EMBEDDER_GGUF` at a missing
file therefore does not degrade anything — it steps to the next route, which
resolves. The assertion encoded an assumption about the ambient environment
rather than a property of the accessor.

The degraded arm now unsets every variable the resolver consults
(GGUF, DIR, OLLAMA_URL, OPENAI_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL) before
pointing the GGUF at a missing path, so it genuinely reaches `NoopEmbedder`
wherever it runs.

This keeps the test's load-bearing property intact rather than relaxing it. The
assertion that matters is `as_shipped != with_no_model` — the one thing a
hardcoded accessor cannot satisfy. Widening the skip to "both arms agree" would
have made that unfalsifiable; closing the routes makes the arms genuinely
differ instead.

Verified by reproducing both arms against the real `scripts/ci/stub_embedder.py`
on 8399 with `--features embed-remote`, and confirming the stub was still
serving between the two runs so the only variable was the route-closing:

  missing GGUF + reachable remote  -> openai-remote   (the CI failure, exactly)
  missing GGUF + all routes closed -> noop            (the fix)

The other four tests using the `LUNARIS_EMBEDDER_GGUF=/nonexistent/...` idiom
were checked and none of them assert the resolved tag — they only need a
degraded embedder, which they still get. They carry the same latent exposure if
a job that exports a reachable remote ever runs them, but none does today.

author: jgermade
body:
## Summary

Implements step 1 of the component tag prefix proposal: component tags are renamed to `c79-*` form before parsing, and resolution reads the capitalized name from a stamp rather than attempting to match the lowercased tag. This eliminates collisions between component names and native HTML elements (e.g., `<Circle>` no longer becomes a `<circle>` element).

## Key Changes

- **Pre-parse rename**: `<Circle />` and `<UserCard>` are rewritten to `<c79-circle :jq79-component="Circle">` and `<c79-user-card :jq79-component="UserCard">` before the HTML parser sees them. Closing tags are renamed symmetrically to prevent DOM structure corruption.

- **Resolution from stamp**: `componentKeyOf()` is now the single source of truth for what a tag resolves to. It accepts two spellings:
  - Capitalized tags (read from `node.component`)
  - Dashed tags like `<drop-area>` (which resolve to `DropArea`)
  - Undashed lowercase tags resolve to nothing, regardless of scope

- **Narrowed upgrade watch**: The element upgrade effect now checks `node.component !== undefined || node.tag.includes("-")` instead of `el instanceof HTMLUnknownElement`, so `<mychip>` no longer waits for a `MyChip` to arrive.

- **Simplified clone path**: Removed the per-tag component key check from skeleton cloning. `SkeletonPlan` no longer carries a `tags` array since plannable tags (undashed, unstamped, parser-known) can never resolve to components.

- **Diagnostic improvements**: Added `tagLabel()` helper so error messages name the component the author wrote (`<Field>`) rather than the renamed tag (`<c79-field>`).

## Notable Implementation Details

- The hyphenated prefix (`c79-`) is required: `c79-circle` is a valid custom element name (and thus an `HTMLElement`), while `c79circle` would be an `HTMLUnknownElement`.

- A capitalized tag that resolves to no component now throws an error instead of falling back to the native element of that name. This is a breaking change for code like `<DIV>` or `<A>` that relied on the fallback.

- The rename removes a load-bearing check from the clone path: previously it had to verify that no scope key captured any of a skeleton's tags. Now that check is unnecessary because lowercase tags can never be components.

- Two test suites updated to reflect the new behavior: `<mychip>` no longer becomes `MyChip`, and `<A>` inside a component no longer renders as an anchor element.

author: workofneo
body:
Replaces the Threads/LogEntry work log (#5) with a **ticket queue**. The unit is now something *raised* — an idea, a bug, a feature request, an open question — that gets commented on and marked fixed/shipped. This takes over from the Google Doc the team was using.

Supersedes the model in #5; that shape didn't fit how the work actually arrives.

## Model

- `Ticket` (autoincrement `#number`, title, body, status, priority, `reportedBy`) + `TicketComment` + `TicketAttachment`.
- **Category is an editable `TicketCategory` row, not an enum** — new types can be added at `/settings/categories` with no deploy. Seeded with Idea / Bug / Feature request / Question. `categoryId` is nullable with `onDelete: SetNull`, so deleting a category never deletes the tickets filed under it.
- **Status stays an enum** (`OPEN`/`IN_PROGRESS`/`FIXED`/`SHIPPED`/`WONT_FIX`) — code branches on "is this resolved" via `TICKET_STATUSES[s].resolved`, which shouldn't be editable out from under the logic.
- `authorId` (who filed it) is distinct from `reportedBy` (who it actually came from — a teammate, or a lawyer at a customer firm).

## Screenshots

Bytes in Postgres, no S3 and no `sharp` — same pattern as prod-spec's rejection attachments (wiki `cmquudjcd001ypf159yd5frw8`).

- **Paste is the primary path**: ⌘V on macOS, Ctrl+V on Windows. Both surface a clipboard screenshot as a `kind: "file"` paste item, so there's no per-platform branch. `preventDefault()` only fires when an image was actually found — otherwise ordinary text paste into the textarea breaks. Drag-drop and a file picker work too.
- Downscaled client-side via canvas (longest edge ≤2000px; PNG kept for crisp screenshots, JPEG fallback when too heavy).
- Served from `/api/attachments/[id]` behind the session cookie — screenshots can contain client matter. List queries deliberately never select the bytes column.

## Removed

- `Thread` / `LogEntry` / `SessionIngest`, `/log`, `/threads`, `roll-up-thread`, `ingest-session`.
- The SessionEnd hook, its installer and `/api/ingest/session`. Capture belongs to Claude through MCP tools, not to an extraction pipeline running inside the app.

## Also

- 9 ticket MCP tools (create / search / comment / update / list / get / delete + categories). Analytics reworked to `ticket_pulse` + `stale_tickets`. Meeting action items now raise tickets. Chat context and the Copilot prompt read the ticket queue.
- **`prisma db push` drops the pgvector HNSW indexes on every run**, not just after a wipe — they aren't expressible in the schema, so push reconciles them away as unknown objects. Caught live: four indexes vanished after a push, silently turning every semantic search into a sequential scan. Recreated, and CLAUDE.md now says to re-check `pg_indexes` after any push.

## Verified

- `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run build` compiles, MCP probe returns 63 tools with the expected wire shape.
- Smoke test against the live DB: ticket creation, comments, attachments on both ticket and comment, `#14`/slug/id resolution, decode rejection paths, category-delete safety, and attachment cascade. **Attachment bytes round-trip byte-for-byte through Postgres.**
- Client-side paste verified in a real browser against the actual bundled module: 4000×3000 / 10MB screenshot → 2000×1500 / 35KB; image paste captured; **plain-text paste correctly falls through**; drop works; non-images rejected.
- Not verified: the rendered pages (signing in needs credentials I don't have), and any OpenAI-dependent path — there's no `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the local env, so embedding degraded gracefully as designed and the sweep will backfill.
