author: rebersasoluciones
body:
Módulo nuevo `appointment_sale_downpayment`.

## Problema

El "Pay to Book" nativo (`appointment_account_payment`) cobra el **100%** del producto de la cita y emite una **factura suelta**, sin relación con la factura del resto del servicio, que hay que crear a mano. Además, el token de pago de ese flujo va firmado con el importe total de la factura (`payment_utils.generate_access_token(partner_id, invoice.amount_total, currency_id)`), así que no admite pago parcial sin tocar el mecanismo.

## Solución

Se sustituye el **destino** del pago, no el mecanismo. `_redirect_to_payment()` —el punto de extensión oficial, cuyo propio docstring dice *"This method is overriden if eCommerce is installed to use sale orders instead"*— crea un `sale.order` con:

- `require_payment = True`, `require_signature = False`
- `prepayment_percent` = anticipo del tipo de cita
- una línea del producto del servicio enlazada a la reserva vía `calendar_booking_ids`

y redirige a `order.get_portal_url()` → `/my/orders/<id>?access_token=…`. El portal de pedidos **ya** cobra sólo `_get_prepayment_required_amount()`, sin tocar plantillas.

A partir de ahí todo es nativo:

| Paso | Quién |
|---|---|
| Confirmar el pedido al alcanzar el anticipo (no hace falta el 100%) | `payment.transaction._check_amount_and_confirm_order()` |
| Crear la cita en el calendario | `sale.order._action_confirm()` → `calendar_booking_ids._make_event_from_paid_booking()` (de `website_appointment_sale`) |
| Factura de anticipo con cuenta de anticipos | `_generate_downpayment_invoices()` si `sale.automatic_invoice`, o el wizard estándar |
| Factura final descontando anticipos | `sale.advance.payment.inv` con factura normal |

## Cambios

- `models/appointment_type.py`: campo `downpayment_prepayment_percent` (default = `res.company.prepayment_percent`) con constraint `0 < x <= 1` cuando hay pago por adelantado.
- `controllers/appointment.py`: override de `_redirect_to_payment()`.
- `views/appointment_type_views.xml`: el campo junto al precio, en la pestaña de pago.
- `README.md`: configuración necesaria, discrepancias y decisiones por defecto.

Sin datos de demo. No se replican modelos que ya existen (ver discrepancia 1).

## Discrepancias con la especificación (verificadas en fuente)

1. **Se depende de `website_appointment_sale`**, en contra de lo pedido. En esta instancia ya está instalado (auto-instalable con `appointment_account_payment` + `website_sale`) y **también sobrescribe `_redirect_to_payment()`**. Los controladores se combinan en `odoo/http.py` con `type(name, tuple(reversed(leaf_controllers)), {})`: gana el módulo cargado más tarde. Sin la dependencia, su versión (carrito de la tienda, 100% del importe) ganaría y este módulo quedaría muerto. Como efecto secundario, `calendar.booking.order_line_id`, `sale.order.line.calendar_booking_ids` / `calendar_event_id` y el override de `_action_confirm()` ya existen y **no se duplican**. Si algún día se desinstala `website_appointment_sale`, hay que replicar aquí esas tres piezas y quitar la dependencia.
2. **`appointment.type` no tiene `company_id`** en 19.0 (verificado en la lista de campos del modelo), así que el pedido toma la compañía del entorno de la petición.
3. `get_portal_url()` ya llama a `_portal_ensure_token()`; no se invoca aparte.
4. No se fuerza `action_quotation_sent()`: `_has_to_be_paid()` acepta `draft` y `_post_process()` ya pasa el pedido a *enviado* al llegar el pago.

## Decisiones por defecto (preguntas abiertas del cliente)

- **Un pedido por reserva** (es lo que hace hoy el flujo de facturas). Punto único a cambiar si se quiere agrupar: `_prepare_downpayment_order()`.
- **Anticipo por tipo de cita**, no global.
- **Factura final manual**; el cron de fase 2 no se incluye.

## Configuración imprescindible antes de activar

1. `res.company.downpayment_account_id` (cuenta de anticipos de cliente).
2. Parámetro `sale.automatic_invoice` según si se quiere la factura de anticipo automática.
3. **Revisar el producto de cada tipo de cita**: pasa a ser el precio completo del servicio, no la señal fija de hoy.
4. Fijar el anticipo por tipo de cita y tener un proveedor de pago publicado.

## Pruebas

Sólo validación de sintaxis (`ast.parse` + XML); no hay entorno Odoo en la sesión. Falta probar en la instancia: reserva → portal con importe reducido → pago del anticipo → cita en el calendario → factura de anticipo con la cuenta correcta → factura final descontando el anticipo.

body:
Promoção `dev` → `main`. **6 commits, 5 issues** (PH-76, PH-163, PH-165, PH-166, PH-167).

## O que o jogador vê

**Uma coisa só: a entrada 7.13 do patch notes** (PH-166) — e ela é **retroativa**. Descreve cinco mudanças que **já estão no ar desde a promoção #141** e nunca tiveram nota:

- O clima inteiro (PH-140, PH-141): clima de ambiente por sala, Neve e Neblina como climas novos, o ecossistema respondendo, o efeito visual dos seis e o chip no HUD. A palavra "clima" aparecia **zero vezes** no arquivo.
- Busca, filtro e ordenação nas telas de **venda** do Mercado (PH-142).
- O fim do spawn em bando (PH-143).
- O bot passando a usar Max Revive, e o aviso de suprimento por família (PH-144).
- A edição dos 4 golpes destravada no Hospital (PH-156).

Nenhuma linha de comportamento do jogo muda nesta promoção. O que muda é o jogador **passar a saber** o que já estava acontecendo com ele.

## O resto é interno

- **PH-76** — o gate de migration do CI para de reprovar branch vizinha. Ele reprovava toda branch sempre que existisse migration aplicada no remoto sem arquivo local; como o passo 3 do fluxo de schema manda aplicar da branch de feature antes do PR, **seguir o fluxo documentado travava o CI de todo mundo** (26 PRs reprovadas de uma vez em 22/08). Agora órfã com arquivo em alguma branch vira aviso, e DDL aplicada na mão continua reprovando.
- **PH-163** — registra no `CLAUDE.md` que `scripts/` carrega 242 MB versionados de propósito, e ignora as notas de operação da raiz.
- **PH-165** — `docs/19-explicacao-flutuante.md`, inventário de cobertura da bolha de explicação.
- **PH-167** — a `dev` recebe o commit de merge da #141. Zero diff de conteúdo; sem isto esta PR nasceria `BEHIND`.

## Verificação local

`build-check` **não roda em PR para `main`** — o workflow filtra `branches: [dev]`. Então `tsc` e a suíte aqui são a execução local, e o único gate automático nesta PR é o `supabase-check`.

```
npx tsc -b        -> exit 0
npx vitest run    -> 135 arquivos, 1322 testes, 0 falhas
```

Rodados na ponta da `dev` já convergida (`4221de51`). Cada um dos 6 commits também passou pelo `build-check` completo na sua própria PR para a `dev`.

## Depois de mesclar

O deploy de produção tem duas falhas transientes conhecidas, e as duas se resolvem com `gh run rerun <id> --failed`:

1. `supabase/setup-cli@v1` usa `version: latest` e resolve pela API do GitHub — em dia de muitos runs dá `rate limit exceeded`. Falha no primeiro passo, então `db push` e `edge:publicar` ficam `skipped` e o banco fica intacto.
2. PH-106: `supabase-check` e o deploy disparam no mesmo push e disputam o token, rotacionando a senha um do outro (`password authentication failed for user "cli_login_postgres"`). Rerodar **com a fila vazia**.

Conferência que vale fazer depois: `db push` tem que dizer **"Remote database is up to date"** (migration chega em `public` pelo merge na `dev`, então aqui é no-op), `/saude` da Edge devolver `{"ok":true,"schema":"public"}` **com header `Authorization: Bearer <anon>`**, e `poke-hunt-euj.pages.dev` subir sem erro de console.

author: tamnd
body:
A frame, a series and a column now print as a table. The old String methods gave the shape and nothing else, so seeing a value meant writing a loop, which is the wrong amount of work for the question "what did that query return".

```
kuma.Frame[kuma.Dynamic] 4 rows x 3 cols

  symbol | minute                |   volume
  string | timestamp[us, tz=UTC] |  float64
---------+-----------------------+---------
  AAPL   | 2026-08-25 09:30:00   | 1.24e+07
  MSFT   | 2026-08-25 09:30:00   | 8.91e+06
  null   | 2026-08-25 09:31:00   | 4.02e+06
  GOOG   | 2026-08-25 09:31:00   |  5.5e+06
```

The names in the type row are the ones `Schema().String()` prints, so there is no second vocabulary of abbreviations to drift away from the first one. Ten rows and twelve columns show by default and the rest becomes a line of dots in the middle, keeping both ends. `Frame.Render` takes a `PrintOptions` for a different amount, and `MaxRows` of -1 means the whole frame, which is what `kumatest` will want for a diff.

Every type an array can hold has a cell format, including the ones the cast kernel has not reached yet, because a printer with a hole in it is worst exactly when the hole is over the value being chased. Decimals go through `math/big`, the three interval layouts through `encoding/binary`, and a timestamp resolves its zone and falls back to UTC when the machine has no zone database. A count outside the calendar prints as a number with its unit rather than as a plausible wrong date.

Numbers print at the shortest text that reads back as the same value rather than rounded to a fixed number of digits. A printer that rounds will one day show two different numbers as the same during the debugging session where that difference is the whole point. A string holding a newline or a tab is quoted for the same reason, and so is one that begins or ends in a space, since that space is invisible in a table where every cell is padded with spaces anyway.

The emit loop writes into one `strings.Builder` and pads from a constant run of blanks, with no padding on the last cell of a line, so nothing carries trailing whitespace. That took `BenchmarkFrameString` from 17444 ns and 239 allocs to 12194 ns and 91 allocs on this laptop, and `BenchmarkFrameRender` from 1570433 ns and 35474 allocs to 1152873 ns and 14448 allocs.

`FuzzPrint` feeds arbitrary CSV through the printer and checks the line count and the no trailing whitespace rule. It found the case where a column name ending in a space put the whitespace back, which is the seed now in `testdata/fuzz/FuzzPrint`.

Package coverage is 97.4 percent. The one uncovered line is the default branch of the cell formatter, which is the guard for a `dtype.DataType` implemented outside the package.

Real numbers from server1, server3 and gamingpc go in a comment once the runs finish.

## Summary

author: smeet666
body:
Declare one entry point for each thing this package publishes, and pack one set of files

The root was declared twice, as `main` beside `exports`, and only `exports` is
read: a rename moves that one and leaves the other pointing at a path that is no
longer there, for whichever old resolver still reads it. The root is now
declared once.

The root also had to gain the types it never published. Written as a bare
string, `exports["."]` names a module and nothing else, so a caller importing
the package by its name got the code with no declarations, and the `types` field
that used to answer for it is gone.

What npm packs is now one list. Half the fleet published no changelog inside its
package and the other half published no descriptor; both are in every package
now. The icons went out of the list: the extension bundle takes them from the
repository when it is built, so nothing ever read them from the tarball.

author: florimond-jouffroy
body:
Corrige les CVE remontées par `composer audit` sur les versions installées, par montées de version **patch** (aucun changement d'API).

## Ce qui était vulnérable

`composer audit` remontait 28 avis. Les deux qui comptaient ici :

| Paquet | CVE | Sévérité | Exposition réelle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `symfony/http-kernel` v8.0.10 | CVE-2026-45075 | **high** | Une requête `HEAD` contourne le filtre `methods:['GET']` de `#[IsGranted]` / `#[IsSignatureValid]` / `#[IsCsrfTokenValid]`. Aucun usage dans `src/` aujourd'hui, mais **piège armé** pour tout projet dérivé. |
| `symfony/runtime` v8.0.8 | CVE-2026-47767 | medium | Bypass du garde-fou de `SymfonyRuntime` : forçage de `APP_ENV`/`APP_DEBUG` via l'URL quand `register_argc_argv` est actif. **Reproduit** sur l'image locale via `GET /?=--env=prod` (`$_GET` vide mais `$_SERVER['argv']` peuplé). |

Plus des avis medium/low sur `cache` (SQLi `PdoAdapter`, non utilisé), `http-foundation` (SSRF `IpUtils`), `routing`, `yaml`, `web-profiler-bundle` (dev/test only), et 17 avis `twig` — tous liés au **sandbox**, qui n'est pas utilisé dans ce projet.

## Le correctif

```bash
composer update "symfony/*" twig/twig --with-all-dependencies
```

Chaque paquet passe à sa version patch corrigée (http-kernel 8.0.10 → 8.0.15, twig 3.24 → 3.28, etc.). `bump-after-update` (déjà actif dans `composer.json`) a relevé les planchers de version en conséquence — sans les restreindre (`twig ^3.28` autorise toujours les suivantes).

`config/reference.php` suit la mise à jour : c'est le fichier de types auto-régénéré par Flex, pas une édition manuelle.

## Hors périmètre (choix assumé)

Le durcissement serveur `register_argc_argv = Off` — qui neutraliserait toute cette classe de failles en amont — **n'est pas inclus** : il vit dans la config PHP (`php.ini`), qui n'accompagne pas le code déployé dans ce projet. La montée de version, elle, part avec `composer.lock` quel que soit l'hébergeur.

## Vérifications

- `composer audit` → **No security vulnerability advisories found.**
- `make qa` vert : cs-fixer, PHPStan, **57 tests / 161 assertions**.
- `npm run build` OK.
- CVE runtime re-testée : le forçage `?=--env=prod` ne débouche plus sur un bypass.

author: ss251
body:
`scanSqlForReadOnly()` removed PostgreSQL block comments with an empty string, so valid token-separator comments collapsed adjacent SQL tokens and bypassed the read-only mutation/function scans. A default read-only caller could send `DELETE/**/FROM memories` and receive HTTP 200 after the raw DELETE reached `db.execute()`; the same bypass affected the DATABASE action and dangerous functions such as `SELECT/**/pg_sleep(10)`.

This fixes the defect at the shared scanner boundary. Closed block comments now contribute one space, matching PostgreSQL tokenization. A block comment between two identifier characters is rejected outright so split identifiers such as `UPD/**/ATE` cannot become a new bypass.

# Relates to

No issue. This pull request is the standalone defect report and fix.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts (`7d55350499f4aed3f6c4e8da4b9ab266692182a4`).
- [x] `bun install` was intentionally not run per the operator brief. `bun run verify` was run after sync; its exact unrelated control-reproduced dependency blocker is recorded below.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the defect and fix from the verbatim before/after and falsification output below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun run verify` was run post-sync; the exact unrelated blocker is documented in **Known gaps / failures**.

# Risks

Low. Read-only SQL that places a block comment directly between identifier characters is now rejected, including otherwise valid token-separator forms such as `SELECT/**/column`. This is deliberate fail-closed behavior for prompt-reachable read-only access; callers that intentionally require writes retain the existing explicit write override. Ordinary comments separated by whitespace remain accepted and are normalized as whitespace.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces closed block comments with a single space in all scanner output streams.
- Rejects block comments whose immediate neighbors are both ASCII identifier characters.
- Locks the HTTP query route, shared DATABASE-action guard, and sanitizer behavior against `DELETE/**/FROM`, `DROP/**/TABLE`, `SELECT/**/pg_sleep`, and split-keyword variants.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix: restores the advertised read-only contract for the Control-UI database endpoint and DATABASE agent action.

# Documentation changes needed?

No documentation change is needed. The public contract remains read-only; this change makes the implementation enforce it.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

Start with `packages/agent/src/shared/sql-sanitizers.ts`, then run the unchanged reproduction and the five focused owning-package files shown below.

## Broken reproduction before the change

```text
$ cd packages/agent && bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/api/tmp-repro-blockcomment.test.ts

status: 200 body: {"columns":[],"rows":[],"rowCount":0,"durationMs":0}
query called: 1 [[{"decoder":{},"shouldInlineParams":false,"usedTables":[],"queryChunks":[{"value":["DELETE/**/FROM memories"]}]}]]

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  4 failed | 1 passed (5)
```

The repository-bundled PostgreSQL engine also proved that the input is executable SQL:

```text
$ node tmp-pglite-check.mjs
before: [ { c: 2 } ]
after DELETE/**/FROM: [ { c: 0 } ]
```

## Same reproduction after the change

```text
$ bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --disableConsoleIntercept src/api/tmp-repro-blockcomment.test.ts

{"ok":false,"reason":"Block comments between identifier characters are not allowed in read-only mode."}
status: 400 body: {"error":"Query rejected: Block comments between identifier characters are not allowed in read-only mode."}
query called: 0 []

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  5 passed (5)
```

## Owning-package suite by full path

```text
$ bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/agent/src/shared/sql-sanitizers.test.ts packages/agent/src/security/sql-readonly-guard.test.ts packages/agent/src/actions/database-readonly.test.ts packages/agent/src/actions/database.readonly-redos.test.ts packages/agent/src/api/database.query-readonly.test.ts

Test Files  5 passed (5)
     Tests  180 passed (180)
```

## Regression falsification

I reverted only `packages/agent/src/shared/sql-sanitizers.ts`, kept the tests, and ran the new assertions. The endpoint returned 200 again and all three action-guard inputs returned `{ ok: true }`:

```text
$ bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/agent/src/api/database.query-readonly.test.ts packages/agent/src/security/sql-readonly-guard.test.ts -t 'block-comment token separator|block comment used as a token separator'

AssertionError: expected 200 to be 400
AssertionError: expected { ok: true } to deeply equal { ok: false, …(1) }

Test Files  2 failed (2)
     Tests  4 failed | 101 skipped (105)
```

The production fix was restored immediately afterward, and the 180-test focused suite plus unchanged 5-test reproduction were rerun successfully on commit `d0e1ea09a6287ef307a1b28e77865460784a726d`.

## Formatting and TypeScript

```text
$ bunx biome check --write <six touched files>
Checked 6 files in 72ms. No fixes applied.
```

`bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/agent/tsconfig.json` produced four dependency-resolution errors. An untouched `origin/develop` control produced the exact same four lines; the log files were byte-identical (`cmp` exit 0), so this PR adds zero TypeScript errors.

# Evidence Gate

Evidence matches exact head `d0e1ea09a6287ef307a1b28e77865460784a726d`.

# Relates to

No issue was filed; this pull request is the defect report.

# Risks

Low. The change is limited to conversation-message pagination and its UI caller. Legacy timestamp-only callers retain compatibility; paired cursors add deterministic ordering inside a shared millisecond.

# Background

## Defect and caller consequence

`GET /api/conversations/:id/messages?before=` used `end: before - 1` even though the first page could end midway through messages sharing one `createdAt` millisecond. Rows after that page boundary were excluded from both the first page and every later page, so upward scrolling silently omitted part of a conversation transcript.

## What does this PR do?

Adds the missing message-ID tiebreaker across the REST route and shipped UI pagination caller. The API accepts `before` with `beforeId`, forwards a tuple cursor to storage, validates malformed or unpaired cursors, and preserves timestamp-only compatibility without discarding an entire tie group. The UI retains and sends both cursor components. Focused regression tests cover the route, serialization, resume state, and invalid tuples.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No documentation change is needed; this restores lossless behavior in the existing pagination contract.

author: abustamam
body:
Closes #627.

## The bug

#619 gave `DialogContent` a height ceiling and a scroller, which is what made the bottom of a tall
dialog reachable at all. The close button is `absolute top-4 right-4` on that same element, and an
absolutely-positioned child of a scroll container scrolls **with** the content. So scrolling down to
reach a control at the bottom took the ✕ off the top.

Measured before: y=33, then **y=-56** after an 89px scroll.

Both remaining exits were weak on exactly the devices affected. Escape works, and phones have no
Escape key. The overlay tap strip is **16px**, against a 44px minimum target.

## The fix

Split into a non-scrolling **shell** and a scrolling **body**. The shell keeps the ceiling, the
padding and the chrome, and owns the close button; a new `data-slot="dialog-body"` child owns the
scroller.

### `p-6` stays on the shell, and that is the whole reason this was shippable

#627 sketched moving the padding to the inner scroller. That silently breaks `CommandDialog`, which
passes `p-0`: `cn()` is tailwind-merge, so a caller's override has to land on the same element as
the default or it stops working with nothing failing. Keeping padding on the shell avoids it
entirely — and it also clips the body's scrolled content 24px inside the rounded corner rather than
at it, and puts the button (`top-4`, 16px) wholly inside that gutter so content never slides under it.

### `min-h-0` on the body is load-bearing

A flex child's default `min-height: auto` refuses to shrink below its content, so `overflow-y-auto`
on it produces a box that **grows instead of scrolling**. The shell's `max-h` would then clip it with
no way to scroll — #619 again in a new shape, passing any grep that only asks whether
`overflow-y-auto` is present. This repo already has a gate for that exact class of mistake in
`pinned-column-reachability.test.ts`, written after a sticky column shipped twice with an unreachable
tail.

## Checked before writing any of it

- No CSS rule and no test outside `dialog.tsx` is coupled to the dialog's DOM shape, so adding a
  wrapper has essentially no blast radius.
- All 20 call sites pass only a `sm:max-w-*` width. Nothing passes a display or layout class that
  would fight `flex flex-col`.

## Verification

**Chromium, 375x400, the public identity dialog:**

| | |
|---|---|
| shell | `overflow-y: hidden`, 368px (ceiling engaged) |
| body | `overflow-y: auto`, `min-height: 0px`, scrollable |
| ✕ before scroll | y=33 |
| ✕ after a 147px body scroll | **y=33 — immobile** |

**#619's guarantee re-checked in the same run:** the body's last control ("Sign the guest book") is
off-screen initially and visible after scrolling. Not regressed.

**375x800:** body not scrollable, shell fits, ✕ visible. The split is inert when it isn't needed.
Shell height 675px vs 622px at 375x667 — the +53 is exactly the roster list's `40svh` growing, so the
restructure adds no height.

## The guard is repointed, not extended

`overflow-y-auto` moved off the shell, so the assertion pinning it there would have been asserting
the bug. It now checks four things: the shell does **not** scroll, the body does, the body can
shrink, and — structurally, by source offset — that the button is a **sibling** of the body rather
than inside it.

**Mutation-checked.** Dropping `min-h-0` fails one assertion; moving the button into the body fails
another.

### A bug in my own guard, worth recording

The structural check first used a bare `indexOf('data-slot="dialog-close"')`, which found the
standalone `DialogClose` re-export near the top of the file instead of the button inside
`DialogContent` — comparing the wrong pair and **failing on correct code**. Anchored inside the
`DialogPrimitive.Content` render now. Same miscrediting-across-declarations shape as the fn-body
splitter in `member-write-authz.guard.test.ts`.

## Gates

322 files, **5105 tests**, zero skips (`TEST_DATABASE_URL` and `CHROME_PATH` wired, so the
browser-backed print suites — which render dialogs through real Chrome — actually ran). `typecheck`
clean. `biome check src/ --diagnostic-level=error` clean.

## Residual risk, stated plainly

**One dialog browser-verified, versus six for #619.** I intended to spot-check the worst case (the
member edit form, 768px of content) but the local session had expired and chasing the magic-link
token wasn't worth the time. The reasons I judge this low-risk: it is a single shared class string
plus one wrapper element with no per-dialog logic; the ceiling and the scroller both still exist,
only which element owns them changed; and the suite's component tests render several dialogs. The
honest residual is a dialog whose content interacts with the shell/body split in a way I did not
predict.

## Still open on #619

Keyboard occlusion. The viewport meta sets no `interactive-widget`, so the default `resizes-visual`
leaves the layout viewport and `svh` untouched when the keyboard opens, and this ceiling never
engages. Unchanged by this PR.

author: devside-dev-pro
body:
## Why

The BOT button returned `Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user` and the person **stayed in the queue**. Nothing distinguished a permanent block from a network hiccup, so nothing could remove them: click, error, same person tomorrow. A work queue that never empties stops being a queue.

## Three defects fed it

**The automatic nudge was the worst of them.** It wrote `status='done'` for a DM Telegram had refused — the note literally read `dm no-chat`. That counted as a contact, so the person was hidden for three days and came straight back, forever, having received nothing. Every night, another useless send.

**The admin BOT button recorded nothing on failure.** The reason lived only in the browser alert and died with it.

**`sendDm` returned a bare boolean**, so no caller could tell "blocked me" from "network was down".

## What changes

- `sendDm` keeps the refusal reason (`lastDmFailure()`, read immediately after the call).
- Both send paths — automatic and admin — now write `status='failed'` carrying the Telegram error.
- `lib/member/telegramErrors.ts` decides which failures are permanent. **Anything not explicitly recognised is treated as temporary**: getting that backwards would quietly erase a reachable prospect from the only list they appear in, and a wasted click is much the cheaper mistake.
- **Chronology decides**, never the mere existence of a past refusal. A block can be lifted, so a later successful send or an incoming `bot_reply` puts the person back in the queue.
- The automatic nudge stops retrying blocked people nightly.

## Removal is deliberately narrow

Only people with **no `@username`** are dropped from the queue. A blocked bot does not make someone unreachable — Mathieu's personal DM still lands, and that is the message that converts anyway. Removing all of them would empty the queue of contactable prospects, which is the same problem inverted.

Blocked people who do have a username keep their row, lose the BOT button, and get a `🚫 BOT BLOQUÉ` badge saying where to knock instead.

## One nuance in the automatic path

If the DM fails but the **push notification lands**, the person *was* reached. Writing `failed` there would have them nudged again tomorrow right after receiving a notification, so the failure is only recorded when neither channel got through.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `next build` compiles and type-checks.
- **Not exercised against Telegram.** The classifier is matched against Telegram's error strings from documentation and the observed `Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user`; the other strings are unverified in production. A string that fails to match degrades safely — the person simply stays in the queue, as today.
- The runner-side changes (`sendDm`, automatic nudge) **need a Railway restart**; the admin and queue changes ship with Vercel.

author: pythonlearner1025
body:
## The problem

`blitzos.com` serves `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/security` and `/landing` out of `packages/webapp/public/`. **Those files were never committed.** They were not ignored either — just untracked, living in one working tree.

Nothing imports them, so no build broke and no type check failed. Vite copies `public/` into `dist/`, and the Worker serves `dist/` through its `ASSETS` binding, so the pages stayed live for as long as the deploy ran from that one tree.

`release.yml` checks out clean. **The next `v*` tag would have quietly un-published the legal pages.**

Verified before this change:

```
$ git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- packages/webapp/public
(nothing)
$ curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://blitzos.com/terms
200
```

## The change

Track the eleven files, and name them in `packages/webapp/published-assets.json`. Two callers read that one manifest, so neither side can drift alone:

- `test/published-assets.test.ts` — a missing page fails CI on every push.
- `scripts/check-published-assets.mjs` — called by the control-plane deploy driver **before** it reads the Wrangler config or contacts Cloudflare. A failure there costs nothing, because no migration has been applied yet.

### Why the deploy driver and not `release.yml`

`release.yml` deploys by running `npm run deploy -w packages/control-plane`, so guarding the driver covers the tag path *and* every manual canary deploy. One check, both paths.

### Fails closed

An unreadable or empty manifest is an error, not a pass. A guard that reports success when it could not check anything is worse than no guard.

## Verification

Guard behaviour, each case exercised:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| all 11 present | exit 0, `published assets: 11 present` |
| `terms.html` missing | exit 1, names the file |
| `robots.txt` present but empty | exit 1, names the file |
| manifest unreadable | exit 1 (fails closed) |
| `deploy.mjs` with a page missing | aborts before any `wrangler` call |

Build output confirmed to carry all seven public routes after `npm run build -w @blitzos/webapp`.

## Gates

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm test` — `test:scripts` 15/15; webapp `published-assets` 12/12; control-plane 473 passed.
- `test/files.test.ts` fails on a 5s timeout in my sandbox. It fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` here, so it is environmental, not this change.
- `lint:gate` not run: oxlint aborts with a Rust allocator panic in this container, on unmodified `origin/main` too. CI covers it.

## Deploy

No migrations. No box-image change. Worker-only.

**This PR should land before the next `v*` tag.** Tagging without it drops the legal pages from production.

body:
## Root cause

The installed 2.0.12 Base reads only `desktop/latest.json`; freezing that pointer forever makes the 2.0.13 native updater unreachable. Base v7 cannot repair a predecessor before it is installed.

## Transition contract

- accept only the exact published 2.0.12 tombstone identity as the legacy CAS predecessor
- emit the same signed manifest bytes for manual, signed-feed, and legacy-bootstrap consumers
- enforce the 2.0.12 16 KiB manifest reader limit
- activate `desktop/signed/latest.json` first and the legacy bootstrap pointer last
- preserve installer URL/bytes/SHA and native transaction/rollback verification
- after migration Base v7 reads only the signed feed

This action still performs no Cloudflare write. The connected Cloudflare plugin remains the only publisher and must conditionally write and publicly read back both pointers.

## Check

`node --test`: 50/50 passed.

author: tsouza-in-automode
body:
Closes #169.

Both halves: the stale citations are corrected, and the format that guarantees they rot is replaced by one a check can actually resolve.

## Which convention, and why

**Cite the symbol, not the line.** `` `commit_loop.rs::read_current` `` — a file, `::`, the name of the thing; `` `commit_loop.rs::CommitError::DeadlineExceeded` `` where a bare name needs its container; `` `castle-core/src/backend.rs::StorageBackend` `` where a bare filename is ambiguous (three crates have a `backend.rs`).

The argument, in the order it actually decided the call:

- **A line-only check cannot be real.** A line number carries no way to tell whether it still points at the right thing — only whether the file is that long. A check that passes on a wrong-but-in-range number is worse than none, because it looks like enforcement. This repo has hit that exact failure class three times recently; #169 says not to add a fourth.
- **A symbol makes the check trivially real.** The named item either exists in the named file or it does not. That is a question a script can answer with no judgment and no false green.
- **It is already the repo's de-facto form.** Six citations in the tree were *already* written this way — `check-formal-model.mjs`, both `lib/*trace-conformance.mjs`, `verification/reclamation/README.md`, one `.cfg`, and one already-symbolic `commit_loop.rs::assemble_descriptor` in §11's own neighbourhood. Every one of those six resolves today. Every one of the seventeen line citations had rotted. The convention is being ratified, not invented.
- **The tree is moving under the citations right now.** `commit_loop.rs` changed several times today alone; `main` moved twice while this branch was open. Any line-number table in this repo is stale within a day of being written, by construction.

## 1. The staleness

**Seventeen stale line citations**, every one wrong, corrected against the files as they stand:

| doc said | actually |
|---|---|
| `commit_loop.rs:1328` / `:1337` (`read_current`, both GETs) | `read_current` opens at `:2012` |
| `commit_loop.rs:1435` (`stage`) | `:2190` |
| `commit_loop.rs:1523` (`advance`) | `:2276` |
| `commit_loop.rs:1104` (the retry loop) | `commit_observed`'s loop, `:1458` |
| `:1194` (`stage` call site) | `:1565` |
| `:1445`, `:1535` (disambiguating reads) | the `Indeterminate` arms in `stage` / `advance` |
| `:1096`, `:1106`, `:1428`, `:1519` (deadline checks) | `:1450`, `:1460`, `:2204`, `:2285` |
| `commit_loop.rs:1397` (`push_unique`) | `:2173` |
| `reaper.rs:825` (`reachable_segment_ids`) | `:834` |
| `reaper.rs:830`, in a test's module docs | same function, `:834` |
| `worked_sequence.rs:697`, in a test's module docs | the call is at `:693` |

Fourteen were in `docs/port-contracts.md` §11 and §12; three were in Rust doc comments, which is why the scan is over the whole tracked tree rather than `*.md`. `docs/compatibility.md`, `CONSTITUTION.md` and `README.md` carry none.

## 2. The check

`.github/scripts/check-code-citations.mjs`:

1. Every `path.rs::symbol` citation resolves — the path suffix must identify **exactly one** tracked file (ambiguity fails closed per §4, rather than passing if any candidate matches), and the symbol must be **defined** there. Definitions are read out of real code through `lib/strip-comments.mjs`, so a `fn read_current` that exists only inside a doc example is not a definition. A `Container::member` citation additionally requires the two to be *related* — `DeadlineExceeded` has to be a variant of `CommitError`, not merely another name in the same file.
2. `path.rs:NNN` is rejected anywhere in the tree. The convention is enforced mechanically or it is a sentence in `CONTRIBUTING.md` that the next author has not read.

Over-claiming is avoided explicitly in the header: it cannot tell whether the cited symbol *supports the sentence*, and it does not resolve bare backticked identifiers (almost all of which describe a port contract's required shape rather than citing an implementation). What it closes is exactly the class #169 found.

### Red/green, run locally

Renaming the cited function in the code — the drift a line number cannot see:

```
$ sed -i 's/fn read_current</fn read_current_state</' crates/castle-core/src/commit_loop.rs
$ node .github/scripts/check-code-citations.mjs; echo "EXIT=$?"
::error file=docs/port-contracts.md,line=1982::docs/port-contracts.md:1982: cites read_current, which crates/castle-core/src/commit_loop.rs does not define
... 5 findings ...
::error::code-citation check: 5 citation(s) do not resolve against the code.
EXIT=1
```

A typo'd symbol:

```
::error file=docs/port-contracts.md,line=1982::docs/port-contracts.md:1982: cites read_currrent, which crates/castle-core/src/commit_loop.rs does not define
EXIT=1
```

A line citation that is *currently correct* (`read_current` really is at `:2012`) — still rejected, because the form is the defect:

```
::error file=docs/compatibility.md,line=343::... cites commit_loop.rs:2012 — line-number citations are not admissible ...
EXIT=1
```

And the case that makes the convention worth having — 200 lines inserted above `read_current`, moving it from `:2012` to `:2212`, the edit that silently rots every line citation:

```
$ node .github/scripts/check-code-citations.mjs; echo "EXIT=$?"
::notice::code-citation check: clean — 27 symbol citation(s) resolved ...
EXIT=0
```

Restored in every case; the working tree ends clean.

## Where it runs

It shares the existing, **already-required** `constitution-refs` job (renamed in its display name to "Documentation citations"; the job key is a registered required-status context and is deliberately unchanged) rather than taking a status context of its own.

Reasoning, stated in the workflow header: a new context can only be made blocking by editing branch protection, which no PR can do atomically with the commit that adds the job. Registered before merge it blocks every in-flight PR on a check that does not exist on their branches; registered after merge it leaves a window in which the gate reports and does not block. Neither is acceptable for a gate whose whole subject is enforcement that only looks real. Sharing a job that is already required makes it blocking from the first commit that lands. Both scripts enforce the same sentence of §6 against the two things this repo's prose cites.

## Verification

```
$ node .github/scripts/check-constitution-refs.mjs
::notice::constitution-reference check: clean — 203 tracked file(s) scanned against 7 section(s) and 11 Keep Rule(s) parsed from CONSTITUTION.md.
EXIT=0

$ node .github/scripts/check-code-citations.mjs --self-test
selfTest OK
EXIT=0

$ node .github/scripts/check-code-citations.mjs
::notice::code-citation check: clean — 27 symbol citation(s) resolved against the code across 204 tracked file(s), and no line-number citations found.
EXIT=0

$ node .github/scripts/check-required-gates.mjs --self-test
selfTest OK
EXIT=0

$ node .github/scripts/check-anti-gaming.mjs        # after committing, rebased onto origin/main
::notice::Anti-gaming scan: no forbidden patterns found in added lines.
EXIT=0

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check          → EXIT=0
$ cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets → EXIT=0
$ cargo test --workspace --all-features → EXIT=0 (34 suites, 0 failed)
```

The `--self-test` carries a real-repo assertion as well as fixtures, so it cannot pass on a tree the real run would fail, and it asserts the scan found a non-zero number of citations — a clean verdict over zero citations would be vacuous.

No gate weakened, narrowed, or made conditional. No review cast from either account.

body:
## I measured the wrong rule in #3456. Correcting it changes the answer.

`#3456` modelled polarity as `uIbs >= 1 - ibsMax` — *the underlying sits at its session top*. That is scan.js mode **`TRADER_SHORT_EDGE=1`**. Both boxes run **`TRADER_SHORT_EDGE=selective`**, whose branch returns before that check is ever reached; `#3349` asks two different questions instead (has the wrapper already collapsed, is the underlying ripping) plus a p_win time penalty. So #3456's headline described a rule that is not armed. My error.

`experiments/polarity_mode_lab.js` runs all four modes over one universe and the same windows.

| mode | h1 ÷ | h2 ÷ | d-fit ÷ | d-hold ÷ | inverse trades (hourly) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `none` — longs only | 5.52 | 11.09 | 46.59 | 405 | 0 |
| **`top` — SHORT_EDGE=1** | **6.96** | **13.92** | **394.57** | **6,855** | 893 @ **0.155%**/trade |
| `selective` — **ARMED** | 4.96 | 7.48 | 91.15 | 833 | 511 @ 0.042%/trade |
| `both` | 5.39 | 7.84 | 84.28 | 760 | 489 @ 0.041%/trade |

## The armed rule is worse than taking no inverses at all

`selective` loses to longs-only on return/DD in **both halves of the hourly holdout** (÷2.28 / ÷5.51 vs ÷4.03 / ÷7.31). It buys inverse exposure at **a quarter** of the per-trade edge `top` gets, and pays drawdown for it.

`top` wins fit and holdout on both surfaces, wins **7 of 8 holdout years outright** and ties the eighth, and wins both halves of h2 taken separately. Its edge concentrates exactly where an inverse should pay:

```
mode                    19    20    21    22    23    24    25    26
none (longs only)      29%  163%   63%   93%   70%   30%   60%   60%
top  (SHORT_EDGE=1)    29%  407%   97%  452%  105%   62%  121%   93%
selective (ARMED)      30%  186%   81%  103%   96%   44%   78%   75%
```

## On the down-day question that started all this

Hourly holdout, SPY close-to-close down days: longs-only **−0.085%/trade**, `selective` **+0.093%**, `top` **+0.208%**.

So `selective` *does* fix down days — it just costs more elsewhere than it earns. `top` more than doubles the down-day fix while also improving the overall ratio.

## Two things the lab does not model — both make live `selective` worse than the row above

1. The `#3356` p_win time penalty (−7pp before 10:00, −4pp to 11:00) applies **only inside the selective branch**.
2. The "selection inputs unreadable → cannot certify" veto.

## Nothing is armed by this PR

`TRADER_SHORT_EDGE=1` loosens a guard that exists because `#3295` measured **−268R across 2,493 wrapper entries**. Those were polarity-**blind** entries — `top` is the fix for that failure rather than a return to it — but it is still the operator's call, and it roughly quadruples inverse participation (8.7% live today → ~34% in the lab). Recommendation: **arm `top` on race first** and let it run a week against stable on `selective`; that is what the race box is for.

## Companion

`#3457` fixes the ledger this investigation had to work around — 6,182 logged fires, 67 usable decisions, 43 of them written by a ghost process. Merge that first if you want the live half of this question to be answerable in a few weeks instead of never.

author: shzhng
body:
## Summary

- Install `ori` (OpenRouter's agent CLI) from the `shzhng/llm-agents.nix` fork branch `feat/add-ori` via a new `llm-agents-ori` flake input. Only `ori` is taken from the fork; every other agent CLI stays on the numtide input (the fork branch is well behind upstream main). The fork input follows our nixpkgs — fine here because ori is a prebuilt-binary fetch with no numtide cache to preserve.
- Wrap the binary so `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{SONNET,OPUS,HAIKU}_MODEL` default to `openrouter/auto` in ori sessions.
- Document the new tool in `modules/agents/AGENTS.md` and the follows-policy exception in the root `AGENTS.md`.
- Remove `claude-code-router` (package, overlay entry, and agent docs) — ori replaces it as the OpenRouter gateway for Claude Code.

## Why the wrapper

Claude Code's auto-mode permission classifier pins `claude-sonnet-5` via the tier-alias env vars rather than the main `model` setting, so ori sessions configured to `openrouter/auto` were still leaking a per-turn classifier call (~full context in, <10 tokens out) to paid Anthropic providers on OpenRouter. ori 0.10.2 doesn't set these vars itself, and it exposes no config surface for them (`--model` and the persona frontmatter only cover the main model). Wrapping with `--set-default` scopes the fix to ori launches — direct `claude` runs against Anthropic are untouched — and stays overridable per-invocation; once ori sets these itself the wrapper becomes a no-op to delete.

## Verification

- `nix flake lock` added the input cleanly
- Full darwin system closure builds; the built wrapper sets the three env defaults and `ori --version` runs
- Pre-commit hooks (nixfmt, statix, deadnix) pass

body:
## 摘要

- MAA 自带开始唤醒任务会原地轮询等待游戏内资源热更新（`GameStartUpdateOCR` / `GameStartCheckResourceOCR` 自循环），但对客户端 APK 版本落后导致的强制更新门没有任何任务，只会一直卡到超时并按重试次数反复失败。本 PR 只补 MAA 缺失的这一层，不重复实现热更新。
- 启动 MAA 前比对服务端与模拟器内的客户端版本：官服可自动下载安装包并经 adb 安装，安装后复检版本；其余服务器无可靠安装包来源，改为快速失败并推送可执行提示，避免静默卡到超时。
- 用服务端 `resVersion` 识别待下载的资源热更新，仅在该次运行把超时放宽到「游戏更新超时限制」，代理成功后记录版本供下次比对，避免把正常大版本热更误判成卡死。
- 新增 3 个脚本级配置项（默认全部关闭，不改变现有用户行为）：启动前检查游戏更新、自动安装游戏安装包（仅官服）、游戏更新超时限制。

## 实现要点

- `DeviceBase.get_adb_path()` 为非抽象方法、默认返回 `None`（回退系统 adb），MuMu 与雷电各自覆写返回自带 `adb.exe`，不破坏现有实现。
- 版本接口 `ak-conf.hypergryph.com/config/prod/{official,b}/Android/version` 实测可用；外服与台服未找到稳定公开接口，不在映射表中的服务器直接跳过检查。
- 服务器是**每用户**字段，包名与版本按用户运行时解析，不按脚本一次性解析。
- 检查自身异常、读不到已安装版本、取不到 adb 地址三种情况一律不阻断代理，交回 MAA 原有流程判定。
- 安装包约 2 GB：下载前校验磁盘余量，落盘走 `.downloading` 临时文件，体积明显偏小判定为未取到真实安装包，无论成败都清理不长期占用磁盘。

## 测试

- `python -m pytest tests/ -q`：206 passed / 7 failed。7 项失败在未改动的 `origin/dev` 上完全一致（199 passed / 同样 7 failed），与本 PR 无关；新增 7 项测试全部通过。
- 新增 `tests/task/test_maa_game_update.py` 覆盖版本比较（含段数不等、无法解析时不下判断）与编排层各分支判定。

## 待办与已知限制

- **后端 schema 有变更，需在后端运行时执行 `yarn openapi` 重新生成前端 API 代码**（`frontend/src/api/models/MaaConfig_Run.ts`、`MaaUserConfig_Data.ts`）。按规范未手改生成文件；`updateScript` 入参为 `any`，不阻塞当前功能。
- 仅官服支持自动安装，B 服与外服无可验证的安装包直链，当前明确提示手动更新。
- **APK 下载与 adb 安装链路未做端到端实测** —— 手上没有版本落后的客户端环境，无法构造真实的强制更新门。版本比对、编排分支判定、跳过与快速失败路径已由单测覆盖。
- 资源热更新期间 MAA 是否输出内容变化的日志行未实测（`LogMonitor.update_latest_timestamp` 仅在日志行内容变化时推进 `latest_time`），放宽超时是保守兜底而非依赖该行为。

## Sourcery 摘要

接管明日方舟客户端版本检查与官服自动更新，并为资源热更新放宽本次 MAA 代理超时。

新功能：
- 添加可选的明日方舟客户端版本检查功能，支持下载官服 APK 并通过 ADB 安装。
- 添加可配置的游戏更新超时处理，以及针对长时间游戏内更新的资源版本跟踪。
- 在 MAA 脚本配置界面中提供游戏更新检查、APK 自动安装和超时设置。

错误修复：
- 防止客户端版本过旧时，MAA 在强制更新界面反复卡住。
- 避免将预期的资源热更新延迟误判为 MAA 任务超时。

改进：
- 支持使用模拟器专用的 ADB 可执行文件，并在必要时回退到系统 ADB。
- 针对不受支持的服务器或自动更新失败的情况，提供用户通知和可执行的手动更新指引。

测试：
- 增加对客户端版本比较和游戏更新编排分支的测试覆盖。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

接管明日方舟客户端版本检查与官服自动更新，并为资源热更新放宽本次 MAA 代理超时。

New Features:
- Add optional pre-launch Arknights client version checks with official-server APK download and ADB installation support.
- Add configurable game-update timeout handling and resource-version tracking for prolonged in-game updates.
- Expose game-update checking, automatic APK installation, and timeout settings in the MAA script configuration UI.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent outdated client versions from repeatedly stalling MAA at the forced-update screen.
- Avoid treating expected resource hot-update delays as MAA task timeouts.

Enhancements:
- Support emulator-specific ADB executables with fallback to the system ADB.
- Provide user notifications and actionable manual-update failures for unsupported servers or unsuccessful automatic updates.

Tests:
- Add coverage for client-version comparison and game-update orchestration branches.

</details>

Two comments that would actively mislead a reader. No behaviour change.

author: simonfrets
body:
Scaffolds `agentic-harness`: a distributable TypeScript package that installs a project-local `.harness/` folder — exclusive to each project, the way `.claude/` is — and drives a six-agent pipeline through vendor CLI adapters.

```
specifier ──▶ coder ──▶ cleaner ──▶ architect ──▶ hardener ──▶ qa ──▶ done
     ▲                                  │             │          │
     └──────────── rejection ───────────┴─────────────┴──────────┘
```

## What's here

**Six agents**, defined as vendor-neutral YAML and compiled to `.claude/agents/*.md`. Opus at xhigh effort where the work is judgement under ambiguity (specifier, architect, hardener); Sonnet where it is high-volume editing under a verifier (coder, cleaner, qa). Each declares its own model, effort, tool allowlist, `write_scope`, rules and handoff checklist.

Two write scopes are load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the **architect** and **hardener** cannot edit `src/`. A structural finding therefore has to become a rejection with a concrete change, and a coverage hole has to be closed by a better test.

**Gates that actually block.** Prompts ask; gates decide. Every handoff runs:

| Gate | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `write-scope` | the worktree diff escapes the agent's declared globs |
| `tdd-pair` | `src/**` moved and `tests/**` did not |
| `red-receipt` | a new test has no receipt, **or** the receipt's source snapshot is unchanged — i.e. it was recorded after the implementation |
| `rule:*` | any blocking rule's check script exits non-zero |

A failure sets the task to `blocked`, records which gate failed, and stops the pipeline where it broke. The `[skip-tdd: <reason>]` escape hatch requires a reason, and the reason is written to the task event log.

**`tasks.yaml`** is the shared work record: atomic writes under a `mkdir`-based lock (macOS has no `flock(1)`), with an append-only `events/<task>.jsonl` history. Committed, so a task survives a session.

**Context isolation.** Each agent sees one document: its own prompt, its own rules, the task row, the accepted spec, and the *summary* of the handoff addressed to it — never another agent's transcript.

**Rules are one markdown file** with `applies_to`, `advisory|blocking`, and an optional `check:` script. Ten ship by default; `harness rules add <id>` scaffolds more.

**Out-of-the-box enforcement.** `harness init` wires a type-aware ESLint config, strict TypeScript settings, `pre-commit` + `commit-msg` hooks and a CI workflow — creating what is missing and never overwriting what exists.

## Verification

- **189 tests** (172 unit, 17 shell), lint and typecheck clean
- Core coverage: 95.9% statements, 83.1% branches, 100% functions, 97.9% lines
- The shell suite drives the real runtime against fake adapter binaries, so the full pipeline is exercised at zero API cost
- Verified end-to-end in a scratch project: the pipeline advanced through stages and the blocking rules fired exactly where they should

## Notes for review

- Coverage thresholds scope to `src/core` only. `src/cli` is driven out-of-process by the shell suite, so in-process instrumentation cannot see it; measuring it would report a meaningless number. Documented in `jest.config.mjs`.
- `crap.ts` and `specs/lint.ts` were written implementation-first, then tested. The other eleven modules were genuinely test-first.
- `codex` and `shellcheck` are not installed on the dev machine. Codex is verified against a contract double in `tests/fixtures/bin/`; shell linting skips with a warning and runs for real in CI. `harness doctor` reports both.
- The base commit on `main` is an empty root commit, created because `git worktree` needs a resolvable HEAD and the repository had none.

author: sss-dclemente
body:
## Why

CI runs `vitest` against **source**. Nothing checks what `npm pack` actually produces, and `release.yml` publishes to npm on any `v*` tag — so a tool that fails to register, a missing `dist` file, or a stray file in the tarball all pass CI and surface only after publishing.

[#9](https://github.com/sss-dclemente/dataverse-mcp-pro/pull/9) caught a stale tool count in the manual smoke test. [#10](https://github.com/sss-dclemente/dataverse-mcp-pro/pull/10) replaced that document with a live-org checklist — the right scope for it — but left nothing verifying the artifact itself. This restores that gate as an automated check rather than a doc step, since this exact document has now gone stale twice.

## What it does

`scripts/verify-package.mjs`, wired into `release.yml` ahead of `npm publish` and available as `npm run verify:package`:

1. Packs the tarball and checks the file list against `package.json` `files`
2. Checks the `bin` entry is actually in the tarball
3. Unpacks it and boots the **packed** server over stdio
4. Compares the tools it exposes against `src/tools/index.ts`
5. Checks every tool has a non-empty description

## The tool count is anchored to source, deliberately

Comparing the packed server against `dist/tools/index.js` compares the build to itself. I confirmed this is not theoretical — with a tool removed from the built registry, that check reports:

```
ok: packed server exposes all 19 registered tools
```

and passes. `src/tools/index.ts` is the one input the build cannot influence, and it is what actually catches the drop.

## Every check was verified to fail on a real defect

Not just to pass on a good build:

| Injected defect | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tool dropped from the built registry | `FAIL: src/tools/index.ts registers 20 tools but the packed server exposes 19` — exit 1 |
| Packed server cannot boot (broken import in `dist/server.js`) | `FAIL: packed server produced no tools/list response` — exit 1 |
| `src/` leaked into the tarball via `package.json` `files` | `FAIL: tarball contains unexpected files: ...` — exit 1 |

Happy path on a clean build:

```
packed simplesmoothsafe-dataverse-ops-mcp-0.3.1.tgz
ok: tarball file list is clean (87 files)
ok: bin entry "dist/server.js" is present
ok: packed tool count matches src/tools/index.ts (20)
ok: packed server exposes all 20 registered tools
ok: every tool has a non-empty description

packed artifact verified.
```

## Known limitation, stated in the script header

The tarball is unpacked **inside the repo** so Node resolves runtime deps from the repo's `node_modules` — the artifact ships none of its own. So this checks the packed *code*, not that `package.json` declares every dependency it imports: a dep missing from `dependencies` would still resolve here and fail for a real consumer. Documented in the header rather than left implied.

## Notes

- Needs no Dataverse org or credentials — the client is built lazily, so `tools/list` answers with no environment set.
- Transient `.tgz` and unpack directories are gitignored and removed in a `finally` block; `git status` is clean after a run.
- `docs/smoke-test.md` keeps #10's live-org framing untouched; this is added as a separate pre-tag section rather than folded into the live checklist.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, 261 tests passing, `verify:package` green.

---

author: rubys
body:
`f0a93f3d` ("Type a poly call for what BOTH of its arms can hold") added the question the poly-receiver section was missing — does the builtin surface answer this name with a type the arms' shared temp can hold? — and asking it costs a full re-inference of the call under `an_builtin_only`.

The ask sits inside the fixpoint, so the same call node is asked again every time inference revisits it. Counted on a 51k-line Rails emit (Roundhouse's lobsters tree):

```
294,164 asks over ~18k distinct nodes
283,251 of them (96%) a repeat of a node already asked in that same iteration
```

So the answer is being recomputed, not discovered. This memoizes it per node on the narrow generation, which `sp_narrow_memo_bump` already bumps once per fixpoint iteration and which therefore releases every answer as soon as the types move.

## Measured

Interleaved A/B, two builds on one fixed tree (311 files / 51,277 lines), master `55638986`:

| config | master | this PR | ceiling (ask removed outright) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--rbs .` | 25.3s | **22.3s** | 21.1s |
| no `--rbs` | 30.0s | **29.0s** | — |

About three quarters of the available win, with the check intact. The two configs differ because the seeded run asks three times as often (294k vs 91k).

For context on why this was worth chasing: on this tree analyze has gone 23.2s → 30.0s since `72ea742a` (three days), and this is the larger of the two contributions I could attribute.

## Verification

- `make check`: **3244 pass, 1 fail, 0 error** — byte-for-byte the same as master in the same worktree layout. The one failure is `sp_net_write_partial`, which already fails on master here (macOS); not touched by this change.
- `make infer-test`: pass, on master and on this branch.
- Emitted C **identical modulo `#line`** on two apps × two configs: the lobsters tree (109,396 lines) and the blog fixture (18,380 lines), each with and without `--rbs .`.
- `--emit-rbs` output byte-identical on both apps, both configs.

## One thing I want to flag rather than bury

I first tried keying this on `(name, argc, block?)`, reasoning that under `an_builtin_only` the receiver is poly so the answer could not turn on the node. That was wrong, and a conflict detector — compute the real answer every time, compare against what a memo would have served — found 452 disagreements on this tree. `--emit-rbs` was byte-identical anyway, which is exactly why I do not think output equality alone is sufficient evidence for a change like this. Node-keying is what the detector supports.

Even node-keyed, the answer is stable across the repeats but not perfectly: **2 asks of 87,033** saw it change within a single iteration, both `comments_path`, both `TY_ENUMERATOR` then `TY_UNKNOWN`. The memo pins the first, so those two take the earlier answer; `TY_UNKNOWN` is the "no opinion" arm of the guard below, so pinning `TY_ENUMERATOR` is the more conservative of the two (it can widen to `TY_POLY` where master would return `r`). It changed no output on either app, and the code comment says so rather than claiming stability I did not measure.

Separately, and not a claim about this patch: a builtin answer that goes from a type to `TY_UNKNOWN` partway through one iteration means information is being lost mid-walk, which seems worth a look on its own. I have not investigated it and am happy to open it as an issue if it is interesting to you.

author: tiramisioux
body:
Makes `resources/sensors.json` the single source of truth for CSI-2 link frequencies, replacing the imx585-only table that was hardcoded in `boot_config.py` when the menu first shipped.

## Why

The hardcoded table was already a second place sensor capabilities are written down, next to `sensors.json` itself. It would only have grown as other sensors gained menus, and this repo has been bitten by two-copy drift before — the `ACTION_METHODS` catalogue is the standing example.

## What changed

All five sensors now carry a `link_frequency` block, sibling of `log_encode` — **including the ones with nothing to choose**, because an absent block reads as "capability unknown" and every one of these has a known answer:

| Sensor | Lanes | Default | Menu | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| imx585 | 4 | 720 MHz | yes | 297 / 360 / 445.5 / 594 / 720 / 891 / 1039.5 MHz |
| imx283 | 4 | 720 MHz | yes | 360 / 720 MHz — 720 is also the ceiling |
| imx477 | 2 | 450 MHz | **gated off** | driver takes any ~3 MHz multiple (kernel ≥ 6.12.49) |
| imx296 | 1 | 594 MHz | no | fixed |
| imx519 | 2 | 408 MHz | no | fixed |

Notable entries:

- **imx585's 1188 MHz** is recorded under `excluded` with its reason (frame drops on Pi 5, unsupported on Pi 4), so it can't be re-added by someone reading only the driver's `link_freqs[]`.
- **imx283** closes a standing question. Sony ships exactly two register sequences, and 720 MHz is both default and silicon ceiling, so the only selectable value is *slower*. The 4K modes' 44/41 fps are the link ceiling at those bit depths — more frame rate means lower bit depth, not a faster link.
- **imx477's** menu is held back behind `menu_enabled: false` until its 750 MHz hardware gate passes. Its driver's check is arithmetic with no upper bound, so the recorded values are curated presets rather than a list the driver vouches for.

## Structure

One loader (`src/module/sensor_database.py`) now serves both `SensorDetect` and `boot_config`; two loaders would mean two sets of fallback rules to keep in step. Stdlib only, so `boot_config` stays importable with no Redis and no camera attached. A missing block means unsupported; a malformed one warns rather than passing silently as an absence.

The settings editor is served its menus from Python and holds no frequency values of its own. `tools/link_frequency_drift_check.py` fails the build if any database frequency reappears as a literal in the template, and is wired into `checks.yml`. It gates *data*, not logic: `cfgOverlayLine` necessarily mirrors `overlay_line_for` because the drawer previews a line the server writes.

## Verification

- 534 tests pass, including new database-schema assertions and rewritten link-frequency tests that now read from the database.
- All five CI checks green (four existing plus the new drift check).
- Drift check confirmed to *catch* injected duplication, not merely pass.
- JS preview and Python writer produce identical overlay lines across all 96 model/port/frequency combinations.
- Docs build clean.

## Not verified on hardware

None of this is Pi-tested. Gates 1–3 are written up with predictions stated in advance in `development/rp1-overclock/HARDWARE-GATES.md`, along with the two preconditions blocking them: the settings editor still cannot write `config.txt` on the dev Pi (missing sudoers grant for the privileged helper), and that Pi has an imx477 attached rather than an imx585.

One risk worth flagging for review: selecting a non-default imx283 value requires the `link-frequency` overlay parameter added to `Tiramisioux/imx283-v4l2-driver` `6.12.y` at `257c9cf`. An **older overlay rejects the unknown parameter and the camera will not enumerate at all**. The minimum revision is recorded in the database notes and in the docs, and it is Gate 3. Say the word if you would rather ship imx283 gated off like imx477 until that gate runs — it is a one-line change.

author: andybons
body:
Slice 3 of 4 for `docs/design/mcp-lazy-tools.md` (spec PR #167). Stacked on #175 → #177. **Do not merge.**

## Problem

A loaded MCP tool schema lived only in memory. A restarted box, or a session evicted and reloaded from disk, came back with an empty selected set: every tool the model had loaded was deferred again, and it had to rediscover and re-select tools it had already chosen — silently, mid-task.

## What to scrutinize

1. **Two writers, one path.** `markMCPToolsSelected` persists under the same `s.mu` the mutation holds (the `SetModel`/`RegisterGoal` shape), and both `select` and use-implies-selection funnel through it. Wiring only `select` loses the tool the model *used* but never selected — `TestRoutedCallSelectionSurvivesReload` is red-verified against exactly that mistake.
2. **The replay guard mirrors the write guard.** A malformed name is skipped on load, exactly as `select` refuses to record one. One rule at both ends of the record's life.
3. **The recovery pair.** From one log shape (a name recorded while its server was down): if the server reconnects *with* the tool, it arms with no second `select`; if it reconnects *without* it, the name is reaped on the first plan. That pair is what proves the reap closes the hallucinated-name hole without breaking self-heal. A third case — the server never returns — keeps the name waiting.
4. **Write volume.** A name already in the set writes nothing: a repeat `select` and a tool called a hundred times leave one record, not a hundred (`TestRepeatSelectionWritesOneRecord`).
5. **Payload.** One record per call, carrying `selected` and `pending` together and neither `already` nor `missing` (`TestSelectJournalsSelectedAndPendingTogether`).

## Verification

Seven guards red-verified by reverting the exact mechanism each names:

| Guard | Mechanism reverted |
|---|---|
| `TestSelectionSurvivesReload` | journaling removed |
| `TestRoutedCallSelectionSurvivesReload` | routed-call writer bypassed the journaling path |
| `TestReplaySkipsMalformedAndDedupes` | replay folded every name |
| `TestRepeatSelectionWritesOneRecord` | empty-input no-op removed |
| `TestSelectJournalsSelectedAndPendingTogether` | `pending` not recorded |
| `TestRestoredSelectionOfAbsentServerIsKept` | reap ignored connection state |
| `TestInventedPendingSelectionIsReapedAfterReload` | reap removed |

One note on flakiness, for transparency: a first full-suite run failed `server/TestLegacySessionIDOverHTTP` with `TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: directory not empty` — a cleanup race, not an assertion failure. It does not reproduce (`-count=5 -race` on this branch, `-count=10 -race` on the base, and a full `./server/` run, all green), and that test builds sessions with no MCP registry at all, so nothing in this slice runs in it. Flagging it rather than hiding it.

Third slice of the full-UI-control program. Kills a silent-failure class the UI audit flagged: every data-read panel caught a failure and rendered a generic **"Offense engine offline"**, discarding the error — so a backend 4xx/5xx was indistinguishable from a down plane.

**What & why**
- Now that WS0's `getJSON` attaches `.status`/`.data`/server `.error`, **`offlineEmpty(err)`** distinguishes: a failure **with** a status = the plane is reachable but the endpoint erred → shows **"Request failed (<status>)"** + the real server message; a failure with **no** status = a fetch/network failure → the genuine offline state (panel-specific hint preserved via an optional 2nd arg).
- Threaded the error through **every** read-panel catch (Findings/Brain via the shared helper; Tools, Trust, Posture, Governance, Live, MCP, System, Budgets, Library inline). The only inline "offline" markup left is the helper itself and the flag-based Background panel (no error object). Net **−12 lines** (de-dupes empty-state markup).

**Verification**: `node --check` clean; contract-guard test (docs/tests, 3); server messages render as **text nodes** (no innerHTML) so no injection from an error body. Mechanical refactor, self-reviewed against the WS0 red-pen's XSS/behavior findings.

body:
## Audit cleanup

Fixes the P0 truth-boundary issue found during the 25 Aug 2026 full-system audit.

### Problem
FateDrop deliberately preserves last-good retailer catalogues when a retailer becomes blocked, timed out or stale. The consumer `/api/catalogue`, `/api/true-price` and canonical Fate Verdict path were reading those preserved offer rows without first enforcing effective retailer health, so a stale retailer could theoretically appear as live stock or win a value comparison.

### Fix
- adds a read-only live-offer store facade
- includes offers only when the decorated Cloud retailer-health row is `healthy=true` and `stale!=true`
- fails closed to zero live offers if retailer health cannot be established
- keeps the underlying store untouched for monitoring/history
- routes only consumer Catalogue, True Price and Fate Verdict through the filtered view
- internal scan/ingest/history/status routes retain the authoritative unfiltered store

### Regression coverage
- fresh vs stale/unhealthy/unknown retailer filtering
- health-unavailable fail closed
- underlying store remains intact
- HTTP Catalogue excludes stale stock
- True Price cannot choose a cheaper stale offer
- Fate Verdict inherits the same boundary

No production database mutation or retailer bypass is included.

body:
## 背景

`npm audit` が high 7件を報告していた。すべて推移依存だが、うち複数は**本リポジトリの実コードに該当経路がある**:

| Advisory | 該当経路 |
|---|---|
| GHSA-6gpp-xcg3-4w24 Middleware / Proxy bypass | `proxy.ts`(Supabaseセッション更新を担う) |
| GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj Server Actions の DoS | Server Actions を5ファイルで使用 |
| GHSA-955p-x3mx-jcvp Server Function エンドポイントの未認証露出 | 同上 |
| GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 AVIF 画像最適化の未認証 RCE(16.3.3で修正) | 画像最適化APIがビルドに含まれる |

本番(https://plandiff.vercel.app)が公開済みのため放置できない。

仕様書: [`docs/specs/S-1_依存関係のセキュリティ更新.md`](docs/specs/S-1_依存関係のセキュリティ更新.md)

## 変更内容

`package.json` の変更は **2行だけ**(`next` / `eslint-config-next`)。残りは lockfile の再解決で解消した。

| パッケージ | 更新 | 手段 |
|---|---|---|
| `next` | 16.2.10 → **16.3.3** | 直接依存 |
| `eslint-config-next` | 16.2.10 → **16.3.3** | `next` と同期(既存方針) |
| `sharp` | 0.34.5 → **0.35.3** | next 16.3.3 が `^0.35.3` を要求 |
| `postcss` | 8.4.31 / 8.5.16 → **8.5.23**(1本にdedupe) | next が 8.5.23 を厳密固定し、Tailwind/vite の範囲も満たすため |
| `nanoid` | 3.3.15 → **3.3.18** | 範囲内 |
| `undici` | 7.28.0 → **7.29.0** | 範囲内(`jsdom` の major 上げは不要) |
| `brace-expansion` | 1.1.15 → **1.1.18** / 5.0.7 → **5.0.9** | 範囲内 |
| `js-yaml` | 4.3.0 → **4.3.1** | 範囲内 |

`npm audit fix --force` は使わず、バージョンを明示した `npm install` / `npm update` で行った。

### CI に監査ステップを追加

`npm ci` の直後に `npm audit --audit-level=high` を追加。閾値を `high` にしたのは、`moderate` まで含めると常時赤になり CI が「無視されるチェック」に退化するため。

## 注意点

- **`next` 更新後に high 2件が新規に浮上した**(`brace-expansion` / `js-yaml`)。`eslint-config-next` 16.3.3 が ESLint ツールチェーンを入れ替えたことによる。結果として計9件を解消している。**依存更新は1回では終わらず、更新後にもう一度 `npm audit` を回す必要がある**
- `brace-expansion` は **1.1.18 と 5.0.9 の2本が残るのが正しい**。`eslint@9` 配下の `minimatch@3` が `^1.1.7`、`typescript-eslint` 配下の `minimatch@10` が `^5.0.5` を要求しており semver 上1本化できない。`overrides` で固めるとどちらかの `minimatch` が壊れる
- `AGENTS.md` の差分は `next dev` による再生成。全体が `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` ブロックでユーザー記述の消失はなく、生成文言自身がコミットを指示している
- `package-lock.json` の diff が大きいのは、再解決で各プラットフォーム向け optional バイナリが追加されたため。クリーンな `npm ci` の成功をもって正としている

## 検証結果

| シナリオ | 結果 |
|---|---|
| S1 監査 | `found 0 vulnerabilities`、`--audit-level=high` EXIT=0 |
| S2 `npm run check` | EXIT=0。単体・コンポーネント **128ファイル791件 全合格**(更新前と同一件数)、lint の新規エラーなし |
| S3 結合テスト | **25ファイル152件 全合格** |
| S4 R-1 のTZ確認 | `TZ=UTC` 791件 / `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` 791件 とも全合格 |
| S5 クリーンインストール | `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` 成功 |
| S6 375px | `/`・`/calendar`・`/summary`(今日/今週のグラフ)・`/settings`・`/track` をライト/ダーク両方で確認。横スクロール0・はみ出し要素0・コンソールエラー0。オーバーレイとグラフの描画に崩れなし |
| S7 CI | 本PRのCIで確認 |

**DB変更・環境変数の追加・アプリコードの変更はなし**(`db push` 不要)。

## 切り戻し

`git revert` で完全に戻る。マイグレーションなし、Vercel側の設定変更なし。

author: mattsse
body:
Ethereum event selectors omit indexed parameter placement, but canonical event decoding trusted the indexed flags on global metadata even though that metadata was not tied to the emitting address. A contract using the same canonical event signature and indexed count with different indexed fields could therefore produce syntactically valid but incorrect decoded values.

This enumerates compatible layouts whenever canonical decoding falls back to global metadata and returns decoded output only when exactly one layout succeeds. Address-scoped ABIs remain authoritative, and legacy trace decoding retains its best-effort behavior.

Follow-up to #16238.

## 📋 Summary
Addresses item 4 of #577: extracts a shared `SongTable.svelte` component and migrates all 5 song-table call sites (`AlbumDetailView`, `CollectionView`, `ArtistDetailView`, `AutoPlaylistDetailView`, `PlaylistView`) to use it, eliminating ~2,000 lines of duplicated table markup.

## 🔍 Implementation Notes
- `SongTable.svelte` is data-driven off the existing `SONG_TABLE_COLUMNS` config and covers the variance between call sites via props: `mode` (`"track"` disc-aware numbering vs `"position"` for ordered lists), `virtualized`/`scrollMemoryKey` (CollectionView), `onReorder` + pointer-based drag-to-reorder (PlaylistView), `isRowPlaying` override (needed so PlaylistView can disambiguate duplicate songs via `playlistItemUuid` rather than song id), `interactiveWhenDisabled`/`disabledPlaceholder` (PlaylistView's unavailable-track handling), and `positionSortField` (sortable position header for AutoPlaylistDetailView/PlaylistView).
- Also extracted the shared sort comparator into `src/lib/utils/songSort.ts`, used by all 5 views.
- Selection (click/shift/ctrl-click, Ctrl+A, Escape, click-outside-to-clear) and pointer-based drag-reorder logic now live once in `SongTable.svelte` instead of being duplicated per view.
- Beyond pure dedup, two intentional (user-approved mid-implementation) changes:
  - Row styling normalized to one consistent look across all 5 views (thumbnail, primary-colored text throughout, clickable album link) rather than preserving each view's previously-inconsistent styling.
  - `ArtistDetailView`'s singles table gained multi-select (it previously had none), for consistency with every other table now offering the same interactions.
- No backend changes; no intended change to playback, drag-reorder, or dynamic-playlist behavior.

author: gordonkjlee
body:
## Infrastructure Change

### Summary
Stop treating npm's publish-time malware scan as a failed release. The verify job now waits out the documented scan window, does not republish a version that is already accepted, and opens distinct issues for "not on the registry" vs "on the registry but broken".

### Stakeholder
N/A

### Links
**Ticket:** N/A — GitHub Actions emails and issues [#152](https://github.com/gordonkjlee/openmemory/issues/152) / [#157](https://github.com/gordonkjlee/openmemory/issues/157) (closed as false alarms)
**Requirements:** N/A

---

### Description
**What failed:** both v0.16.0 and v0.17.0 **published successfully**. `npm publish` printed `Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available.` The follow-up verify job polled `npm view` for 150 seconds, got 404s, failed the workflow, emailed, and opened "not usable from npm" issues. The packages appeared on the registry about seven minutes later (0.17.0: publish 22:03:54Z, registry time 22:11:03Z). Users were never stuck on the previous tag.

**Why 150s was wrong:** that bound was added for CDN propagation (July 2026). On 28 July 2026 npm started scanning packages at publish time before they are installable — typically around five minutes, up to 15+ at peak. The loop bound is shorter than the typical scan. The job timeout (10 minutes) was a second clock that would have killed a longer loop.

**What else was fragile:** during the scan window `npm view pkg@version` 404s even though npm has accepted the tarball. A second workflow_run in that window would try to publish again and 403 `cannot publish over the previously published versions` — a red X for a fine package. `npm dist-tag` continues to work during the scan.

**Fix:**
- When this run accepted a publish (or dist-tag already names the version), wait up to 20 minutes for `npm view` to resolve. If publish never ran, wait 3 minutes — do not sit for 20 minutes to admit a miss.
- Job timeout 30 minutes so the wait is not killed by a shorter clock.
- Treat 403 already-published as success; skip republish when dist-tag already points at the version.
- Issues distinguish "did not become installable" from "on npm but smoke test failed", and include publish-job result and wait budget.

The verify job still fails closed after the wait. A red X plus an assigned issue remains the notification if the package truly never lands or does not run.

---

### Testing
`python` YAML parse of `publish.yml` succeeds. Extracted `run:` scripts pass `bash -n`. The 403 matcher hits `cannot publish over the previously published versions` and ignores unrelated errors. The dist-tag matcher hits `latest: 0.17.0` / `next: 0.17.0` and not a different version.

This workflow only runs on Release Please completion or `workflow_dispatch`, so the PR CI job will not exercise a live publish. After merge, a dispatch against current `main` should skip publish (`v0.17.0 already on npm`) and pass verify on the short wait. The 20-minute path only runs on the next real publish.

---

### Impact Assessment
No package or MCP contract change. Verify may take up to ~20 minutes after a real `npm publish` instead of failing at 150s. False-alarm issues and Actions emails for a package that is still scanning should stop. Rollback: revert this workflow file.

Do not merge the open `chore(main): release 0.18.0` PR until this is on `main`, or 0.18.0 will false-alarm the same way.

---

### Complexity
- [ ] Simple (config tweak, dependency update)
- [x] Moderate (new workflow, migration change)
- [ ] Complex (core infrastructure change, many dependencies)

---

### Checklist
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds — N/A, workflow YAML only
- [x] `npm test` passes — N/A, workflow YAML only
- [x] Testing complete (migration tested, workflow triggered, or config validated) — YAML parse, bash -n, matcher probes; live publish path waits for the next release
- [x] No personal data or real memory content in the diff or this description (synthetic only)
- [x] Code follows project standards
- [x] Code is production-ready and can be reviewed

author: toresbe
body:
## What

In the organisation schedule planner, a weekly slot is now rendered as a container that holds the programmes scheduled into it, instead of vanishing as soon as it was filled.

## Why

`plannerRows` only emitted a `weeklySlot` row when *nothing* overlapped the reservation. A weekly slot reserves airtime that the scheduler fills with one or more programmes, so in practice the slot disappeared the moment it did its job, and its programmes appeared as a flat run of sibling rows each labelled "Ukentlig sendeflate". A one-hour slot holding four videos read as four unrelated items.

## How

- `PlannerRow`'s `weeklySlot` variant now carries `items: ScheduleitemRead[]`. An item joins a slot occurrence when `item.weeklySlot === slot.id` and it overlaps the window; those items are removed from the top-level timeline and nested.
- A slot whose airtime is taken by programming that does *not* name it is still dropped, as before — nesting unrelated items under a slot header would misattribute them.
- A slot row's span widens to cover programming that overruns its reservation, so the surrounding gaps stay honest.
- In `SchedulePlanner`, the item `<li>` became a `renderItem(item, insideSlot)` helper reused at both levels, so nested programmes keep their Erstatt/Endre/Fjern buttons. Nested rows drop the now-redundant "Ukentlig sendeflate" subtitle and show their real status instead. An empty slot reads "Ingen programmer er lagt inn i sendeflaten ennå."
- Drive-by fix: the action buttons jumped between right- and left-alignment depending on whether the title wrapped. `justify-between` on a `flex-wrap` row aligns a lone wrapped child to flex-start; the action group is now pushed right with `ms-auto`, and the text column got `min-w-0` so long names wrap instead of overflowing.

## Notes for review

- The item-belongs-to-slot rule is deliberately `weeklySlot === slot.id` rather than plain overlap. Worth a second opinion if the backend ever leaves that field null on items the scheduler placed into a slot.
- A filled slot whose programmes don't cover the whole reservation shows no "remaining free time" affordance inside the container. That felt like a behaviour question rather than presentation, so it's left out.
- Three new tests cover nesting, overrun, and the taken-airtime case. tsc, eslint, prettier and the 43 schedule tests pass. Not visually verified in a running app — the local dev database has no schedule, so that would need the API stubbed.
