### Motivation

- Convert the repository to a purely public, browser-only Free Business Plan Generator that requires no backend services, authentication, payments, or AI provider access. 
- Remove legacy server-side, commercial, and admin codepaths (Supabase, Stripe, AI generation) so the app is suitable for static hosting (S3 + CloudFront). 
- Preserve all client-side financial modelling, PDF/XLSX exports, local draft persistence, and UI flows used by the free product.

### Description

- Removed backend, commercial and AI modules and assets, including `src/lib/ai`, `src/lib/admin`, `src/lib/payments`, `src/lib/supabase`, the `supabase` directory, and the SQL `migrations` and database generation scripts and many docs that described server-side setup. 
- Simplified and kept only client-side export types and renderers (PDF/XLSX), retained `src/lib/free-exports.ts`, and moved/trimmed financial-review logic to a browser-only normalization and local hash in `src/financial-review.ts`. 
- Updated tooling and packaging by removing the Supabase dev dependency, renaming the package to `thebizplans-free-business-plan-generator`, pruning server-oriented scripts, and adding a README describing static deployment (build → `dist`). 
- Added a small regression test for local draft storage (`test/local-draft-storage.test.js`) and adjusted/retained the core financial tests and export tests while removing tests that targeted removed backend/AI/payment features.

### Testing

- Ran TypeScript checks with `npm run type-check` and targeted automated tests with `node --test` (selected financial engine, analysis, export, payroll, loans, and draft-persistence tests); the targeted suite passed (73 tests passed, 0 failed). 
- Built the production bundle with `npm run build` (Vite) and verified `dist/` was produced successfully. 
- Verified there are no unresolved relative imports and inspected the tree and grep results to confirm removal of Supabase/Stripe/OpenAI operational references.

body:
Answers everything from the last live test of the reel builder on /quick.

## The analysis is watchable now
The mp4 you attached showed the real problem: the analysis wasn't too fast because of the 2× — its cut defaulted to **2 beats ≈ 0.94s of a 5.5-second breakdown**, so you saw a sixth of it. Now:
- **Auto hold**: by default the analysis holds exactly long enough to play the whole breakdown at its speed. Nothing is cut off unless you ask for it.
- **Its own editor**: tap the analysis tile (after the song is attached) to choose how many beats it holds and its breakdown speed — 1×, 1.5×, or 2×.

## Adjust the beats of every clip
Tap any clip → **"Plays for"**: Auto (the pace decides) or 1/2/3/4/6/8 beats, each priced in seconds at the song's tempo. Pins are honoured exactly — the totals stay whole-beat, the spares go to the unpinned clips, and the planner never silently shrinks a length you chose (the window grows instead). With a drop marked, the reveal never moves: before-side pins are capped at the drop, after-side pins extend the reel.

## The transport you asked for
- **Space** pauses and resumes **from where you paused** — never back to the start of the clip.
- **← / →** step one frame (1/30s) along the song; **shift + arrow** steps a whole beat. The paused position shows as a dimmer playhead and is exactly where play resumes.

## The waveform tells the truth
- The **drop is a full-height red line labelled DROP** — the loudest mark on the canvas, like you asked.
- **Every beat gets a small tick along the bottom**; bars keep their taller blue marks.

## Why it only allowed 1 or 4 clips before the drop
That was real: each clip before the drop needs at least one beat, so a drop N beats after the window start fits at most N clips before it. Your drop sat 1 beat in, so the planner clamped to 1 — but the input silently accepted 4. The input now states its true ceiling and the note explains it: *"the drop is 8♩ after the start, so at most 2 clips fit before it."*

## Live preview
**► Preview the reel** plays the whole plan in real time in a phone-shaped frame — the song from your chosen start, clips seeked and cut exactly where the export will cut them, the analysis synthesised the same way the encoder does it. Same `activeCut`, same `coverRect`, same draw code as the render, so what it shows is what exports. Any edit stops it (a preview of a stale plan is a lie in motion); one tap restarts it.

## Verified
Driven end to end in headless Chromium against a 128 BPM click: space pause/resume in place, 30 frame-steps moving the marker exactly one second, shift-step one beat, resume from the stepped spot, 63 beat ticks on the wave, the red drop with the honest before-clip max, a 4♩ clip pin reshaping the cut map to `4♩ / 12♩ / 2♩`, the analysis auto-hold going 12♩ at 2× → 24♩ at 1×, the preview painting across a cut boundary, and a full render decoding at 1080×1920 for exactly the planned 10.32s. `tsc` clean, 587 tests pass (3 new planner-pin tests).

author: samirmoustafa
body:
## Problem

`pip install torch-floating-point` fails on macOS because the build unconditionally passes `-fopenmp`, which Apple's clang rejects:

```
clang++: error: unsupported option '-fopenmp'
```

Even if the flag is removed, the extension source includes `<omp.h>`, which Apple's toolchain does not ship unless libomp is installed from Homebrew.

## Change

- **`floating_point/float_round.cpp`**: guard the `#include <omp.h>` with `#ifdef _OPENMP` so the source compiles when OpenMP headers are unavailable.
- **`setup.py`**: skip `-fopenmp` (compile and link flags) on macOS, keeping it on Linux where gcc/clang support it. On macOS the `#pragma omp parallel for` becomes a no-op, so the build falls back to a single-threaded implementation.

No behaviour change on Linux/Windows: OpenMP is still enabled there.

## Verification

- Built and installed on macOS (Apple Silicon, Python 3.13, torch 2.13) without libomp — build succeeds and the quantizer produces correct fp8 e4m3 results.
- Linux/Windows paths are unchanged by construction (`platform.system() != "Darwin"` guard only).

body: City presentation was bound to Bevy's coarse `Res` change detection: eighteen continuously registered synchronizers plus a dozen "this entity is property X" components. Camera origin was already pulled out of `GameSession` so scrolling would not mark gameplay changed; that workaround exposed the larger problem. This replaces that ad-hoc binding framework with one coarse explicit dirty bit. - Entering City binds entity references once (`CityScreenUi`, `IndustryDialogUi`, and the other dialog UI structs) and marks `CityUiDirty`. - City actions mutate `GameState`, then insert `CityUiDirty`. - One `refresh_city_ui` system consumes the marker and rewrites the visible City screen and open dialogs from `GameState`. - Cursor hover and building-action animation stay frame-driven; they are not GameSession projections. - `GameState` remains one ordinary Rust aggregate. It is not split into Bevy resources. A unit test covers the ownership rule: mutating `GameSession` without `CityUiDirty` leaves bound text stale; inserting the marker refreshes it. author: d0ubled0uble
body:
Closes #503.

ECMWF's ordinary output is a reduced Gaussian grid, where each parallel holds a different number of points. GRIB2 opened such a file, named the grid `N32`, and then refused every value — `dimensions()` returned `None` because there is no constant `Ni`, and the decode path stopped at `reader.rs:159`. GRIB1 has decoded its reduced grids since #47, and that is the blueprint this follows.

## What changed

**The `PL` widths survive the parse.** #500 read them only to classify `O`/`N` and dropped them to keep `GridDefinitionSection: Copy`. This is the consumer that justifies paying that cost: the section owns the list and is `Clone` instead. `points_per_row()` mirrors GRIB1's accessor; `dimensions()` reports the raster the rows expand into (widest row × row count), exactly as GRIB1 reports it; `size_label` still answers `N32`/`O32`, which is what a display prefers.

**Decode is sized to the storage layout** (`sum(PL)`), cross-checked against the point count §3 declares for itself. Expansion to the raster happens once, at the napi decode boundary, where `Grib1Handle` already does it. `expand_reduced_to_regular` moved to `fieldglass_core` so both format crates share one definition; the old `fieldglass_grib1` path is kept as a re-export.

**Three things the GRIB1 path had not had to face:**

- An octahedral grid's widest row is 144 where the file still declares `lo2 = 357.1875`, the last column of the narrower `4N` reference grid. The render geometry derives the raster's east edge from the row widths instead; the message table keeps showing what the file says. This is the §3.11 code-1 caveat in the spec — "extreme coordinate values given in grid definition may not be reached in all rows" — made operational.
- One wide row among a million narrow ones is an 8 KB file describing a 262-million-point rectangle. Both readers now cap the raster, not just the stored field.
- A reduced grid reaches every consumer already widened, so its forward map is its family's. GRIB1 was refused one while its *inverse* map already treated it as regular — the image and the contours over it disagreed about one grid.

## How each acceptance criterion was demonstrated

| Criterion | Where |
|---|---|
| Both fixtures decode to the values eccodes decodes | They left `NO_VALUE_CHECK` in `eccodes_reference.rs` and rejoined the fixture walk; the staleness test required it |
| ...and leave the exemption list | `the_exemption_list_has_no_stale_entries`, `the_value_exemptions_have_not_outlived_their_reason` |
| A reduced field renders, probes and contours | `a_reduced_field_renders_probes_and_contours` (napi), and by hand through the built `.node` addon |
| Positions match `grib_get_data` | `rows_sit_on_gaussian_parallels_and_span_the_full_circle` — verified in-session with `grib_get_data -L "%.9f %.9f"`: every row's latitude matches `gaussian_latitudes(32)` to 1e-6°, every point's longitude matches `k·360/PL[j]` to 5e-10°, on both fixtures |
| GRIB1 and GRIB2 place the same grid the same way | `the_two_crates_place_the_same_grid_the_same_way` — corners and a mid-grid point through two different dispatch arms, agreeing to 1e-9 |
| Gaussian latitudes check out | Same test, plus `an_expanded_octahedral_raster_inverts_every_grid_point` in `grid_round_trip.rs` |

The octahedral fixture is a `index mod 50` sawtooth (its builder's own choice), so `the_octahedral_field_decodes_point_for_point` walks all 5,248 values individually — a stronger oracle than the snapshot's min/max/average, which a dropped or reordered point would pass.

## Numbers

- `cargo test --workspace`: 91 test binaries, 0 failures.
- The eccodes value walk's ratchets rise **38 → 46** fixtures, **95 → 120** statistic comparisons, **600 → 770** point comparisons. Raised in this PR so the gain cannot silently regress.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` and `--hook-stage pre-push` both clean, including `cargo deny` and semgrep.

## Found by the pre-PR review pass

Reviewing the diff against eccodes' own `section.3.def` and `docs/architecture/planned/` turned up four things, all fixed here:

- **The grid-type column disagreed across editions.** GRIB1 showed `reduced_gaussian`, GRIB2 `gaussian`, for the same grid — the same class of inconsistency #500 fixed one column over. eccodes draws the distinction (`regular_gg` / `reduced_gg`); GRIB2 now does too. **This is the one behaviour change outside the issue's scope** — see below.
- **The contour seam.** `contour_seam_wraps` listed the regular families only, so the same grid got a one-column gap down the antimeridian in GRIB1 and none in GRIB2.
- **The `PL` gate was stricter than eccodes.** I had gated on Code Table 3.11 reading 1 or 2. eccodes reads the list from the octet count alone and never consults the interpretation, so a file leaving it at its `0` default is one eccodes reads and this would have refused — a breadth regression. Only code 3 is refused now, where the numbers are latitudes in microdegrees.
- **`Nj = 0` with a list the section does not carry** satisfied the length gate (zero entries, zero rows) and reported a `0 × 0` raster where the same octets read as a regular grid report no shape at all.

## Against `docs/architecture/planned/`

`02-trait-seams.md` names the round-trip walk as *the* acceptance test for any inverse, and says a new family belongs in `grid_round_trip.rs` the day it is written — so the expanded octahedral raster is now in it.

`03-composition.md` said GRIB2 "has no answer at all since it does not yet decode reduced grids", which this makes stale; it is updated, and it now records two things **#464 has to carry across**: a `GridGeometry::Gaussian` built straight from the GDS would take `lo2` at face value and misplace every octahedral grid, and `GridGeometry::kind()` answers `"gaussian"` for the variant that holds it, which would undo the family-tag alignment above. Both are choices to make deliberately rather than discover.

## What to look at hardest

1. **The derived east edge.** `reduced_raster_lon_last` deliberately contradicts the message's own `lo2`. The reasoning is in its doc comment and in `the_expanded_raster_east_edge_is_derived_not_declared`; the evidence is that `grib_get_data` puts the O32's widest row at `k·2.5°`, so its last column is at 357.5 and the declared 357.1875 describes a grid the file does not contain. If that reading is wrong, every octahedral render is a fraction of a cell out.
2. **`GridDefinitionSection` losing `Copy`.** The issue called for it; the blast radius turned out to be two call sites. Worth confirming nothing out of tree depended on it — there is a `### Rust API` note.
3. **`template_name` returning a new string.** The only change here a caller could notice that #503 did not ask for. It is small and every in-tree dispatch site already handled both arms, but it is a behaviour change on public API, and splitting it into its own PR is a reasonable ask.
4. **Alternate-row scanning on a reduced grid.** `undo_alternate_reduced_rows` exists so the flag is honoured rather than quietly ignored, and runs on the stored field before expansion (reversing an expanded row is a different operation). No file in the corpus sets it, so it is tested only by construction.

author: sadlilas
body:
## Problem

Everything below the YAML frontmatter in a bundle file is loaded verbatim as the session's **system instruction**, and it is placed **first** — ahead of every context file. Four bundle manifests in this repo carried a title and a descriptive paragraph there, so a session rooted on any of them opened by telling the model a third-person description of itself instead of an instruction.

The same three-line block had been copied across all four:

```markdown
---

# Anchors

A lean, principle-driven bundle. Behavior is shaped by a short set
of named principles loaded once at the head of the system prompt, backed by thin
purposeful agents and a standard tool roster.

@anchors:context/system.md
```

## Mechanism

This is all in this repo:

| Step | Location |
|---|---|
| Body below frontmatter becomes `instruction` | `amplifier_foundation/registry.py` — `bundle.instruction = body.strip()` |
| `instruction` becomes the main system prompt | `amplifier_foundation/bundle/_prepared.py` — `main_instruction = captured_bundle.instruction` |
| It is emitted first, before context | `_prepared.py` — `f"{main_instruction}\n\n---\n\n{all_context}"` |
| Registered as the prompt factory | `_prepared.py` — `context_manager.set_system_prompt_factory(factory)` |

Only instruction — or `@mention` pointers to instruction files — belongs below the frontmatter.

Note that `Bundle.compose()` applies "later replaces earlier" to `instruction`, and `registry.py` composes includes first and then the current bundle. So the body that reaches the system prompt is the **root** bundle's — which is exactly the case for all four of these.

## Change

| File | Removed |
|---|---|
| `bundles/anchors/bundle.md` | heading + descriptive paragraph |
| `bundles/anchors-amp-dev/bundle.md` | heading + descriptive paragraph |
| `experiments/behavioral-anchor/behavioral-anchor.md` | heading + descriptive paragraph |
| `experiments/behavioral-anchor-amplifier-dev/behavioral-anchor-amplifier-dev.md` | heading + descriptive paragraph |

Each file retains the `@mention` that loads its `context/system.md`, which is the actual instruction.

Nothing is lost: every one of these bundles already carries the same description in its frontmatter `bundle.description` field, which is manifest metadata and is never sent to the model.

## Scope

Deliberately narrow: four files, twenty deleted lines, no renames and no frontmatter changes. Two related follow-ups are separate PRs — a validator check that detects this pattern, and the authoring rule written into `docs/BUNDLE_GUIDE.md`.

author: pichinov-jose
body:
## The bug

On narrow screens (`max-width: 767px`), the stylesheet hides the empty product placeholders through the `divempty` class:

```css
.div5 .wrapper2.divempty { ... display gets hidden ... }
```

That class is correctly managed by `LoadProducts()`, which removes it from the tiles it fills and puts it back on the ones it empties.

But **`Search2()` and `MoreProducts()` never touch it**: a tile filled by a search or by pagination keeps its `divempty` class and stays hidden. Searching for a product on a narrow screen therefore displays **nothing at all**, while the data is actually there (the tiles are filled — `prodesc`, `data-rowid`… — but remain `display: none`).

## The fix

`Search2()` and `MoreProducts()` now manage `divempty` exactly like `LoadProducts()` already does: removed from the tiles they fill, added back on the ones they reset. 5 lines, JS only.

## Default behaviour is unchanged on desktop

Above 767px nothing hides `divempty` tiles, so the class change has no visible effect there.

author: stalkervmr
body:
Single commit: **#1691**.

An App that `abi.decode`s its metadata takes raw **bytes** (#1617 pinned that contract), and the scoring path assumed a dict. `AlphaYieldApp` on chain 964 is exactly that shape — plan is data, not code, with `abi.encode(bytes32, uint16)` and no interactions.

Live for ~20 minutes on 2026-08-25: ~300 tracebacks, **0 scored for every miner on every row**, and a sandbox solver run burned per attempt.

```
'str' object does not support item assignment
'str' object has no attribute 'get'
```

Adds `shared.types.plan_metadata_fields(plan)` and reads through it across the scoring path — **eight sites**, four more than the symptom pointed at, including `subtensor_simulator.py:235`, the 964 path itself. Fixing only the obvious four would have left the app equally unscoreable with the error one frame lower.

Also removes a latent bug worth more than the crash: `if "chain_id" not in plan.metadata` is a **substring test** on a str. It passed here for the wrong reason, and on metadata containing that text it would have silently *skipped*. `isinstance`, not `try/except`, precisely so the silent path goes away too.

Safe to drop the injection: chain selection already comes from the authoritative `chain_id` kwarg (`orchestrator.py:2072`); `_get_simulator` uses the metadata hint only as a cross-check.

## Scope

This stops the crash. It is **not** a claim that `optimizeYield` scores — whether the 964 path handles an empty-interactions plan end to end is the next question, answerable via the signed dry-run without consuming a round.

The 964 app stays **paused** until that dry-run passes.

Twelve tests; 4234 unit tests pass.

author: kdedev
body:
## Symptom

Nemo crashes (SIGABRT) while a video is playing in the F3 Quick Preview. The abort comes from glibc heap corruption reached via GDK's window invalidation:

```
#7  cairo_region_destroy (libcairo)
#8  libgdk-3
#11 g_signal_emit_valist
#13 libgdk-3
#14 libgdk-3
#18 g_main_context_iteration
#19 g_application_run
```

Meanwhile, GStreamer streaming threads are active (playbin / appsink / mpegtsdemux).

## Root cause

`new_sample_cb` in `src/nemo-quick-preview.c` is invoked on the GStreamer **streaming thread** (its own comment says so). It was calling `gtk_widget_queue_draw()` directly from that thread. GTK/GDK is not thread-safe, so this races with GDK's window invalidation region on the main thread and eventually frees a `cairo_region_t` under GDK's feet — matching the backtrace exactly.

## Fix

Marshal the redraw to the main thread via a coalesced `g_idle_add_full()`:

- Add `guint redraw_idle_id` to the instance struct, guarded by `frame_mutex`.
- In `new_sample_cb`, schedule a single idle callback (holds a ref on `self`) instead of touching GTK directly. Multiple frames arriving between draws collapse into one queue_draw.
- New `redraw_idle_cb` runs on the main thread and safely calls `gtk_widget_queue_draw()`.
- `media_stop()` cancels the pending idle after tearing down the pipeline, so no leftover redraw can fire against a torn-down state.

## Testing

Reproduced the crash reliably by opening a video in F3 preview. With this patch applied and installed locally, the preview plays without crashing.

author: matthewpmunger
body:
## What & why

Three chunks, one branch, one commit each — read them in order.

**S3 — the page detail is one scroll.** Four tabs meant four routes into one
object, three of which a reader had to guess at. The order is now the argument:
status, then cases, then every reading. `PAGE_DETAIL_SECTIONS` is the only
statement of that order in `src/`, so reading order is data and testable without
a DOM. The same commit retires `NativeElementDisposition` — one word spanning
two registry concepts, which is why one button meant "this does not apply here"
and "I have seen this and I am not acting" at the same time. It becomes
`excluded` (applicability, reason required) and `dismissed` (work_state), which
may both be set because they answer different questions.

**S6 — the pages destination leads with what changed.** The matrix answered
"what are all the numbers" for a reader whose question is "what do I need to
look at". Changes is now the default view; the matrix is the other tab,
untouched. Every actively monitored page lands in exactly one of four groups, no
group claims a reading nobody took, and direction is read over the longest
window a page has evidence for rather than through a seven-day selector that let
a thirty-day slide render as calm.

**S7 — one digest per run.** The webhook was the only outbound channel and wrote
its own summary of the night, in the vocabulary F2 retired. There is one digest
now and everything else is a transport for it. A message is built for every run,
including quiet ones, so an absent message can only mean an absent run — the one
free diagnostic a nightly job can give a reader, and the reason the footer states
the cadence. Following a line lands on the case with a banner naming it, and the
reader can act on arrival.

## Changes

- **S3** — one-scroll page detail driven by `lib/page-detail-sections.ts`; `lib/audits.ts`, the four tabs and 216 lines of tab CSS removed; `NativeElementDisposition` split into `excluded`/`dismissed` with `normalizeNativeElementControls` as the single migrating, validating gate; `setNativeElementApplicability` no longer moves the matching record's lifecycle; `ExclusionReasonPicker` and `HealthChip` extracted; `casePath`/`caseHref` moved to `lib/paths.ts`; registry allowlist entry for `pages/[id]/page.tsx` removed.
- **S6** — Changes view (`lib/pageChanges.ts`, `pages-changes.tsx`) as the default; `lib/pagesView.ts` owns the URL contract; `TabStrip` and `EmptyState` extracted from the issues destination; two rule-18 defects fixed in the Watcher (P35: a device with no comparison rendered as `+0`; P36: an unmeasured page sorted as a perfect one).
- **S7** — `lib/digest.ts` and friends; `issueCasesFrom` extracted to `lib/issue-cases.ts` so a Worker need not import a `"use client"` module; `partitionByImpact` to `impact-format.ts`; digest arrival banner on `/issues/[id]`; `case-detail` actions derived from the registry's actor list; webhook payload **version 2**; `PUBLIC_APP_URL` wired through the collector.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run build` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] Each of the three commits typechecks, lints and passes the suite **on its own**, not only at the branch tip
- [ ] Drove the affected route(s) in the browser (dev server on :3100)

Full suite at the tip: 96 files, 1193 tests, all passing.

## Notes

- **Webhook consumers must be updated.** The daily-digest payload is `version: 2` with a new shape (`site`, `subject`, `text`, `sections[]`). It is a new version rather than a reshaped `version: 1` because a consumer parsing v1 is parsing a summary that no longer exists.
- **`PUBLIC_APP_URL` needs setting per deployment.** Left empty, the digest still sends, with root-relative links that visibly do not resolve. That is deliberate — a deployment that has not been told its own address should fail where someone can see it rather than send links that quietly resolve against whatever opened them.
- **Deferred by design:** the digest cadence is stated, not settable. S8 owns the switch. A persisted field with nothing writing to it is rule 15's empty slot.
- Reading order and group order are asserted as data, not through a renderer. Where a future chunk needs real geometry — overlap, wrapping, measured contrast at a rendered size — that is a program-level decision rather than one to take inside a chunk.

author: nmorasb

author: alexandrefimov
body:
Substrait takes the grouping columns of an aggregate to be the distinct grouping expressions in the order they first appear across its grouping sets, while Calcite takes them from a bit set and emits them ordered by field index. Neither direction accounted for that, so a plan whose sets first mention field 1 and then field 0 changed meaning on the way through: a reference to the aggregate's first column reached the column Calcite had put there instead, and its type changed with it.

Both directions now carry the difference in the emit mapping rather than in the shape of the plan. On the way in, the mapping a relation carries is translated into the order the converted aggregate emits, and a relation that emits directly gets the mapping that puts its columns back in the declared order. On the way out, the mapping presents the aggregate's output in Calcite's order, so a parent converted from the same Calcite plan finds its columns where it left them. Neither direction adds a relation the plan did not have, so a plan that already agrees with Calcite round-trips unchanged — which is what `Substrait2SqlTest.simpleTestGroupingSets` checks, and it is also how I found that fixing only one direction is not enough.

The pre-aggregate projection now reuses one column for a field grouped on by several sets. Two copies of it would each be missing from a grouping set, and Calcite would make both nullable.

Worth a second look, since the change touches a branch that had no coverage: the GROUP_ID branch of `SubstraitRelVisitor.visit(Aggregate)` used a grouping-field count that included a field shared by several sets more than once, which disagrees with `Aggregate.deriveRecordType`. It now uses the distinct count. No query reaches that branch — Calcite folds `GROUP_ID()` into a literal wherever it can work out the answer, including over duplicated grouping sets — so the test that covers it builds the Calcite aggregate directly.

One difference is left alone: the grouping-set index comes back as an i64. The conversion builds Calcite's `GROUP_ID` call as a BIGINT while the spec gives the aggregate an i32 column, and Calcite folds the call to a literal of its own type. That is #1162.

Closes #1159

author: somuai
body:
## What does this PR do?
Fixes #38239

When calling `litellm.rerank()` with Vertex AI semantic ranker models and `return_documents=True` (the default), the response transformer previously discarded the returned `content` field from each record.

This change:
1. In `transform_rerank_response`, checks whether `return_documents` is true (via `optional_params`, `request_data`, `litellm_params`, or default `True`) and populates `document={"text": record["content"]}` when `record.get("content")` is present.
2. If `return_documents=False`, the `document` field is omitted from results as expected.
3. Adds unit and integration tests verifying vertex rerank response transformation with `return_documents=True` and `return_documents=False`.

author: wjduvall-cmd
body:
`help@jwlabs.ai` is live: Email Routing is provisioned on the `jwlabs.ai` zone, `MAIL` in `build-md.mjs` is `help@jwlabs.ai`, and all 26 served pages publish that address and no other.

Three passages in this README still said the opposite — and each told the next reader to leave it that way. Left alone they are an instruction to un-fix something already fixed. Worklist: foray's `docs/jwlabs-dev-domain-inventory.md`, items **W1–W4**.

## What was wrong

| # | Passage | Why it had to change |
|---|---|---|
| **W1** | The note at the top of the file | Said Email Routing was on the `jwlabs.dev` zone **only**, that `help@jwlabs.ai` "would accept nothing and drop mail silently", and that publishing a `.dev` address on a `.ai` site was therefore deliberate. All false now — and the block already contradicted its own heading. |
| **W2** | The cutover bullet | Gated the mismatch on "until Email Routing exists on the new zone", and pointed the reader back at W1 before "fixing" it. That gate has been met. |
| **W3** | "The `jwlabs.dev` zone stays" | Right conclusion, falsified reason. If the reason is disproved someone deletes the zone — taking out the 301 that every stale `.dev` URL still depends on. |
| **W4** | The Pages-origin claim | `https://jw-incorporated.github.io/jwlabs.dev/` now **301s to `http://jwlabs.ai/`**, so the site can no longer be previewed there before DNS propagates. |

## The part this deliberately does not claim

It does **not** say the address is proven to work. DNS shows the zone is *configured*; it does not show a routing rule exists with a *verified* destination, and Cloudflare publishes MX and reports `status: ready` before that is true — in which state mail is rejected or dropped.

So **step 13** (send a real message, confirm it arrives) is marked as the unticked check that settles it, and its old rationale — "The address did not change" — is corrected, because the published address *did* change and this is the mailbox's first delivery. If the test fails, fix the routing rule; the answer is still not to republish a `.dev` address.

That safeguard replaces the one W1 was providing, so removing W1 does not remove the caution.

## Untouched on purpose

- The runbook `curl` probes that target `jwlabs.dev` and expect a 301 — verified still passing.
- Step 14's instruction to move the store URLs to `jwlabs.ai` (that is the action item, not a defect).
- Every repository/Pages URL spelling `jwlabs.dev` — the repo really is named that.

## Verification

- `node build.mjs` → exit 0, **26 pages, 737 internal links all resolve**, `CNAME` + `.nojekyll` guards pass.
- **`docs/` is byte-for-byte unchanged** — this is prose and comments only. No hand-editing under `docs/`.
- No `<script>`, no dependencies, no remote origins.
- No size or headcount signalling introduced (grepped every added line).
- MX/SPF values quoted in the new text re-resolved from this machine; the Pages 301 and `https_enforced: false` measured, not assumed.

author: hidetzu
body:
## What this records

⚠ **`CLAUDE.md` §9 gets its first row.** It is not an analogy from another project — it happened
here, found in review of hidetzu/tcpip-stack#3.

`docs/SPEC.md` §1 claimed that a read that could not be made is reported as its own outcome, and
named `tests/static.sh` and `tests/real.sh` as asserting it. ⚠ **Neither did.** ⚠ **The gap was
already written down** — the completion report on hidetzu/tcpip-stack#2 said that check was
missing — ⚠ **and the row was left standing anyway.** A human reading the table found it; no check
did.

## Where the rule lives

⚠ **One subject, one owner. No second copy.**

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/SPEC.md` §1 | ⚠ **"What asserts it" names a case, not a file.** Run it before filling the row in, and read whether it covers every clause of the claim |
| `.claude/rules/README.md` | a pointer to that, and nothing else |
| `CLAUDE.md` §9 | the row, citing both |

## The wall is partial, and the row says so

`tests/static.sh` `spec_names_checks_that_exist` reads §1's "What asserts it" column and checks
every case name it finds against that entry point's `--list`.

⚠ **It catches a case name that does not exist.** ⚠ **It cannot catch a case that exists and does
not cover the clause — which is exactly what happened here.** Reading the case is still the
reviewer's job, and `CLAUDE.md` §9 states that limit rather than implying a wall it does not build.

## Verification

⚠ **Copied from what each runner announced**, on a clean tree:

```
static: 5 of 5 cases passed          (checked 8 entry points and 6 case names named by docs/SPEC.md §1)
  report: 6 of 6 cases passed
real: 5 of 5 cases passed
foreign: 2 of 2 cases passed
```

### Mutation check — ⚠ broken on purpose, both sides, failure text verbatim

| What was broken | What it said |
|---|---|
| a case renamed in `docs/SPEC.md` so it no longer exists | `docs/SPEC.md says tests/real.sh asserts a_timer_running_out_is_handled, and that case does not exist` |
| the §1 heading renamed, so the parsing matches nothing | `read 0 entry points and 0 case names out of docs/SPEC.md §1, which cannot be right` |

⚠ **The second is the one that matters.** Without it the case stays green when the parsing quietly
matches nothing — a check that passes on an empty table asserts nothing.

## ⚠ What did not run

⚠ **There is still no CI here.** Every number above was measured by hand on one machine
(Arch Linux, kernel `7.0.2-arch1-1`, `unshare -Urn` as uid 1000, 2026-08-26).
⚠ **Nothing has been shown reproducible elsewhere.**

author: katagun
body:
Lands the fixes from the two rounds of security/architecture review onto `main`. The branch also carries the docs-archive cleanup and (already on `main`) the landing page + hardened Pages workflow.

## Round 1 — High-severity fixes

- **Path traversal** in snapshot loading (`storage/filesystem.py`): `load_disk_snapshot` / `load_memory_snapshot` joined a caller-supplied name onto the storage dir with no validation, reachable via `/api/diff` and `/api/memory/snapshots/diff` query params. Added a `_safe_component` guard.
- **Recipe-quoting injection** (`providers/large_files.py`): the advice recipe hand-built `echo '...'` around a raw path — an apostrophe crashed cleanup and a crafted filename injected into the generated script. Now quotes the whole message with `shlex.quote`.
- **Docker feature silently broken** (`providers/docker.py`): parsed `docker system df --format json` as one object, but modern Docker emits NDJSON keyed by `Type`, so it reported nothing. Rewrote to parse NDJSON (with legacy fallback).

## Round 1 — "Fix now" tier (threat-model-independent)

- **M5** kill re-validates the PID still maps to the shown process before signalling.
- **M7b** `serve` opens the browser only after the server answers (no bind race).
- **P1** memory-observation polling is O(1) / amortized instead of a full read+rewrite per poll.
- **P3** cleanup console buffer capped.
- **P4/L2** SQLite gets WAL + `busy_timeout`.
- **A4** microsecond snapshot names (no same-second clobber).
- **L10** treemap tiles navigate via the SPA router.

## Round 2 — Findings from a deeper adversarial pass

- **`build_script` newline injection** (HIGH): a file with a newline in its name injected *uncommented* executable lines into the "everything is commented out" script — the Round-1 recipe-quoting fix didn't cover the comment embedding. Now escapes control chars in labels + recipes.
- **Prune regression** (HIGH, introduced by P1): prune wrote observations newest-first while `latest_memory_observation` reads the last line as newest. Now writes oldest-last.
- **Rich terminal injection** (MEDIUM): a filename with markup crashed the scan table and ANSI/OSC escapes reached the terminal. Cells now render as inert `Text` with control chars stripped.
- **`_names_match` false-accepts** (MEDIUM): a recycled PID running any `* Helper` passed the kill guard on a generic shared token. Generic tokens no longer count.
- **paths.yaml data-loss labels** (MEDIUM): `open-webui-data` → dangerous + advice; `gpt4all` / `invokeai` / `tabby` scoped to model files/subdirs instead of whole app-data dirs (chat DBs, images).
- Hygiene: browser-poll thread catches any startup-race error; `entry_ids` bounded; dead electron-builder glob removed; tailwind alpha floor → `^4.0.0`; `.claude/settings.local.json` gitignored.

## Not included (out of scope / needs a decision)

macOS codesigning/notarization (needs an Apple cert), the Electron port TOCTOU and `deploy.sh` shell replay (local-attacker only under a single-user threat model), and floor-only dependency pins (standard Python practice). The `diskdoctor` PyPI name is still unclaimed — worth reserving before publishing.

## Verification

Full suite **298 Python tests** + **162 web tests** pass; `ruff`, `mypy --strict`, and `tsc --noEmit` clean. Each behavior change ships with a regression test.

author: zxypro1
body:
## 这一关和第 10 关的区别

NetworkPolicy 判的是「这个 IP 属于一个带某某标签的 Pod」。标签是 apiserver 里的一个字段，有权限的人随时能改。网格判的是另一件事：**对面出示的证书属于谁** —— 一次真的 mTLS 双向验证，身份来自 ServiceAccount。

两者不是替代关系：一个管网络可达性，一个管身份，叠着用。

## 做进来的

**Istio ambient 的判定面**（`src/lib/opslab/mesh/`）。PeerAuthentication（STRICT 拒明文）、AuthorizationPolicy（DENY > 无策略放行 > 有 ALLOW 则其余默认拒绝）、SPIFFE 身份。按设计文档的路线，不做 HBONE 的字节流：那一层对「排查网格」没有教学价值，实现量却足以淹没其余部分。

**L7 要有 waypoint**。带 `methods` / `paths` 的规则 ztunnel 求值不了，于是那一条等于不存在，而 apiserver 照样收下它。和第 10 关「没有 CNI 时 NetworkPolicy 是废纸」是同一类问题 —— 这次 `istioctl analyze` 会直接报出来（IST0162）。

**istioctl**，行为等价重写。真 istioctl 编进多合一二进制要多背一份 Istio 的 API 与 proto，产物会涨一大截，而它在这里的价值全在输出上：`ztunnel-config workload` 的 PROTOCOL 列（HBONE / TCP 一眼看出谁进了网格）、`x describe pod` 把身份/mTLS 模式/命中的策略摆在一起、`analyze` 的三类告警、`proxy-status`。

## 被自己的判定抓到两件事

**curl 把连接层的 RST 也报成 35**。35 是 TLS 握手阶段的问题（拿明文打 HTTPS 端口那种）；ztunnel 拒绝一条明文连接是**建连之后收到 RST**，curl 报的是 `(56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`。两个码指向不同的层，混在一起就白瞎了这条线索。

**参考解一开始是错的**：只把 `payments` 接进网格，STRICT 一开，Gateway 的数据面（在 `envoy-gateway-system`，不在网格里）自己第一个被挡在外面，门户对外直接不可用。这正是真集群里上 STRICT 最常见的事故，写进 pitfalls 了，参考解也补上了入口命名空间的接入。

## 验证

19 个网格用例 + 3 个关卡反向验证。全量 1433 个通过。

Both approved by Joseph 2026-08-25, from the measured 39m09 run
(deploy.full_convergence_seconds=2349).

**1. The pre-warm regression, fixed.** Priming the candidate revision
with the FULL service minimum made the no-traffic deploy wait for that
many instances to go Ready — us-east4 pins 8, and the parallel warm
step ran **7m37** instead of ~2m: the 100%-stall cost moved into the
warm and grew. The revision minimum is now a primer,
`min(TR_CLOUD_RUN_PREWARM_MIN_INSTANCES=2, service minimum)`: enough to
absorb the 10% step instantly, with the staged 10/50/100 ramp giving
Cloud Run scale time for the rest. Pinned by two harness executions: a
high-min region (8) primes at 2; a cold region (1) never exceeds its
own steady state.

**2. Per-secondary post-100% watch: 3m → 1m** (9 of the measured 39
minutes). By the time a secondary reaches 100%, the image has served
the primary's full ramp AND its 3-minute canary — which is untouched,
and is now the only `duration-min 3` in the workflow — plus that
region's own two gated windows.

Expected next full deploy: **~27-28m** full convergence, self-reported
by the run per the existing metrics step.

author: marcostaz
body:
## Failing-before state-machine probe

`FAILING_BEFORE_PROVEN / DRAFT / DO NOT MERGE / NOT OWNER REPAIR / NOT CANONICAL`

Exact base: Notification owner candidate #442 `bcf1aa9ea41dceb78e28a69e5204ffdb5680e440`.
Exact HEAD: `438ca20ef805dd4397104ab8a594d7fffc0deae0`.

### Proven sequence
Current mobile notification fallback does:

`opportunity_event unread -> scheduleNotificationAsync(trigger:null) resolves -> api.markAlertDelivered(event_id) -> opportunity_events.delivered_at becomes non-NULL`

Expo SDK 57 documents `scheduleNotificationAsync()` as scheduling a notification and resolving with its identifier; scheduling success does not prove that the notification was presented when triggered.

### State invariant
`SCHEDULE_ACCEPTED != DELIVERY_COMPLETED`.

A scheduling acknowledgement may authorize a durable `scheduled/accepted` state, but it must not by itself authorize a semantic `delivered` completion state.

### Exact-head failing-before evidence
ObraSignal Quality on `438ca20ef805dd4397104ab8a594d7fffc0deae0`:
- Python check `97998367469`: FAILURE, as intended; the new state-machine probe detects the current schedule->delivered transition.
- Mobile check `97998367302`: SUCCESS; the owner mobile surface still builds/bundles while the semantic state invariant is deliberately RED in Python.

### Reproducer
Adds one intentionally failing Python Quality probe that detects the exact current `showLocalOpportunityAlert(item)` followed by `markAlertDelivered(item.event_id)` transition.

### Ownership
Notification Delivery owns the repair/policy. This State Machines Factory owns only the state invariant and failing-before proof. Do not repair on this probe branch.

### Reopen/passing-after condition
Notification owner must introduce an authority-correct state transition in which scheduling acceptance cannot write semantic delivery completion. Passing-after must prove the repaired exact owner HEAD and preserve tenant binding, retry/exhaustion policy and provider-delivery semantics.

No merge/deploy/prod/provider/config/secret/device/customer mutation.

author: noureldinshobier
body:
Probed the ORM for SQL injection across `order`, `select`, `group`, `joins`, `where` keys, `updateAll`, `insertAll` and `annotate`.

**It held.** Identifiers are validated rather than escaped — the right call, since a column name cannot be a bound parameter — and `annotate` already strips `*/`, so an annotation cannot close its own comment and turn the rest of the string into statements. Rails patched exactly that.

A negative result is still worth writing down. The checks exist and nothing said so, which is how a later refactor removes one without anybody noticing. `order` taking a column straight from a query string is the ordinary way this gets reached.

### One real fix

`LIMIT` and `OFFSET` cannot be bound either, so the number is interpolated — through `Number`, which is what stops a string being SQL, and what lets a non-number through as the text `NaN`:

```
Post.all().limit(Number(params.get("per_page")))
-> SELECT ... LIMIT NaN
```

With no `per_page` in the query string, that is what an ordinary pagination call produces. The failure then arrives from the database as a syntax error pointing at generated SQL, rather than at the call that was wrong. Refused at the call now, and `limit(0)` still works because no rows is a real page size.

19 tests. Suite at 2,772.

author: claudespice
body:
## Summary

`base_path` in `CreateTableOptions` is a real filesystem location, not a label: for every
non-S3, non-memory-mode table, `create_table` creates `<base_path>/<table_id>/<snapshot_id>`
(`cayenne_catalog.rs`, the initial-snapshot durability step).

35 of the 56 `cayenne_catalog` tests pinned that root under `/tmp` — `/tmp/cayenne_test` and
about twenty siblings — so the root is shared with every other account on the machine. Where
the suite also runs under CI, the runner account creates those directories first (mode 755),
and every later run as any other account fails `create_dir_all` with `PermissionDenied`.
`/tmp`'s sticky bit means no other account can remove or replace them, so it does not
self-heal. Concurrent runs of the suite collide there for the same reason, and a test that
leaves a root behind changes what the next run sees.

Measured on a host that doubles as a self-hosted runner:

```
$ cargo test -p cayenne --lib cayenne_catalog        # before
Failed to create table: Io { source: Os { code: 13, kind: PermissionDenied, ... } }
test result: FAILED. 21 passed; 35 failed

$ ls -ld /tmp/cayenne_test
drwxr-xr-x  222 runner  wheel  ...
```

Because `make signoff` runs `make nextest` over the whole workspace, this failed local
sign-off on such a host for **any** PR, whatever it touched.

## Changes

- A `test_table_root()` helper hands each test a `tempfile::TempDir` of its own plus the
  `base_path` string, and every affected test binds the guard for its whole body, so the root
  is private and removed on drop. The four tests that go through
  `setup_table_with_delete_file` pass a named subdirectory of their own root, keeping the
  distinct locations those tests are about.
- The FS-free configuration-comparison tests (`configuration_matches` /
  `log_configuration_differences`) keep opaque roots — their `base_path` is only ever compared
  for equality and never reaches the filesystem — but no longer spell them as `/tmp` paths.
  That is what lets the new guard be absolute instead of carrying an exception list.
- Recorded delete-file and partition `path:` values are left alone: they are metastore row
  content, never opened.

No production code changes; the whole diff is inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.

## Test plan

- `make lint` — clippy over `--tests` is what this needed: the first cut tripped
  `items_after_statements` (an inserted binding pushed a `const`/`use` below a statement) and
  `implicit_clone`, neither of which `cargo test` sees.
- `make test` / `make nextest`
- Targeted, on a host where `/tmp/cayenne_test` is owned by another account:
  `cargo test -p cayenne --lib cayenne_catalog` — **21 passed / 35 failed before, 57 passed /
  0 failed after** (56 pre-existing tests plus the new guard), same host, same account.
- `cargo test -p cayenne --lib` on the same host: **1097 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored** — the
  whole crate suite, which could not run to completion here before.
- New regression test `no_table_root_is_pinned_under_tmp` fails on the pre-fix source (it
  reports 47 pinned lines) and passes after. Verified non-vacuous by a neuter matrix: both
  arms of its predicate were re-introduced one at a time (`base_path: "/tmp/…".to_string()`
  and `let base_path = "/tmp/…".to_string();`) and each failed the guard with the offending
  line named. It is textual on purpose — the failure it prevents is environmental, so a run on
  a host where the running account happens to own the path cannot catch a new one.

## Review gate

- Adversarial review: **skipped** — re-run on the current head (`af91e78`) after the review-comment
  fix, same outcome. `codex` is the only engine installed here and it returned
  `Codex error: Your workspace is out of credits. Ask your workspace owner to refill in order
  to continue.` (receipt `engine=none exit=1`); the `grok` companion is not installed on this
  host, and under `claudespice` it is the only permitted fallback.
- `/security-review`: no findings. The whole diff sits inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (first
  changed line 5360; the module starts at 5356) in one file, adds no production code path, and
  introduces no external input, process, network, crypto, or auth surface. The one notable
  addition is a compile-time `include_str!` of the file's own source inside a test.
- `/simplify`: two cleanups applied — the guard now trims each line once via `filter_map`
  instead of trimming the start in the filter and both ends in the report, and its doc no
  longer claims "every table root these tests create" for a guard that reads a single file
  (the failure message now names that file). The guard was re-neutered after the rewrite to
  confirm it still fires. No behaviour changed and no test was weakened.
- Copilot raised one finding — `to_string_lossy()` would build the table tree at a
  replacement-character path while the guard removed the real one — which is valid and in scope;
  fixed in `af91e78` by taking `to_str()` and failing where the path is produced. Thread replied
  to and resolved.

Fixes #13527

## Checklist

- [x] Reproduced the failure and confirmed the mechanism directly (`mkdir /tmp/cayenne_test/probe` → `Permission denied`)
- [x] Regression test fails on the pre-fix source and passes after
- [x] Neuter matrix run over both arms of the guard's predicate
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cayenne --tests` clean
- [ ] `make signoff` green and `Attestation` re-run

scripts/lib/schema-cli.ts:14        AZURE_HOST = forestgeo-mysqldataserver.mysql.database.azure.com
```

Every dev deploy already runs `apply-schema-migrations --all-sites --apply` and `deploy-validations-to-all-schemas` against that host, so the live schemas have been migrated forward all along. This is an **app-only promotion** — the database is already at the target state:

```
apply-schema-migrations --all-sites --check   ->  12/12 schemas, pending: (none), contract OK
check-schema-contract   --all-sites           ->  schema-contract OK: 12 schemas
```

The `migrate-and-verify-production` job should therefore be a no-op, and there is no schema rollback to consider.

## Conflict resolution

Two conflicts, both in the docs site, both resolved in favor of dev:

- `frontend/docs/astro.config.mjs` — sidebar label rename, same slug
- `frontend/docs/src/content/docs/publishing-census-to-smithsonian-db.mdx` — main's copy predates the docs audit and carries stale limits (Tag max 10 vs the correct 20)

The resulting tree is **byte-identical** to `forestgeo-app-development`; `main` contributed no file that dev lacks.

## Required follow-up after deploy

Async upload ships in this promotion but is **not enabled on live**. The feature gate is fail-closed and `forestgeo-livesite` has no `ASYNC_*` app settings, so every live user silently keeps the synchronous upload path. Enabling it requires setting `ASYNC_UPLOAD_ENABLED`, `ASYNC_UPLOAD_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS`, and `ASYNC_UPLOAD_ALLOWED_USERS` on the web app. `alwaysOn` is already `true`, so the worker prerequisite is met.

## Known issue this does not fix

Cooks Branch ingestion. `forestgeo_cooksbranch` census 2 holds 11,028 measurements, 0 ingested, 100% parked, and the root cause predates the June deploy — that site has never ingested a measurement. Being tracked separately.

AutoFit previously used JavaScript truthiness (`!cell.value` / `if (cell.value)`) in the row path, main-thread column path, and worker input path. Canonical zero and FALSE render values were therefore treated as empty and did not contribute to measured dimensions.

author: hjosugi
body:
The library screen wraps its whole read and reports a storage failure as an alert:

```ts
const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
  try { /* listDocuments, listNotes, listRecoveryCopies */ }
  catch (error) { showStorageError(error); }
}, []);
```

The Recovery screen did neither:

```ts
const refresh = useCallback(async () => setCopies(await listRecoveryCopies()), []);
useEffect(() => { void refresh(); }, [refresh]);
```

No try/catch, and `void` with no `.catch`. A storage failure left the rejection
unhandled — silent in a release build — and `copies` empty, which this screen
renders as:

> 復旧が必要な中断編集はありません。
> No interrupted edits need recovery.

A reassurance. On the one screen whose entire job is to say whether interrupted
work survived. Given at the moment it had failed to look — and someone reading it
would reasonably stop looking.

This is reachable through the exact failure fixed in #140: a database that will
not open. Before that fix it also persisted for the life of the process, so the
screen would have gone on saying it.

### The fix

The read is guarded like the library screen's, and **unreadable is now a distinct
state from empty**: it says storage is unavailable and so whether anything can be
recovered is unknown, as an alert, with a retry.

### What is and is not tested

A test pins the contract the distinction rests on — `listRecoveryCopies` **rejects
rather than resolving empty** when the database cannot be opened. An empty resolve
would be indistinguishable from having looked and found nothing, and the fix would
be pointless. It uses the `failNextOpen` seam from #140.

The screen itself is not rendered in any test: mobile has no UI test harness, which
is #60. So it is verified by typecheck and by the catalogue's ja/en parity test,
and I am saying so rather than implying more.

`npm test` 176 passing, typecheck clean.

author: baldugus
body:
# Describe what this PR does #

Refreshes CephFS recursive statistics before collecting filesystem usage.

Linux CephFS `statfs()` overrides filesystem statistics for quota-backed mounts using the quota inode's cached `rbytes` value ([source](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/26260251022fbc2f248a3d747a9b2b961b18d2d8/fs/ceph/quota.c#L531)) instead of using the fresh values like the regular `statfs()` path  ([source](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/26260251022fbc2f248a3d747a9b2b961b18d2d8/fs/ceph/super.c#L74)).

On the other hand, Ceph MDS only broadcasts new statistics when usage changes by approx. 1/16 of the difference between the last reported usage and the max quota available ([source](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/162eb4aeca88382affe501526ab04c3bcd087dad/src/mds/MDCache.cc#L2129)).

Slow growing volumes can remain for long periods with stale usage and consequently stale `kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes`. In my cluster I noticed my metrics database had several PVCs reporting the same used bytes for a whole month, despite constant write activity.

Neither behavior is wrong on its own, so I wrote this patch intending to make the statistics accurate in ceph-csi.

I've ran the added E2E test on the latest commit at devel (f4ce351) and in this PR and I could reproduce a fail before and a pass after.

I've also replaced my production ceph-csi with this patch and all affected volumes started reporting the current usage.

This is my manual reproduction before the patch on my kubernetes host:

```bash
$ df -B1 <kubelet globalmount path>
Filesystem 1-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted on
<path> 10737418240 0 10737418240 0% <path>

$ # fetched ceph.dir.rbytes using a perl script as the host lacks getfattr
203487451

$ df -B1 <kubelet globalmount path>
Filesystem 1-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted on
<path> 10737418240 201326592 10536091648 2% <path>
```

## Is there anything that requires special attention ##

This is my first contribution to ceph-csi. I believe this change is backward compatible.

If this is accepted, is it worth updating the pending release notes? I was unsure about it, so I didn't include an update in this PR.

## Related issues ##

#2579

## Future concerns ##

This adds an MDS request when collecting CephFS volume statistics. If a CephFS-side change makes `statfs()` sufficient in the future, this patch could be reconsidered.

**Checklist:**

* [x] **Commit Message Formatting**: Commit titles and messages follow
  guidelines in the [developer
  guide](https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/blob/devel/docs/development-guide.md#commit-messages).
* [x] Reviewed the developer guide on [Submitting a Pull
  Request](https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/blob/devel/docs/development-guide.md#development-workflow)
* [ ] [Pending release
  notes](https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/blob/devel/PendingReleaseNotes.md)
  updated with breaking and/or notable changes for the next major release.
* [ ] Documentation has been updated, if necessary.
* [ ] Unit tests have been added, if necessary.
* [x] Integration tests have been added, if necessary.

body:
Follow-up to #201 / v0.17.1. The tag workflow built and uploaded wheels it never imported, which is how a 3.11-only import shipped on the declared 3.10 floor in two releases.

**New `smoke-floor` job** (after the wheel/sdist builds, before either registry): downloads the `wheels-*` artifacts, sets up Python **3.10**, installs the engine's declared runtime deps from PyPI, then installs **only the engine** with `--no-index --find-links dist --no-deps "yantrikdb==${TAG#v}"` — so the artifact under test provably comes from this run — and asserts `import yantrikdb`, `__version__ == importlib.metadata.version == tag`, and a `record_text` → `get(rid)` round trip (no recall, no async-index race).

**Gating**: `publish-pypi` needs `smoke-floor`; `publish-crates` needs `smoke-floor` **and** `publish-pypi` — serialized, as its own comment already required ("the irreversible surface must not publish ahead of the recoverable one").

Not exercised by PR CI (tag-triggered workflow); first real run is the next tag.

body:
## Outcome

Implements issue #17: the accessible desktop authoring experience (Studio). The visual deck editor edits the versioned domain model through its typed API — every user action is one closed-vocabulary op applied and revalidated fail-closed in Rust — with drag/drop PLUS full keyboard parity, inspector validation, undo/redo, atomic autosave through the #15 persistence pipeline, zoom, en-US/pt-BR localization, and a component-level UI suite including keyboard-path parity and screen-reader semantics for all control states. No Cloud collaboration, no generative builder.

Issue: #17
Dependencies merged: yes (#5, #7, #15, #16)
Base SHA: b4be4826057dd31a6e2b3abc6782812e1fc9b890
Expected head SHA: 550a909ce14435abc7633c4ee61f230fe2fa093a

AGENT_PLANNER: m1-studio-planner
AGENT_IMPLEMENTER: m1-studio-implementer
AGENT_VERIFIER: m1-studio-verifier
AGENT_REVIEWER: m1-studio-reviewer
AGENT_SECURITY: m1-studio-security
AGENT_EVALUATOR: m1-studio-evaluator

## Binding constraint honored (PR #75 gate)

NO source-visibility/input-mute OBS consent surface exists anywhere in this PR. The editing vocabulary (`StudioOp`) cannot express action configuration at all this milestone — only deck/page/control/profile authoring. The capability file still grants zero plugin/core permissions; no network surface exists.

## Scope

In:

- **Schema v2** (`migrations/sqlite/0002_workspace_documents.sql` + `WorkspaceStore`): authored deck/profile documents as canonical validated JSON keyed by closed kind + UUIDv7; deterministic load order; whole-snapshot all-or-nothing rewrite transactions (WAL + `synchronous=FULL`); fail-closed refusal of structurally damaged rows. The crate-global chain upgrade path is exercised against the real v1→v2 step; fresh multi-step installs no longer produce pointless pre-migration backup artifacts.
- **Authoritative editing service** (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/studio.rs`): closed serde-tagged `StudioOp` vocabulary (22 ops across decks/pages/controls/profiles/folders); `apply_op` mutates through `openstream-domain` by value, bumps revisions via the domain API, validates entire documents fail-closed, and leaves input byte-identical on refusal with typed tokens; grid collisions are recomputed as non-blocking diagnostics (reported, never rejected). `EditorSession` keeps bounded snapshot stacks (100/direction) and persists the ENTIRE workspace in one transaction after every accepted mutation/undo/redo; persistence failures degrade honestly (`saved=false` + token) while memory keeps serving. UUIDv7 minting stays in Rust.
- **Four application-defined commands** (`studio_load/apply/undo/redo`): the only new WebView authority; capability file still grants zero plugin/core permissions and its description now states this truthfully.
- **Studio UI** (`apps/desktop/ui/src/studio/`): typed wire-contract mirror; fail-closed decoder pinning the Rust golden fixtures byte-for-byte as cross-language serialization evidence; bridge port (Tauri IPC realization + scripted fake); pure view reducer (selection reconciliation, zoom levels 50–200%, lift state, polite announcements); pure keyboard bindings; plain-factory views (canvas grid, pages rail, folders tree, profiles panel, inspector, toolbar/footer).
- **Keyboard parity**: lift→arrows→drop emits byte-identical `move_control` ops to pointer drag+drop; Shift/Alt+Shift resize paths match inspector resizes; Delete matches inspector delete; Ctrl+Z/Y match toolbar undo/redo; Escape cancels cleanly; typing targets keep native text editing.
- **Executable accessibility contract** (`src/testing/shell-a11y.test.ts`, evolved from the M0 shell contract): renders the exact shipped markup over a 20+-state × 2-locale matrix asserting document language/title/self-containment, single h1 before labelled h2s, DOM order as reading order, zero manual tabindex, hidden decorative shapes with textual status beside them, accessible names for every button, label/field associations, grid geometry stated in words, disabled/selected/lifted/overlap states carried by TEXT (aria-label suffixes, badges, aria-describedby), role="alert" refusals, role="status" autosave honesty, polite announcement region, and full catalog coverage per locale (placeholder templates matched as patterns).
- **Localization**: catalog extended (~110 keys × en-US/pt-BR) with identical key coverage, trimmed non-empty values, `{name}` placeholder formatting, and localized refusal sentences for every error token.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture/STUDIO_EDITOR.md` (architecture, op vocabulary, keyboard map, failure-path table, security note, compatibility/rollback); `DESKTOP_LIFECYCLE.md` artifact inventory updated to three files (`workspace.sqlite3` joins journal + lock).

Out:

- No Cloud collaboration or generative builder (issue out-of-scope rule). No action binding/graph wiring (later milestones). No OBS consent surfaces (binding constraint). No engine connection changes; the footer still states "not connected" honestly.

## User-visible behavior

The Studio window is now a working editor: create/rename/delete decks into folder paths, add/remove/reorder pages, place/move/resize/relabel/disable controls of four kinds with kind-appropriate interaction policies, group decks into profiles with ordered switching, undo/redo everything, zoom 50%–200% (44 px minimum target preserved), and see autosave truth plus collision warnings at all times — fully operable by keyboard alone and announced legibly to screen readers, in English or Brazilian Portuguese.

## Security, privacy, and permissions

- Risk: medium (issue-declared). Effective authority does not exceed explicit grants: four local document-editing commands; zero plugin permissions; no network; documents hold authored labels/titles only (no secrets, no execution evidence, no telemetry).
- Fail-closed posture end-to-end: unknown op variants reject at serde; ids parse as canonical UUIDv7 or refuse; client decoder refuses invalid snapshots before render; service revalidates every document after every op; unreadable persisted rows refuse the whole load instead of silent drops.
- Threat-model impact: none negative — no new capability rows, no peer-triggerable surface, secrets untouched behind the OS vault boundary.

## Compatibility and migration

Fresh installs create schema v2 directly; existing v1 stores (journal AND workspace) upgrade through the standard verified-backup path with rollback-on-failure; older builds refuse newer stores (`SchemaTooNew`). Rollback: revert the three commits; `workspace.sqlite3` is ignored by older builds and can be deleted to drop authored content without touching journal evidence.
